**1.** The process of buying, selling and distribution of goods and services is known as:

a) Trade.
b) Commerce.
c) Marketing,
d) Wholesale trade.

**Commerce** covers all the activities that bring goods and services from producers to consumers: buying, selling and distribution, together with the services that help them (transport, banking, insurance, warehousing, communication, advertising). Trade is only the buying and selling part, marketing is the management of the marketing mix, and wholesale trade is one stage of distribution.

**Answer: B.**

**2.** Branding is suitable for which of the following?

*Options as printed:* A) Competitive advertising.   B) Persuasive advertising.   C) Informative advertising.   D) Marketing mix.

Branding gives a product a name, symbol or design that sets it apart from rival products. It is therefore closely tied to **competitive advertising**, which promotes one brand against competing brands. Persuasive advertising also uses brands, so the printed options overlap and the question is left open.

**Intended answer: A (Competitive advertising).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

**3.** A clean bill of lading signifies that:

a) The colour is pure white.
b) It has no record of damaged goods.
c) It is a document of authority.
d) It could be transferred to anybody.

A bill of lading is signed by the shipping company. It is called **clean** when the captain or the shipping company has noted no damage and no shortage on the goods received on board. If damage is noted the bill is called claused (or dirty). The colour has nothing to do with it.

**Answer: B.**

**4.** Profits are rewards paid to :

a) Shareholders.
b) Capital.
c) Manager.
d) Entrepreneur.

The factors of production are rewarded as follows: land gets rent, labour gets wages, capital gets interest and the **entrepreneur** gets profit, because he organises production and takes the risk. A manager receives a salary, and shareholders of a company receive dividends, which are a share of the profit.

**Answer: D.**

**5.** Which of the following is NOT a necessary sea port facility?

*Options as printed:* A) Crane.   B) Docks.   C) Warehouse.   D) Containers.

Cranes, docks (berths) and warehouses (transit sheds) are fixed facilities of a port. Containers are boxes that carry the goods rather than equipment of the port itself, so they are the best candidate for the intended answer. However a container terminal is also a port facility, so the printed question is ambiguous and is left open.

**Intended answer: D (Containers).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

**6.** The price quotations which contains the cost, insurance charges and the cost of transportation is..?

a) F.O.R.
b) C&F
c) F.A.S
d) C.I.F.

**C.I.F.** means Cost, Insurance and Freight: the price covers the goods, the insurance and the carriage up to the port of destination. C&F has no insurance, F.A.S. (free alongside ship) and F.O.R. (free on rail) stop earlier.

**Answer: D.**

**7.** Which of the following trade documents is NOT necessary when ordering goods?

a) Quotation.
b) Letter of enquiry.
c) Invoice.
d) Order form.

The buyer first sends a letter of enquiry, the seller replies with a quotation, and the buyer then places the order on an order form. The **invoice** is made by the seller after the order, when the goods are sent, so it is not needed to order the goods.

**Answer: C.**

**8.** A shipping document detailing the charges for carrying cargo for a specified journey is known as:

a) Duck warrant.
b) Freight Note.
c) Carriage Forward.
d) Weight note.

A **freight note** (freight account) is the shipping document that states the charges for carrying the cargo on a given voyage. A dock warrant (printed here as "Duck warrant") is a document of title for goods stored at the docks, Carriage Forward is a delivery term (the buyer pays the carriage) and a weight note only gives the weight.

**Answer: B.**

**9.** Which of the following shows a summary of the financial position of a business within a given period?

a) Bank statement.
b) Balance sheet.
c) Journal.
d) Cash book.

The **balance sheet** lists assets, liabilities and capital on a given date and so summarises the financial position of the business. A bank statement comes from the bank, the journal and the cash book are books of original entry.

**Answer: B.**

**10.** The major divisions of commerce are:

a) Import, Export, and Transport.
b) Trade, Communication and Warehousing.
c) Trade and auxiliaries to trade.
d) Exchange, Consumption and Production.

Commerce is divided into **trade** (home trade and foreign trade) and the **auxiliaries to trade** (transport, banking, insurance, warehousing, communication, advertising). The other options mix parts of these two divisions or refer to economics.

**Answer: C.**

**11.** The advertising medium that combine the advantage of sound and image is:

a) Radio.
b) Bill boards.
c) Television.
d) Posters.

**Television** gives both sound and moving pictures. Radio has sound only, billboards and posters have images only.

**Answer: C.**

**12.** A restriction on the quantity of a commodity that could be imported into a country is known as:

a) Import License.
b) Tariffs.
c) Quota.
d) Embargo.

A **quota** fixes the maximum quantity (or value) of a product that may be imported in a given period. A tariff is a tax, an embargo is a total ban on trade, and an import licence is the permit to import.

**Answer: C.**

**13.** Rate of stock turnover is calculated to determine:

a) Number of times average stock is sold.
b) Number of times goods are counted.
c) Total value of goods in the store.
d) The quantity of goods sold

Rate of stock turnover = cost of goods sold / average stock. It shows **how many times the average stock is sold (and replaced)** during the period.

**Answer: A.**

**14.** Speculators who buy and sell new stocks and shares in their own names are called:

*Options as printed:* A) Jobbers.   B) Bulls.   C) Bears.   D) Stags.

Stags are speculators who apply for new issues of shares hoping to sell them quickly at a premium. Jobbers also buy and sell in their own names but they are market makers, not speculators in new issues, so the printed wording fits both D and A and the question is left open.

**Intended answer: D (Stags).**

**15.** A shoe repairer is best classified as:

a) Service occupation.
b) Manufacturing.
c) Tertiary Occupation.
d) Commercial occupation.

A shoe repairer does not make a new product and does not trade in goods: he gives a personal service to customers. He is classified in a **service occupation** (direct services). Tertiary occupation is also true in general, but the question asks for the best classification.

**Answer: A.**

**16.** Business losses in Public Corporations are borne by:

a) Shareholders.
b) Debenture holders.
c) Board of directors.
d) Tax payers.

A public corporation is owned by the State and financed by public money. When it makes a loss the government covers it with money from taxes, so the loss is borne by the **tax payers**.

**Answer: D.**

**17.** A means taken by the manufacturer to prevent substandard production is:

a) Consumer protection.
b) Free samples.
c) Test marketing.
d) Quality control.

**Quality control** checks the products during and after production so that goods below the standard are not sold. Consumer protection is done by the State and by consumer associations, free samples and test marketing are promotion and research methods.

**Answer: D.**

**18.** An insured's ability to make profits from claims by taking more than one policy for the same risk is prevented by:

a) Subrogation.
b) Contribution.
c) Utmost good faith.
d) Proximate cause.

If a person insures the same risk with several insurers, the principle of **contribution** makes the insurers share the loss between them, so the insured cannot recover more than the real loss and cannot profit from the claim. Subrogation deals with the rights of the insurer against a third party.

**Answer: B.**

**19.** Which of the following is NOT a commercial bank in Cameroon.?

a) SGBC.
b) Union Bank.
c) BEAC.
d) BICEC.

SGBC (Societe Generale de Banques au Cameroun), Union Bank and BICEC are commercial banks. **BEAC** (Bank of Central African States) is the central bank of the CEMAC zone.

**Answer: C.**

**20.** The following are services performed by wholesalers to retailers EXCEPT:

a) Warehousing.
b) Selling in bulk.
c) Information on market.
d) Variety of goods.

Wholesalers store goods for retailers, give them market information and supply a wide variety of goods. What they do for the retailer is **breaking bulk** (buying large quantities and selling small quantities), not selling in bulk, which is the opposite. The wording is imprecise, so the key is given with some doubt.

**Answer: B.**

**21.** Tariffs imposed on imported goods based on prices of such goods are known as:

a) Customs duties,
b) Excise duties.
c) Value added tax.
d) Ad valorem taxes.

A duty calculated as a percentage of the value (price) of the goods is an **ad valorem** duty (Latin: according to value). A specific duty is a fixed amount per unit or weight. Customs duties is the general name of all taxes on imports.

**Answer: D.**

**22.** Visible exports mean:

a) Selling goods abroad.
b) Services sold abroad.
c) Buying goods from abroad.
d) Goods sold abroad.

Visible exports are the **goods** (tangible products) sold to other countries. Services sold abroad (banking, tourism, insurance) are invisible exports, and buying goods from abroad is importing. Option A is close, but only option D names the goods themselves.

**Answer: D.**

**23.** The phrase 'Caveat Emptor' means:

a) Let the buyer beware.
b) Goods are fit for consumption.
c) Goods are of poor quality.
d) Let the seller beware.

**Caveat emptor** is Latin for "let the buyer beware": the buyer must check the goods before buying because the seller is not responsible for defects that could be seen. "Let the seller beware" is caveat venditor.

**Answer: A.**

**24.** The highest authority of a public company is:

a) General Assembly.
b) Chief executive Officer.
c) The General Manager.
d) Board of Directors.

The shareholders meet in the **General Assembly** (general meeting). It elects the Board of Directors and approves the accounts and the dividend, so it is above the Board, the CEO and the General Manager.

**Answer: A.**

**25.** Which of the following is NOT a principle of a co-operative society?

a) Equal Voting Rights.
b) Profits are shared equally.
c) Membership open to all.
d) Members enjoy limited liabilities.

In a co-operative every member has one vote, membership is open to all, and the liability of members is limited to their shares. The surplus is not shared equally: it is distributed as a dividend in proportion to the purchases or the work of each member. So **"profits are shared equally"** is not a principle.

**Answer: B.**

**26.** Orders to buy items needed by any department in an enterprise are addressed to:

a) Commercial department.
b) Purchasing department.
c) Production department.
d) Marketing department.

Every department sends a purchase requisition to the **purchasing department**, which chooses the suppliers and places the orders.

**Answer: B.**

**27.** Quality control is the function of which department of an enterprise?

a) Stocks control department.
b) Stores department.
c) Purchase department.
d) Production department.

Quality control is done during manufacturing, so it belongs to the **production department** (with its inspectors). The stores, stock control and purchasing departments deal with keeping and buying goods.

**Answer: D.**

**28.** Warehousing performs all of the following functions EXCEPT:

a) Avoid price fluctuations.
b) Ensures continuous availability of goods.
c) Guarantees quality of goods.
d) Eases continuous production of goods.

Warehousing keeps goods when they are plentiful and releases them when they are scarce, so it avoids price fluctuations, ensures continuous availability and allows continuous production. It protects the goods against damage and theft but it does not **guarantee their quality**.

**Answer: C.**

**29.** Goods costing 2,400,000 CFAF were sold 3,000,000 CFAF. What is the mark up?

a) 20%.
b) 25%.
c) 33%.
d) 24%.

Profit = 3,000,000 - 2,400,000 = 600,000 CFAF. Mark-up = profit / cost x 100 = 600,000 / 2,400,000 x 100 = **25%**. The trap is to divide by the selling price, which gives 20% (the margin).

**Answer: B.**

**30.** A Sole Trader business is NOT a legal [word missing in the print] because:

*Options as printed:* A) It lacks continuity.   B) Has unlimited liabilities.   C) Owner bears all the risks alone.   D) Cannot sue or be sued.

In the printed question the word after "legal" is missing (probably "entity"). A sole trader business has no legal personality separate from its owner, and one consequence is that the owner has **unlimited liability** for the debts. Several options describe real features of a sole trader, so the question is left open.

**Intended answer: B (Has unlimited liabilities).**

**31.** Which of these transport systems do other systems rely upon ?

a) Sea transport.
b) Road transport.
c) Air transport.
d) Rail transport.

Goods reach ports, airports and railway stations by lorry, and leave them the same way, so every other system relies on **road transport** for the first and last part of the journey.

**Answer: B.**

**32.** Monetary policy means:

a) Controlling inflation.
b) Money supply.
c) Open market
d) Market Interest Rates.

Monetary policy is the action of the central bank to regulate the **money supply** (and the cost of credit) in the economy. Controlling inflation is one aim of it, open market operations and interest rates are tools. The options overlap, so the key is given with some doubt.

**Answer: B.**

**33.** A customer with a current account can withdraw money from his account by:

a) Filling a paying-in slip.
b) Filling a cash book.
c) Completing a passbook.
d) Drawing a cheque.

The holder of a current account withdraws money by **drawing a cheque**. A paying-in slip is used to deposit money, and the cash book and the passbook are not instructions to the bank.

**Answer: D.**

**34.** A service that allows a bank customer to withdraw money without passing through the counter:

a) Credit cards.
b) Automatic cash register.
c) Cash dispenser.
d) Night safe facility.

A **cash dispenser** (automatic teller machine, ATM) gives cash to a customer who uses his card and his PIN. A night safe is used to deposit takings, and "automatic cash register" is not a bank service.

**Answer: C.**

**35.** A firm that is granted the right to use the trade mark of another is called:

a) Leaser.
b) Franchisor.
c) Leasee.
d) Franchisee.

In a franchise, the owner of the trade mark (the franchisor) gives another firm the right to use it. The firm that receives the right is the **franchisee**. A leaser is the one who leases a property.

**Answer: D.**

**36.** A method of buying goods without the services of shops' attendants is:

a) Impulse buying.
b) Self-service.
c) Branding.
d) Auto vending.

In **self-service** the customer picks the goods from the shelves and pays at the checkout without the help of a shop attendant. Impulse buying is an unplanned purchase, branding is a marketing tool and auto vending uses machines instead of shops.

**Answer: B.**

**37.** In a hire purchase contract, 40,000 CFAF is paid as deposits and the remainder paid in six equal installments of 25,000 CFAF. Hire purchase price is:

a) 150,000 CFAF.
b) 180,000 CFAF.
c) 125,000 CFAF.
d) 190,000 CFAF.

Hire purchase price = deposit + installments = 40,000 + 6 x 25,000 = 40,000 + 150,000 = **190,000 CFAF**. The trap is to forget the deposit (150,000).

**Answer: D.**

**38.** The following are functions of customs Department EXCEPT:

a) Collect duties.
b) Keep statistics of X + M
c) Guarantee goods as transit.
d) Check contraband goods.

The customs department collects duties, keeps statistics of exports (X) and imports (M) and checks for contraband (smuggled or prohibited) goods. It does not guarantee goods in transit: that is the role of the carrier or of the insurer.

**Answer: C.**

**39.** Branding plays the role of product:

a) Advertising.
b) Differentiation.
c) Modeling.
d) Publicity.

A brand name or symbol lets the customer tell the product from similar products of other makers: it plays the role of product **differentiation**.

**Answer: B.**

**40.** Which of these documents shows details of a customer's transactions in a bank?

a) Cheque booklet.
b) Bank statement.
c) Standing order form.
d) Paying-in slip.

The **bank statement** is sent by the bank to the customer and lists the deposits, withdrawals and balance of the account.

**Answer: B.**

**41.** The most profitable activity of commercial banks is:

a) Lending to customers.
b) Current Account.
c) Deposit Account.
d) Saving Account.

Banks earn their main income from the interest charged on loans and overdrafts, which is higher than the interest they pay on deposits. **Lending to customers** is therefore their most profitable activity.

**Answer: A.**

**42.** The abbreviation PMB stands for:

a) Postal Mail Bag.
b) Prime Minister's Box.
c) Private Mail Bag.
d) Post Master Box.

**PMB** means Private Mail Bag, a postal address given by a post office to a customer who receives letters in a locked bag or box.

**Answer: C.**

**43.** An insurance doctrine which gives the right for an insurer to stand in the shoes of the insured is:

a) Utmost good faith.
b) Subrogation.
c) Indemnity.
d) Proximate cause.

After the insurer has paid a claim, **subrogation** gives him the rights of the insured against a third party responsible for the loss: he takes the place ("stands in the shoes") of the insured.

**Answer: B.**

**44.** Which of these categories of marine losses [the end of the question is missing in the print]

*Options as printed:* A) General average.   B) Particular average.   C) Actual total loss.   D) Constructive loss.

The printed question stops after "marine losses" and a stray word "is" appears on the next line, so the question cannot be marked. Useful facts: general average and particular average are partial losses (a general average loss is a sacrifice made on purpose to save the ship and cargo and is shared by all the interested parties, a particular average loss falls on the owner of the damaged goods), while actual total loss and constructive total loss are total losses.

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

**45.** Which of the price quotations below is the seller responsible for transportation up to the ship?

a) C I F .
b) F OB .
c) FRANCO.
d) LOCO.

With **F.O.B.** (free on board) the seller pays the costs up to the moment the goods are loaded on the ship. With C.I.F. he also pays freight and insurance to the destination, Franco means delivered free to the buyer, and Loco means the buyer collects the goods at the seller's premises.

**46.** A joint effort by producers to advertise a particular product is called

a) Persuasive advertising.
b) Generic advertising.
c) Competitive advertising.
d) Mass advertising.

When several producers of the same product share the cost of an advertisement for the product as a whole (for example milk or cotton) without naming one brand, it is **generic (collective) advertising**.

**Answer: B.**

**47.** The document used to inform a buyer that goods are on transit is:

a) Proforma invoice.
b) Dispatch note
c) Advice note.
d) Quotation.

The **advice note** is sent by the seller to tell the buyer that the goods have been dispatched and are on their way. A dispatch note travels with the goods, a proforma invoice is a preliminary invoice and a quotation gives prices. The dispatch note is close, so the key is given with some doubt.

**Answer: C.**

**48.** An internal source of capital to a company is:

a) Trade credit
b) Debentures.
c) Overdraft.
d) Plough-back profits.

Internal sources come from inside the company: **ploughed-back (retained) profits**. Trade credit, debentures and overdrafts come from outside creditors.

**Answer: D.**

**49.** An insured's ability to make profits from claims by taking more than one policy for the same risk is prevented by:

a) Subrogation.
b) Contribution.
c) Utmost good faith.
d) Proximate cause.

This question is printed twice in the paper (it is the same as question 18). If a person insures the same risk with several insurers, the principle of **contribution** makes the insurers share the loss between them, so the insured cannot recover more than the real loss.

**Answer: B.**

**50.** Shops which look identical, dealing in the same line of products and having branches in other parts of the country are known as:

a) Supermarkets.
b) Chain stores.
c) Mail order business.
d) Department stores.

**Chain stores** (multiple shops) belong to one firm, have the same appearance, sell the same lines and are spread over many towns. Supermarkets and department stores are single big shops, and mail order sells by post.

**Answer: B.**

Each of the $n$ devices is linked to the other $n - 1$, which counts every link twice, so the number of links is $\dfrac{n(n-1)}{2}$. Check with $n = 5$: $5 \times 4 / 2 = 10$ links, whereas B gives 12, C gives 15 and D gives 6. **Answer: A.**

**43.** The main function of a browser is to:

a) Compile HTML
b) Interpret HTML
c) Decompile HTML
d) Transfer HTML.

A web browser fetches an HTML document and **interprets** it, that is, reads the markup and displays (renders) the page. HTML is not compiled to machine code or decompiled, and the transfer of pages is done by the HTTP protocol, not by the browser's display function. **Answer: B.**

**44.** The concept by which we apply existing operations to new data types is:

a) Inheritance
b) Polymorphism
c) Encapsulation
d) Prototyping.

**Polymorphism** lets the same operation (for example `+` or `print`) work on different or new data types, each type supplying its own behaviour. Inheritance reuses the attributes and methods of a parent class, encapsulation hides the data inside the object, and prototyping is a software development method. **Answer: B.**

**45.** If the state of a database no longer reflects a real life state the database is supposed to capture, then such a database state is said to be:

a) Consistent
b) Durable
c) Parallel
d) Inconsistent.

A database state that does not match the real-world situation it models (or violates its integrity constraints) is **inconsistent**. A consistent state is the opposite; durability concerns data surviving failures and 'parallel' is not a database-state property. **Answer: D.**

**46.** Recursive algorithms use a:

a) Divide-and-conquer approach
b) Modular approach
c) Structural approach
d) Hierarchical approach.

A recursive algorithm solves a problem by reducing it to smaller instances of the same problem and combining the results, which is the **divide-and-conquer** approach. **Answer: A.**

**47.** The benefit of prototyping is:

a) Missing functions of the user can be identified
b) Misunderstanding between software developer and user can be identified
c) Incomplete or inconsistent user requirements may be detected.
d) All of the above.

Showing the user a working model early reveals functions the user forgot to mention (A), misunderstandings between developer and user (B), and incomplete or inconsistent requirements (C). All three are benefits, so the answer is 'All of the above'. **Answer: D.**

**48.** A database table is in $3^{rd}$ normal form if:

a) It is in $2^{nd}$ normal form (2NF) and in $1^{st}$ normal form (1NF)
b) It is in 2NF and all non-key fields depend on all key fields
c) It is in 2NF and all non-key fields depend only on the key
d) It is in 2NF and all non-key fields may depend indirectly on all key fields.

A table is in 3NF when it is in 2NF and no non-key attribute depends on another non-key attribute: every non-key field depends **only on the key** (no transitive dependency). Option A only describes 2NF (and 1NF), option B repeats the 2NF requirement (full dependence on the whole key), and option D allows indirect (transitive) dependence, which 3NF forbids. **Answer: C.**

**49.** Given the relations CLASS(ClassID, Cycle, Teachinghours) and STUDENT(StudentID, ClassID, StudName). What is the possible relation between STUDENT and CLASS?

a) A class must have at least a student.
b) A student must have a class
c) A student may have no class
d) A class may have no students.

ClassID in STUDENT is a foreign key referring to CLASS: one class can be referred to by many students (one-to-many). Because a CLASS row exists independently of the STUDENT rows, nothing forces a class to have a student, so a **class may have no students**. Nothing in the schema forces a class to contain a student (A), and whether a student's ClassID may be empty (B, C) is not shown by the schema. **Answer: D.**

**50.** When requirements analysis goes wrong, what could happen?

a) The system may cost more than projected.
b) The system will become unreliable
c) The system may not meet user requirements
d) All of the above.

Errors in requirements analysis lead to rework (higher cost), to a system that misbehaves (unreliable) and to a product that does not do what users need. All three consequences can occur, so the answer is 'All of the above'. **Answer: D.**

**7.** The type of computer that does most of the work in a weather forecasting organization is most likely to be a ___

a) Workstation
b) Minicomputer
c) Mainframe computer
d) Supercomputer

**9.** When using a command line interface, the signal indicating that the computer is waiting for input from the user is known as a (an)

a) Event
b) Prompt

d) Delay

**10.** Which one of the following copies itself into memory or external storage device until no more space is left?

b) Worm

A Trojan horse pretends to be useful software but does not replicate by itself, antivirus software is a defence, and a crawler is a program that browses web pages to index them. **Answer: B.**

**11.** Which one of the following is/are not part of the CPU?

a) Control unit
b) ALU
c) Registers
d) RAM

The CPU consists of the control unit, the arithmetic and logic unit (ALU) and the registers. **RAM** is main memory, a separate component connected to the CPU by the buses. **Answer: D.**

**12.** The term Green Computing refers to the use of computers and resources:

a) In green revolution.
b) To generate green house gases.
c) In an environmentally friendly way.
d) In printing on green paper.

Green computing means using computers and related resources in an **environmentally friendly** way, for example by saving energy, recycling equipment and reducing paper. It has nothing to do with the colour green or with producing greenhouse gases. **Answer: C.**

**13.** A key difference between the first and second generation of electronic computers is:

a) Transistors replaced electronic circuits.
b) Transistors replaced vacuum tubes.
c) Vacuum tubes replaced transistors.
d) Vacuum tubes replaced integrated circuits.

First generation computers used vacuum tubes (valves). Second generation computers replaced them with **transistors**, which are smaller, faster, cheaper and produce less heat. Options C and D reverse the order of the technologies. **Answer: B.**

**14.** A set of computers in an office building are connected together so that staff can share files, printers and other resources. What is this arrangement of computers called?

a) WAN
b) LAN
c) WWW
d) PAN

Computers connected over a small area such as one office building form a **Local Area Network (LAN)**. A WAN covers a large area (towns, countries), the WWW is a service on the Internet, and a PAN connects personal devices within a few metres of one person. **Answer: B.**

**15.** Which of the following is the correct name for the screen image shown below:

**16.** If the binary code for letter A is 01000001, then the binary code for letter C is

a) 01000111
b) 01000011
c) 01001101
d) 01000101

Codes of letters follow the alphabet order. A is 01000001 (decimal 65), so B is 66 and C is 67. In binary $67 = 64 + 2 + 1 = 01000011$. The other options are the codes of G (01000111), M (01001101) and E (01000101). **Answer: B.**

**17.** Which of the following is NOT a feature of electronic commerce?

a) Goods can be advertised and prices compared.
b) There is physical contact. between buyer and seller.
c) Transactions can be processed quickly.
d) Services are available 24 hours a day.

In electronic commerce, buyer and seller trade over the Internet without meeting, so **physical contact between them is not a feature**. Advertising and price comparison, fast processing and 24 hour availability are all advantages of e-commerce. **Answer: B.**

**18.** A company decides to introduce a new information system into three of its stores initially, and then three additional stores each fortnight until all stores have the new system. This approach to introducing the new system is referred as:

a) parallel conversion.
b) phased conversion.
c) direct conversion.
d) pilot conversion.

Introducing the new system a part at a time, in stages, until all stores use it is **phased conversion**. Parallel conversion runs old and new systems together, direct conversion replaces the old system at once, and pilot conversion tries the system in one location only (and then usually extends it to the rest). **Answer: B.**

**19.** The processing type that groups several transactions is

a) Real-time.
b) Batch.
c) Online.
d) Offline

In **batch processing**, transactions are collected together over a period and processed as one group (for example monthly payroll). Real-time processing handles each transaction immediately. **Answer: B.**

**20.** During data transmission over a standard telephone line, digital signals are converted into analogue signals in the:

a) Source modem.
b) Destination modem.
c) Cable linking the source computer to the source modem.
d) Cable linking the destination to the destination modem.

A telephone line carries analogue signals, so the **sending (source) modem** modulates the computer's digital signal into an analogue one. The destination modem does the reverse (demodulation). Cables only carry the signals and do not convert them. **Answer: A.**

**21.** Commonly used object oriented languages are:

a) C and Pascal.
b) C++ and Fortran.

b) Assembler.

**26.** The term Constant as used in computer programming means.

a) A function whose value does not change
b) An identifier whose value is not allowed to change
c) A variable that is used across the whole code.
d) A value that is used frequently

A constant is a named item (an identifier) that receives a value once and whose value cannot be changed while the program runs (for example `const Pi = 3.14159;`). A variable used across the whole code is a global variable, and a function is something different. **Answer: B.**

**27.** Which printer uses a combination of light beam and electro photographic techniques?

a) Dot matrix printer
b) Daisy wheel printer
c) Line printer
d) Laser printer

A **laser printer** uses a laser beam to draw the page image on a charged drum, then toner sticks to the charged areas and is fused to the paper (electrophotography). Dot matrix, daisy wheel and line printers are impact printers. **Answer: D.**

**28.** The Internet is a gigantic network but the World Wide Web is a (an)

a) Gigantic database
b) Gigantic Interconnection of computers
c) Service that lets users access a gigantic collection of documents.
d) Internet protocol.

The Internet is the physical network of connected computers. The World Wide Web is a **service running on the Internet** that lets users access a huge collection of linked documents (web pages) with a browser. It is not a database, not the interconnection itself (that is the Internet) and not a protocol (HTTP is the protocol). **Answer: C.**

**29.** A set of instructions that a computer executes is called?

a) An application
b) A program
c) An algorithm
d) A software

A set of instructions that the computer executes is a **program**. An algorithm is the step-by-step method written independently of a machine, and software and application are wider terms that cover many programs. **Answer: B.**

**30.** What name is given to the separate pages of a spreadsheet?

a) Workbooks
b) Workpages
c) Workspaces
d) Worksheets

A spreadsheet file is a **workbook**, which contains several separate pages called **worksheets**. "Workpages" and "workspaces" are not spreadsheet terms. **Answer: D.**

**31.** A lag in project management is a delay between tasks:

a) a predecessor and a successor
b) two predecessor
c) two successor
d) two dummy

In project scheduling a lag is a waiting time between a task that must come first (the predecessor) and the task that follows it (the successor), for example waiting for concrete to dry between two building tasks. The other options do not describe a dependency between two linked tasks. **Answer: A.**

**32.** Which of these devices is used to read printed material into a computer?

a) Light pen
b) Graphics
c) Joy stick
d) Scanner

**33.** In a system in which 1 means TRUE and 0 means FALSE, what is the result of 1 +T?

a) 2
b) 10
c) 1
d) 0

**34.** The number of bits a CPU processes each time is called a

a) Nibble
b) Word
c) Thread
d) Megabyte

The **word** is the number of bits the CPU handles in one operation (for example 32 or 64 bits). A nibble is only 4 bits, a thread is a sequence of instructions in a process and a megabyte is a unit of storage. **Answer: B.**

**35.** The main input device required by a command line interface is:

b) Mouse.

b) HTTP.
c) SMTP.
d) TCP/IP

**HTTP** (HyperText Transfer Protocol) manages the transfer of web pages between web servers and browsers. FTP transfers files, SMTP sends e-mail and TCP/IP is the general suite used by the whole Internet. **Answer: B.**

**37.** Which of the following programming languages requires the use of an interpreter?

a) C
b) Pascal
c) HTML
d) Machine language

HTML is not compiled: the web browser reads it line by line and interprets the tags to display the page. C and Pascal are normally translated by a compiler, and machine language is already in the form the processor executes, so it needs no translation. **Answer: C.**

**38.** Which of the following data types is most appropriate to represent the averages of numbers?

a) Integer
b) String
c) Real
d) Boolean

An average usually has a fractional part (for example $(3+4)/2 = 3.5$), so it must be stored as a **real** number. An integer would lose the decimals, a string stores text and a Boolean stores TRUE or FALSE. **Answer: C.**

**39.** Data saved on a magnetic tape can be accessed

*Options as printed:* A) Randomly   B) Sequentially   C) Serially   D) Directly

A magnetic tape must be read from the start, one record after another, until the wanted data is reached: it is accessed **sequentially** (also called serial access). Random or direct access (as on a disk) is not possible.

d) Synchronous transmission

Both directions at the same time is **full-duplex** (a telephone call). Half-duplex allows both directions but one at a time, simplex is one direction only, and synchronous describes the timing of the data, not its direction. **Answer: B.**

**41.** In a certain computer laboratory, the server is placed at one corner of the room and connected directly to each of the other computers through a switch. This is an example of a ________ topology.

a) star
b) bus
c) peer-to-peer
d) ring

Each computer has its own link to a central device (the switch) which connects it to the server: this is a **star** topology. A bus uses one shared cable, a ring joins the computers in a closed loop, and peer-to-peer describes a network model without a server, not a topology. **Answer: A.**

**42.** What name is given to a program that provides synonyms?

a) Dictionary
b) Thesaurus
c) Editor
d) Compiler

A **thesaurus** gives words with similar meanings (synonyms). A dictionary gives meanings and spelling, an editor is used to type text or code and a compiler translates programs. **Answer: B.**

**43.** A well-designed database of employees in a company would place all the information for single employee in:

a) a table
b) a field
c) a record
d) a cell

In a database table, all the data about one item (one employee) is held in one row, called a **record**. A field holds one piece of data (for example the surname), a table holds all the records, and a cell is a spreadsheet term. **Answer: C.**

**44.** The preliminary investigation of an information system project is known as:

a) system analysis
b) system design
c) documentation
d) feasibility study

The first stage of the systems development life cycle, a short preliminary investigation to decide whether the project is technically, economically and socially worthwhile, is the **feasibility study**. Analysis, design and documentation come later. **Answer: D.**

**45.** An English-like language that can be used in program design is?

a) BASIC
b) COBOL
c) PASCAL
d) Pseudocode

**Pseudocode** describes the steps of a program in structured English-like statements, independent of any programming language. BASIC, COBOL and Pascal are real programming languages with strict syntax. **Answer: D.**

**46.** In programming, the programmer simply states what needs to be done, and the system figures out how to do it.

a) Object oriented
b) Procedural
c) Declarative
d) Imperative

In **declarative** programming (for example SQL or Prolog) the programmer states the result wanted and the system decides how to obtain it. Procedural and imperative styles give the exact steps, and object oriented programming organises code in objects. **Answer: C.**

**47.** A mechanism to protect private networks from outside attacks is?

a) Antivirus
b) Encryption
c) Firewall
d) Lightening conductors

A **firewall** filters traffic between a private network and the outside (the Internet) and blocks unauthorised access. Antivirus removes malware, encryption scrambles data, and a lightning conductor protects buildings from lightning. **Answer: C.**

**48.** Which of the following is most likely when computers are introduced in the workplace?

a) There is a lot of laissez faire
b) The rate of corruption increases
c) Demand for computer expertise increases
d) People become less reliable

When a workplace becomes computerised, it needs people able to operate, program and maintain the machines, so **demand for computer expertise increases**. The other statements are not general effects of computerisation. **Answer: C.**

**49.** The efficiency of an algorithm can be measured in terms of:

a) Correctness
b) Clarity
c) Precision
d) Execution time.

Efficiency measures the resources an algorithm uses: **execution time** (and memory). Correctness, clarity and precision describe the quality of the result or the description, not the efficiency. **Answer: D.**

**50.** How many bytes are required to encode 32 different bits?

a) 32
b) 8
c) 5
d) 4

One byte holds 8 bits, so 32 bits need $32 / 8 = 4$ bytes. The question wording is odd ("32 different bits"), but only 4 bytes is consistent with the options: 32 is the number of bits, 8 is the number of bits in a byte and 5 is the number of bits needed to tell 32 values apart. **Answer: D.**

**1.** Which of the following is an internal method through which firms can grow?

a) Plough back profit
b) Vertical integration
c) Horizontal integration
d) Lateral integration

A firm grows **internally** when it expands using its own resources, for example by ploughing back (re-investing) part of its profit to buy new machines or open new branches. Vertical, horizontal and lateral integration (B, C, D) are **external** methods: the firm grows by joining or taking over another firm. **Answer: A.**

**2.** Study the table and answer the question that follows.

| Year | 2010 | 2011 | 2012 | 2013 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Index of export prices | 100 | 92 | 97 | 130 |
| Index of import prices | 100 | 94 | 94 | 110 |

In which year did this country experience an unfavourable terms of trade?

a) 2010
b) 2011
c) 2012
d) 2013

Terms of trade index = (index of export prices / index of import prices) $\times 100$.

- 2010: $100/100 \times 100 = 100$ (base year)
- 2011: $92/94 \times 100 \approx 97.9$
- 2012: $97/94 \times 100 \approx 103.2$
- 2013: $130/110 \times 100 \approx 118.2$

The terms of trade are **unfavourable** when the index falls below 100, because the country must give more exports to buy the same imports. This happens only in 2011. In 2012 and 2013 the terms of trade improved. **Answer: B.**

**3.** Which of the following is the condition necessary for a business unit to be considered as a "corporate body"?

a) Should show prove of cooperation amongst shareholders
b) Should possess valuable business license
c) Should possess the certificate of incorporation
d) Can sell shares to members of the public

A **corporate body** has a legal personality separate from its owners. It acquires this status when it is registered and receives the **certificate of incorporation**. A business licence (B) is only permission to trade, co-operation among shareholders (A) is not a legal condition, and selling shares to the public (D) is true only of public limited companies, not of every corporate body. **Answer: C.**

**4.** A teacher of Economics in Buea becomes a banker in a commercial bank in Buea. This is an example of:

a) Horizontal mobility of labour
b) Vertical mobility of labour
c) Geographical mobility of labour
d) Occupational mobility of labour

**Occupational mobility** is the movement of a worker from one occupation (type of job) to another: from teaching to banking. The place stays the same (Buea), so it is not geographical mobility (C). Vertical mobility (B) means promotion to a higher grade in the same line of work. Horizontal mobility (A) means a change of employer or job at the same level in the same trade. **Answer: D.**

**5.** Use this passage and answer question 5.

On the 1st January 2012, the population was 400,000 inhabitants. During the year, the number of births were 18,000 and 10,000 deaths were recorded.

The natural growth rate is:

a) 2 per 1000
b) 2 per 100
c) -2 per 100
d) -2 per 1000

Natural increase = births - deaths $= 18{,}000 - 10{,}000 = 8{,}000$ people.

Natural growth rate $= \dfrac{8{,}000}{400{,}000} \times 100 = 2\%$, that is **2 per 100** (or 20 per 1000). The rate is positive because births exceed deaths, which rules out C and D, and 2 per 1000 (A) is ten times too small. **Answer: B.**

**6.** The most acceptable economic reason for trade protection is to:

a) Improve the standards of living
b) Offering a wider market for home produced goods
c) Improve the rate of unemployment
d) Protect newly established industries

The strongest economic argument for protection is the **infant industry argument**: new industries are small, have high costs and cannot compete with established foreign firms, so tariffs or quotas shelter them until they grow and enjoy economies of scale. Protection does not by itself raise living standards (A), a wider market for home goods is not what protection offers (B), and "improve the rate of unemployment" (C) is badly worded. **Answer: D.**

**7.** When the price of good A increases and the quantity of good B increases, goods Q and B are said to be:

a) Inferior goods
b) Complementary goods
c) Close substitutes
d) Goods of ostentation

When the price of A rises, consumers buy less of A and switch to B, so the quantity of B demanded rises. Goods behaving like this are **substitutes** (positive cross elasticity of demand), for example tea and coffee. Complementary goods (B) move in opposite directions: a rise in the price of A would reduce the demand for B. Inferior goods (A) and goods of ostentation (D) are defined by income and price effects, not by the price of another good. The printed stem says "goods Q and B" where "A and B" is meant. **Answer: C.**

**8.** The exchange of goods between Cameroon and France is:

a) Specific trade
b) Bilateral trade
c) Multilateral trade
d) Direct trade

**Bilateral trade** is trade between two countries only. Trade among three or more countries is multilateral (C). "Specific trade" and "direct trade" are not the standard names for this type of international trade. **Answer: B.**

**9.** The grouping of population into male and female is:

a) Sex distribution
b) Age distribution
c) Population distribution
d) Population pyramid

Dividing a population into males and females gives its **sex distribution** (sex ratio). Age distribution (B) groups people by age, population distribution (C) is about where people live, and a population pyramid (D) is a diagram that shows age and sex together. **Answer: A.**

**10.** X's age is three times Y's age. If Y is 5 years now, their mean age is:

a) 15 years
b) 20 years
c) 5 years
d) 10 years

$X = 3 \times 5 = 15$ years and $Y = 5$ years. Mean age $= \dfrac{15 + 5}{2} = 10$ years. 15 years (A) is only X's age, and 20 years (B) is the sum of the two ages. **Answer: D.**

**11.** A country's index of import prices in 2009 was 50 and the index of export prices was 70. What is the terms of trade?

a) 0.71
b) 71
c) 1.4
d) 140

Terms of trade $= \dfrac{\text{index of export prices}}{\text{index of import prices}} \times 100 = \dfrac{70}{50} \times 100 = 140$. A value above 100 means that export prices have risen faster than import prices, a favourable change. 0.71 and 71 come from inverting the fraction (50/70), and 1.4 forgets to multiply by 100. **Answer: D.**

**12.** In calculating the National Income of a country, the national income statisticians include the costs of raw materials and the costs of finished goods. This is a case of:

a) Over repetition
b) Double counting
c) Over estimation
d) Double estimation

Raw materials are already part of the value of the finished goods. Counting both the raw materials and the finished goods counts the same output twice: this is **double counting**. It is avoided by counting only final goods or only the value added at each stage. **Answer: B.**

**13.** In the circular flow diagram of National Income, the word K indicates:

![Circular flow diagram of national income between household and firm, with arcs labelled flow of capital goods, payment for factors of production, payments for goods and services, and the unlabelled arc K (Question 13).](/media/figures/cm/gce-ol-economics-2017-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_1.webp)

a) The flow of output
b) Payments for factors of production
c) The flow of capital goods

In the diagram, the arrow labelled "Payments for goods and services" goes from the households to the firms. The arrow K goes in the **opposite direction**, from the firms to the households: it is the **real flow of goods and services (the flow of output)** that households receive in exchange for their payments. The payments for factors of production (B) and for goods and services (D) are money flows with their own labels, and the flow of capital goods (C) is already named on the outer upper arc. **Answer: A.**

**14.** If Cameroon's National Income is estimated to be 790,900 million FCFA and its population is about 8 million people. What will be the per capita income?

a) 6,327,200 FCFA
b) 790,892 FCFA
c) 790,908 FCFA

Per capita income = national income / population $= \dfrac{790{,}900 \times 10^6}{8 \times 10^6} = 98{,}862.5$ FCFA. Option A multiplies instead of dividing, and B and C wrongly subtract or add the population to the national income. **Answer: D.**

**15.** The theory of Comparative Costs Advantage states that a commodity should be produced in the country whose:

a) Absolute money costs is low
b) Opportunity costs is least
c) Production potential increases
d) Absolute costs is least

According to the theory of comparative cost advantage, a country should produce and export the good for which it gives up the **least other output** (the lowest opportunity cost), even if another country is more efficient in everything (absolute advantage). Options A and D describe absolute advantage. **Answer: B.**

**16.** Study the information in this table on the cost of producing cars and answer question 16.

| Output (Numbers of cars) | Total Costs (in million FCFA) |
|---|---|
| 0 | 50 |
| 1 | 70 |
| 2 | 80 |

What is the average cost of producing the second car?

a) 25 million FCFA
b) 30 million FCFA
c) 40 million FCFA
d) 35 million FCFA

Average cost $=$ total cost / output. For an output of 2 cars, $AC = \dfrac{80}{2} = 40$ million FCFA. (The marginal cost of the second car would be $80 - 70 = 10$ million FCFA, which is not offered. Dividing 70 by 2 gives 35, which uses the wrong total cost.) **Answer: C.**

**17.** The most risky form of capital in a company is:

a) Ordinary shares
b) Preference shares
c) Debentures
d) Cumulative preference shares

Ordinary shareholders are paid last: dividends depend on profit and in liquidation they are repaid only after debenture holders and preference shareholders. Their dividend is not fixed or guaranteed, so ordinary shares are the **riskiest** form of capital. Preference shares and debentures carry a fixed return. **Answer: A.**

**18.** In a market economic system, most resources are owned by:

a) The state
b) Private individuals
c) The government and individuals
d) The public sector

In a market (capitalist) economy, factors of production are mainly owned by **private individuals and firms** who decide what to produce through the price mechanism. State ownership (A, D) is typical of a command economy, and joint ownership (C) describes a mixed economy. **Answer: B.**

**19.** What is the market price when quantity demanded is 400 - p and quantity supplied is 40 + p, where p = price of the good in FCFA?

a) 40 FCFA
b) 360 FCFA
c) 400 FCFA
d) 180 FCFA

At equilibrium, quantity demanded = quantity supplied: $400 - p = 40 + p$, so $2p = 360$ and $p = 180$ FCFA. Check: $Qd = 400 - 180 = 220$ and $Qs = 40 + 180 = 220$. **Answer: D.**

**20.** What do people achieve when they consume goods and services?

a) Prestige
b) Self-esteem
c) Utility
d) Honour

The satisfaction that consumers obtain from using goods and services is called **utility**. Prestige, self-esteem and honour may be side effects for some goods but are not what consumption achieves in general. **Answer: C.**

**21.** When large firms buy and sell in bulk, they experience:

a) Marketing economies
b) Financial economies
c) Welfare economies
d) Risk bearing economies

Buying raw materials in bulk at a discount and selling in large quantities, with lower advertising and distribution cost per unit, are **marketing economies** of scale. Financial economies (B) concern cheaper loans, welfare economies (C) concern workers' facilities, and risk-bearing economies (D) concern spreading risk over several products or markets. **Answer: A.**

**22.** To perform its function of being a store of wealth and standard of deferred payments, money must be:

a) Durable
b) Portable
c) Stable in value
d) Scarce

Money can store wealth and settle future (deferred) payments only if it keeps its purchasing power over time, that is if it is **stable in value**. If prices rose quickly, savings and debts would lose their real value. Durability (A) and portability (B) help but are not the key; scarcity (D) is a general quality that supports value. **Answer: C.**

**23.** An example of a regressive tax is:

a) Personal income tax
b) Value added tax
c) Corporation tax
d) Poll tax

A **regressive** tax takes a larger percentage of income from the poor than from the rich. A **poll tax** is the same fixed amount for every adult, so it is a bigger share of a small income: this is the classic example. Personal income tax (A) is progressive and corporation tax (C) is a percentage of company profit. Value added tax (B) is a tax on spending and is also regressive in its effect, but the poll tax is the standard textbook example. **Answer: D.**

**24.** The farming type practiced by C.D.C and PAMOL is called:

a) Mixing farming
b) subsistence agriculture
c) Cooperative agriculture
d) Plantation agriculture

The Cameroon Development Corporation (CDC) and PAMOL run large estates with hired labour that grow cash crops (rubber, banana, oil palm, tea) for sale: this is **plantation agriculture**. Subsistence farming (B) feeds the farmer's family, and mixed farming (A) combines crops and livestock on one farm. **Answer: D.**

**25.** If the death rate of country X is 25 per thousand and the birth rate is 50 per thousand, the natural growth rate is:

*Options as printed:* A) 25‰   B) 25 %   C) 2.5%   D) 2.5‰

Natural growth rate = birth rate - death rate $= 50 - 25 = 25$ per thousand $= \dfrac{25}{1000} \times 100 = 2.5\%$. Option C gives this value. Option A (25 per thousand, written 25‰) is the same quantity in another unit, so two options are correct; option B (25 %) and D (2.5 per thousand) are ten times too large and too small.

**Intended answer: C (2.5%).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

**26.** Public expenditure on services such as education and health are known as expenditure on:

a) Public services
b) Administrative services
c) Social services
d) Economic services

Government spending on education, health, housing and social welfare is classified as spending on **social services**. Administrative services cover running the government (civil service, defence, police), and economic services cover roads, energy and agriculture. **Answer: C.**

**27.** Which is a form of indirect government intervention in the Cameroon economy:

a) Physical policy
b) Fiscal policy
c) Price control policy
d) Regulating hire purchase policy

**Indirect intervention** influences the market through incentives without giving orders: **fiscal policy** (taxes and government spending) changes incomes and costs, and firms and consumers still decide freely. Physical controls such as quotas and licences (A), price controls (C) and regulations on hire purchase terms (D) are direct controls that fix what may be done. **Answer: B.**

a) Budget deficit
b) Balanced budget
c) Programmed budget
d) Budget surplus

Revenue greater than expenditure is a **budget surplus**. Expenditure greater than revenue is a deficit (A), and revenue equal to expenditure is a balanced budget (B). **Answer: D.**

**29.** CAMTEL, MTN and Orange communication companies in Cameroon are appropriate examples of which structure of production?

a) Direct production
b) Secondary production
c) Tertiary production
d) Indirect production

Telecommunication companies sell a **service**, and the production of services is **tertiary production**. Secondary production (B) manufactures goods, and direct and indirect production (A, D) describe whether people produce for themselves or for the market, not the structure of production. **Answer: C.**

**30.** An ad valorem tax is imposed on:

a) Special goods
b) The value of a good
c) Imports
d) Exports

"Ad valorem" means "according to value": the tax is a percentage of the **value** (price) of the good, for example value added tax at a given percentage. It is not limited to special goods, imports or exports. **Answer: B.**

**31.** The full meaning of COBAC is:

*Options as printed:* A) The Banking Commission of Central African States   B) Central Africa Banking Commission   C) Central Commission of African States Banking   D) The Banking Commission of Central Africa

COBAC stands for the Banking Commission of Central Africa (in French, Commission Bancaire de l'Afrique Centrale), the CEMAC body that supervises banks and financial institutions of the region. The intended option is D. Option B is only a different word order of the same name, and A and C are wrong.

**Intended answer: D (The Banking Commission of Central Africa).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

**32.** Which of the following is an example of a direct tax?

a) Sales tax
b) Excise tax
c) Value added tax
d) Corporation tax

A direct tax is levied on income or profit and is paid by the person it is meant to burden. **Corporation tax** is charged on company profit. Sales tax, excise tax and value added tax (A, B, C) are indirect taxes on spending, collected by sellers. **Answer: D.**

**33.** Which of the following reasons to hold money is also known as idle balances:

a) Transaction motive
b) Liquidity motive
c) Speculative motive
d) Precautionary motive

Money held for the **speculative motive** is kept idle, waiting for a good chance to buy bonds, shares or other assets when their prices fall. For this reason it is called idle balances, whereas transaction and precautionary balances (A, D) are held to be spent on everyday and emergency needs. **Answer: C.**

**34.** If a car company takes over a tobacco company, this is an example of:

a) Vertical integration
b) Conglomerate
c) Lateral integration
d) Horizontal integration

A car company and a tobacco company are in unrelated lines of business, so the takeover is a **conglomerate** merger (diversification). Vertical integration (A) joins firms at different stages of the same product, and horizontal integration (D) joins firms making the same product at the same stage. Lateral integration (C) joins firms making related but different products, which does not apply to cars and tobacco. **Answer: B.**

**35.** A major function of the capital market is to:

a) Provide funds for long term financing
b) Provide funds for short term financing
c) Stabilize the value of the local currency
d) Stabilize domestic prices

The **capital market** (stock exchange and long-term lenders) supplies **long-term funds** through shares and bonds. Short-term funds come from the money market (B), and stabilising the currency and prices (C, D) are tasks of the central bank. **Answer: A.**

**36.** The function of money that has solved the problem of double coincidence of wants in the barter system of trade is known as:

a) Store of value
b) Measure of value
c) Medium of exchange
d) Unit of account

In barter, a trade needs a double coincidence of wants: each person must want what the other offers. Money used as a **medium of exchange** is accepted by everyone for goods and services, so one can sell first and buy later from someone else. **Answer: C.**

**37.** The main advantage of Division of Labour is:

a) Increase use of machines
b) Increased output
c) Less fatigue
d) Saves time

When each worker specialises in one task, skill and speed rise and machines can be used, so **total output increases**. This is the main advantage. Greater use of machines and time saving are ways in which output rises, and less fatigue is not an advantage (repetitive work causes boredom). **Answer: B.**

**38.** When the numerical value of the price elasticity of demand is zero, demand is said to be:

a) Perfectly elastic
b) Perfectly inelastic
c) Fairly elastic
d) Fairly inelastic

$PED = 0$ means that quantity demanded does not change at all when the price changes: the demand curve is vertical and demand is **perfectly inelastic**. Perfectly elastic demand has $PED = \infty$. Fairly elastic and fairly inelastic demand have values greater than 1 and between 0 and 1. **Answer: B.**

**39.** The rate at which money changes hands is:

*Options as printed:* A) Velocity of liquidity   B) Velocity of transaction   C) Velocity of money   D) Velocity of circulation

The number of times a unit of money is used in transactions in a period is the **velocity of circulation of money**. The intended option is D. Option C ("velocity of money") is also used for the same idea, which makes the printed question unreliable; A and B are not standard terms.

**Intended answer: D (Velocity of circulation).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

**40.** Goods of ostentation refer to those goods:

a) For which demand increases when prices increases
b) That is bought mostly by the poor
c) For which demand decreases as price increases
d) When price falls, more is demanded

Goods of ostentation (Veblen goods, for example luxury cars and jewels) are bought for show, so a **higher price makes them more attractive** and demand rises: the demand curve slopes upward. Option C describes the normal law of demand and D is the same law, with a lower price. Goods bought mostly by the poor (B) are inferior goods. **Answer: A.**

**41.** If the initial deposit in a commercial bank is 1,000,000 FCFA and the cash ratio is 12.5%, then the amount this bank will create will be:

a) 5,000,000 FCFA
b) 8,000,000 FCFA
c) 9,000,000 FCFA
d) 10,000,000 FCFA

Credit multiplier $= \dfrac{1}{\text{cash ratio}} = \dfrac{1}{0.125} = 8$. Total deposits created $= 8 \times 1{,}000{,}000 = 8{,}000{,}000$ FCFA. (The new credit created in addition to the initial deposit would be 7,000,000 FCFA, which is not offered, so B is the only option that fits.) **Answer: B.**

**42.** A civil servant earns an income of 300,000 FCFA per month and pays a tax of 15,000 FCFA. Calculate the average rate of taxation.

a) 5%
b) 15%
c) 10%
d) 3%

Average rate of taxation $= \dfrac{\text{tax paid}}{\text{income}} \times 100 = \dfrac{15{,}000}{300{,}000} \times 100 = 5\%$. Option B (15%) comes from using 15,000 as a percentage by mistake. **Answer: A.**

**43.** An upward movement along the same demand curve is caused by:

a) A fall in price
b) A rise in price
c) A decrease in quantity demanded
d) An increase in quantity demanded

A movement along a demand curve is caused only by a **change in the price** of the good itself. Moving up the curve means that the price rises, and the quantity demanded then falls (a contraction of demand). Option C describes the result, not the cause. A fall in price (A) causes a downward movement. **Answer: B.**

**44.** An industry that locates in an area without considering the location factors of production is known as:

a) Weight gaining industry
b) Weight losing industry
c) Footloose industry
d) Industrial Inertia

A **footloose industry** is not tied to raw materials, power or the market, so it can be sited almost anywhere. Weight-losing industries (B) locate near raw materials and weight-gaining industries (A) near the market. Industrial inertia (D) means that an industry stays where it started although the original advantages have gone. **Answer: C.**

**45.** An example of two commodities which are in joint demand are:

a) Palm oil and palm kernels
b) Hides and skin
c) Meat and fish
d) Lamp and kerosine

**Joint (complementary) demand** exists when two goods are wanted together because one is of no use without the other: a lamp needs kerosine. Palm oil and palm kernels and hides and skin (A, B) are in **joint supply**, because they come from the same source. Meat and fish (C) are substitutes. **Answer: D.**

**46.** A carpentry workshop is able to produce per week as follows:

| Number of Carpenters | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Number of chairs produced | 10 | 24 | 33 | 40 | 45 |

Calculate average number of chairs produced per week by 3 carpenters:

a) 10 chairs
b) 12 chairs
c) 11 chairs
d) 13 chairs

Average product $=$ total product / number of workers. With 3 carpenters the total product is 33 chairs, so average product $= \dfrac{33}{3} = 11$ chairs per carpenter. The marginal product of the third carpenter is $33 - 24 = 9$, and 12 (B) is the average of 2 carpenters ($24/2$). **Answer: C.**

**47.** A perfect competitive market will maximize profits when:

*Options as printed:* A) MC = P   B) MC = AR   C) MC = MR   D) AR = AC

A firm maximises profit where **marginal cost equals marginal revenue** ($MC = MR$), with MC cutting MR from below. In perfect competition, price, average revenue and marginal revenue are equal, so $MC = P$ and $MC = AR$ also hold at that output; this makes options A and B true as well, and the printed question unreliable. The general rule is C. $AR = AC$ (D) gives only normal profit.

**Intended answer: C (MC = MR).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

**48.** The total costs of producing 10 bags of coffee is 150,000 FCFA. If fixed costs is 50,000 FCFA, then variable cost is:

a) 100,000 FCFA
b) 50,000 FCFA
c) 75,000 FCFA
d) 200,000 FCFA

Total cost = fixed cost + variable cost, so variable cost $= 150{,}000 - 50{,}000 = 100{,}000$ FCFA. Adding the two figures (200,000) is wrong. **Answer: A.**

**49.** Average income increases from 20,000 FCFA to 22,000 FCFA per week and quantity demanded per week increases from 5,000 units to 6,000 units. The income elasticity of demand will be:

a) The price elasticity of demand is - 2
b) The income elasticity of demand is - 2
c) The income elasticity of demand is + 0.5
d) The income elasticity of demand is + 2

$YED = \dfrac{\%\ \text{change in quantity demanded}}{\%\ \text{change in income}}$.

% change in quantity $= \dfrac{6{,}000 - 5{,}000}{5{,}000} \times 100 = 20\%$; % change in income $= \dfrac{22{,}000 - 20{,}000}{20{,}000} \times 100 = 10\%$.

$YED = \dfrac{20}{10} = +2$: demand rises more than income, so the good is a normal good with elastic income demand. Option C inverts the fraction, and A is about the wrong elasticity (price). **Answer: D.**

**50.** The demand for a good or service not for its own sake but for the sake of what it helps to produce is known as:

a) Joint demand
b) Composite demand
c) Derived demand
d) Complementary demand

**Derived demand** is demand for a factor or intermediate good because of the demand for the product it helps to make, for example the demand for cocoa beans by chocolate makers, or for labour. Joint and complementary demand (A, D) are goods demanded together, and composite demand (B) is demand for a good with several uses. **Answer: C.**
