Questions 43 - 47 (as printed). The setup in figure 7 is used by a student to investigate the relationship between the current flowing through a conductor Y and the potential difference across its ends.

![Figure 7: circuit with cell, rheostat X, ammeter A, conductor Y and voltmeter V across Y (questions 43 to 46)](/media/figures/cm/gce-ol-physics-2017-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_7.webp)

The component X is called

a) ammeter
b) resistor
c) rheostat
d) voltmeter

X is a variable resistor in series with the cell; its sliding contact (the arrow) changes the current. A variable resistor is called a rheostat. The ammeter and voltmeter are the circles marked A and V, and a fixed resistor has no arrow. **Answer: C.**

**44.** Using the setup of figure 7: what property of A permits it to be connected as shown?

a) It has a very high resistance
b) It has a very low resistance
c) It cannot easily be damaged
d) It has a very low conductivity

A is the ammeter, which is connected in series with the conductor. It must have a very low resistance so that it does not change the current it measures. A very high resistance is the property of the voltmeter, which is connected in parallel. **Answer: B.**

**45.** Using the setup of figure 7: the slope of a graph of the p.d. across Y plotted against the current through it represents

a) conductivity
b) Current
c) Voltage
d) Resistance

From $V = IR$, a graph of $V$ (vertical) against $I$ (horizontal) has gradient $\frac{V}{I} = R$. The slope therefore represents the resistance of Y. Conductivity would be the slope of $I$ against $V$. **Answer: D.**

**46.** Using the setup of figure 7: if Y is a filament bulb, which of the following graphs shows how p.d. V varies with current I?

![Four p.d.-current graphs (question 46), left to right](/media/figures/cm/gce-ol-physics-2017-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_8.webp)

(Graphs A to D from left to right; the labels of the third and fourth graphs are not printed.)

a) A
b) B
c) C
d) D

As the current increases the filament gets hotter and its resistance rises. Since $V = IR$ with $R$ increasing, the graph of $V$ against $I$ starts at the origin and gets steeper (curves upwards): the fourth graph, D. A straight line would be an ohmic conductor, and the horizontal line (C) and falling curves (A, B) do not correspond to any bulb behaviour. **Answer: D.**

**47.** Questions 47 - 50. The waveform in figure 8 is produced by an instrument vibrating at a frequency of 50 Hz connected to a cathode ray oscilloscope.

![Waveform with crest W, trough X, crest Y, trough Z, 4 cm marked from crest to trough, time axis ending at 0.05 s (questions 47 to 50)](/media/figures/cm/gce-ol-physics-2017-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_9.webp)

The amplitude of the wave is

a) 4 cm
b) 0.05 cm
c) 2 cm
d) 8 cm

The $4\ \mathrm{cm}$ arrow on the figure goes from the crest W to the trough X, i.e. it is the peak-to-peak height. The amplitude is the maximum displacement from the rest (time-axis) position, which is half of it: $\frac{4}{2} = 2\ \mathrm{cm}$. Option A is the full peak-to-trough height. **Answer: C.**

**48.** The waveform in figure 8 is produced by an instrument vibrating at a frequency of 50 Hz. The period of oscillation of the wave is

a) 50 s
b) 2.5 s
c) 0.01 s
d) 0.02 s

$T = \frac{1}{f} = \frac{1}{50} = 0.02\ \mathrm{s}$. This agrees with the figure: 2.5 cycles take $0.05\ \mathrm{s}$, so one cycle takes $0.02\ \mathrm{s}$. Option A is the frequency used as a time. **Answer: D.**

**49.** If the wave in figure 8 is travelling at a speed of $100\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, the wavelength of the wave is

a) 5000 m
b) 150 m
c) 2 m
d) 0.5 m

$v = f\lambda$, so $\lambda = \frac{v}{f} = \frac{100}{50} = 2\ \mathrm{m}$. Option A multiplies $v$ by $f$ instead of dividing, and D inverts the ratio. **Answer: C.**

**50.** Two points in phase on the waveform of figure 8 are

a) W and X
b) W and Y
c) W and Z
d) X and Y

Points in phase are at the same stage of the cycle, one whole wavelength apart. W and Y are consecutive crests, so they are in phase. W and X (crest and trough) are in antiphase, and X and Y are a crest and a trough. W and Z are a crest and a trough as well. **Answer: B.**

Given that $\dfrac{P}{1-x}+\dfrac{Q}{2+x}\equiv\dfrac{2x+1}{(1-x)(2+x)}$,

a) $P=1,\ Q=1$
b) $P=1,\ Q=-1$
c) $P=-1,\ Q=-1$
d) $P=-1,\ Q=1$

Multiply through by $(1-x)(2+x)$: $P(2+x)+Q(1-x)\equiv 2x+1$. Put $x=1$: $3P=3$, so $P=1$. Put $x=-2$: $3Q=-3$, so $Q=-1$. Check the coefficient of $x$: $P-Q=1-(-1)=2$, which matches $2x$. The slip behind options A and D is a sign error in $Q$. **Answer: B.**

c) $\dfrac{32}{9}$

$\int(3x+1)^5dx=\dfrac{(3x+1)^6}{18}$. So $\displaystyle\int_0^{1/3}(3x+1)^5dx=\dfrac{2^6-1^6}{18}=\dfrac{63}{18}=\dfrac72$. **Answer: B.**

**20.** The function $f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ is defined by $f:x\mapsto\dfrac{8x-3}{2x-7},\ x\ne\dfrac72$. $f$ is

a) odd
b) surjective
c) even
d) injective

$f'(x)=\dfrac{8(2x-7)-2(8x-3)}{(2x-7)^2}=\dfrac{-50}{(2x-7)^2}<0$, so $f$ is strictly decreasing on each of the intervals $x<\frac72$ and $x>\frac72$. On $x<\frac72$ the values lie below $4$ and on $x>\frac72$ above $4$ (since $f(x)=4+\dfrac{25}{2x-7}$), so no value is taken twice: $f$ is injective. It is never equal to $4$, so it is not surjective onto $\mathbb R$; $f(-x)\ne\pm f(x)$ (e.g. $f(1)=-1$, $f(-1)=\frac{11}{9}$), so it is neither odd nor even. **Answer: D.**

**21.** A bag contains $10$ small balls of equal size. Given that two of the balls are green and the others are of different colours, the number of different selections of $2$ balls that can be made from the bag is

a) $\dfrac{10!}{2!}$
b) $29$
c) $37$
d) $36$

The two green balls are indistinguishable by colour and the other $8$ balls all have different colours. Count selections by colour: two non-green balls: $\binom82=28$; one green and one non-green: $8$ (the choice of green ball does not matter); two green balls: $1$. Total $28+8+1=37$. (Counting all $\binom{10}2=45$ pairs would treat the green balls as different; option D is $28+8$, missing the green pair.) **Answer: C.**

**22.** Given that the complex number $z$ is such that $|z|=4$ and $\arg z=-\dfrac\pi3$, then $z=$

a) $4(1+i\sqrt3)$
b) $2(1+i\sqrt3)$
c) $4(1-i\sqrt3)$
d) $2(1-i\sqrt3)$

$z=4\left[\cos\left(-\dfrac\pi3\right)+i\sin\left(-\dfrac\pi3\right)\right]=4\left(\dfrac12-i\dfrac{\sqrt3}2\right)=2-2\sqrt3\,i=2(1-i\sqrt3)$. The negative argument gives the minus sign; the modulus $4$ gives the factor $2$ (not $4$) once $\frac12$ is used. **Answer: D.**

**23.** The distance of the origin from the plane $2x-3y+6z=14$ is

a) $2$
b) $14$
c) $-2$
d) $-14$

For the plane $\mathbf n\cdot\mathbf r=d$ the distance from the origin is $\dfrac{|d|}{|\mathbf n|}=\dfrac{14}{\sqrt{2^2+(-3)^2+6^2}}=\dfrac{14}{7}=2$. A distance cannot be negative, so C and D are excluded. **Answer: A.**

**24.** The determinant of the matrix $\begin{pmatrix}1&-1&2\\1&1&0\\-1&1&2\end{pmatrix}$ is

a) $4$
b) $8$
c) $6$
d) $2$

Expand along the first row: $1(1\cdot2-0\cdot1)-(-1)(1\cdot2-0\cdot(-1))+2(1\cdot1-1\cdot(-1))=1(2)+1(2)+2(2)=2+2+4=8$. **Answer: B.**

**25.** The vector $\mathbf v$, where $|\mathbf v|=28$, is in the direction of the vector $2\mathbf i+3\mathbf j-6\mathbf k$. $\mathbf v=$

a) $14\mathbf i+21\mathbf j-42\mathbf k$
b) $8\mathbf i+12\mathbf j-24\mathbf k$
c) $26\mathbf i+25\mathbf j-22\mathbf k$
d) $14\mathbf i+\dfrac{28}3\mathbf j-\dfrac{14}3\mathbf k$

$|2\mathbf i+3\mathbf j-6\mathbf k|=\sqrt{4+9+36}=7$, so the unit vector is $\dfrac17(2\mathbf i+3\mathbf j-6\mathbf k)$ and $\mathbf v=28\cdot\dfrac17(2\mathbf i+3\mathbf j-6\mathbf k)=4(2\mathbf i+3\mathbf j-6\mathbf k)=8\mathbf i+12\mathbf j-24\mathbf k$. Option A has magnitude $7\times 7=49$ (it is $7$ times the given vector). **Answer: B.**

**26.** The area of the finite region enclosed by the curve $xy=4$, the $x$-axis and the ordinates $x=2$ and $x=8$ is

a) $4\ln6$
b) $16\ln2$
c) $8\ln2$
d) $\ln4$

$y=\dfrac4x$, so the area is $\displaystyle\int_2^8\dfrac4x\,dx=4\left[\ln x\right]_2^8=4(\ln8-\ln2)=4\ln4=8\ln2$. **Answer: C.**

**27.** A linear relationship between the logarithms of the variable $x$ and $y$ which are connected by the relation $y=ax^n$ is

a) $\log y=n(\log a+\log x)$
b) $\log y=n\log a+\log x$
c) $\log y=\log a+\log nx$
d) $\log y=\log a+n\log x$

Take logarithms of $y=ax^n$: $\log y=\log a+\log x^n=\log a+n\log x$. This is a straight line of gradient $n$ and intercept $\log a$ when $\log y$ is plotted against $\log x$. **Answer: D.**

**28.** The values of $y$ for various values of $x$ are given in the table below.

| $x$ | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| $y$ | 3 | 4.2 | 5.2 | 6 | 6.7 | 7.3 |

Using the trapezium rule, $\displaystyle\int_1^6y\,dx\approx$

a) $32.40$
b) $27.25$
c) $25.90$
d) $27.52$

There are $6$ ordinates, so $5$ strips of width $h=1$. Trapezium rule: $\dfrac h2\left[y_1+y_6+2(y_2+y_3+y_4+y_5)\right]=\dfrac12\left[3+7.3+2(4.2+5.2+6+6.7)\right]=\dfrac12\left[10.3+44.2\right]=\dfrac{54.5}2=27.25$. **Answer: B.**

**29.** Given that $f(x)=x^2\ln(x-2)$, $f'(3)=$

a) $9$
b) $6$
c) $6\ln5-9$
d) $-9$

By the product rule $f'(x)=2x\ln(x-2)+x^2\cdot\dfrac1{x-2}$. At $x=3$: $6\ln1+\dfrac{9}{1}=0+9=9$. **Answer: A.**

**30.** $\dfrac{1}{(1+\sqrt3\,i)^3}=$

a) $-8$
b) $-\dfrac18$
c) $\dfrac18$
d) $8$

$1+\sqrt3\,i=2\left(\cos\dfrac\pi3+i\sin\dfrac\pi3\right)$, so by de Moivre $(1+\sqrt3\,i)^3=8(\cos\pi+i\sin\pi)=-8$. Hence $\dfrac1{(1+\sqrt3 i)^3}=-\dfrac18$. **Answer: B.**

**31.** The vector perpendicular to both $3\mathbf i-6\mathbf j-4\mathbf k$ and $-3\mathbf i+2\mathbf j+2\mathbf k$ is

a) $-4\mathbf i+6\mathbf j+12\mathbf k$
b) $-4\mathbf i+6\mathbf j-12\mathbf k$
c) $4\mathbf i-6\mathbf j-12\mathbf k$
d) $-2\mathbf i+3\mathbf j+6\mathbf k$

The cross product $\begin{vmatrix}\mathbf i&\mathbf j&\mathbf k\\3&-6&-4\\-3&2&2\end{vmatrix}=\mathbf i(-12+8)-\mathbf j(6-12)+\mathbf k(6-18)=-4\mathbf i+6\mathbf j-12\mathbf k$. Check with dot products: $3(-4)-6(6)-4(-12)=-12-36+48=0$ and $-3(-4)+2(6)+2(-12)=12+12-24=0$. The other options fail one of these tests (e.g. option A: $-12-36-48\ne0$). **Answer: B.**

**32.** The remainder when $x^3-5x^2+7$ is divided by $(x-1)^2$ is

a) $3$
b) $5$
c) $-7x+10$
d) $7x-10$

The remainder has the form $ax+b$: $x^3-5x^2+7=(x-1)^2Q(x)+ax+b$. Put $x=1$: $3=a+b$. Differentiate: $3x^2-10x=2(x-1)Q+(x-1)^2Q'+a$; at $x=1$: $-7=a$. Then $b=10$ and the remainder is $-7x+10$. **Answer: C.**

**33.** Given that the complex numbers $z_1=3+i$ and $z_2=-3-i$ are such that $|z-z_1|=|z-z_2|$, the locus of $z$ is

a) a circle
b) the line $3y=-x$
c) the line $y=3x$
d) the line $y=-3x$

$|z-z_1|=|z-z_2|$ means $z$ is equidistant from $(3,1)$ and $(-3,-1)$, so the locus is the perpendicular bisector of the segment joining them. Algebraically, with $z=x+iy$: $(x-3)^2+(y-1)^2=(x+3)^2+(y+1)^2$ gives $-12x-4y=0$, i.e. $y=-3x$. The line passes through the midpoint $(0,0)$ with gradient $-3$, perpendicular to the gradient $\dfrac13$ of the segment. **Answer: D.**

**34.** Let $A=\{1,2,3,4\}$ and $R$ be a relation defined on $A$. Given that $R=\{(1,1),(1,3),(2,2),(2,1),(3,1),(1,2),(4,4)\}$, $R$ is

a) Reflexive
b) Symmetric
c) Anti-symmetric
d) transitive

Reflexive needs $(3,3)\in R$: missing, so not reflexive. Symmetric: the reverse of every pair is present ($(1,3)\leftrightarrow(3,1)$, $(2,1)\leftrightarrow(1,2)$, and $(1,1),(2,2),(4,4)$ are their own reverse), so $R$ is symmetric. Anti-symmetric fails because $(1,2)$ and $(2,1)$ are both in $R$ with $1\ne2$. Transitive fails: $(3,1)$ and $(1,2)$ are in $R$ but $(3,2)$ is not. **Answer: B.**

**35.** Given that $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=6(\sin2x-\cos3x)$ and $y=0$ when $x=0$, $y=$

a) $-3\cos2x-2\sin3x-3$
b) $3\cos2x-2\sin3x+3$
c) $-3\cos2x-2\sin3x+3$
d) $3\cos2x+2\sin3x-3$

Integrate: $y=6\left(-\dfrac{\cos2x}{2}-\dfrac{\sin3x}{3}\right)+C=-3\cos2x-2\sin3x+C$. At $x=0$: $0=-3-0+C$, so $C=3$ and $y=-3\cos2x-2\sin3x+3$. **Answer: C.**

**SECTION B: MECHANICS**

The work done by a force $(3\mathbf i+4\mathbf j+5\mathbf k)$ N acting on a particle which moves from a point with position vector $(\mathbf i+\mathbf j+2\mathbf k)$ m to another point with position vector $(3\mathbf i-2\mathbf j+4\mathbf k)$ m is

a) $46$ J
b) $4$ J
c) $(6\mathbf i-12\mathbf j+10\mathbf k)$ J
d) $(12\mathbf i+4\mathbf j+30\mathbf k)$ J

Displacement $\mathbf d=(3\mathbf i-2\mathbf j+4\mathbf k)-(\mathbf i+\mathbf j+2\mathbf k)=2\mathbf i-3\mathbf j+2\mathbf k$. Work done $=\mathbf F\cdot\mathbf d=3(2)+4(-3)+5(2)=6-12+10=4$ J. Work is a scalar, so C and D (vectors, componentwise products) are wrong. **Answer: B.**

**37.** A small sphere of mass $10$ kg is moving with speed $5\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ and collides with another sphere of mass $4$ kg moving in the opposite direction with speed $2\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. If after collision the speed of the $4$ kg mass is $5.5\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, the coefficient of restitution between the spheres is

a) $\dfrac12$
b) $\dfrac13$
c) $\dfrac14$
d) $\dfrac34$

Take the direction of the $10$ kg sphere as positive: before, $u_1=5$ and $u_2=-2$. Conservation of momentum: $10(5)+4(-2)=42=10v_1+4v_2$. The $4$ kg sphere must leave in the positive direction (the spheres cannot pass through each other), so $v_2=5.5$ and $10v_1=42-22=20$, $v_1=2$. Newton's law of restitution: $v_2-v_1=e(u_1-u_2)$, so $5.5-2=7e$ and $e=\dfrac{3.5}{7}=\dfrac12$. (With $v_2=-5.5$ we would get $v_1=6.4$ and the spheres would overlap, which is impossible.) **Answer: A.**

**38.** The displacement $\mathbf r$ of a particle at time $t$ is given by $\mathbf r=(t^3\mathbf i-2t\mathbf j+3t^2\mathbf k)$ m. The speed of the particle after $1$ second is

a) $\sqrt{14}\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$
b) $(3\mathbf i-2\mathbf j+6\mathbf k)\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$
c) $7\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$
d) $49\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$

$\mathbf v=\dfrac{d\mathbf r}{dt}=3t^2\mathbf i-2\mathbf j+6t\,\mathbf k$. At $t=1$: $\mathbf v=3\mathbf i-2\mathbf j+6\mathbf k$ and the speed is $|\mathbf v|=\sqrt{9+4+36}=\sqrt{49}=7\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. Option B is the velocity (a vector), option D is $|\mathbf v|^2$. **Answer: C.**

**39.** Four particles of masses $5,2,1$ and $4$ kg are placed at the points with position vectors $2\mathbf j-\mathbf k$, $5\mathbf i-\mathbf j$, $4\mathbf i-3\mathbf j+\mathbf k$ and $\mathbf i+\mathbf j+3\mathbf k$ respectively. The position vector of their centre of mass is

a) $\dfrac23\mathbf i+\dfrac34\mathbf j+\dfrac32\mathbf k$
b) $\dfrac32\mathbf i+\dfrac34\mathbf j+\dfrac32\mathbf k$
c) $\dfrac32\mathbf i+\dfrac43\mathbf j+\dfrac23\mathbf k$
d) $\dfrac32\mathbf i+\dfrac34\mathbf j+\dfrac23\mathbf k$

Total mass $=5+2+1+4=12$ kg. $\sum m\mathbf r=5(2\mathbf j-\mathbf k)+2(5\mathbf i-\mathbf j)+1(4\mathbf i-3\mathbf j+\mathbf k)+4(\mathbf i+\mathbf j+3\mathbf k)$. $\mathbf i$: $0+10+4+4=18$; $\mathbf j$: $10-2-3+4=9$; $\mathbf k$: $-5+0+1+12=8$. So $\bar{\mathbf r}=\dfrac{18\mathbf i+9\mathbf j+8\mathbf k}{12}=\dfrac32\mathbf i+\dfrac34\mathbf j+\dfrac23\mathbf k$. **Answer: D.**

**40.** A car moves at constant speed of $60\ \mathrm{km\,h^{-1}}$ on a level road when the engine is working at $15$ kW. The resistance to the motion of the car is

a) $375$ N
b) $37{,}500$ N
c) $90{,}0000$ N
d) $900$ N

At constant speed the driving force equals the resistance, and $P=Fv$. $v=60\ \mathrm{km\,h^{-1}}=\dfrac{60000}{3600}=\dfrac{50}3\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ and $P=15000$ W, so $R=F=\dfrac Pv=\dfrac{15000}{50/3}=900$ N. The units must be SI: using $60$ instead of $\frac{50}3$ gives $250$ N. **Answer: D.**

**41.** A particle of mass $4$ kg is placed on a smooth horizontal table and connected by a light inextensible string passing over a small fixed smooth pulley at the edge of the table to a mass of $6$ kg hanging freely. The system is released from rest. Taking $g$ as $10\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$, the tension in the string is

a) $36$ N
b) $24$ N
c) $24\sqrt2$ N
d) $48$ N

Let $a$ be the common acceleration and $T$ the tension. For the $4$ kg particle on the smooth table: $T=4a$. For the hanging $6$ kg mass: $60-T=6a$. Adding: $60=10a$, so $a=6\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$ and $T=4\times6=24$ N. (Option A, $36$ N, is the net force $6a$ on the hanging mass.) **Answer: B.**

**42.** Two boats $B_1$ and $B_2$ are moving with velocities $(4\mathbf i-3\mathbf j+7\mathbf k)\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ and $(2\mathbf i+3\mathbf j+4\mathbf k)\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ respectively. The relative velocity of $B_1$ when viewed from $B_2$ is

a) $(-2\mathbf i+6\mathbf j-3\mathbf k)\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$
b) $(6\mathbf i+11\mathbf k)\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$
c) $(2\mathbf i+3\mathbf k)\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$
d) $(2\mathbf i-6\mathbf j+3\mathbf k)\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$

The velocity of $B_1$ relative to $B_2$ is $\mathbf v_1-\mathbf v_2=(4-2)\mathbf i+(-3-3)\mathbf j+(7-4)\mathbf k=2\mathbf i-6\mathbf j+3\mathbf k$. Option A is $\mathbf v_2-\mathbf v_1$ (velocity of $B_2$ seen from $B_1$) and option B is the sum. **Answer: D.**

**43.** A particle of mass $m$ is attached by a light inelastic string of length $2$ m to a fixed point $O$. The particle moves with constant speed $v\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ in a horizontal circle whose centre is $1.5$ m vertically below $O$ and radius $\dfrac{\sqrt7}2$, $v^2=$

a) $\dfrac76g$
b) $\dfrac67g$
c) $\dfrac9{16}g$
d) $\dfrac{16}9g$

Let $\theta$ be the angle of the string to the vertical: $\tan\theta=\dfrac{r}{h}=\dfrac{\sqrt7/2}{3/2}=\dfrac{\sqrt7}3$ (consistent with the string length: $1.5^2+\frac74=4=2^2$), and $\cos\theta=\dfrac{1.5}2=\dfrac34$, $\sin\theta=\dfrac{\sqrt7}4$. Vertically: $T\cos\theta=mg$. Horizontally: $T\sin\theta=\dfrac{mv^2}{r}$. Dividing: $\tan\theta=\dfrac{v^2}{rg}$, so $v^2=rg\tan\theta=\dfrac{\sqrt7}2\cdot\dfrac{\sqrt7}3\,g=\dfrac76g$. **Answer: A.**

**44.** A particle moves horizontally with retardation $3v^2$, where $v$ is its speed at time $t$. If the initial speed of the particle is $2\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, $v=$

a) $\dfrac{2}{1-6t}$
b) $\dfrac{2}{6t-1}$
c) $\dfrac{2}{1+6t}$
d) $\dfrac{-2}{1+6t}$

Retardation means $\dfrac{dv}{dt}=-3v^2$. Separate variables: $\displaystyle\int\dfrac{dv}{v^2}=-3\int dt$, so $-\dfrac1v=-3t+c$, i.e. $\dfrac1v=3t+k$. At $t=0$, $v=2$: $k=\dfrac12$. So $\dfrac1v=3t+\dfrac12=\dfrac{6t+1}2$ and $v=\dfrac2{1+6t}$. The speed decreases from $2$ towards $0$, as it must. **Answer: C.**

**45.** A particle moves horizontally with velocity $\mathbf v$, where $\mathbf v=(t^2\mathbf i+3\mathbf j)\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, at time $t$ seconds. Initially, $\mathbf r=(3\mathbf i-4\mathbf j)$ m. The distance covered in $3$ seconds is

*Options as printed:* A) $9\sqrt2$ m   B) $(12\mathbf i+5\mathbf j)$ m   C) $13$ m   D) $(9\mathbf i+9\mathbf j)$ m

Integrate the velocity: $\mathbf r=\left(\dfrac{t^3}3+3\right)\mathbf i+(3t-4)\mathbf j$. At $t=3$: $\mathbf r=12\mathbf i+5\mathbf j$ (option B is this final position), so the displacement over $3$ s is $\mathbf r(3)-\mathbf r(0)=9\mathbf i+9\mathbf j$ (option D) and its magnitude is $9\sqrt2\approx12.73$ m (option A), which is the straight-line distance between the start and end points. The path is NOT straight, because the direction of $\mathbf v$ changes, so the distance actually travelled along the path is the arc length $\displaystyle\int_0^3\sqrt{t^4+9}\,dt\approx13.93$ m, a value that is not among the options. The question is therefore ambiguous (distance versus magnitude of the displacement).

**Intended answer: A, $9\sqrt2$ m (magnitude of the displacement); the true path length is about $13.93$ m.**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

**46.** The forces $\mathbf F_1=(-4\mathbf i+3\mathbf j)$ N, $\mathbf F_2=(-2\mathbf i+4\mathbf j)$ N act through the points $\mathbf r_1=(2\mathbf i-\mathbf j)$ m and $\mathbf r_2=4\mathbf j$ m respectively. The total moment of the forces about the origin is

a) $-10$ Nm
b) $10$ Nm
c) $-16$ Nm
d) $16$ Nm

In the plane, the (anticlockwise) moment of $\mathbf F$ through $\mathbf r=(x,y)$ about the origin is $xF_y-yF_x$. For $\mathbf F_1$: $2(3)-(-1)(-4)=6-4=2$ Nm. For $\mathbf F_2$: $0(4)-4(-2)=8$ Nm. Total $=2+8=10$ Nm (anticlockwise). **Answer: B.**

**47.** The events $E_1$ and $E_2$ are such that $P(E_1)=\dfrac13$, $P(E_1|E_2)=\dfrac14$ and $P(E_2|E_1)=\dfrac12$. $P(E_2)=$

a) $\dfrac23$
b) $\dfrac1{12}$
c) $\dfrac18$
d) $\dfrac56$

$P(E_1\cap E_2)=P(E_2|E_1)P(E_1)=\dfrac12\cdot\dfrac13=\dfrac16$. Also $P(E_1\cap E_2)=P(E_1|E_2)P(E_2)$, so $P(E_2)=\dfrac{1/6}{1/4}=\dfrac46=\dfrac23$. **Answer: A.**

**48.** The probability that Ekane gets out of bed is $\dfrac25$. If he gets out of bed late; the probability that he is late to school is $\dfrac45$. If he gets out of bed early, the probability that he is late to school is $\dfrac3{10}$. The probability that Ekane is late to school is

a) $\dfrac12$
b) $\dfrac8{25}$
c) $\dfrac9{50}$
d) $\dfrac{12}{125}$

As printed, the first sentence omits the word late (it reads: the probability that Ekane gets out of bed is $\frac25$); the only reading that gives an answer among the options is $P(\text{gets out of bed late})=\dfrac25$ and so $P(\text{early})=\dfrac35$. By the law of total probability: $P(\text{late to school})=\dfrac25\cdot\dfrac45+\dfrac35\cdot\dfrac3{10}=\dfrac8{25}+\dfrac9{50}=\dfrac{16+9}{50}=\dfrac12$. (The other reading, $P(\text{early})=\frac25$, gives $\frac3{25}+\frac{12}{25}=\frac35$, which is not an option.) Options B and C are the two partial products. **Answer: A.**

**49.** The equation of the trajectory of a projectile is given by $y=x-\dfrac{x^2}{40}$. The horizontal distance travelled by the projectile when it has risen a height of $9.6$ m is

a) $16$ m or $24$ m
b) $16$ m or $10$ m
c) $10$ m or $30$ m
d) $24$ m or $30$ m

Put $y=9.6$: $x-\dfrac{x^2}{40}=9.6$, so $x^2-40x+384=0$. The discriminant is $1600-1536=64$, so $x=\dfrac{40\pm8}2=24$ or $16$. The projectile is at height $9.6$ m twice (once rising, once falling), after $16$ m and after $24$ m. **Answer: A.**

**50.** The speed-time graph of a body is shown below.

![Speed-time graph of a body (Q50): speed 3 m/s at t = 0, rising uniformly to 8 m/s at t = 4 s, constant until t = 9 s, then decreasing uniformly to 0 at t = 15 s.](/media/figures/cm/gce-al-pm-mechanics-2017-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_1.webp)

The distance covered by the body in $15$ seconds is

a) $80$ m
b) $112$ m
c) $86$ m
d) $88$ m

The distance is the area under the speed-time graph. From the graph, $v=3$ at $t=0$, rises uniformly to $8$ at $t=4$, stays at $8$ until $t=9$, then falls uniformly to $0$ at $t=15$. Trapezium $0$ to $4$: $\dfrac{3+8}2\times4=22$. Rectangle $4$ to $9$: $8\times5=40$. Triangle $9$ to $15$: $\dfrac12\times6\times8=24$. Total $=22+40+24=86$ m. **Answer: C.**

**1.** A type of classification of organisms based on similarities and differences in as many observable characteristics is

a) artificial classification.
b) phylogenetic classification.
c) numerical classification.
d) phenetic classification.

Phenetic classification (numerical taxonomy) groups organisms according to their overall similarity, using as many observable characters as possible and giving them equal weight, without trying to reflect evolutionary history. Artificial classification uses only a few convenient characters, phylogenetic classification reflects evolutionary relationships (common ancestry), and numerical classification names the statistical method rather than the principle. **Answer: D.**

**2.** An enzyme that is inactive and must associate with a specific cofactor molecule in order to function is

a) apoenzyme.
b) coenzyme.
c) enzyme activator.
d) allosteric enzyme.

An apoenzyme is the protein part of an enzyme that is inactive on its own. It becomes the active holoenzyme only when it combines with its specific cofactor (a coenzyme, a prosthetic group or a metal ion activator). A coenzyme is the organic cofactor itself, not the enzyme, and an allosteric enzyme is regulated at a site other than its active site. **Answer: A.**

**3.** Which of these carbohydrates has residues linked by $\alpha$-1,4 glycosidic bonds?

a) Maltose.
b) Lactose.
c) Sucrose.
d) Glycogen.

Maltose is a disaccharide of two $\alpha$-glucose units joined only by an $\alpha$-1,4 glycosidic bond. Lactose is galactose and glucose joined by a $\beta$-1,4 bond, and sucrose is glucose and fructose joined by an $\alpha$-1,2 bond. Glycogen also contains $\alpha$-1,4 bonds but it is branched, with $\alpha$-1,6 bonds at the branch points, so it is not linked by $\alpha$-1,4 bonds alone. The best answer is maltose. **Answer: A.**

**4.** The presence of a periviscceral cavity in the mesoderm of triploblastic multicellular animals makes them to be called

a) acoelomates.
b) pseudocoelomates.
c) coelomates.
d) coelenterates.

A true coelom is a fluid-filled body cavity completely lined by mesoderm, so animals that have it are coelomates. Acoelomates have no cavity, pseudocoelomates have a cavity only partly lined by mesoderm, and coelenterates (cnidarians) are diploblastic with no mesoderm at all. **Answer: C.**

**5.** Because .................... occurs more frequently between genes situated far apart on a chromosome and less frequently on genes situated close together, this information is used to draw a chromosome map. Which of the following best fills the space above?

a) Mutations.
b) Cross over value.
c) Cross over frequency.
d) Crossing over.

The further apart two linked genes are, the more likely it is that a chiasma forms between them and that crossing over separates them. Recombination frequency (cross over value) therefore measures distance and is used to build chromosome maps. The word that fills the space in the sentence is the process itself, crossing over. Mutations are unrelated to gene distance, and cross over value and cross over frequency are the measurements derived from the process, not the process that occurs. **Answer: D.**

**6.** Smoking destroys the cilia in the respiratory passage. This

a) makes it harder to move air in and out of the lungs.
b) decreases the surface area for respiration.
c) slows blood flow through the blood vessels in the lungs.
d) makes it harder to keep the lungs clean.

Cilia beat to sweep mucus, trapped dust and bacteria up and out of the airways. When smoke paralyses and destroys them, mucus and particles stay in the passage, so it becomes harder to keep the lungs clean and the risk of infections and bronchitis increases. Smoking does not directly reduce the surface area or slow the blood flow, and air movement is not made harder by loss of cilia alone. **Answer: D.**

**7.** Epithelial tissues arise from

a) all the three germ layers.
b) the ectoderm.
c) the endoderm.
d) the mesoderm.

The three embryonic germ layers all give epithelia: the ectoderm forms the epidermis, the endoderm forms the lining of the gut and respiratory tract, and the mesoderm forms the lining of blood vessels, body cavities and kidney tubules. So epithelial tissues arise from all three germ layers. **Answer: A.**

**8.** The complete breakdown of 1 glucose molecule releases 2880 kJ (38 ATP). If 1 ATP molecule contains 30.6 kJ, what will be the percentage efficiency of energy transfer in aerobic respiration?

a) 40.1%
b) 40.3%
c) 40.2%
d) 40.4%

Energy trapped in ATP $= 38 \times 30.6 = 1162.8\ \mathrm{kJ}$. Efficiency $= \dfrac{1162.8}{2880} \times 100 = 40.375\% \approx 40.4\%$ (to 1 decimal place). The nearest option is 40.4%; 40.3% would result only from truncating instead of rounding. **Answer: D.**

**9.** Secretory vesicles that carry products for exocytosis in cells are produced in the

a) ribosomes.
b) golgi complex.
c) endoplasmic reticulum.
d) lysosomes.

The Golgi complex modifies, sorts and packages proteins and other products received from the rough endoplasmic reticulum into secretory vesicles that bud off and fuse with the plasma membrane (exocytosis). Ribosomes only make proteins, the endoplasmic reticulum sends transport vesicles to the Golgi, and lysosomes are vesicles of digestive enzymes kept inside the cell. **Answer: B.**

**10.** The parasitic protoctist that causes dysentery is

a) *Amoeba histolytica.*
b) *Entamoeba gingivalis.*
c) *Shigella dysenterae.*
d) *Entamoeba histolytica.*

Amoebic dysentery is caused by the protoctist *Entamoeba histolytica*, which invades the wall of the large intestine. *Amoeba histolytica* is an obsolete name, *Entamoeba gingivalis* lives in the mouth and does not cause dysentery, and *Shigella dysenteriae* is a bacterium causing bacillary dysentery. **Answer: D.**

**11.** In leaves, gaseous exchange and transport takes place in the

a) cuticle.
b) spongy mesophyll.
c) palisade mesophyll.
d) guard cells.

The spongy mesophyll has loosely packed cells with large air spaces connected to the stomata, so carbon dioxide, oxygen and water vapour diffuse and are transported through it between the atmosphere and the cells. The cuticle is waterproof and gas-tight, the palisade layer is tightly packed and specialised for light capture, and guard cells only control the opening of the stomata. **Answer: B.**

**12.** The function of deamination is to

a) produce $\mathrm{NH_3}$.
b) produce urea.
c) remove excess amino acid.
d) synthesize ornithine.

Deamination, which takes place in the liver, removes the amino group ($-\mathrm{NH_2}$) from excess amino acids, producing ammonia ($\mathrm{NH_3}$) and a keto acid that is respired or converted to carbohydrate or fat. The ammonia is then converted to urea in the ornithine cycle, so producing urea and synthesising ornithine are later steps and not deamination itself. Of the options, producing $\mathrm{NH_3}$ is the direct function. **Answer: A.**

**13.** In recombinant DNA technology, plasmids may be used to

a) cut DNA at specific locations.
b) introduce foreign DNA into bacteria.
c) introduce foreign DNA into human cell.
d) activate DNA.

Plasmids are small circular DNA molecules of bacteria. They are cut with a restriction enzyme, a foreign gene is inserted and sealed in with ligase, and the recombinant plasmid acts as a vector that carries the foreign DNA into bacterial cells. Cutting DNA is done by restriction enzymes, not by plasmids, and introducing DNA into human cells needs other vectors such as viruses. **Answer: B.**

**14.** The greatest volume of water is reabsorbed from the nephron by the

a) proximal tubule.
b) Bowman's capsule.
c) distal tubule.
d) collecting duct.

About 80 to 85% of the water in the glomerular filtrate is reabsorbed in the proximal convoluted tubule, together with glucose, amino acids and most of the salts. The distal tubule and collecting duct reabsorb a smaller, variable volume under the control of ADH, and the Bowman's capsule does not reabsorb but filters. **Answer: A.**

**15.** An inheritance pattern explained by multiple alleles is

a) ABO blood group.
b) cystic fibrosis.
c) Down's syndrome.
d) haemophilia.

The ABO blood group is controlled by one gene with three alleles ($I^A$, $I^B$ and $i$), so it is the classic example of multiple alleles. Cystic fibrosis (autosomal recessive allele) and haemophilia (X-linked recessive allele) involve two alleles, and Down's syndrome is a chromosome mutation (trisomy 21). **Answer: A.**

**16.** Organisms that have been genetically modified to carry foreign genes are

a) homogenous organisms.
b) legated organisms.
c) plasmids.
d) transgenic organisms.

A transgenic organism has had a gene from another species inserted into its genome by genetic engineering (for example bacteria making human insulin). Plasmids are only the vectors used, and homogenous and legated organisms are not recognised terms for this. **Answer: D.**

**17.** Which of the following compounds is the product of the reaction between carbon dioxide and phosphoenol pyruvate (PEP) in tropical plants such as sorghum?

a) Ribulose bisphosphate carboxylase.
b) Ribulose biphosphate.
c) Oxaloacetic acid.
d) Phosphoglyceraldehyde.

In $\mathrm{C_4}$ plants such as sorghum, carbon dioxide is first fixed in the mesophyll cells by PEP carboxylase. The three-carbon PEP combines with $\mathrm{CO_2}$ to give the four-carbon compound oxaloacetic acid (later converted to malate or aspartate). Ribulose bisphosphate carboxylase (rubisco) is the enzyme of the $\mathrm{C_3}$ pathway, ribulose bisphosphate is its substrate, and phosphoglyceraldehyde (triose phosphate) is a later product of the Calvin cycle. **Answer: C.**

**18.** Why is the pancreas described as a mixed gland having both endocrine and exocrine functions?

a) It produces digestive enzymes which are passed via the pancreatic duct to the duodenum and insulin and glucagon which are passed to the liver and muscles via blood vessels.
b) Produces peptidases to digest proteins.
c) It produces digestive enzymes which are passed via the pancreatic duct to the duodenum.
d) It produces insulin and glucagon which are passed to the liver and muscles via blood vessels.

Exocrine part: acinar cells make digestive enzymes (amylase, lipase, proteases) that reach the duodenum through the pancreatic duct. Endocrine part: the islets of Langerhans secrete insulin and glucagon directly into the blood, which carries them to target organs such as the liver and muscles. Only option A states both functions correctly; B, C and D each describe only one of them. **Answer: A.**

**19.** What plant hormone is responsible for the stimulation of cell elongation in shoots?

a) Indole acetic acid.
b) Ethylene.
c) Abscisic acid.
d) Cytokinins.

Indole acetic acid (IAA), the main auxin, is made in the shoot tip and stimulates cell elongation in shoots (the basis of phototropism). Ethylene promotes fruit ripening, abscisic acid closes stomata and maintains dormancy, and cytokinins promote cell division. **Answer: A.**

**20.** When does the second meiotic division in oogenesis likely to occur?

a) When sperm head is inside the secondary oocyte.
b) When the sperm and secondary oocyte meet.
c) When the secondary oocyte is inside the uterus.
d) When the secondary oocyte is released from the ovary.

In humans the secondary oocyte is arrested at metaphase II at ovulation. The second meiotic division is completed only when a sperm penetrates it, that is when the sperm head is inside the secondary oocyte, producing the ovum and the second polar body. It does not occur in the uterus or on release from the ovary, and it is triggered by sperm entry and not by the mere meeting of the cells. **Answer: A.**

**21.** In a food chain with four links,

(i) there are three energy transfers.

(ii) there are four trophic levels.

(iii) primary consumers are more numerous than producers.

(iv) there are five organisms.

a) (i), (ii) and (iii) are correct.
b) (i) and (iii) are correct.
c) (ii) and (iv) are correct.
d) only (iv) is correct.

The phrase 'four links' is read as four feeding links (arrows) joining organisms, e.g. producer $\to$ primary consumer $\to$ secondary consumer $\to$ tertiary consumer $\to$ quaternary consumer. Four arrows join five organisms, so (iv) is correct. There are then four energy transfers (not three), so (i) is wrong; there are five trophic levels (not four), so (ii) is wrong; and (iii) is wrong because in general producers are more numerous than primary consumers. Only (iv) is correct. **Answer: D.**

**22.** An inverted pyramid can be produced from

(i) orange tree $\to$ caterpillar $\to$ bird.

(ii) grass $\to$ locust $\to$ hen.

(iii) mango tree $\to$ ants $\to$ lizard.

(iv) carrot $\to$ goat $\to$ foxes.

a) (i), (ii) and (iii) are correct.
b) (i) and (iii) are correct.
c) (ii) and (iv) are correct.
d) only (iv) is correct.

An inverted pyramid of numbers occurs when a single large producer supports many consumers. One orange tree supports many caterpillars, so (i) gives an inverted base; one mango tree supports very many ants, so (iii) is also inverted at the base. Grass (many plants) and carrot (many plants) support fewer consumers, so (ii) and (iv) give upright pyramids. So (i) and (iii) are correct. **Answer: B.**

**23.** A community includes

(i) different species in the same habitat.

(ii) the same species in different habitats.

(iii) different populations in the same habitat.

(iv) the same population in different habitat.

a) (i), (ii) and (iii) are correct.
b) (i) and (iii) are correct.
c) (ii) and (iv) are correct.
d) only (iv) is correct.

A community is all the populations of the different species living together in the same habitat at the same time. (i) and (iii) express exactly this, since different species form different populations. (ii) and (iv) describe a single species or population spread over different habitats, which is not a community. So (i) and (iii) are correct. **Answer: B.**

**24.** Characteristics of parenchyma tissues include:

(i) presence of living protoplasmic material.

(ii) presence of lignified cell wall.

(iii) cells which are isodiametric in shape.

(v) presence of pits.

a) (i), (ii) and (iii) are correct.
b) (i) and (iii) are correct.
c) (ii) and (iv) are correct.
d) only (iv) is correct.

Parenchyma cells are living, with a protoplast, thin cellulose walls and roughly isodiametric shape, so (i) and (iii) are correct. Lignified walls are a feature of sclerenchyma and xylem, so (ii) is wrong. The fourth statement (printed '(v)', meant as (iv)) about pits is true only in the weak sense that parenchyma walls have primary pit fields; it is not a distinguishing characteristic, and no option offers (i), (iii) and (iv) together. The combination that fits is (i) and (iii). **Answer: B.**

**25.** Asexual reproducing organisms exhibit little or no genetic variation because:

(i) asexual reproduction does not involve gamete formation.

(ii) asexual reproduction involves only one parent.

(iii) in asexual reproduction no fusion of gametes is involved.

(iv) during asexual reproduction many offspring are produced.

a) (i), (ii) and (iii) are correct.
b) (i) and (iii) are correct.
c) (ii) and (iv) are correct.
d) only (iv) is correct.

Asexual offspring arise by mitosis from a single parent, with no meiosis, no gamete formation and no fusion of gametes, so there is no shuffling or mixing of genes and the offspring are clones of the parent. (i), (ii) and (iii) are all valid reasons. (iv) is a result of asexual reproduction, not a reason for the lack of variation. **Answer: A.**

**26.** The electron transport system

(i) occurs in the cristae of the mitochondria.

(ii) involves electrons and protons reducing oxygen to water.

(iii) involves oxidative phosphorylation.

(iv) occurs in the cytoplasm of cells.

a) (i), (ii) and (iii) are correct.
b) (i) and (iii) are correct.
c) (ii) and (iv) are correct.
d) only (iv) is correct.

The electron transport chain is carried by carriers in the inner mitochondrial membrane (the cristae). Electrons pass along it and, with protons, finally reduce oxygen to water, and the energy released drives ATP synthesis by oxidative phosphorylation. It does not occur in the cytoplasm (that is glycolysis), so (iv) is wrong. (i), (ii) and (iii) are correct. **Answer: A.**

**27.** Which of the following is true about nervous tissue?

(i) Composed of neurons.

(ii) Has dendrites which conduct impulses towards the cell body.

(iii) Has axons which conduct impulses away from the cell body.

(iv) Has myelin sheath which facilitates conduction of impulses across the synapse.

a) (i), (ii) and (iii) are correct.
b) (i) and (iii) are correct.
c) (ii) and (iv) are correct.
d) only (iv) is correct.

Nervous tissue consists of neurons (and supporting glial cells). Dendrites carry impulses towards the cell body and axons carry them away from it, so (i), (ii) and (iii) are true. The myelin sheath speeds conduction along the axon by saltatory conduction between the nodes of Ranvier; it has nothing to do with crossing the synapse, so (iv) is false. **Answer: A.**

**28.** In enzyme activity the molecule NADP can be considered as

(i) a prosthetic group.

(ii) a cofactor.

(iii) a coenzyme.

(v) an activator.

*Options as printed:* A) (i), (ii) and (iii) are correct.   B) (i) and (iii) are correct.   C) (ii) and (iv) are correct.   D) only (iv) is correct.

NADP is a non-protein organic molecule that carries hydrogen and is loosely bound to dehydrogenase enzymes. It is therefore a coenzyme, and a coenzyme is a type of cofactor, so (ii) and (iii) are correct. It is not a tightly bound prosthetic group and it is not an inorganic activator. None of the four printed combinations contains exactly (ii) and (iii) (the option containing both, A, also includes (i)), and the fourth statement is printed '(v)'. The question is left open for self-assessment. The expected answer is: (ii) and (iii), NADP is a coenzyme and therefore also a cofactor.

**29.** In mice the dominant allele B determines black coat colour. Brown coat colour results from a recessive allele b. The dominant allele N determines hair which grows straight. Wavy hair is caused by the recessive allele n. What will be the genotype of the $F_1$ generation from a cross between a black wavy haired male and a brown straight haired female?

a) $BBNn$
b) $Bbnn$
c) $BbNn$
d) $bbnn$

The question does not state the parents' genotypes, so true-breeding (homozygous) parents are assumed. Black wavy male: $BBnn$; brown straight female: $bbNN$. Gametes: male $Bn$ only, female $bN$ only. Every $F_1$ mouse is $BbNn$ (black coat, straight hair). The other options cannot arise from these parents: $BBNn$ needs two B alleles from the female, and $Bbnn$ and $bbnn$ need an n allele from the female. **Answer: C.**

**30.** One of the differences between $\mathrm{C_3}$ and $\mathrm{C_4}$ plants is that

a) $\mathrm{C_3}$ plants have two types of chloroplast.
b) $\mathrm{C_4}$ plants carry out photorespiration.
c) $\mathrm{C_4}$ plants carry out double fixation of carbon dioxide.
d) $\mathrm{C_3}$ plants are found in temperate regions.

$\mathrm{C_4}$ plants fix carbon dioxide twice: first in the mesophyll cells by PEP carboxylase giving a four-carbon acid, and then again in the bundle sheath cells, where the $\mathrm{CO_2}$ released is fixed by rubisco in the Calvin cycle. $\mathrm{C_3}$ plants have only one type of chloroplast, so A is wrong; photorespiration is negligible in $\mathrm{C_4}$ plants and occurs in $\mathrm{C_3}$ plants, so B is wrong; and where the plants grow (D) is a distribution, not a biochemical difference between the two groups. **Answer: C.**

**31.** The act of concentration of urine was found to decrease shortly after a person had drunk a glass of distilled water. This is because

a) less salt is excreted in the urine.
b) more water is excreted in the urine.
c) there is a drop in the water potential of the blood.
d) more ADH released into the blood.

Drinking distilled water raises the water potential of the blood plasma. The osmoreceptors in the hypothalamus detect this, less ADH is released, the collecting ducts become less permeable to water, and so a large volume of dilute urine is produced: more water is excreted in the urine. Option C is the opposite of what happens (the water potential of the blood rises), option D is wrong because less ADH, not more, is released, and option A is not the main cause. **Answer: B.**

**32.** The water content of the mammalian blood is regulated by antidiuretic hormone (ADH). In which part of the nephron does this regulation occur?

a) The ascending limb of the loop of Henle.
b) The collecting duct.
c) The descending limb of the loop of Henle.
d) The proximal convoluted tubule.

ADH makes the distal convoluted tubule and above all the collecting duct more permeable to water by inserting aquaporins in their cells, so more water is reabsorbed by osmosis into the hyperosmotic medulla. Of the options given, the collecting duct is the part of the nephron where this regulation occurs. The loop of Henle creates the concentration gradient but is not controlled by ADH, and the proximal tubule reabsorbs a fixed fraction of water. **Answer: B.**

**33.** At which rate of reaction of the maximum velocity can the Michaelis-Menten constant be obtained?

a) the rate of reaction is 25% of its maximum velocity.
b) the rate of reaction is 50% of its maximum velocity.
c) the rate of reaction is 75% of its maximum velocity.
d) the rate of reaction is 90% of its maximum velocity.

The Michaelis-Menten constant $K_m$ is defined as the substrate concentration at which the reaction rate is half of the maximum velocity: $v = \tfrac{1}{2}V_{max}$. So $K_m$ is read from the graph at a rate of 50% of $V_{max}$. **Answer: B.**

**34.** Which of the following mammalian glands is an exocrine gland?

a) Thyroid gland
b) Mammary gland
c) Adrenal gland
d) Ovary and testis

An exocrine gland releases its secretion through a duct. The mammary gland secretes milk through ducts to the nipple. The thyroid and adrenal glands are purely endocrine (they secrete hormones into the blood), and the ovary and testis are mixed glands (they produce both gametes and hormones). **Answer: B.**

**35.** The cascade effect describes a situation where:

a) the secretion of a hormone is in response to the presence of another hormone.
b) the presence of a particular hormone stops the activity of other hormones.
c) hormones perform synergistic actions.
d) hormones act on similar gland.

In a hormonal cascade, one hormone stimulates the secretion of the next (for example the hypothalamic releasing hormone stimulates the pituitary, which secretes a tropic hormone that stimulates a target gland), so the secretion of a hormone is a response to the presence of another hormone. Inhibition of other hormones, synergism and action on similar glands are different ideas. **Answer: A.**

**36.** Blood flow through capillaries is slow because

a) blood volume is reduced from the capillaries.
b) the pressure in the venules is high.
c) the total cross sectional area of the capillaries is larger than that of the arteries.
d) the osmotic pressure in the capillaries is very high.

Each artery divides into very many capillaries, so the total cross-sectional area of the capillary bed is much larger than that of the arteries that feed it. For a given volume of blood per second, a larger total cross-sectional area means a lower velocity, which gives time for exchange of materials between blood and tissues. The pressure in the venules is low, and the blood volume is not reduced from the capillaries. **Answer: C.**

**37.** Which of these animals have a common ancestry based on possession of similar bones in upper arm?

*Options as printed:* A) Bat, bird, whale, humans.   B) Bat, whale, horse, humans.   C) Bird, whale, bat, fox.   D) Bird, bat, whale, horse.

Similar bones in the forelimb (humerus, radius and ulna, carpals, metacarpals and phalanges) show homologous structures, which point to common ancestry. However, all the animals named in the options (bat, bird, whale, horse, human, fox) are tetrapods whose forelimbs are homologous, so every printed option is correct in principle and the question does not allow a single answer to be chosen. The question is left open for self-assessment. The expected answer: animals with a pentadactyl-derived forelimb (for example bat, whale and humans) share common ancestry through homologous limb bones, and every option listed contains only such animals.

**38.** What will be the likely consequence if the enzyme pepsin was to be produced in an active form in the zymogen cells?

a) Pepsin will digest the cell protein.
b) Pepsin will split nucleoprotein into nucleic acids and protein.
c) Pepsin will digest more proteins.
d) Pepsin will be inactivated in the stomach.

Pepsin is made as inactive pepsinogen so that it cannot attack the cells that make it. If it were made in its active form in the zymogen (chief) cells, it would digest the proteins of those cells and damage the gastric glands, as in ulcer formation. It does not split nucleoproteins specifically, and it would not be inactivated in the stomach because it works best in the acid pH of the stomach. **Answer: A.**

**39.** The volume of air taken in during inspiration which does not take part in gaseous exchange is known as

a) residual volume.
b) inspiratory reserve volume.
c) Vital capacity.
d) dead space air.

Dead space air is the air that fills the trachea, bronchi and bronchioles (about 150 $\mathrm{cm^3}$) and never reaches the alveoli, so it takes no part in gaseous exchange. Residual volume stays in the lungs after a forced expiration, the inspiratory reserve volume is the extra air that can be breathed in by effort, and the vital capacity is the maximum volume that can be exchanged in one breath. **Answer: D.**

**40.** Which of the following will usually contain blood with the lowest amount of oxygen?

a) The left ventricle.
b) The left atrium.
c) The pulmonary veins.
d) The pulmonary arteries.

The pulmonary arteries carry deoxygenated blood from the right ventricle to the lungs, so they hold the blood with the least oxygen. The left ventricle, the left atrium and the pulmonary veins all contain oxygenated blood returning from the lungs. **Answer: D.**

**41.** What are the phenotypes of the parents of a haemophiliac son and a normal daughter?

| | Father | Mother |
|---|---|---|
| A | Carrier | Normal |
| B | Haemophiliac | Carrier |
| C | Haemophiliac | Haemophiliac |
| D | Normal | Carrier |

Haemophilia is X-linked recessive ($X^hY$ son, $X^hX^h$ affected daughter). The haemophiliac son must receive $X^h$ from his mother, so the mother is a carrier ($X^HX^h$) or haemophiliac. A father cannot be a 'carrier' (males have one X), so A is impossible. In C both parents are haemophiliac and every daughter would be haemophiliac, so C is impossible. Both B (father $X^hY$, mother $X^HX^h$, normal daughter $X^HX^h$ carrier) and D (father $X^HY$, mother $X^HX^h$, normal daughter $X^HX^H$ or $X^HX^h$) are genetically possible, and the question does not give enough information to choose between them. The question is left open for self-assessment. The expected answer is D (normal father, carrier mother), the most likely, with B also possible.

**First statement:** Asexual reproduction is a very fast process and produces offspring that are identical to the parents.

**Second statement:** Asexual reproduction results in variation.

a) Both statements are true and the second explains the first.
b) Both statements are true but the second does not explain the first.
c) The first statement is true and the second is false.
d) The first statement is false and the second is true.

The first statement is true: asexual reproduction is rapid and the offspring are genetically identical clones of the single parent. The second statement is false: because there is no meiosis, no gamete fusion and no gene shuffling, asexual reproduction produces no variation (apart from rare mutations). **Answer: C.**

**First statement:** Relative growth rate curves compare growth rate at a given time against the original measurement as a percentage.

**Second statement:** If a ten year old boy and a thirty year old man both increase 2 cm in height in one month, the ten year old boy has a higher relative growth rate.

a) Both statements are true and the second explains the first.
b) Both statements are true but the second does not explain the first.
c) The first statement is true and the second is false.
d) The first statement is false and the second is true.

Both statements are true. Relative growth rate is the increase expressed as a percentage of the size at the start. The boy is shorter than the man, so the same 2 cm increase is a larger percentage of his original height (for example about 1.4% of 140 cm compared with about 1.1% of 175 cm). The second statement is an example that illustrates and explains why the original measurement matters in the first. **Answer: A.**

**First statement:** In meiotic cell division the offspring produced have different genetic contents.

**Second statement:** During mitotic division sister chromatids move while in meiosis whole chromosomes move.

a) Both statements are true and the second explains the first.
b) Both statements are true but the second does not explain the first.
c) The first statement is true and the second is false.
d) The first statement is false and the second is true.

The first statement is true: meiosis produces genetically different cells through crossing over and independent assortment. The second is also broadly true: in mitosis the sister chromatids of each chromosome separate at anaphase, whereas in anaphase I of meiosis whole homologous chromosomes (each still of two chromatids) move to opposite poles. However this is only a description of how the chromosomes move; the genetic variation is explained mainly by crossing over and the random assortment of homologues, so the second statement is not a complete explanation of the first. Both true, second does not explain the first. **Answer: B.**

**First statement:** Antipodal cells are found in the chalaza end of the embryo sac mother cell.

**Second statement:** Polar nuclei are also most often found in the chalaza end of the embryo sac mother cells.

a) Both statements are true and the second explains the first.
b) Both statements are true but the second does not explain the first.
c) The first statement is true and the second is false.
d) The first statement is false and the second is true.

The first statement is true: the three antipodal cells lie at the chalazal end of the embryo sac, opposite the micropyle (the printed 'embryo sac mother cell' is taken to mean the embryo sac). The second is false: the two polar nuclei lie close together in the centre of the embryo sac (they fuse to form the endosperm nucleus), while the egg cell and synergids are at the micropylar end. **Answer: C.**

**First statement:** Pure water has the lowest water potential value of zero.

**Second statement:** Dissolving solutes lower the water potential of pure water.

a) Both statements are true and the second explains the first.
b) Both statements are true but the second does not explain the first.
c) The first statement is true and the second is false.
d) The first statement is false and the second is true.

The first statement is false: pure water has the highest water potential, which is defined as zero; all solutions have negative values. The second statement is true: dissolving solutes lowers (makes more negative) the water potential of pure water. **Answer: D.**

**First statement:** Suckling actions by a baby help in ovulation.

**Second statement:** Suckling actions prevent the release of FSH and LH.

a) Both statements are true and the second explains the first.
b) Both statements are true but the second does not explain the first.
c) The first statement is true and the second is false.
d) The first statement is false and the second is true.

The first statement is false: suckling stimulates prolactin secretion, which inhibits the release of FSH and LH, so ovulation is delayed (lactational amenorrhoea) and not helped. The second statement is true. **Answer: D.**

**First statement:** A hormone originating in the terminal buds of plants suppresses the growth of lateral buds.

**Second statement:** Plant hormones may promote or inhibit growth.

a) Both statements are true and the second explains the first.
b) Both statements are true but the second does not explain the first.
c) The first statement is true and the second is false.
d) The first statement is false and the second is true.

Both statements are true. Auxin (IAA) made in the terminal bud suppresses the lateral buds (apical dominance). This is a specific case of the general fact in the second statement that plant hormones can inhibit growth in some tissues while promoting it in others, so the second statement explains the first. **Answer: A.**

**First statement:** Ciliated epithelium is associated with goblet cells which secrete mucus in which cilia set up currents.

**Second statement:** Epithelia that line various ducts e.g. oviduct generate ciliary currents which propel the zygote to the uterus.

a) Both statements are true and the second explains the first.
b) Both statements are true but the second does not explain the first.
c) The first statement is true and the second is false.
d) The first statement is false and the second is true.

Both statements are true. Ciliated epithelium has goblet cells whose mucus is moved by the beating cilia, for example in the trachea. The oviduct lining also has cilia that waft the ovum or zygote towards the uterus. The second is a separate example of ciliary currents and does not explain why the cilia and goblet cells are associated, so the second does not explain the first. **Answer: B.**

**First statement:** Lysosomes are vesicles from a golgi apparatus that contain enzymes.

**Second statement:** Lysosomes break down food, cellular debris and foreign invaders such as bacteria.

a) Both statements are true and the second explains the first.
b) Both statements are true but the second does not explain the first.
c) The first statement is true and the second is false.
d) The first statement is false and the second is true.

Both statements are true. Lysosomes are vesicles budded from the Golgi apparatus that contain hydrolytic (digestive) enzymes. It is these enzymes that digest food particles, worn-out organelles and engulfed bacteria, so the second statement follows from the first and explains the role of the contents. **Answer: A.**
