**9.** During human development, which part of the blastocyst will develop into a foetus?

a) Morula.
b) Trophoblast.
c) Chorion.
d) Inner cell mass.

The blastocyst has an outer layer, the trophoblast, which forms the chorion and the foetal part of the placenta, and an inner cell mass (embryoblast) which gives the embryo and then the foetus. The morula is the earlier solid ball of cells, not a part of the blastocyst. **Answer: D.**

**11.** The hormone which promotes the ripening of fruits is

a) Abscisic acid.
b) Cytokinins.
c) Ethylene.
d) Gibberellins.

Ethylene is a gaseous plant hormone that stimulates the ripening of fruits (and leaf fall). Abscisic acid promotes dormancy and stomatal closure, cytokinins promote cell division and delay senescence, and gibberellins promote stem elongation and seed germination. **Answer: C.**

**12.** Which of the following correctly describes plasmids?

a) They are composed only of RNA.
b) They are composed of RNA and protein.
c) They are DNA segments in chromosomes of bacteria.
d) Small circular piece of DNA located in the cytoplasm of many bacteria.

A plasmid is a small, circular, double-stranded DNA molecule, separate from the main bacterial chromosome, found in the cytoplasm of many bacteria. It replicates independently and often carries genes for antibiotic resistance, which is why it is used as a vector in genetic engineering. Plasmids are made of DNA, not RNA or protein, and are outside the bacterial chromosome. **Answer: D.**

**13.** According to the Hardy-Weinberg principle, allele frequency in a randomly mating population will

a) increase with the growth of the population.
b) decrease with the increase in the population.
c) change when birth rate exceeds death rate.
d) remain constant.

The Hardy-Weinberg principle states that in a large, randomly mating population with no mutation, migration or selection, allele and genotype frequencies remain constant from generation to generation. Population size and birth or death rates do not change allele frequencies by themselves. **Answer: D.**

**14.** The period of human gestation is divided into three trimesters (stages). Which of the following events is correctly matched to its trimester of occurrence?

a) Development and differentiation characterize the third trimester.
b) The greatest growth in size occurs in the first trimester.
c) The limb buds develop in the first trimester.
d) Organ development develops in the second trimester.

The limb buds appear at about the fourth to fifth week, in the first trimester, which is the period of development and differentiation of the organs (organogenesis). The greatest growth in size occurs in the third trimester, and in the second trimester the organs mature and the foetus grows. So only C is correctly matched. **Answer: C.**

**15.** When you bend your arm, the bulge seen at your elbow is part of the

a) humerus.
b) ulna.
c) radius.
d) carpel.

The point of the elbow that sticks out when the arm is bent is the olecranon process, the upper end of the ulna, which forms the hinge joint with the humerus. The radius lies on the thumb side of the forearm, and a carpel is part of a flower (the carpals are wrist bones). The humerus also takes part in the joint, but the bulge itself is the olecranon of the ulna. **Answer: B.**

**18.** The exchange of materials across membranes is/are

(i) to obtain nutrients.

(ii) to excrete waste substances.

(iii) to maintain a suitable pH and ionic concentration.

(iv) to transmit impulses across synapses.

a) (i), (ii) and (iii) are correct.
b) (i) and (iii) are correct.
c) (ii) and (iv) are correct.
d) only (iv) is correct.

Exchange across cell membranes lets the cell take in nutrients (i), get rid of wastes (ii) and keep a suitable pH and ionic concentration (iii). The transmission of an impulse across a synapse is done by the diffusion of a neurotransmitter across the synaptic cleft rather than by an exchange of materials across a membrane, so (iv) is not retained. **Answer: A.**

**19.** Which of the following characteristics does an endocrine gland have?

(i) It has a rich supply of blood with a relatively large number of blood vessels.

(ii) It secretes its products into a duct.

(iii) It secretes chemicals called hormones.

(iv) It is effective at high concentrations.

a) (i), (ii) and (iii) are correct.
b) (i) and (iii) are correct.
c) (ii) and (iv) are correct.
d) only (iv) is correct.

An endocrine gland is richly supplied with blood so that its hormones enter the blood quickly (i), and it secretes hormones (iii). It is ductless, so (ii) is wrong (that describes an exocrine gland), and hormones are effective at very low concentrations, so (iv) is wrong. **Answer: B.**

**20.** Which of the following does DNA replication require?

(i) DNA polymerase.

(ii) Deoxyribonucleotides.

(iii) DNA helicase.

(iv) RNA polymerase.

a) (i), (ii) and (iii) are correct.
b) (i) and (iii) are correct.
c) (ii) and (iv) are correct.
d) only (iv) is correct.

Replication needs DNA polymerase to join the nucleotides (i), deoxyribonucleotides as building blocks (ii) and helicase to unwind the double helix (iii). RNA polymerase is the enzyme of transcription, so (iv) is not required (the short RNA primers are made by primase, a special RNA polymerase, which is outside the usual syllabus answer). **Answer: A.**

**21.** The following mechanisms will favour cross pollination?

(i) Dichogamy.

(ii) Cleistogamy.

(iii) Self sterility.

(iv) Homogamy.

a) (i), (ii) and (iii) are correct.
b) (i) and (iii) are correct.
c) (ii) and (iv) are correct.
d) only (iv) is correct.

Dichogamy (anthers and stigma ripening at different times) and self-sterility (pollen cannot fertilise the ovules of the same plant) both prevent self-pollination, so they favour cross-pollination. Cleistogamy (flowers that never open) and homogamy (anthers and stigma ripening together) favour self-pollination. Statements (i) and (iii) are correct. **Answer: B.**

**22.** Which of the following statement is/are true of the mammalian liver?

(i) It is supplied by only one artery.

(ii) It detoxifies toxins that enter the blood from the gut.

(iii) It produces insulin that reduces blood glucose.

(iv) It is the largest organ of the body.

*Options as printed:* A) (i), (ii) and (iii) are correct.   B) (i) and (iii) are correct.   C) (ii) and (iv) are correct.   D) only (iv) is correct.

The liver detoxifies harmful substances absorbed from the gut and carried by the hepatic portal vein, so (ii) is true. Insulin is made by the beta cells of the pancreas, so (iii) is false. The liver receives blood from the hepatic artery and from the hepatic portal vein, so (i) is misleading, and it is the largest internal organ (the skin is the largest organ of the body), so (iv) is true only in a restricted sense.

**Intended answer: strictly only (ii) is correct; this is not offered, the nearest printed options being C (if the liver is taken as the largest organ) or none.**

**23.** Allometric growth can be defined as

(i) a type of growth pattern seen in fish and certain insects such as locust.

(ii) growth in which the organism grow at the same rate as the rest of the body.

(iii) growth in which the relative proportions of the organs and the whole body remain the same.

(iv) growth in which the organs grow at different rates from the rest of the body.

a) (i), (ii) and (iii) are correct.
b) (i) and (iii) are correct.
c) (ii) and (iv) are correct.
d) only (iv) is correct.

In allometric growth different parts or organs grow at different rates from the rest of the body, so the body proportions change during development (as in humans, whose head grows relatively slowly). Statements (ii) and (iii) describe isometric growth, and (i) describes the isometric pattern of fish and locusts. Only (iv) is correct. **Answer: D.**

**24.** In enzyme activity, the molecule NADP can be considered as

(i) an apoenzyme.

(ii) a cofactor.

(iii) an activator.

(iv) a coenzyme.

a) (i), (ii) and (iii) are correct.
b) (i) and (iii) are correct.
c) (ii) and (iv) are correct.
d) only (iv) is correct.

NADP is a non-protein organic molecule that carries hydrogen and electrons for dehydrogenase enzymes, so it is a coenzyme (iv), and a coenzyme is a type of cofactor (ii). It is not the protein part (apoenzyme) and it is not an activator (an activator is usually an inorganic ion such as Cl-). **Answer: C.**

**25.** During photosynthesis, the light dependent reactions will

(i) take place in the stroma.

(ii) occur in a cycle divided into phases.

(iii) use ATP and reduced NADP.

(iv) not need enzymes for proper functioning.

*Options as printed:* A) (i), (ii) and (iii) are correct.   B) (i) and (iii) are correct.   C) (ii) and (iv) are correct.   D) only (iv) is correct.

The light-dependent reactions take place in the thylakoid membranes and grana, not in the stroma, so (i) is wrong. They are not a cycle divided into phases (that describes the Calvin cycle), so (ii) is wrong. They produce ATP and reduced NADP, which are used by the light-independent reactions, so (iii) is wrong as printed (the stem probably meant 'use ADP and NADP'). They need enzymes such as ATP synthase, so (iv) is wrong.

**Intended answer: none of the printed statements is correct as printed.**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

**26.** The sertoli cells play which of the following role(s) in the testes?

(i) They undergo first and second meiotic division to form sperms.

(ii) They remould sperms to form spermatids.

(iii) They transport sperms from testis to penis.

(iv) They exchange nutrients and wastes between sperm and blood.

*Options as printed:* A) (i), (ii) and (iii) are correct.   B) (i) and (iii) are correct.   C) (ii) and (iv) are correct.   D) only (iv) is correct.

Sertoli (nurse) cells in the seminiferous tubules nourish the developing sperm cells and exchange nutrients and wastes between them and the blood (iv), and they help the transformation of spermatids into spermatozoa (spermiogenesis). Statement (ii) is printed the wrong way round ('remould sperms to form spermatids'): taken literally it is false. They do not undergo meiosis (that is done by the spermatocytes) and they do not transport sperms to the penis.

**Intended answer: (ii) as meant (spermatids remoulded into sperms) and (iv), that is option C.**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

**27.** Which of the following statements apply to members of the class Aves?

(i) They have feathers.

(ii) They excrete urea.

(iii) They are homoeothermic.

(iv) They are poikilothermic.

a) (i), (ii) and (iii) are correct.
b) (i) and (iii) are correct.
c) (ii) and (iv) are correct.
d) only (iv) is correct.

Birds have feathers (i) and are homoeothermic (warm-blooded, constant body temperature) (iii). They excrete uric acid, not urea, and they are not poikilothermic. Statements (i) and (iii) are correct. **Answer: B.**

**28.** An "ecological niche" can be defined as

a) the place where an organism lives.
b) a group of individuals living together.
c) the role an organism plays in an ecosystem.
d) the type of food an organism feeds on in an ecosystem.

The niche is the functional role of an organism in its ecosystem: its feeding, its relations with other organisms and its use of the environment. The place where it lives is its habitat, a group of individuals living together is a population, and food is only one aspect of the niche. **Answer: C.**

**29.** Which of the following communities tend to produce more organic material than it uses?

a) The shrub community.
b) The herb community.
c) The pine community.
d) The dense shrub community.

A young, pioneer community such as the herb community (early in succession) has a gross production greater than its respiration, so it accumulates organic material (net production is positive) and grows quickly. In older, more mature communities (shrub, pine, dense shrub) the respiration of the many consumers and of the large mass of plant tissue rises until production and use are almost equal. The herb community is the earliest stage listed. **Answer: B.**

**30.** In which of the following habitats would it be most likely to find an animal which maintains a constant body temperature, excretes urea, has a large surface area in proportion to its volume and long kidney tubules?

a) A tropical fresh water.
b) A tropical terrestrial.
c) A temperate terrestrial.
d) A temperate freshwater.

A constant body temperature and urea excretion point to a mammal. A large surface area to volume ratio helps to lose heat, which is an advantage in a hot (tropical) climate and a disadvantage in a cold one, and long kidney tubules (loops of Henle) reabsorb water, which is needed on land where water is scarce. All these features fit a tropical terrestrial habitat. **Answer: B.**

**31.** The following is an example of discontinuous variation in humans

a) Height.
b) Skin colour.
c) Haemophilia.
d) Weight.

Discontinuous variation has distinct classes with no intermediates and is controlled by one or few genes with little environmental effect: haemophilia is either present or absent. Height, skin colour and weight show a range of values (continuous variation) controlled by many genes and influenced by the environment. **Answer: C.**

**First statement:** The cytoplasm cells are generally not isolated from one another.

**Second statement:** The cellulose cell wall is interrupted at intervals by plasmodesmata.

a) Both statements are true and the second explains the first.
b) Both statements are true but the second does not explain the first.
c) The first statement is true and the second is false.
d) The first statement is false and the second is true.

Both statements are true. Plasmodesmata are narrow cytoplasmic channels passing through gaps in the cellulose cell wall, which connect the cytoplasm of neighbouring plant cells, so the second statement explains why the cytoplasm of the cells is not isolated. **Answer: A.**

**First statement:** Ruminants chew the cud or ruminate.

**Second statement:** The diastema helps ruminants chew grass by keeping grass freshly cropped from that being chewed.

a) Both statements are true and the second explains the first.
b) Both statements are true but the second does not explain the first.
c) The first statement is true and the second is false.
d) The first statement is false and the second is true.

Ruminants regurgitate food from the rumen and chew it again (chewing the cud), so the first statement is true. The diastema is the gap between the lower incisors and the premolars, which lets the tongue move the freshly cropped grass separately from the food being chewed, so the second is also true. The diastema does not explain why the cud is chewed (this is to break down cellulose-rich food further), so the second does not explain the first. **Answer: B.**

**First statement:** Nematodes have a coelom.

**Second statement:** Nematodes are triploblastic.

a) Both statements are true and the second explains the first.
b) Both statements are true but the second does not explain the first.
c) The first statement is true and the second is false.
d) The first statement is false and the second is true.

Nematodes have a pseudocoelom (a body cavity not completely lined by mesoderm), not a true coelom, so the first statement is false. They have three germ layers (ectoderm, mesoderm and endoderm), so they are triploblastic and the second statement is true. **Answer: D.**

**First statement:** As opposed to pyramid of numbers, pyramid of energy is never inverted.

**Second statement:** Only about 10% of energy flows from a lower trophic level to a higher trophic level.

a) Both statements are true and the second explains the first.
b) Both statements are true but the second does not explain the first.
c) The first statement is true and the second is false.
d) The first statement is false and the second is true.

Both statements are true. Only about 10 % of the energy passes from one trophic level to the next (the rest is lost as heat, in excreta and in uneaten parts), so the energy available always decreases up the chain and the pyramid of energy is always upright, whereas pyramids of numbers can be inverted. The second statement explains the first. **Answer: A.**

**First statement:** With "fed-batch" culture, the period of growth is extended by adding nutrients at high concentration during fermentation.

**Second statement:** With "fed-batch" culture, rate of growth can be regulated to keep pace with the rate at which oxygen can be supplied.

a) Both statements are true and the second explains the first.
b) Both statements are true but the second does not explain the first.
c) The first statement is true and the second is false.
d) The first statement is false and the second is true.

In fed-batch culture a concentrated nutrient is added gradually during the run, which prolongs the growth period, so the first statement is true. By controlling the rate of feeding, the growth rate can be held at the level at which the oxygen supply can meet the demand, so the second statement is also true. The second describes a way of controlling growth, not the reason why growth is prolonged, so it does not explain the first. **Answer: B.**

**First statement:** During manipulation of a gene, a plasmid may be used as a vector.

**Second statement:** A plasmid contains extra DNA.

a) Both statements are true and the second explains the first.
b) Both statements are true but the second does not explain the first.
c) The first statement is true and the second is false.
d) The first statement is false and the second is true.

A plasmid can be used as a vector to carry a foreign gene into a bacterium, so the first statement is true. A plasmid is extra-chromosomal DNA, so the second is true. The reason why plasmids are good vectors is that they are small, circular, replicate independently and can be cut and joined with enzymes, not just that they hold extra DNA, so the second does not explain the first. **Answer: B.**

**First statement:** Parthenogenesis is a form of asexual reproduction.

**Second statement:** Parthenogenesis involves gamete formation.

a) Both statements are true and the second explains the first.
b) Both statements are true but the second does not explain the first.
c) The first statement is true and the second is false.
d) The first statement is false and the second is true.

Parthenogenesis is the development of an unfertilised egg into a new individual without fusion of gametes, and it is usually classed as asexual (or modified sexual) reproduction, so the first statement is retained as true. The egg is a gamete formed by the female, so the second statement is true. As the second does not explain why it is asexual (no fertilisation takes place), it does not explain the first. **Answer: B.**

**39.** The following pairs represent an analogous evolutionary feature.

a) Elephant tusks and human incisors.
b) Insect wing and bat wing.
c) Teleost erythrocyte and mammalian erythrocyte.
d) Mole forelimb and bird wing.

Analogous structures have the same function but a different origin and structure. The wing of an insect (a fold of the cuticle) and the wing of a bat (modified forelimb with skin membrane) are used for flight but have different origins. The other pairs are homologous: tusks and incisors are both teeth, the two erythrocytes are the same kind of cell, and the forelimb of a mole and the wing of a bird share the pentadactyl plan. **Answer: B.**

**40.** Gonadotrophic hormones include:

a) Oestrogen and progesterone.
b) Oestrogen, progesterone and testosterone.
c) Luteinizing hormone and testosterone.
d) Luteinizing hormone and follicle stimulating hormone.

Gonadotrophic hormones are those released by the anterior pituitary gland which act on the gonads: luteinizing hormone (LH) and follicle stimulating hormone (FSH). Oestrogen, progesterone and testosterone are sex hormones made by the gonads themselves. **Answer: D.**

**41.** The most immediate effect on FSH synthesis is a

a) rise in progesterone.
b) fall in progesterone.
c) rise in LH.
d) fall in testosterone.

Progesterone and oestrogen exert negative feedback on the pituitary and hypothalamus, which reduces FSH secretion. When the corpus luteum degenerates at the end of the cycle, the level of progesterone falls, the inhibition ends and FSH synthesis rises immediately. A rise in progesterone would reduce FSH, and LH and testosterone are not the immediate cause in the female cycle. **Answer: B.**

**42.** Which of these is a characteristic of hormones?

a) A large quantity is needed to produce a desired effect.
b) They are produced in the tissue that they effect.
c) Small quantities can produce effects.
d) They work independently from other hormones.

Hormones are effective in very small quantities. They are carried by the blood to target tissues away from where they are made, and they often work together or in antagonism with other hormones. **Answer: C.**

**43.** The group of organisms that contributes to the primary productivity of an ecosystem is:

a) Algae.
b) Protozoans.
c) Bacteria.
d) Fungi.

Primary productivity is the production of organic matter from inorganic substances by photosynthesis. Algae are photosynthetic producers, whereas protozoans are consumers and bacteria and fungi are mostly decomposers (a few bacteria are photosynthetic or chemosynthetic, but algae are the group that is clearly a producer). **Answer: A.**

**44.** In which of the following natural areas or situations might nitrification be favoured?

a) Anywhere there is insufficient oxygen for decomposition of all accumulated organic matter.
b) Anywhere there is sufficient oxygen for decomposition of all accumulated organic matter.
c) Anywhere there is sufficient carbon dioxide for decomposition of all accumulated organic matter.
d) Anywhere there is insufficient carbon dioxide for combustion of all accumulated inorganic matter.

Nitrification (ammonium to nitrite by *Nitrosomonas*, then to nitrate by *Nitrobacter*) is done by aerobic bacteria and is favoured where there is enough oxygen, for example in well aerated, well drained soil where organic matter is fully decomposed. Where oxygen is lacking (waterlogged soil), denitrification is favoured instead. Carbon dioxide is not the limiting factor. **Answer: B.**

**45.** A drug that inhibits excretion of bicarbonate will cause the blood to become:

a) acidic.
b) alkaline.
c) first acidic and then alkaline.
d) first alkaline and then acidic.

Bicarbonate ions are the main base of the blood buffer. If their excretion by the kidney is inhibited they accumulate in the blood, which removes H+ ions and raises the pH, so the blood becomes alkaline. **Answer: B.**

**46.** The active portion of the cytochrome oxidase enzyme is a haem group. It contains a mineral element which can exist in the oxidized or reduced state. This element is

a) Sodium.
b) Potassium.
c) Iron.
d) Iodine.

The haem group contains iron, which changes between Fe2+ (reduced) and Fe3+ (oxidized) when cytochrome oxidase passes electrons to oxygen in the last step of the electron transport chain. Sodium and potassium are not found in haem and iodine is a component of thyroxine. **Answer: C.**

**47.** The enzyme acetylcholinesterase which hydrolyses acetylcholine to choline is at;  at

*Options as printed:* A) postsynaptic membrane.   B) presynaptic membrane.   C) Presynaptic cleft.   D) Neuromuscular junction.

Acetylcholinesterase breaks down acetylcholine into choline and acetate in the synaptic cleft and on the surface of the postsynaptic membrane, so that the transmission stops. 'Presynaptic cleft' is not a correct term (the gap is the synaptic cleft) and the neuromuscular junction is also a place where the enzyme works.

**Intended answer: A (postsynaptic membrane).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

**48.** The role of RNA polymerase is to

a) bind ribonucleotides together during translation.
b) bind ribonucleotides together during transcription.
c) break down RNA during digestion.
d) add ribosomes during translation.

RNA polymerase attaches to the promoter of a gene and joins ribonucleotides complementary to the DNA template strand to make RNA, which is transcription. Translation (making a polypeptide on the ribosome) does not need RNA polymerase, and RNA is broken down by ribonuclease, not RNA polymerase. **Answer: B.**

**49.** The volume of air taken in during inspiration which does not take part in gaseous exchange is known as

a) residual volume.
b) inspiratory reserve volume.
c) expiratory reserve volume.
d) dead space air.

The dead space air is the air that stays in the trachea, bronchi and bronchioles, where no gaseous exchange occurs (about 150 cm3). Residual volume is the air left in the lungs after a maximum expiration, and the reserve volumes are extra volumes that can be breathed in or out by force. **Answer: D.**

**50.** The immunity produced when the body manufactures antibodies on exposure to an infectious agent, is known as

a) natural passive immunity.
b) artificial passive immunity.
c) natural active immunity.
d) artificial active immunity.

Active immunity means that the body makes its own antibodies (and memory cells). Here the exposure is to an infectious agent by natural infection, not by vaccination, so it is natural active immunity. Passive immunity is given as ready-made antibodies (across the placenta, in milk or by injection). **Answer: C.**

**1.** *SECTION I - directions as printed, summarised:* Each of these questions or incomplete statements is followed by four suggested answers. Select the best answer in each case.

Upon oxidation, which food sample will generate the largest amount of energy?

a) Glycogen
b) Starch
c) Fat
d) Proteins

Gram for gram, fat releases about 39 kJ on oxidation, roughly twice the energy given by carbohydrates (glycogen, starch: about 17 kJ per gram) or proteins (about 17 kJ per gram). Fat has more hydrogen and less oxygen in its molecules, so more can be oxidised. **Answer: C.**

**2.** Anaerobic respiration of yeast in a solution of sugar is known as

a) Reduction
b) Oxidation
c) Decomposition
d) Fermentation

When yeast respires without oxygen it changes sugar into ethanol and carbon dioxide with little energy released. This process is called alcoholic fermentation. Oxidation and reduction are chemical processes, and decomposition is the breakdown of dead matter. **Answer: D.**

**3.** Solar energy is converted to chemical energy by:

a) Producers
b) Herbivores
c) Decomposers
d) Consumers

Producers (green plants and algae) trap light energy with chlorophyll and store it as chemical energy in glucose and starch during photosynthesis. Herbivores, consumers and decomposers cannot do this; they obtain chemical energy from food. **Answer: A.**

**4.** Which of the following formulae represent glucose?

a) $\mathrm{C_6H_{12}O_6}$
b) $\mathrm{C_2H_5OH}$
c) $\mathrm{C_{12}H_{22}O_{11}}$
d) $\mathrm{C_{57}H_{104}O_6}$

Glucose is a monosaccharide with the formula $\mathrm{C_6H_{12}O_6}$. $\mathrm{C_2H_5OH}$ is ethanol, $\mathrm{C_{12}H_{22}O_{11}}$ is a disaccharide such as sucrose or maltose, and $\mathrm{C_{57}H_{104}O_6}$ is a fat (a triglyceride). **Answer: A.**

**5.** Both leaf cuticle and insect exoskeleton

a) Provide camouflage
b) Contain sensory cells
c) Assist in respiration
d) Reduce water loss

The waxy cuticle of a leaf and the waterproof exoskeleton of an insect are both coverings that prevent water from evaporating from the body, which is an adaptation to life on land. Neither is a sensory or respiratory structure. **Answer: D.**

**6.** Which of the following structures is a protective adaptation of the Agama lizard in a terrestrial habitat?

a) Claws
b) Gular fold
c) Scaly skin
d) Nuchal crest.

The dry scaly skin of the Agama lizard reduces water loss and protects the body from injury and drying out on land, so it is a protective adaptation to the terrestrial habitat. The claws are used for climbing, while the gular fold and the nuchal crest are mainly used in display. **Answer: C.**

**7.** The hormone insulin is produced by

a) Liver
b) Kidney
c) Stomach
d) Pancreas

Insulin is secreted by the beta cells of the islets of Langerhans in the pancreas. It lowers the blood glucose level by making the liver and muscles store glucose as glycogen. The liver stores glycogen but does not make insulin. **Answer: D.**

**9.** Where does ultra filtration take place in the kidney?

a) Glomerulus
b) Bowman's capsules
c) Proximal convoluted tubules
d) Collecting duct

Ultrafiltration occurs in the glomerulus: the blood in the glomerular capillaries is at high pressure, so water, glucose, urea and salts are forced through the capillary wall and the basement membrane into the Bowman's capsule, while blood cells and large proteins stay in the blood. The proximal tubule reabsorbs and the collecting duct adjusts the water content of the urine. **Answer: A.**

The cell body of a neuron is made of the dendrites (1) and the cytoplasm with the nucleus (2). The structures 3, 4 and 5 (the myelin sheath, a node of Ranvier and the sheath cell) belong to the axon, and 6 is the muscle fibre. Only the pair 1 and 2 describes the cell body. **Answer: B.**

**12.** Which structure in the vertical section of the mammalian eye contains a high concentration of cones?

a) Sclera
b) Fovea
c) Choroid
d) Blind spot

The fovea is the small pit in the centre of the yellow spot of the retina where cones are most concentrated, so it gives sharp, colour vision. The sclera is the tough outer layer, the choroid contains pigment and blood vessels, and the blind spot has no light receptors at all. **Answer: B.**

**13.** The diagram below represents the feeding relationship in an ecosystem. It is a pyramid with four levels: **Shark** at the top, then **Tilapia**, then **Tadpole**, and **Algae** at the bottom.

b) Tilapia

In a pyramid of energy about 90 % of the energy is lost as heat and in waste at each step, so the stored energy decreases at each higher trophic level. The shark at the top is the last consumer and has the least total energy, and the algae (producers) at the base have the most. **Answer: A.**

**15.** Which of the following is a hinge joint?

a) Knee joint
b) Shoulder joint
c) Wrist joint
d) Ankle joint

A hinge joint allows movement in one plane only, like a door hinge. The knee (and the elbow) is the standard example. The shoulder is a ball-and-socket joint and the wrist is a gliding joint. **Answer: A.**

**16.** Which part of the brain is concerned with the regulation of heart beat and breathing rate in humans?

a) Cerebellum
b) Cerebrum
c) Medulla oblongata
d) Hypothalamus

The medulla oblongata, at the base of the brain, contains the centres that control involuntary activities such as heart rate and breathing rate. The cerebellum controls balance and coordination, the cerebrum controls thought and voluntary action, and the hypothalamus controls body temperature and water balance. **Answer: C.**

**17.** The structure that separates the mammalian heart into two parts is?

a) Bicuspid valve
b) Tendon
c) Tricuspid valve
d) Septum

The septum is the thick muscular wall that divides the mammalian heart into a right and a left side and keeps oxygenated and deoxygenated blood from mixing. The valves control the direction of flow between the chambers and the tendons hold the valves. **Answer: D.**

**18.** The part of the leaf containing numerous chloroplasts is?

a) Spongy mesophyll
b) Upper epidermis
c) Palisade layer
d) Lower epidermis

The palisade layer lies just below the upper epidermis. Its tall cells are packed with chloroplasts, so most photosynthesis takes place there. The spongy mesophyll has fewer chloroplasts, and the epidermis cells have almost none (apart from the guard cells). **Answer: C.**

**19.** The structure that prevents water evaporation from the cells of the spirogyra is?

a) Cell wall
b) Mucilage
c) Cell membrane.
d) Vacuole

Spirogyra is a filamentous alga whose filaments are covered with a slimy layer of mucilage. This slippery layer holds a film of water around the cells and protects them from drying out. The cell wall and the cell membrane let water pass through, and the vacuole only stores sap. **Answer: B.**

**20.** Below is the diagram of a bread mould.

In the bread mould (Rhizopus) 1 is a stolon running over the bread, 2 is an upright stalk that carries a sporangium at its top (the sporangiophore), 3 is the sporangium and 4 are the spores released. **Answer: D.**

**21.** *SECTION III - directions as printed, summarised:* For each question, ONE or MORE of the responses is (are) correct. Decide which responses are correct, then choose: A if 1, 2 and 3 are all correct; B if 1 and 2 only are correct; C if 2 and 3 only are correct; D if 1 only is correct.

Menopause is a condition in female mammals. In this condition,

1. The female stops ovulating
2. The female can no longer become pregnant
3. The menstrual cycle continues

a) If 1, 2 and 3 are all correct.
b) If 1 and 2 only are correct.
c) If 2 and 3 only are correct.
d) If 1 only is correct.

At menopause the ovaries stop releasing eggs (1 is correct), so the woman can no longer become pregnant (2 is correct). Without ovulation and the hormones of the ovary, the menstrual cycle stops (3 is false). **Answer: B.**

**22.** Arteries differ from veins in that

1. Arteries have thick elastic walls
2. Arteries have large lumen
3. Arteries have valves

a) If 1, 2 and 3 are all correct.
b) If 1 and 2 only are correct.
c) If 2 and 3 only are correct.
d) If 1 only is correct.

Arteries carry blood at high pressure, so they have thick, elastic and muscular walls (1 is correct). Their lumen is narrow, while veins have the wide lumen (2 is false). Valves are found in veins, not in arteries (3 is false). **Answer: D.**

**23.** The structures of a plant cell absent in an animal cell:

1. Chloroplast and cell membrane
2. Chloroplast and cell wall
3. Chloroplast and starch grains

a) If 1, 2 and 3 are all correct.
b) If 1 and 2 only are correct.
c) If 2 and 3 only are correct.
d) If 1 only is correct.

Animal cells have a cell membrane, so 1 is false. Chloroplasts and the cellulose cell wall are found only in plant cells (2 is correct). Animal cells have no chloroplasts and do not store starch grains (they store glycogen), so 3 is correct. **Answer: C.**

**24.** Platelets play a role in

1. Causing haemorrhage
2. Blood clotting
3. Blocking holes in damaged capillary walls

a) If 1, 2 and 3 are all correct.
b) If 1 and 2 only are correct.
c) If 2 and 3 only are correct.
d) If 1 only is correct.

Platelets help the blood to clot at a wound (2 is correct) and also form a plug that seals small breaks in damaged capillary walls (3 is correct). They stop bleeding; they do not cause haemorrhage (1 is false). **Answer: C.**

**25.** Plasmolysis occurs when

1. The cell is placed in a hypertonic solution
2. Water is drawn from the vacuole
3. The cell is placed in a hypotonic solution

a) If 1, 2 and 3 are all correct.
b) If 1 and 2 only are correct.
c) If 2 and 3 only are correct.
d) If 1 only is correct.

In a hypertonic (more concentrated) solution water leaves the cell by osmosis, drawn from the vacuole and the cytoplasm, so the cytoplasm shrinks away from the cell wall: this is plasmolysis (1 and 2 are correct). In a hypotonic solution the cell takes in water and becomes turgid (3 is false). **Answer: B.**

**26.** *SECTION IV - directions as printed, summarised:* Each question consists of a statement in the left-hand column followed by a second statement in the right-hand column. Decide whether the first is true or false and whether the second is true or false, then choose: A if both are true and the 2nd statement is a correct explanation of the first; B if both are true and the 2nd statement is NOT a correct explanation of the first; C if the first is true and the second false; D if the first is false and the second true.

First statement: Deforestation leads to global warming.

Second statement: Lack of vegetation increases carbon dioxide concentration in the atmosphere.

a) Both statements are true and the 2nd statement is a correct explanation of the first.
b) Both statements are true and the 2nd statement is NOT a correct explanation of the first.
c) The first statement is true and the second is false.
d) The first statement is false and the second is true.

Both statements are true. Fewer trees means less carbon dioxide is removed by photosynthesis (and burning or rotting wood releases more), so carbon dioxide builds up and traps heat, which gives global warming. The second statement therefore explains the first. **Answer: A.**

**27.** First statement: Denitrification deprives plants of nitrates.

Second statement: Denitrification releases Nitrogen from the soil.

a) Both statements are true and the 2nd statement is a correct explanation of the first.
b) Both statements are true and the 2nd statement is NOT a correct explanation of the first.
c) The first statement is true and the second is false.
d) The first statement is false and the second is true.

Both statements are true. Denitrifying bacteria change nitrates in the soil into nitrogen gas, which escapes into the air. Because the nitrates are lost from the soil, plants are deprived of them, so the second statement explains the first. **Answer: A.**

**28.** First statement: Saprophytic bacteria help in the decay of dead plants and animals.

Second statement: Saprophytic bacteria reduce soil fertility.

a) Both statements are true and the 2nd statement is a correct explanation of the first.
b) Both statements are true and the 2nd statement is NOT a correct explanation of the first.
c) The first statement is true and the second is false.
d) The first statement is false and the second is true.

The first statement is true: saprophytic bacteria feed on dead matter and decompose it. The second is false: decay returns mineral salts and humus to the soil, so these bacteria increase soil fertility. **Answer: C.**

**29.** First statement: Phagocytic white blood cells contribute to body defence.

Second statement: Phagocytes engulf bacteria forming food vacuoles.

a) Both statements are true and the 2nd statement is a correct explanation of the first.
b) Both statements are true and the 2nd statement is NOT a correct explanation of the first.
c) The first statement is true and the second is false.
d) The first statement is false and the second is true.

Both statements are true. Phagocytes defend the body by engulfing and digesting bacteria: the bacterium is surrounded and enclosed in a vacuole where enzymes break it down. This is how they contribute to defence, so the second statement explains the first. **Answer: A.**

**30.** First statement: Insects undergo metamorphosis.

Second statement: The housefly undergoes incomplete metamorphosis.

a) Both statements are true and the 2nd statement is a correct explanation of the first.
b) Both statements are true and the 2nd statement is NOT a correct explanation of the first.
c) The first statement is true and the second is false.
d) The first statement is false and the second is true.

The first statement is true: insects change form during their life cycle. The second is false: the housefly goes through egg, larva, pupa and adult, which is complete metamorphosis. Incomplete metamorphosis (egg, nymph, adult) is found in grasshoppers and cockroaches. **Answer: C.**

**31.** *SECTION V - directions as printed, summarised:* Each question consists of four lettered headings A, B, C, D. Select the heading which is closely related to the description which follows.

Description: Joins DNA pieces to form recombinant DNA.

a) Restriction enzyme
b) Ligase enzyme
c) Vector
d) Clone

In genetic engineering the restriction enzyme cuts the DNA, and the ligase enzyme joins the cut pieces together to form recombinant DNA. A vector carries the DNA into a cell and a clone is a group of identical organisms or cells. **Answer: B.**

**32.** Description: A group of organisms of different species living together.

a) Population
b) Community
c) Ecosystem
d) Colony

A community is all the populations of different species living together in one habitat. A population is one species only, an ecosystem is the community together with its non-living environment, and a colony is a group of one species (such as ants or bacteria). **Answer: B.**

**33.** Description: Promotes green house effect.

a) Carbon monoxide
b) Carbon dioxide
c) Sulphur dioxide
d) Nitrogen dioxide

Carbon dioxide is the main greenhouse gas: it traps heat radiated from the earth and warms the atmosphere. Carbon monoxide is poisonous, and sulphur dioxide and nitrogen dioxide mainly cause acid rain. **Answer: B.**

**34.** Description: Loss of water vapour by plants.

a) Transpiration
b) Excretion
c) Evaporation
d) Guttation

Transpiration is the loss of water vapour from the aerial parts of a plant, mainly through the stomata. Guttation is the loss of liquid water through hydathodes, and evaporation is a physical process that is not specific to plants. **Answer: A.**

**35.** Description: Absent in adult mammals.

a) Rennin
b) Maltase
c) lactase
d) Sucrase

Rennin curdles milk protein in the stomach of a baby mammal and disappears in the adult, which uses pepsin. Maltase, lactase and sucrase are carbohydrases of the intestinal juice that are still present in adults. **Answer: A.**

**36.** Description: The functional unit of the nervous system.

a) Axon
b) Dendrite
c) Dendron
d) Neuron

The neuron (nerve cell) is the structural and functional unit of the nervous system. The axon, dendron and dendrite are only parts of a neuron. **Answer: D.**

**37.** Description: What will be the result of a cross in a homozygous tall pea plant and a heterozygous tall pea plant?

a) Heterozygous tall pea plant and homozygous dwarf pea plant.
b) Heterozygous tall pea plant.
c) Homozygous dwarf pea plant.
d) Homozygous tall pea plant and heterozygous tall pea plant.

Let T be tall and t dwarf. The cross is $TT \times Tt$. The gametes are $T$ (from $TT$) and $T$ or $t$ (from $Tt$), which gives $TT$, $TT$, $Tt$, $Tt$: half the offspring are homozygous tall and half are heterozygous tall. No dwarf plants appear because every offspring receives at least one $T$. **Answer: D.**

**38.** Description: Are antagonistic muscles.

a) Triceps and biceps
b) Striated and skeletal
c) Skeletal and smooth.
d) Smooth and striated.

Antagonistic muscles work in opposite ways: when the biceps contracts and bends the arm, the triceps relaxes, and the reverse happens to straighten it. Striated, skeletal and smooth are types of muscle tissue, not pairs that act against each other. **Answer: A.**

**39.** Description: Secretes antidiuretic hormone.

a) Salivary gland.
b) Pituitary gland.
c) Thyroid gland.
d) Adrenal gland.

Antidiuretic hormone (ADH) is made in the hypothalamus and released by the posterior pituitary gland. It makes the kidney tubules reabsorb more water. **Answer: B.**

**40.** Description: Are required for teeth and bone formation.

a) Vitamin C and Iron.
b) Vitamin D and Magnesium.
c) Vitamin D and Calcium.
d) Vitamin A and Calcium.

Calcium is the mineral that hardens bones and teeth, and vitamin D helps the intestine to absorb calcium. Lack of both causes rickets. Vitamin C prevents scurvy, iron is needed for haemoglobin, and vitamin A is needed for vision. **Answer: C.**

**41.** *SECTION VI - directions as printed, summarised:* This group of questions deals with biological situations. Each situation is followed by a set of questions. Select the best answer for each question.

Below is an experiment on photosynthesis. *(Printed diagram, described: a water plant under an inverted funnel in a beaker of water and sodium hydrogencarbonate, with a test tube above the funnel collecting the gas given off, in sunlight.)*

How can you test the gas released in this experiment?

a) It turns lime water milky
b) It has no effect on lime water
c) It is readily absorbed by pyrogallic acid.
d) It rekindles a glowing splint.

In sunlight the water plant photosynthesises and gives off oxygen, which collects in the test tube. Oxygen relights a glowing splint. Carbon dioxide would turn lime water milky, so A is wrong, and B is wrong because the gas is not carbon dioxide. Alkaline pyrogallic acid does absorb oxygen too, but it is a way of removing oxygen from a gas mixture, not the standard test for the gas; the usual test is the glowing splint. **Answer: D.**

**42.** Below is a set up for an experiment on respiration. *(Printed diagram, described: tube A holds a yeast-glucose suspension covered by a layer of paraffin oil and closed by a cork; a delivery tube carries the gas from A into a test tube B containing lime water.)*

The paraffin oil,

a) Prevents entry of atmospheric oxygen
b) Prevents entry of atmospheric nitrogen
c) Prevents evaporation of glucose suspension.
d) Prevents entry of atmospheric carbon dioxide.

The layer of oil floats on the yeast-glucose suspension and keeps air out, so the yeast respires anaerobically and the carbon dioxide it gives off turns the lime water milky. The oil therefore prevents oxygen from the atmosphere from entering. **Answer: A.**

**43.** The following results were obtained during an investigation on the action of salivary amylase on the digestion of starch.

| Temperature ($^\circ$C) | Rate of reaction |

a) 15
b) 30

The optimum temperature is the temperature at which the rate of reaction is highest. The table shows the maximum rate (52) at $37\,^\circ$C, which is body temperature. At lower temperatures the enzyme works more slowly, and at $45\,^\circ$C and above it starts to be denatured. **Answer: D.**

**44.** A seedling transplanted on a hot, windy day withers

a) Because the air is dry.
b) Because the seedling looses more water than it can absorb.
c) Because wind carries the water faster.
d) Because the roots have not adequately penetrated the soil.

On a hot, windy day transpiration is very fast. The roots of a newly transplanted seedling are damaged and cannot take up water as quickly as the leaves lose it, so the cells lose turgor and the seedling wilts. The dry air and the wind only increase the rate of loss. **Answer: B.**

**45.** A bean seedling was placed in such a way that the auxin migrated to the lower side of the root and shoot. What is the effect of the high auxin concentration on the shoot?

a) Retards growth.
b) Causes the shoot to grow toward the soil.
c) Promotes faster growth.
d) Causes the shoot to bend away from light.

In a shoot a high concentration of auxin promotes cell elongation, so the lower side grows faster and the shoot bends upwards (negative geotropism). In the root the same high concentration retards growth, which is why the root bends downwards. The shoot does not grow towards the soil, and light is not involved here. **Answer: C.**

**2.** Select the molecule which has a dative covalent bond.

a) $\mathrm{NH_3}$
b) $\mathrm{PCl_3}$
c) $\mathrm{N_2}$
d) CO

$\mathrm{NH_3}$, $\mathrm{PCl_3}$ and $\mathrm{N_2}$ only contain ordinary covalent bonds, each atom supplying one electron to every shared pair. In carbon monoxide, $\mathrm{C{\equiv}O}$ is made of two ordinary bonds plus one dative bond in which oxygen donates both electrons of the pair to carbon, so the structure is $\mathrm{C{\leftarrow}O}$ (carbon then has a complete octet). **Answer: D.**

**6.** Select the compound that has the lowest boiling point.

All four are isomeric pentanols ($\mathrm{C_5H_{11}OH}$) with hydrogen bonding through $\mathrm{-OH}$, so the difference comes from the van der Waals forces, which depend on the surface area of contact. **7.** The mass spectrum of a vaporized sample of potassium is given below. Use the information on the spectrum to calculate the relative atomic mass of potassium.

**8.** Calculate the pH of a buffer solution that is made by mixing equal volumes of $0.1\ \mathrm{mol\,dm^{-3}}$ sodium benzoate and $0.04\ \mathrm{mol\,dm^{-3}}$ benzoic acid. ($K_a$ of benzoic acid $= 6.4\times10^{-5}\ \mathrm{mol\,dm^{-3}}$)

a) $4.59$
b) $3.79$
c) $8.38$
d) $1.67$

Mixing equal volumes halves both concentrations but the ratio is unchanged: $[\mathrm{salt}]/[\mathrm{acid}] = 0.1/0.04 = 2.5$. $\mathrm{pH} = \mathrm{p}K_a + \log\dfrac{[\mathrm{salt}]}{[\mathrm{acid}]}$ with $\mathrm{p}K_a = -\log(6.4\times10^{-5}) = 4.19$, so $\mathrm{pH} = 4.19 + \log 2.5 = 4.19 + 0.40 = 4.59$. **Answer: A.**

**9.** Which of the following carboxylic acid derivatives is likely to be least reactive with respect to acid hydrolysis?

a) Ethanamide $\mathrm{CH_3CONH_2}$
b) Ethanoyl chloride $\mathrm{CH_3COCl}$
c) Ethyl ethanoate $\mathrm{CH_3COOCH_2CH_3}$
d) Ethanoic anhydride $\mathrm{(CH_3CO)_2O}$

The reactivity towards hydrolysis follows the ability of the group attached to $\mathrm{C=O}$ to leave and the electrophilicity of the carbonyl carbon: acyl chloride > acid anhydride > ester > amide. The nitrogen lone pair of the amide is delocalised into the $\mathrm{C=O}$ group, which lowers the positive charge on the carbon and makes $\mathrm{NH_2^-}$ a very poor leaving group; amides need prolonged heating with strong acid or alkali. Ethanamide is therefore the least reactive. **Answer: A.**

c) 2
d) 6

The coordination number is the number of dative bonds from the ligands to the metal ion. The ethanedioate (oxalate) ion $\mathrm{C_2O_4^{2-}}$ is a bidentate ligand (two oxygen atoms donate lone pairs), so three of them give $3 \times 2 = 6$ dative bonds. The charge check is $\mathrm{Co^{3+} + 3(2-) = 3-}$. The common mistake is to count the three ligands (option A). **Answer: D.**

**11.** Predict which of the following compounds will undergo a nucleophilic addition reaction.

a) $\mathrm{C_6H_5CH_2CH_3}$
b) $\mathrm{CH_2CH{=}CH_2}$
c) $\mathrm{CH_3CH_2CH_2Cl}$
d) $\mathrm{CH_3CH_2CHO}$

Nucleophilic addition is typical of carbonyl compounds: the $\mathrm{C=O}$ carbon is electron deficient ($\delta+$) and is attacked by a nucleophile ($\mathrm{CN^-}$, $\mathrm{H^-}$...). $\mathrm{CH_3CH_2CHO}$ (propanal) is an aldehyde. The alkene (B) undergoes electrophilic addition, the halogenoalkane (C) nucleophilic substitution and the arene (A) electrophilic substitution. **Answer: D.**

**12.** Hexane and heptane form an ideal solution. The vapour pressures of pure hexane and heptane at $25^\circ\mathrm{C}$ are $19\ \mathrm{kPa}$ and $36\ \mathrm{kPa}$ respectively. Calculate the total vapour pressure of the solution that contains $0.978$ mole of hexane and $0.364$ mole of heptane.

a) $13.85\ \mathrm{kPa}$
b) $9.76\ \mathrm{kPa}$
c) $23.61\ \mathrm{kPa}$
d) $33.37\ \mathrm{kPa}$

Mole fractions: $x_{\mathrm{hexane}} = 0.978/1.342 = 0.7288$ and $x_{\mathrm{heptane}} = 0.364/1.342 = 0.2712$. By Raoult's law $p_{\mathrm{total}} = x_1p_1^\circ + x_2p_2^\circ = (0.7288\times19) + (0.2712\times36) = 13.85 + 9.76 = 23.61\ \mathrm{kPa}$. Options A and B are the partial pressures of hexane and heptane taken separately. **Answer: C.**

**13.** In which of the following complex ions is the ligand bidentate?

a) $\mathrm{[Cu\,EDTA]^{2-}}$
b) $\mathrm{[Co(C_2O_4)_3]^{3-}}$
c) $\mathrm{[Fe(CN)_6]^{3-}}$
d) $\mathrm{[NiCl_4]^{2-}}$

A bidentate ligand forms two dative bonds. Ethanedioate (oxalate) uses two oxygen atoms, so $\mathrm{[Co(C_2O_4)_3]^{3-}}$ is the answer. EDTA is hexadentate, while $\mathrm{CN^-}$ and $\mathrm{Cl^-}$ are monodentate. **Answer: B.**

**14.** Calculate the enthalpy of formation of ethyne, CHCH, given that the enthalpies of combustion of carbon, hydrogen and ethyne (in $\mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}}$) are $-394$, $-286$ and $-1300$ respectively.

a) $+226$
b) $+620$
c) $-1980$
d) $-2374$

Target: $2\mathrm{C(s)} + \mathrm{H_2(g)} \rightarrow \mathrm{C_2H_2(g)}$. By Hess's law $\Delta H_f = 2\Delta H_c(\mathrm{C}) + \Delta H_c(\mathrm{H_2}) - \Delta H_c(\mathrm{C_2H_2}) = 2(-394) + (-286) - (-1300) = -788 - 286 + 1300 = +226\ \mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}}$. Option D, $-788-286-1300 = -2374$, adds the ethyne term instead of subtracting it. **Answer: A.**

**15.** Select the most suitable reagent and reaction conditions for the following conversion.

*Conversion as printed:* benzene $\longrightarrow$ hexabromocyclohexane (a saturated six-membered ring carrying one bromine atom on each carbon).

a) $\mathrm{Br_2}$, UV light
b) $\mathrm{Br_2}$, $\mathrm{AlCl_3}$
c) $\mathrm{Br_2}$, $\mathrm{FeBr_3}$
d) $\mathrm{Br_2}$, $\mathrm{CCl_4}$

The product contains six $\mathrm{C-Br}$ bonds on a saturated ring, so bromine has been added across all three double bonds (free radical addition), not substituted for hydrogen. This needs ultraviolet light (or strong sunlight) with excess bromine. $\mathrm{AlCl_3}$ and $\mathrm{FeBr_3}$ are halogen carriers that cause electrophilic substitution and give bromobenzene, and $\mathrm{CCl_4}$ is only a solvent in which benzene does not react. **Answer: A.**

**16.** Iodine-131 has a half-life of $8.1$ days. How much of $2\ \mathrm{g}$ of the isotope will remain after $56.7$ days?

b) $0.063\ \mathrm{g}$
c) $0.031\ \mathrm{g}$
d) $0.125\ \mathrm{g}$

Number of half-lives $= 56.7/8.1 = 7$. Remaining mass $= 2\times(\tfrac12)^7 = 2/128 = 0.0156 \approx 0.016\ \mathrm{g}$. Option B corresponds to 5 half-lives, C to 6 and D to 4. **Answer: A.**

**17.** Which of the following pairs of oxides will react with both dilute acid and alkali to form salts?

a) GeO, $\mathrm{PbO_2}$
b) CO, $\mathrm{SiO_2}$
c) $\mathrm{SnO}$, $\mathrm{CO_2}$
d) $\mathrm{SnO_2}$, SiO

Both oxides of the pair must be amphoteric. GeO and $\mathrm{PbO_2}$ are amphoteric (the monoxides of Ge, Sn, Pb and the dioxides of Sn and Pb react with acids and with alkalis). In B, CO is neutral and $\mathrm{SiO_2}$ is acidic; in C, $\mathrm{CO_2}$ is acidic; in D, SiO is not amphoteric (and $\mathrm{SiO_2}$, if that was meant, is acidic). **Answer: A.**

**18.** Give the reagents and reaction conditions for the following conversion, $\mathrm{CH_3CH_2COCl \rightarrow CH_3CH_2CH_2OH}$.

a) $\mathrm{LiAlH_4}$/dry ether
b) $\mathrm{H_2}$/Pd, $\mathrm{BaSO_4}$
c) $\mathrm{H^+/K_2Cr_2O_7}$
d) Sn/conc HCl

An acyl chloride is reduced all the way to the primary alcohol by lithium tetrahydridoaluminate(III) in dry ether, followed by dilute acid work-up. $\mathrm{H_2/Pd{-}BaSO_4}$ (Rosenmund) stops at the aldehyde, $\mathrm{K_2Cr_2O_7/H^+}$ is an oxidising agent and Sn/HCl reduces nitro compounds. **Answer: A.**

**19.** From the following reaction scheme, benzene $+$ $\mathrm{CH_3COCl}$ $\xrightarrow{\ \mathrm{FeBr_3}\ }$ phenylethanone ($\mathrm{C_6H_5COCH_3}$) $+$ HCl. When $4\ \mathrm{g}$ of ethanoyl chloride was used, $3.24\ \mathrm{g}$ of phenylethanone was obtained. Calculate the percentage yield of the reaction. ($\mathrm{C}=12$; $\mathrm{H}=1$; $\mathrm{O}=16$)

a) $65.40\%$
b) $81.00\%$
c) $53.03\%$
d) $6.11\%$

The data line omits chlorine; $\mathrm{Cl} = 35.5$ is used. $M_r(\mathrm{CH_3COCl}) = 78.5$ and $M_r(\mathrm{C_6H_5COCH_3}) = 120$. Amount of ethanoyl chloride $= 4/78.5 = 0.0510\ \mathrm{mol}$; with a 1:1 ratio the theoretical mass of phenylethanone is $0.0510\times120 = 6.11\ \mathrm{g}$. Percentage yield $= (3.24/6.11)\times100 = 53.0\%$, matching option C ($53.03\%$). Option D is the theoretical mass itself ($6.11$) read as a percentage. **Answer: C.**

**20.** Given the following bond energies in $\mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}}$: $\mathrm{C{\equiv}O}$ $1077$; $\mathrm{O{=}O}$ $498.3$; $\mathrm{C{=}O}$ $805$, calculate the energy change (in $\mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}}$) for $2\mathrm{CO(g)} + \mathrm{O_2(g)} \rightarrow 2\mathrm{CO_2(g)}$.

a) $+1847.3$
b) $-1042.3$
c) $-567.7$
d) $+1042.3$

Bonds broken: $2\ \mathrm{C{\equiv}O} + 1\ \mathrm{O{=}O} = 2(1077) + 498.3 = 2652.3\ \mathrm{kJ}$. Bonds formed: two $\mathrm{CO_2}$ molecules, each with two $\mathrm{C{=}O}$ bonds, $= 4\times805 = 3220\ \mathrm{kJ}$. $\Delta H = \text{broken} - \text{formed} = 2652.3 - 3220 = -567.7\ \mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}}$. The reaction is exothermic (more energy released in forming the bonds than needed to break the others), so the positive options are wrong. **Answer: C.**

**21.** Which of the following best describes the shape of the sulphite ion, $\mathrm{SO_3^{2-}}$?

a) Trigonal planar
b) Trigonal pyramidal
c) Tetrahedral
d) Trigonal bipyramidal

Count the electrons around sulphur: 6 valence electrons plus 2 from the ionic charge $= 8$, that is 4 pairs (the oxygen atoms are treated as bonded with single or dative S-O bonds): 3 bonding pairs and 1 lone pair. Four electron pairs arrange tetrahedrally, and the lone pair makes the ion trigonal pyramidal (like $\mathrm{NH_3}$). Trigonal planar is the shape of $\mathrm{SO_3}$, and $\mathrm{SO_4^{2-}}$ is tetrahedral. **Answer: B.**

**22.** In which of the following locations in the Periodic Table is the element that has the following electronic configuration, $1s^22s^22p^63s^23p^5$ most likely to be found?

a) Period 3, Group 5
b) Period 3, Group 7
c) Period 7, Group 3
d) Period 2, Group 7

The highest occupied shell is $n=3$, so the element is in Period 3. It has $2+5 = 7$ electrons in that shell, so it is in Group 7 (Group 17). It is chlorine ($Z=17$). **Answer: B.**

**23.** A white crystalline solid reacts with dilute hydrochloric acid to give a pale yellow precipitate and a colourless gas that decolourises aqueous bromine. The solid is most likely to be

a) Sodium carbonate
b) Sodium sulphide
c) Sodium thiosulphate
d) Sodium sulphite

$\mathrm{S_2O_3^{2-} + 2H^+ \rightarrow S(s) + SO_2(g) + H_2O}$. Sulphur is the pale yellow precipitate and sulphur dioxide is the colourless gas which reduces bromine water ($\mathrm{SO_2 + Br_2 + 2H_2O \rightarrow H_2SO_4 + 2HBr}$), decolourising it. Sodium carbonate gives $\mathrm{CO_2}$ (no precipitate, no effect on bromine), sodium sulphide gives $\mathrm{H_2S}$ (smell of bad eggs) and sodium sulphite gives $\mathrm{SO_2}$ without any precipitate. **Answer: C.**

**24.** Which of the following reagents are the most suitable to distinguish between ethanal $\mathrm{CH_3CHO}$ and propanal $\mathrm{CH_3CH_2CHO}$?

a) Ammoniacal $\mathrm{AgNO_3}$
b) 2,4-dinitrophenylhydrazine (2,4-DNPH)

d) $\mathrm{I_2/NaOH}$

Both are aldehydes, so Tollens' reagent (A) gives a silver mirror and 2,4-DNPH (B) gives an orange precipitate with both, while $\mathrm{PCl_5}$ (C) reacts with neither. Only ethanal contains the $\mathrm{CH_3C{=}O}$ group, so it alone gives a yellow precipitate of triiodomethane (iodoform), $\mathrm{CHI_3}$, with $\mathrm{I_2/NaOH}$; propanal does not. **Answer: D.**

**25.** When $^{210}_{\ 82}\mathrm{Pb}$ undergoes two successive beta decays the nuclide produced will be,

a) $^{210}_{\ 84}\mathrm{Po}$
b) $^{210}_{\ 83}\mathrm{Bi}$
c) $^{210}_{\ 81}\mathrm{Tl}$
d) $^{210}_{\ 82}\mathrm{Pb}$

Each $\beta^-$ decay turns a neutron into a proton: the mass number is unchanged and the atomic number rises by 1. $^{210}_{\ 82}\mathrm{Pb} \rightarrow {}^{210}_{\ 83}\mathrm{Bi} + \beta^- \rightarrow {}^{210}_{\ 84}\mathrm{Po} + \beta^-$. After one decay the product is bismuth (option B); after two it is polonium. **Answer: A.**

**26.** Calculate the pH of the solution that results when $40\ \mathrm{cm^3}$ of $0.05\ \mathrm{mol\,dm^{-3}}$ hydrochloric acid solution is added to $10\ \mathrm{cm^3}$ of $0.10\ \mathrm{mol\,dm^{-3}}$ sodium hydroxide solution.

a) $1.7$
b) $1.2$
c) $3.0$
d) $2.7$

Amount of $\mathrm{H^+} = 0.040\times0.05 = 2.0\times10^{-3}\ \mathrm{mol}$; amount of $\mathrm{OH^-} = 0.010\times0.10 = 1.0\times10^{-3}\ \mathrm{mol}$. Excess $\mathrm{H^+} = 1.0\times10^{-3}\ \mathrm{mol}$ in a total volume of $50\ \mathrm{cm^3}$, so $[\mathrm{H^+}] = 1.0\times10^{-3}/0.050 = 0.020\ \mathrm{mol\,dm^{-3}}$ and $\mathrm{pH} = -\log 0.020 = 1.70$. **Answer: A.**

**27.** Which of the following pairs of liquids, on mixing will form a solution that will deviate negatively from Raoult's law?

a) Propan-2-ol and Propan-1-ol
b) Ethanol and water
c) Propanone and trichloromethane
d) Methanol and water

A negative deviation occurs when the new intermolecular attractions between unlike molecules are stronger than those in the pure liquids: the vapour pressure is lower than predicted and mixing is exothermic. Propanone and trichloromethane form a hydrogen bond between $\mathrm{C{=}O}$ and the $\mathrm{C{-}H}$ of $\mathrm{CHCl_3}$. Two isomeric propanols form an almost ideal solution, while ethanol/water and methanol/water deviate positively. **Answer: C.**

**28.** Select the most suitable set of reagents that can be used in reducing ethanamide $\mathrm{CH_3CONH_2}$ to methylamine, $\mathrm{CH_3NH_2}$.

*Options as printed:* A) $\mathrm{Br_2/NaOH}$   B) $\mathrm{LiAlH_4}$/dry ether   C) Sn/HCl   D) $\mathrm{ZnCl_2/HCl}$

The product $\mathrm{CH_3NH_2}$ has one carbon less than ethanamide, so the change is the Hofmann degradation, $\mathrm{CH_3CONH_2 + Br_2 + 4NaOH \rightarrow CH_3NH_2 + 2NaBr + Na_2CO_3 + 2H_2O}$, with $\mathrm{Br_2/NaOH}$. $\mathrm{LiAlH_4}$ would reduce the amide to ethylamine, $\mathrm{CH_3CH_2NH_2}$ (same carbon number), and Sn/HCl and $\mathrm{ZnCl_2/HCl}$ do not reduce amides. The word 'reducing' in the stem is therefore inaccurate.

**Intended answer: A ($\mathrm{Br_2/NaOH}$).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

**29.** Which of the following oxoacids of chlorine contains chlorine in the $+5$ oxidation state?

b) $\mathrm{HClO_2}$
c) $\mathrm{HClO_3}$
d) $\mathrm{HClO}$

In $\mathrm{HClO_3}$: $+1 + x + 3(-2) = 0$, so $x = +5$. For the others: $\mathrm{HClO_4}$ $+7$, $\mathrm{HClO_2}$ $+3$, $\mathrm{HClO}$ $+1$. **Answer: C.**

**30.** Which intermolecular force is responsible for the dimerization of ethanoic (acetic) acid in liquid benzene?

a) Van der Waals forces
b) Dipole-dipole attractions
c) Hydrogen bonding
d) Permanent dipole-permanent dipole attraction

In a non-polar solvent such as benzene, two ethanoic acid molecules pair up through two hydrogen bonds between the $\mathrm{O{-}H}$ of one molecule and the $\mathrm{C{=}O}$ of the other (a cyclic dimer), which is a hydrogen bond: the strongest intermolecular force available. The dimer has $M_r \approx 120$ instead of $60$. **Answer: C.**

**31.** Which of the statements below is (are) true, for a cell composed of the following half cells: $\mathrm{Ag^+(aq) + e^- \rightarrow Ag(s)}$ $E^\circ = +0.80\ \mathrm{V}$; $\mathrm{Cu^{2+}(aq) + 2e^- \rightarrow Cu(s)}$ $E^\circ = +0.34\ \mathrm{V}$

1. The salt bridge must contain saturated KCl solution
2. The standard emf of the cell, $\mathrm{Cu(s)|Cu^{2+}(aq)\,\|\,Ag^+(aq)|Ag(s)}$ is $+0.46\ \mathrm{V}$
3. $\mathrm{Cu(s)}$ is the reducing agent

a) 1, 2 and 3 are all correct
b) 1 and 2 only are correct
c) 2 and 3 only are correct
d) 3 only is correct

1 is false: $\mathrm{Cl^-}$ from KCl would precipitate silver chloride in the silver half-cell, so a salt bridge of $\mathrm{KNO_3}$ must be used. 2 is true: $E^\circ_{\mathrm{cell}} = E^\circ_{\mathrm{right}} - E^\circ_{\mathrm{left}} = 0.80 - 0.34 = +0.46\ \mathrm{V}$. 3 is true: the half-cell with the lower $E^\circ$ (Cu) loses electrons, so $\mathrm{Cu(s)}$ is oxidised and acts as the reducing agent. Statements 2 and 3 only. **Answer: C.**

**32.** The product(s) obtained from the ozonolysis of the alkene, $\mathrm{(CH_3)_2C{=}CH_2}$ is (are),

1. HCHO
2. $\mathrm{CH_3COCH_3}$
3. $\mathrm{CH_3CHO}$

a) 1, 2 and 3 are all correct
b) 1 and 2 only are correct
c) 2 and 3 only are correct
d) 3 only is correct

Ozonolysis cleaves the $\mathrm{C{=}C}$ bond and puts $\mathrm{C{=}O}$ on each carbon: $\mathrm{(CH_3)_2C{=}CH_2 \rightarrow (CH_3)_2C{=}O + O{=}CH_2}$. The fragment $\mathrm{(CH_3)_2C}$ gives propanone ($\mathrm{CH_3COCH_3}$, 2) and the $\mathrm{CH_2}$ end gives methanal (HCHO, 1). Ethanal (3) would need a $\mathrm{CH_3CH{=}}$ end. Statements 1 and 2 only. **Answer: B.**

**33.** Identify the conjugate acids in the following acid-base equilibrium $\mathrm{[Fe(H_2O)_6]^{3+}(aq) + H_2O(l) \rightleftharpoons [Fe(H_2O)_5]^{2+}(aq) + H_3O^+(aq)}$

1. $\mathrm{H_3O^+(aq)}$
2. $\mathrm{[Fe(H_2O)_6]^{3+}(aq)}$
3. $\mathrm{H_2O(l)}$

a) 1, 2 and 3 are all correct
b) 1 and 2 only are correct
c) 2 and 3 only are correct
d) 3 only is correct

The equilibrium is a Bronsted-Lowry one: $\mathrm{[Fe(H_2O)_6]^{3+}}$ donates $\mathrm{H^+}$ to water (it is an acid) and $\mathrm{H_2O}$ accepts it (it is a base). The conjugate acid of $\mathrm{H_2O}$ is $\mathrm{H_3O^+}$ (1), and $\mathrm{[Fe(H_2O)_6]^{3+}}$ (2) is the conjugate acid of the hydroxo complex $\mathrm{[Fe(H_2O)_5(OH)]^{2+}}$ formed. Water (3) is a base on the left, not an acid, so statement 3 is false. Statements 1 and 2 only. **Answer: B.**

**34.** A compound with the formula $\mathrm{C_4H_{10}O}$ can exhibit which of the following types of isomerism?

1. Position isomerism
2. Functional group isomerism
3. Chain isomerism

a) 1, 2 and 3 are all correct
b) 1 and 2 only are correct
c) 2 and 3 only are correct
d) 3 only is correct

Position: butan-1-ol and butan-2-ol (the $\mathrm{-OH}$ group moves). Functional group: butan-1-ol (alcohol) and ethoxyethane (ether), both $\mathrm{C_4H_{10}O}$. Chain: butan-1-ol and 2-methylpropan-1-ol (straight against branched chain). All three types occur. **Answer: A.**

**35.** It can be deduced from the rate equation of the reaction, $\mathrm{CH_3COCH_3 + I_2 \rightarrow CH_3COCH_2I + H^+ + I^-}$ given by $\text{rate} = k[\mathrm{CH_3COCH_3}][\mathrm{H^+}]$, that the reaction is

1. Second order
2. Zero order with respect to $\mathrm{I_2}$.
3. Unimolecular

a) 1, 2 and 3 are all correct
b) 1 and 2 only are correct
c) 2 and 3 only are correct
d) 3 only is correct

The overall order is the sum of the exponents, $1 + 1 = 2$, so statement 1 is true. $\mathrm{I_2}$ does not appear in the rate equation, so the reaction is zero order with respect to $\mathrm{I_2}$ (2 is true). Molecularity describes an elementary step and cannot be deduced from a rate equation; the rate-determining step here involves propanone and $\mathrm{H^+}$ together (bimolecular), so 3 is false. Statements 1 and 2 only. **Answer: B.**

**36.** True statements on 2-aminopropanoic acid, $\mathrm{CH_3CH(NH_2)COOH}$, are : it is

1. Optically active
2. Capable of forming a zwitterion in a neutral solution
3. An amino acid

a) 1, 2 and 3 are all correct
b) 1 and 2 only are correct
c) 2 and 3 only are correct
d) 3 only is correct

The carbon bearing $\mathrm{NH_2}$, $\mathrm{COOH}$, $\mathrm{CH_3}$ and H is chiral, so alanine is optically active (1). In neutral solution the proton of $\mathrm{COOH}$ transfers to $\mathrm{NH_2}$ giving $\mathrm{CH_3CH(NH_3^+)COO^-}$, a zwitterion (2). It has both an amino and a carboxylic acid group on the same carbon, so it is an ($\alpha$-)amino acid (3). All three are correct. **Answer: A.**

**37.** Which of the following compounds is likely to form a white precipitate on reaction with aqueous bromine?

1. Phenol
2. Phenylamine
3. Ethanol

a) 1, 2 and 3 are all correct
b) 1 and 2 only are correct
c) 2 and 3 only are correct
d) 3 only is correct

The $\mathrm{-OH}$ of phenol and the $\mathrm{-NH_2}$ of phenylamine strongly activate the benzene ring, so aqueous bromine (no catalyst) substitutes at positions 2, 4 and 6, giving white precipitates of 2,4,6-tribromophenol and 2,4,6-tribromophenylamine. Ethanol has no aromatic ring and does not give a precipitate. Statements 1 and 2 only. **Answer: B.**

**38.** Which of the following statements is (are) true about lithium, a Group I element of the Periodic Table?

1. Its ionic salts give a deep red flame colour
2. It shows a diagonal relationship with magnesium
3. Its nitrates decompose into nitrites and oxygen

a) 1, 2 and 3 are all correct
b) 1 and 2 only are correct
c) 2 and 3 only are correct
d) 3 only is correct

1 is true: lithium salts colour the flame crimson (deep red). 2 is true: because of its small, highly polarising $\mathrm{Li^+}$ ion, lithium resembles magnesium (its carbonate and nitrate decompose on heating, its hydroxide is sparingly soluble...). 3 is false: $\mathrm{LiNO_3}$ behaves like $\mathrm{Mg(NO_3)_2}$ and gives the oxide, nitrogen dioxide and oxygen, $\mathrm{4LiNO_3 \rightarrow 2Li_2O + 4NO_2 + O_2}$; only the nitrates of the other Group 1 metals give nitrites. Statements 1 and 2 only. **Answer: B.**

**39.** Which of the following pairs of liquids, on mixing will form a solution that will deviate positively from Raoult's law?

1. Nitric acid and water
2. Propanone and trichloromethane
3. Ethanol and water

a) 1, 2 and 3 are all correct
b) 1 and 2 only are correct
c) 2 and 3 only are correct
d) 3 only is correct

A positive deviation occurs when the unlike attractions are weaker than those in the pure liquids, so the mixture has a higher vapour pressure than predicted (and mixing is endothermic). Ethanol and water (3): ethanol molecules break up the hydrogen-bonded structure of water, a positive deviation. Nitric acid and water (1) interact strongly (ionisation, hydrogen bonding) and deviate negatively, as do propanone and trichloromethane (2). 3 only. **Answer: D.**

**40.** Which of the following factors will affect the value of the equilibrium constant, $K_c$ for the exothermic reaction, $\mathrm{2SO_2(g) + O_2(g) \rightleftharpoons 2SO_3(g)}$

1. Change in pressure
2. Change in concentration
3. Change in temperature

a) 1, 2 and 3 are all correct
b) 1 and 2 only are correct
c) 2 and 3 only are correct
d) 3 only is correct

$K_c$ depends only on temperature. A change of pressure or of concentration shifts the position of equilibrium but the ratio of concentrations that defines $K_c$ stays the same. For this exothermic reaction, raising the temperature lowers $K_c$. 3 only. **Answer: D.**

**41.** Which of the following statements are true of the chemistry of Group IV elements of the Periodic Table as the group is descended?

1. The elements change from non-metals to metals
2. The stability of the dioxides decrease
3. The stability of the tetrachlorides increase

a) 1, 2 and 3 are all correct
b) 1 and 2 only are correct
c) 2 and 3 only are correct
d) 3 only is correct

Going down from C to Pb the elements change from non-metal (C), through metalloids (Si, Ge) to metals (Sn, Pb): 1 is true. The inert pair effect makes the $+4$ state less stable relative to $+2$: $\mathrm{CO_2}$ and $\mathrm{SiO_2}$ are very stable, while $\mathrm{PbO_2}$ is a strong oxidising agent that easily gives $\mathrm{PbO}$: 2 is true. For the same reason the tetrachlorides become less stable ($\mathrm{CCl_4}$ stable, $\mathrm{PbCl_4}$ decomposes to $\mathrm{PbCl_2} + \mathrm{Cl_2}$), so 3 is false. Statements 1 and 2 only. **Answer: B.**

**42.** Some species which have five unpaired electrons in the 3d subshell include

1. A manganese atom
2. An $\mathrm{Fe^{3+}}$ ion
3. A chromium atom

a) 1, 2 and 3 are all correct
b) 1 and 2 only are correct
c) 2 and 3 only are correct
d) 3 only is correct

Mn: $[\mathrm{Ar}]3d^54s^2$, five unpaired electrons in 3d (1). $\mathrm{Fe^{3+}}$: $[\mathrm{Ar}]3d^5$, five unpaired (2). Cr: $[\mathrm{Ar}]3d^54s^1$ (a half-filled d subshell is favoured), five unpaired in 3d, plus one in 4s (3). All three are correct. **Answer: A.**

**43.** From which monomers can the polyester Terylene be produced?

1. Ethane-1,2-diol
2. Terephthalic acid (benzene-1,4-dicarboxylic acid)
3. Ethanedioic acid

a) 1, 2 and 3 are all correct
b) 1 and 2 only are correct
c) 2 and 3 only are correct
d) 3 only is correct

Terylene is a condensation polymer (polyester) made from the diol ethane-1,2-diol (1) and the diacid benzene-1,4-dicarboxylic (terephthalic) acid (2), with loss of water. Ethanedioic acid (3) is not a monomer of Terylene. Statements 1 and 2 only. **Answer: B.**

**44.** The rate equation of the reaction, $\mathrm{CH_3COCH_3 + I_2 \rightarrow CH_3COCH_2I + H^+ + I^-}$ can be determine by

1. Titration method
2. Colorimetry
3. Pressure change method

a) 1, 2 and 3 are all correct
b) 1 and 2 only are correct
c) 2 and 3 only are correct
d) 3 only is correct

Titration (1): samples are withdrawn at intervals, quenched with sodium hydrogencarbonate and the remaining iodine titrated with thiosulphate. Colorimetry (2): the brown colour of iodine fades and its absorbance is followed. Pressure change (3) is useless because no gas is produced or consumed (all reagents and products are in solution). Statements 1 and 2 only. **Answer: B.**

**First statement:** An aqueous solution of hydrochloric acid shows a negative deviation from Raoult's law

**Second statement:** When concentrated HCl is mixed with water, heat is evolved

a) Both statements are true and the second statement is a CORRECT explanation of the first statement.
b) Both statements are true and the second statement is NOT a CORRECT explanation of the first statement.
c) The first statement is true, but the second statement is false.
d) The first statement is false, but the second statement is true.

Second: true, mixing is exothermic. The heat released shows that the unlike attractions are stronger, which is the reason for the negative deviation: a correct explanation. **Answer: A.**

**First statement:** An aqueous solution of sodium ethanoate is alkaline having a pH value greater than 7

**Second statement:** Sodium ethanoate is the salt of a weak base and strong acid.

a) Both statements are true and the second statement is a CORRECT explanation of the first statement.
b) Both statements are true and the second statement is NOT a CORRECT explanation of the first statement.
c) The first statement is true, but the second statement is false.
d) The first statement is false, but the second statement is true.

First: true, $\mathrm{CH_3COO^- + H_2O \rightleftharpoons CH_3COOH + OH^-}$ produces hydroxide ions, so $\mathrm{pH} > 7$. Second: false, sodium ethanoate is the salt of a weak acid (ethanoic acid) and a strong base (NaOH). **Answer: C.**

**First statement:** Zinc oxide is amphoteric.

**Second statement:** When heated zinc oxide turns from a white solid to a yellow solid.

a) Both statements are true and the second statement is a CORRECT explanation of the first statement.
b) Both statements are true and the second statement is NOT a CORRECT explanation of the first statement.
c) The first statement is true, but the second statement is false.
d) The first statement is false, but the second statement is true.

First: true, ZnO reacts with acids to give $\mathrm{Zn^{2+}}$ and with alkalis to give zincate ions $\mathrm{[Zn(OH)_4]^{2-}}$. Second: true, ZnO is yellow when hot and white again on cooling (thermochromism). The colour change has nothing to do with amphoterism, so it is not an explanation. **Answer: B.**

**First statement:** Carbon tetrachloride reacts with water.

**Second statement:** Carbon lacks available low lying d-orbitals.

a) Both statements are true and the second statement is a CORRECT explanation of the first statement.
b) Both statements are true and the second statement is NOT a CORRECT explanation of the first statement.
c) The first statement is true, but the second statement is false.
d) The first statement is false, but the second statement is true.

First: false, $\mathrm{CCl_4}$ does not react (hydrolyse) with water; it is insoluble and immiscible. Second: true, carbon is in Period 2 and has no low-lying vacant d orbitals to accept the lone pair of water (it is also sterically crowded), unlike $\mathrm{SiCl_4}$ which is hydrolysed. **Answer: D.**

**First statement:** When ammonium nitrate is dissolved in water, the temperature of the solution drops.

**Second statement:** The lattice energy of ammonium nitrate is greater than the total solvation energy of its ions

a) Both statements are true and the second statement is a CORRECT explanation of the first statement.
b) Both statements are true and the second statement is NOT a CORRECT explanation of the first statement.
c) The first statement is true, but the second statement is false.
d) The first statement is false, but the second statement is true.

First: true, the dissolving of $\mathrm{NH_4NO_3}$ is endothermic, so the solution cools. Second: true, $\Delta H_{\mathrm{solution}} = \Delta H_{\mathrm{lattice\ dissociation}} + \Delta H_{\mathrm{hydration}}$; more energy is needed to break the lattice than is released when the ions are hydrated, so $\Delta H_{\mathrm{solution}} > 0$. This is exactly why the temperature falls: a correct explanation. **Answer: A.**

**First statement:** Ethyne gives a white precipitate when reacted with ammoniacal silver nitrate.

**Second statement:** Ethyne is converted to benzene when strongly heated.

a) Both statements are true and the second statement is a CORRECT explanation of the first statement.
b) Both statements are true and the second statement is NOT a CORRECT explanation of the first statement.
c) The first statement is true, but the second statement is false.
d) The first statement is false, but the second statement is true.

First: true, the terminal $\equiv\mathrm{C{-}H}$ is weakly acidic and gives a white precipitate of silver dicarbide (silver acetylide), $\mathrm{Ag_2C_2}$. Second: true, ethyne trimerises to benzene on passing through a red-hot iron tube ($\mathrm{3C_2H_2 \rightarrow C_6H_6}$). The two facts are unrelated, so the second is not an explanation of the first. **Answer: B.**
