**1.** Atoms of the same element that differ in mass number are called

a) Isomers
b) Isotopes
c) Polymorphs
d) Allotropes

Atoms of one element have the same number of protons (same atomic number) but can have different numbers of neutrons, so their mass numbers differ: these are isotopes. Isomers are compounds with the same molecular formula but different structures; allotropes are different forms of an element in the same state (e.g. diamond and graphite); polymorphs are different crystal forms of one substance. **Answer: B.**

**2.** Name a metal that is readily extracted by heating the ore with coke.

a) Copper.
b) Iron.
c) Aluminium
d) Sodium

Coke (carbon) is a cheap reducing agent that reduces the oxides of the less reactive metals. Iron ore (haematite, $\mathrm{Fe_2O_3}$) is reduced by coke (via carbon monoxide) in the blast furnace. Aluminium and sodium are above carbon in the reactivity series and are extracted by electrolysis of their molten compounds. Copper is mostly obtained from sulphide ores by roasting and then refining, so iron is the standard answer. **Answer: B.**

**3.** Which of the following is an acid that will undergo complete ionization in water?

a) $\mathrm{H_2SO_4}$
b) $\mathrm{H_3PO_4}$
c) $\mathrm{H_2CO_3}$
d) $\mathrm{CH_3COOH}$

A strong acid ionizes completely in water. Sulphuric acid is a strong acid: $\mathrm{H_2SO_4 \rightarrow 2H^+ + SO_4^{2-}}$. Phosphoric acid, carbonic acid and ethanoic acid are weak acids and ionize only partially. **Answer: A.**

**4.** Identify the main apparatus used to prepare a standard solution in the laboratory.

a) Flat bottom flask
b) Round bottom flask
c) 250ml beaker
d) Volumetric flask.

A standard solution has an accurately known concentration. It is made by dissolving an accurately weighed solid in water and making the solution up to the graduation mark of a volumetric flask. Beakers and flat or round bottom flasks are not calibrated to a precise volume. **Answer: D.**

**5.** When an exothermic reaction takes place,

a) heat is absorbed from the surrounding
b) the activation energy is reduced
c) heat is evolved from the system
d) the products have more energy than reactants

In an exothermic reaction heat is given out by the reacting system to the surroundings, so the products have LESS energy than the reactants ($\Delta H$ is negative). Absorbing heat (A) and products with more energy (D) describe an endothermic reaction; the activation energy is lowered only by a catalyst. **Answer: C.**

**6.** In which of the following reactions is light used as a catalyst?

a) $\mathrm{C_2H_6 + Cl_2 \longrightarrow C_2H_5Cl + HCl}$
b) $\mathrm{C_2H_2 + 2Cl_2 \longrightarrow C_2H_2Cl_4}$
c) $\mathrm{C_3H_6 + Cl_2 \longrightarrow C_3H_6Cl_2}$
d) $\mathrm{C_2H_4 + Cl_2 \longrightarrow C_2H_4Cl_2}$

Light (ultraviolet or strong sunlight) is needed to start the substitution of an alkane by chlorine: it splits $\mathrm{Cl_2}$ into chlorine atoms (free radicals). Ethane + chlorine to give chloroethane and hydrogen chloride (A) is the only substitution reaction listed. The other three are addition reactions of unsaturated hydrocarbons, which take place without light. (Strictly, light is an initiator rather than a catalyst; the examiners' wording is kept.) **Answer: A.**

**7.** Write the electronic configuration of an element with atomic symbol ${}^{13}_{7}X$

a) 2.4
b) 2.5
c) 2.8.3
d) 2.8.8.2

The lower number 7 is the atomic number, so a neutral atom has 7 electrons. Shells fill 2, then 5: configuration 2.5. (13 is the mass number; 2.8.3 would be the configuration of an atom with 13 electrons.) **Answer: B.**

**8.** Which of the following reagents will produce zinc sulphate?

a) zinc and sulphur
b) Zinc and calcium sulphate
c) Zinc and dilute sulphuric acid
d) Zinc and barium sulphate

Zinc is above hydrogen in the reactivity series so it reacts with dilute sulphuric acid: $\mathrm{Zn + H_2SO_4 \rightarrow ZnSO_4 + H_2}$. Zinc and sulphur give zinc sulphide; zinc is less reactive than calcium and barium, so it cannot displace them from their sulphates. **Answer: C.**

**9.** The rate of reaction between calcium carbonate and 0.1M HCl can be increased by

a) adding water into the reaction mixture
b) increasing the particle size of the calcium carbonate
c) using 0.4M HCl instead of 0.1M HCl.
d) placing the reaction vessel in an ice bath

A higher concentration means more acid particles per unit volume, so more frequent collisions and a faster reaction. Adding water dilutes the acid, bigger particles reduce the surface area, and cooling lowers the particles' energy: all three slow the reaction. **Answer: C.**

**10.** Which of the following graphs best shows how the volume of $\mathrm{CO_2}$ evolved (on the vertical axis) varies with time when calcium carbonate is strongly heated to complete decomposition?

![Four graphs A to D of CO2 volume against time (question 10)](/media/figures/cm/gce-ol-chemistry-2015-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_1.webp)

a) A
b) B
c) C
d) D

$\mathrm{CaCO_3 \rightarrow CaO + CO_2}$. The volume of gas starts at zero, rises as the carbonate decomposes, and stops rising (a plateau) once all the calcium carbonate has decomposed. Only graph B starts at the origin and levels off. A decreases (CO$_2$ is not being used up); C and D keep rising for ever. **Answer: B.**

**11.** Identify the common gaseous product formed when the nitrates of groups I and II are strongly heated.

a) Nitrogen dioxide
b) Nitrogen monoxide
c) Nitrogen
d) Oxygen

Group I nitrates give the nitrite and oxygen: $\mathrm{2NaNO_3 \rightarrow 2NaNO_2 + O_2}$. Group II nitrates give the oxide, nitrogen dioxide and oxygen: $\mathrm{2Ca(NO_3)_2 \rightarrow 2CaO + 4NO_2 + O_2}$. The only gas formed in both cases is oxygen. **Answer: D.**

**12.** Select the procedure that is most suitable for separating a solid mixture of sodium chloride and ammonium chloride.

*Options as printed:* A) Dissolve the mixture in water and use separating funnel.   B) Dissolve the mixture in water and filter   C) Dissolve the mixture in a non polar solvent and filter   D) Dissolve in water, heat to concentrate and cool to crystallize

Both sodium chloride and ammonium chloride dissolve in water, so options A and B fail: a separating funnel separates immiscible liquids and filtration separates an insoluble solid from a liquid. Neither salt dissolves in a non-polar solvent (C). Crystallization (D) only partly separates two soluble salts. The standard method is SUBLIMATION: on heating, ammonium chloride sublimes (it decomposes to $\mathrm{NH_3}$ and HCl that recombine on a cold surface) while sodium chloride stays behind. This method is not offered among the options; the best of the four printed choices is D (the only recognised separation technique for two soluble solids).

**1.** As a legal entity, a joint stock company can:

a) Close at anytime.
b) Not operate without a certificate of trading.
c) Open at anytime.
d) Sue and be sued.

A joint stock (limited liability) company is a **legal entity**: it exists in law separately from its owners. Because of this it can own property, make contracts, and **sue and be sued** in its own name. Opening and closing at will is not a legal-entity power, and the certificate of trading is a requirement for starting business, not something a company can do.

**Answer: D.**

**2.** The document that shows the quantity of goods that enter and leave a store is:

a) Bin card.
b) Invoice.
c) Delivery note.
d) Statement of account.

A **bin card** is kept at the shelf or bin where goods are stored. It records goods received, goods issued and the balance in stock, so it shows the quantity entering and leaving the store. An invoice shows the price of goods sold, a delivery note accompanies goods being delivered, and a statement of account summarises what a customer owes.

**Answer: A.**

**3.** The amount the assured receives if he decides to discontinue his life policy is known as:

a) Refunded value.
b) Claim.
c) Surrender value.
d) Indemnification.

When a policyholder stops paying premiums on a life policy before it matures and asks the insurer to cancel it, the insurer pays the **surrender value**, the cash value the policy has built up. A claim is made after an insured event, and indemnification is compensation for a loss.

**Answer: C.**

**4.** Which of these documents needs acceptance to guarantee payments?

a) Bank credit.
b) Letter of credit.
c) Letter of hypothecation.
d) Bill of exchange.

A **bill of exchange** is an order written by the drawer telling the drawee to pay a sum on a fixed date. The drawee must sign it (accept it) to agree to pay, and only then does it guarantee payment. A letter of credit is issued by a bank and does not need the buyer's acceptance in this way.

**Answer: D.**

**5.** A document showing details of goods and passengers carried in a ship or aircraft is known as:

a) Bill of lading.
b) Airway bill.
c) Manifest.
d) Indent.

A **manifest** is the carrier's list of the whole cargo and the passengers on board a ship or aircraft, prepared for customs and port authorities. A bill of lading (sea) and an airway bill (air) describe goods only, and an indent is an order for goods placed with an agent abroad.

**Answer: C.**

**6.** Which Act of parliament discourages misleading advertisement?

a) Sales of Goods Act.
b) Unfair Trading Act.
c) Trade Description Act.
d) Advertising Act.

A Trade Description Act forbids sellers from giving a false or misleading description of goods, services or prices in advertisements and labels, so it protects the consumer against misleading advertisement. The Sales of Goods Act deals with the contract of sale (quality, title, fitness), and the other two names are not the standard Acts studied for this topic.

**Answer: C.**

**7.** The act of stealing goods from a shop is described as:

a) Shopping theft.
b) Shop lifting.
c) Organized theft.
d) Theft.

Stealing goods from a shop by a person pretending to be a customer is called **shop lifting**. It is one of the reasons retailers add security measures such as cameras and guards. 'Theft' is the general word for stealing anything, so the question asks for the special term.

**Answer: B.**

**8.** Loss leaders facilities are commonly offered by:

*Options as printed:* A) Supermarkets.   B) Hypermarkets.   C) Department stores.   D) Multiple shops.

A loss leader is an item that a retailer sells at or below cost price to attract customers who will then buy other goods at normal prices. Large self-service retailers such as supermarkets use this technique most often, although hypermarkets and department stores also use it, so the printed options overlap.

**Intended answer: A (Supermarkets).**

**9.** Which of the risks below is NOT covered by a fire policy?

a) Lightening.
b) Explosion of domestic boilers.
c) War.
d) Damage by smoke.

A fire policy covers fire and the damage that goes with it: lightning, explosion of domestic boilers and damage by smoke or water used to put out the fire. **War** (like riot or nuclear risks in many policies) is a special risk that insurers exclude or cover only with an extra premium.

**Answer: C.**

**10.** Which of the following is involved in mail services in Cameroon?

a) CAMTEL.
b) INTELCAM.
c) CAMPOST.
d) MINPOSTEL.

**CAMPOST** is the public company that runs postal services (letters, parcels, money orders and postal savings) in Cameroon. CAMTEL provides telecommunications, and MINPOSTEL is the ministry that supervises posts and telecommunications.

**Answer: C.**

**11.** Advertising that targets the general public is called:

a) Mass advertising.
b) Competitive advertising.
c) Direct advertising.
d) Indirect advertising.

**Mass advertising** is aimed at a very large audience, the general public, through radio, television, newspapers and billboards. Direct advertising is addressed to named individuals (for example by mail), and competitive advertising tries to win customers from rival brands.

**Answer: A.**

**12.** What term below will NOT mean the same as the needs of an enterprise?

a) Resources.
b) Elements of production.
c) Output.
d) Input.

The needs of an enterprise are the things it must have in order to produce: its **resources**, also called **inputs** or **elements (factors) of production** (land, labour, capital and enterprise). **Output** is what the enterprise produces with those inputs, so it does not mean the same.

**Answer: C.**

**13.** A request to an agent abroad to buy goods from a specific producer is known as:

a) Open indent.
b) Indent.
c) Foreign order.
d) Close indent.

An indent is an order sent to an agent abroad to buy goods. In a **close (closed) indent** the importer names the manufacturer or supplier the agent must buy from. In an open indent the agent is free to choose the supplier.

**Answer: D.**

**14.** The document that shows evidence of payment is:

a) Receipt.
b) Promissory note.
c) Invoice.
d) Postal order.

A **receipt** is given by the seller to the buyer as proof that money has been paid. A promissory note is a written promise to pay, an invoice asks for payment, and a postal order is a means of payment.

**Answer: A.**

**15.** The formula "sales - costs of goods sold" gives:

a) Net sales.
b) Gross profits.
c) Net turnover.
d) Net worth.

Sales minus the cost of the goods sold is the **gross profit** (trading profit), before expenses are deducted. Net sales are sales less returns, net turnover is another name for net sales, and net worth is assets minus liabilities.

**Answer: B.**

**16.** Given that the cost of goods sold is 12,000,000 CFAF, and the average stock is 5,000,000 CFAF, then the rate of turnover is:

a) 2 times.
b) 2.4 times.
c) 24 times.
d) 12 times.

Rate of stock turnover = cost of goods sold / average stock = 12,000,000 / 5,000,000 = **2.4 times**. A common error is to divide the other way round (5/12 = 0.42) or to misplace the decimal point (24 times).

**Answer: B.**

**17.** The cost that do not change as output varies in the short-run is called:

a) Opportunity cost.
b) Social cost.
c) Fixed cost.
d) Direct cost.

A **fixed cost** (rent, insurance, managers' salaries) stays the same whatever the level of output in the short run. Direct cost varies with output, opportunity cost is the next best alternative given up, and social cost is the cost borne by society.

**Answer: C.**

**18.** A written agreement for the hiring of a ship is called:

a) Affreightment.
b) Contract policy.
c) Freight policy.
d) Charter party.

A **charter party** is the written contract between a shipowner and a charterer who hires the ship (or part of it). 'Affreightment' is the general name for hiring a ship's space, but the document itself is the charter party. The other two terms do not exist in shipping practice.

**Answer: D.**

**19.** A cheque signed by a bank on behalf of its client to guarantee payment is called:

a) Negotiable cheque.
b) Non negotiable cheque.
c) Certified cheque.
d) Crossed cheque.

A **certified cheque** is a cheque that the bank has marked and signed to confirm that the drawer has enough money in the account and that the amount is set aside. The payee is therefore sure of payment. Negotiable, non-negotiable and crossed cheques carry no bank guarantee.

**Answer: C.**

**20.** The choice of an advertising medium depends on the following factors EXCEPT:

a) Cost of medium.
b) Effectiveness of medium.
c) Target market.
d) Location of medium.

An advertiser chooses a medium (radio, television, press, posters) according to its **cost**, how **effective** it is in reaching people, and the **target market** to be reached. The 'location of the medium' is not one of the usual factors, so it is the exception. The printed option is vague, since a poster's location matters.

**Answer: D.**

**21.** The real owners of a company are:

a) Ordinary shareholders.
b) Preference shareholders.
c) Debentures holders.
d) Participating preference shareholders.

**Ordinary shareholders** carry the main risk, vote at meetings and share in the profits that remain, so they are the real owners. Preference shareholders get a fixed dividend and have limited rights, and debenture holders are lenders (creditors), not owners.

**Answer: A.**

**22.** Imported goods are stored in bonded warehouses in order to await:

a) Payments of transport charges.
b) Collection.
c) Demand.
d) Payment of duties.

A bonded warehouse is supervised by customs. Imported goods stay there, without duty being paid, until the importer pays the **customs duties** or re-exports them. Goods can be released only after the duties are paid.

**Answer: D.**

**23.** Who fills and signs a cheque?

a) Drawer.
b) Drawee.
c) Payee.
d) Customer.

The **drawer** is the account holder who writes the amount and the payee's name on the cheque and signs it. The drawee is the bank that must pay, and the payee is the person who receives the money. (The drawer is also a customer of the bank, but 'drawer' is the exact term.)

**Answer: A.**

**24.** The main purpose of a bill of lading in sea transport is that it allows:

*Options as printed:* A) Ownership of goods to be claimed.   B) Goods to be transported by sea.   C) Goods to be transported abroad.   D) Transfer of ownership of goods.

A bill of lading is a receipt for goods shipped, evidence of the contract of carriage and a **document of title**. The holder can claim the goods at the port of arrival, and by endorsing it the holder can transfer ownership. Options A and D are therefore both defensible and the question is left open.

**Intended answer: A (Ownership of goods to be claimed).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

**25.** Working capital is calculated as:

a) Gross profits - expenses.
b) Current assets - current liabilities.
c) Total assets - current assets.
d) Total assets - debtors.

Working capital is the money available for day-to-day running of a business: **current assets - current liabilities**. For example, current assets of 900,000 FCFA and current liabilities of 400,000 FCFA give working capital of 500,000 FCFA.

**Answer: B.**

**26.** The insurance firm that caters for the welfare of workers as governed by the Cameroon labour code is:

a) Beneficial Life Insurance.
b) National Social Insurance Fund.
c) Coling All Life Insurance.
d) Satelite Insurance Company.

The **National Social Insurance Fund** (CNPS) is the public body that handles workers' social welfare in Cameroon: family allowances, work accident cover and old age pensions. The other names are private insurance companies.

**Answer: B.**

**27.** Commerce as a branch of production is concerned with:

a) Changing location of goods and services.
b) Distributing goods and services.
c) Changing the form of goods.
d) Changing the ownership of goods.

Production is divided into industry, commerce and direct services. **Commerce** is concerned with the **distribution** of goods and services, bringing them from producers to consumers. Changing the form of goods belongs to manufacturing (industry).

**Answer: B.**

**28.** Electrical engineering is a specialized occupation in which branch of production?

a) Manufacturing.
b) Industry.
c) Commerce.
d) Direct Services.

The branches of production are **industry**, commerce and direct services. Electrical engineering (making and installing electrical equipment) is an occupation within industry. 'Manufacturing' is only one sub-division of industry, not a branch of production, which is why B is chosen.

**Answer: B.**

**29.** All of the following have limited liabilities EXCEPT:

*Options as printed:* A) Ordinary shareholders.   B) Underwriters.   C) Sleeping partners.   D) Preference shareholders.

Shareholders (ordinary and preference) have limited liability. The exception has unlimited liability: individual underwriters (such as Lloyd's names) are liable without limit, and a sleeping partner in an ordinary partnership is also liable without limit. Both B and C can be defended, so the question is left open.

**Intended answer: B (Underwriters).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

**30.** A document sent by a potential buyer to many suppliers at the same time is called:

a) Order form.
b) Advice note.
c) Letter of enquiry.
d) Pro forma invoice.

A **letter of enquiry** is sent by a buyer who wants information on prices, quality and delivery terms, often to several suppliers at the same time so that the replies (quotations) can be compared. An order form is sent after choosing a supplier.

**Answer: C.**

**31.** Which of the following resources of an enterprise will be subject to depreciation?

a) Land.
b) Capital.
c) Labour.
d) Entrepreneur.

**Capital** (machines, vehicles, buildings and equipment) wears out with use and time, so it depreciates. Land is not normally depreciated, and labour and the entrepreneur are people, not assets that are written down.

**Answer: B.**

**32.** Which of the following is granted when a customer operates a current account?

a) Short term loan.
b) Discount.
c) Long term loan.
d) Overdraft.

A bank may allow a good customer with a current account to withdraw more than the balance: this is an **overdraft**. Loans are granted on a separate loan account, and a discount is given on bills.

**Answer: D.**

**33.** A recent development in the transportation of goods which is meant to reduce handling cost is by the use of:

*Options as printed:* A) Pallet.   B) Tight Security.   C) Fork lift.   D) Cranes.

A **pallet** (a platform on which goods are stacked and moved as one unit) is the usual answer, because moving one unit load instead of many single packages reduces handling cost. A fork lift and cranes are also handling equipment, so the printed options overlap and the question is left open.

**Intended answer: A (Pallet).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

**34.** A grouping of shipping companies to protect their common interest is:

a) Conference.
b) Charter party.
c) Baltic exchange.
d) Shipping Association.

A **shipping (liner) conference** is a group of shipping lines that agree on common freight rates and sailing schedules to protect their common interest and avoid ruinous competition. A charter party is a contract, and the Baltic Exchange is a market for chartering ships.

**Answer: A.**

**35.** The following are sales promotional techniques EXCEPT:

a) Free samples.
b) Trade fairs.
c) Television.
d) Competition.

Free samples, trade fairs and competitions are sales promotion techniques that give buyers a direct incentive. **Television** is an advertising medium, not a sales promotion technique.

**Answer: C.**

**36.** An organization whose management is democratically elected is called:

a) Public company.
b) Public corporation.
c) Co-operative society.
d) Partnership.

In a **co-operative society** the members elect the management committee, and each member has one vote whatever the number of shares held. A public company is run by directors chosen by shareholders in proportion to shares, and a public corporation is run by government appointees.

**Answer: C.**

**37.** A practice whereby goods are sold below the cost price in a department store is known as:

a) Price leadership.
b) Loss leadership.
c) Breaking bulk.
d) Profits maximization.

Selling some goods below cost price to attract customers into the store is **loss leadership** (the goods are called loss leaders). Price leadership means that one firm sets the price followed by the others, and breaking bulk is dividing large quantities into small ones.

**Answer: B.**

**38.** Nationalization of industry means that its ownership becomes that of:

a) Tax payers.
b) Shareholders.
c) Indigenes.
d) State.

Nationalization is the transfer of a privately owned business or industry to **state (government) ownership**.

**Answer: D.**

**39.** The name given to a mail that is marked with a Blue cross, given a serial number and sealed with wax is called:

a) Registered post.
b) Recorded delivery.
c) Express delivery.
d) Ordinary post.

**Registered post** is the safe postal service: the item is marked with a cross, receives a serial number, is handed over against a receipt and is delivered to the addressee against signature, so compensation is paid if it is lost. Ordinary post has no such protection and express delivery is about speed.

**Answer: A.**

**40.** Which of the facilities below can enable the customer to withdraw money even when a bank has closed?

a) A cheque.
b) Standing order.
c) Cash Dispenser.
d) Direct debit.

A **cash dispenser** (automatic teller machine, ATM) works day and night with a card and a PIN, so a customer can withdraw cash when the bank is closed. Cheques are presented at the bank, and standing orders and direct debits are automatic payments, not withdrawals.

**Answer: C.**

**41.** A means of transport which is NOT easily affected by weather condition is:

a) Road.
b) Sea.
c) Rail.
d) River.

**Rail** runs on its own track and is the means of transport least disturbed by weather. Roads are blocked by floods and landslides in the rainy season, sea transport is affected by storms and fog, and river transport by floods or low water.

**Answer: C.**

**42.** The banking facility that can be used to pay many creditors with one cheque is called:

a) Certified cheque.
b) Standing order.
c) Credit transfer.
d) Bank draft.

With a **credit transfer** (bank giro) the debtor gives the bank one cheque or instruction together with a list of the creditors and the amounts, and the bank credits each creditor's account. A standing order pays one fixed beneficiary regularly.

**Answer: C.**

**43.** A refund of duties on goods meant for re-exportation is called:

a) Discount.
b) Excise drawback.
c) Subsidies.
d) Customs drawback.

When imported goods on which duty was paid are exported again, the customs authority refunds the duty. This refund is a **customs drawback**.

**Answer: D.**

**44.** A contract of charter of a ship for a particular journey is:

a) Time charter.
b) Demise charter.
c) Voyage Charter.
d) Demurrage.

A **voyage charter** hires a ship for one particular journey between named ports. A time charter hires the ship for a fixed period, a demise (bareboat) charter hands over the ship without crew, and demurrage is the payment for delay in loading or unloading.

**Answer: C.**

**45.** When a customer is granted an overdraft, interest will be paid on the:

a) Whole amount.
b) Extra amount overdrawn.
c) Amount drawn.
d) Amount overdrawn.

Interest on an overdraft is charged only on the **amount overdrawn** (the sum that exceeds the balance), and only for the days it is overdrawn. Options B and D mean nearly the same, and D is the standard wording.

**Answer: D.**

**46.** Goods were bought for 200,000 CFAF on the 01/01/2013 with these payment terms: 5% 7days, 2½ % 15days.

What will be the cash discount if payment was made on the 13/01/13?

a) 10,000 CFAF
b) 5,000 CFAF
c) 20,000 CFAF
d) 50,000 CFAF.

Payment on 13 January is 12 days after the purchase on 1 January. It is after the 7 days (5%) and within the 15 days, so the rate is **2.5%**.

Cash discount = 200,000 x 2.5 / 100 = **5,000 CFAF**. The trap is to use 5% (10,000 CFAF), which applies only up to 7 January.

**Answer: B.**

**47.** Limited liability implies that shareholders are:

a) Liable to the debts of the company up to their personal properties.
b) Liable to the debts of the company up to their liabilities.
c) Liable to the debts of the company up to their capital contributed.
d) NOT liable to the debts of the company.

With limited liability a shareholder can lose only the **capital contributed** (the amount of the shares). The shareholder's personal property is protected. Option D is too strong since the shareholder loses the money invested.

**Answer: C.**

**48.** A factor that will NOT determine the location of a warehouse is:

a) Location of factory.
b) Operating cost.
c) Cost of goods.
d) Cost of construction.

A warehouse is placed near the factory or the market, where operating cost and cost of construction (land, building) are favourable. The **cost of goods** stored depends on suppliers, not on where the warehouse stands, so it does not determine its location.

**Answer: C.**

**49.** Goods liable for duties are stored in which warehouse?

a) Bonded.
b) State.
c) Border.
d) Private.

Goods on which duties have not yet been paid are held under customs control in a **bonded warehouse** until the duties are paid.

**Answer: A.**

c) Upgrading

**10.** Which one of the following destroys or corrupts data?

c) Antivirus software
d) Trojan horse

A computer virus is a program that attaches itself to files and damages, destroys or corrupts data. Antivirus software protects against such programs. Worms mainly copy themselves across networks and a Trojan horse hides inside a useful-looking program, but the textbook description of a program that destroys or corrupts data is a virus. **Answer: A.**

**11.** Memory capacity may be expressed in ________.

a) Microseconds
b) Megahertz
c) Megabytes
d) bits/cycle

Memory capacity (how much data can be stored) is measured in bytes and their multiples, for example megabytes. Microseconds measure time, megahertz measures clock speed and bits per cycle measures data transfer. **Answer: C.**

**12.** What name is used to describe the rules that govern usage of programming language statements?

a) Logic
b) Protocols
c) Compiler
d) Syntax

The syntax of a programming language is the set of rules that decides how its statements must be written. Protocols are rules for communication between computers, and a compiler is a translator program. **Answer: D.**

**13.** Simplify the expression 11001 + 1111 in the binary system.

a) 101000
b) 111000
c) 100100
d) 111011

In decimal, $11001_2 = 25$ and $1111_2 = 15$, so the sum is $25 + 15 = 40$. Converting back, $40 = 32 + 8 = 101000_2$. Column by column the addition gives the same result. **Answer: A.**

**14.** Which of the following is a correct spreadsheet formula to multiply 25 by 3?

b) =25*3
c) =25x3

**15.** Which of the following is NOT a requirement for algorithms?

a) It executes in finite time
b) It is effective
c) It eventually terminates
d) It is written in English

An algorithm must finish after a finite number of steps (it terminates) and each step must be effective (clear and doable). It can be written in English, pseudocode, a flowchart or a program: the language is not a requirement. **Answer: D.**

**16.** Which one of the following symbols represents an AND gate?

**17.** In a client-server network

a) The server responds to the request of the client.
b) The server initiates communication with the client.
c) The client provides resources for the server.
d) Both the server and the client can provide resources as need arises.

In a client-server network the client sends a request and the server, which holds the shared resources, responds to it. The server does not start the communication and the client does not supply the resources. **Answer: A.**

**18.** Ten seconds is equal to ________ nanoseconds.

c) $10^{9}$

**19.** A document produced to show that a project is technically possible and worth the cost of development is the:

a) Feasibility report
b) Analysis report
c) Evaluation report
d) Profit and loss account

A feasibility report is written at the start of a systems project to show whether the project is technically possible and worth its cost. An analysis report describes the existing system, an evaluation report judges the finished system, and a profit and loss account is an accounting statement. **Answer: A.**

**20.** The binary equivalent of the octal number 211 is

a) 11101101
b) 10110111
c) 10001001
d) 11110010

Each octal digit is written with three bits: $2 = 010$, $1 = 001$, $1 = 001$. Joining them gives $010001001_2$, that is $10001001_2$ (check: $2 \times 64 + 8 + 1 = 137 = 128 + 8 + 1$). **Answer: C.**

**21.** The term multiprogramming refers to the ability to:

a) Have many programs installed on a computer.
b) Program many computers at a time.
c) Use many computer programs.
d) Run many computer programs at a time.

Multiprogramming means that several programs are held in memory and run at the same time (the processor switches between them). Having programs installed or using them one after the other does not mean running them together. **Answer: D.**

**22.** Examples of hardware that produce softcopy output are?

a) Speaker and monitor
b) Monitor and printer
c) Microphone and speaker
d) Printer and microphone

Softcopy output exists only electronically (screen display, sound). The monitor and the speaker both produce it. A printer produces hardcopy and a microphone is an input device. **Answer: A.**

**23.** A feature that automatically moves the cursor to the next line when the current line is full is:

a) Scrolling
b) Word wrap
c) Search and replace
d) Screen adjust

Word wrap moves a word that does not fit at the end of a line to the next line automatically, so the user does not press Enter at each line end. Scrolling moves the view of the document. **Answer: B.**

**24.** A ________ is used to retrieve specific information from a database.

a) data dictionary
b) query
c) report generator
d) form

A query asks the database a question and returns only the records and fields that match the conditions. A data dictionary describes the structure, a report generator formats output and a form is used for data entry. **Answer: B.**

**26.** People who coordinate the development of an information system are referred to as ________.

a) System users
b) System programmers
c) Systems analysts
d) Systems administrators

Systems analysts study the needs of the organisation and coordinate the design and development of an information system. Users use it, programmers write the code and administrators manage it once it is running. **Answer: C.**

**27.** In ________ programming, both data and the instructions that use the data are handled in the same unit.

a) Object-oriented
b) Procedural
c) Declarative
d) Imperative

In object-oriented programming, data (attributes) and the methods that operate on them are grouped together in one unit called an object (class). In procedural programming, data and procedures are separate. **Answer: A.**

**28.** Which of the following is NOT true about a hard disk?

a) It is a secondary storage device.
b) It sends and receives data through an I/O bus.
c) It retains data when the computer is switched off.
d) It uses optical techniques to store data.

A hard disk is a secondary storage device that keeps its data when the power is off and exchanges data with the computer through an I/O bus. It stores data magnetically, not optically (optical techniques are used by CDs and DVDs). **Answer: D.**

**29.** The fastest and most powerful computer category is:

a) personal computer
b) mini computer
c) mainframe computer
d) super computer

Computers are ranked by speed and power: personal computer, minicomputer, mainframe, and at the top the supercomputer. **Answer: D.**

**30.** Which protocol below is used to transfer files between computers on the Internet?

a) FTP
b) HTTP
c) IP
d) TCP

FTP (File Transfer Protocol) is designed to transfer files between computers. HTTP transfers web pages, IP gives addresses and routes packets, and TCP ensures reliable delivery of data. **Answer: A.**

**31.** Which of the following is NOT a method of data validation?

a) Proof reading
b) Check digits
c) Length checks
d) Type checks

Check digits, length checks and type checks are validation checks made automatically by the program on the data entered. Proof reading is a human comparison of the typed data with the source, which is a method of verification, not validation. **Answer: A.**

**32.** The semantics of program statements has to do with their

a) Structure
b) Efficiency
c) Meaning
d) Length

Syntax deals with the structure (the form) of statements, while semantics deals with their meaning, that is what the statement does. **Answer: C.**

**33.** One gigabyte is equivalent to:

a) 1024 Bytes
b) 1024 Kilobytes
c) 1024 Megabytes
d) 1024 Terabytes

Each storage unit is 1024 times the previous one: 1 KB = 1024 bytes, 1 MB = 1024 KB and 1 GB = 1024 MB. **Answer: C.**

**34.** An ink jet printer is an example of a (an):

a) Laser printer
b) Impact printer
c) Non-impact printer
d) LCD printer

An ink jet printer sprays tiny drops of ink on the paper without any part striking it, so it is a non-impact printer. Dot matrix printers are impact printers, and a laser printer is another type of printer, not a description of an ink jet. **Answer: C.**

**35.** The term multimedia refers to:

a) Any combination of text, graphics, video, sound in the same document
b) A computer laboratory with access to the Internet
c) The use of tele-device to send text messages, pictures and sound.
d) A school that has a computer laboratory with computers scanners and internet

Multimedia is the combination of several media, such as text, graphics, video and sound, in the same document or application. The other options describe places or devices, not a combination of media. **Answer: A.**

**36.** A transmission mode that allows data to move in one direction only is called ________ transmission.

a) half-duplex
b) full-duplex
c) simplex
d) duplex

In simplex transmission data travels in one direction only (for example radio or television broadcast). Half-duplex allows both directions but not at the same time, and full-duplex allows both at the same time. **Answer: C.**

**37.** The process of converting from digital signals to analogue signals for the purpose of data communication is called:

a) Modulation
b) Demodulation
c) Line switching
d) Multiplexing

A modem modulates the digital signal of the computer into an analogue signal that can travel on a telephone line. The reverse operation, analogue to digital, is demodulation. **Answer: A.**

**38.** Which of the following storage devices has the fastest access speed?

a) RAM
b) ROM
c) Cache Memory
d) Hard Disk.

Cache memory is a small, very fast memory placed close to the processor and is faster than RAM and ROM. The hard disk is far slower because it has moving parts. **Answer: C.**

**40.** ISP stands for:

a) Internet Serial Port
b) Internet Switching Protocol
c) Internet Service Provider
d) Internet switching point.

**41.** A hardware or software device used to restrict access to data in a network is a(n):

a) Spam filter
b) Antivirus
c) Extranet
d) Firewall

A firewall (hardware or software) controls the traffic between a network and the outside and blocks unauthorised access to data. A spam filter removes unwanted mail, an antivirus removes malicious programs and an extranet is a network extension for outside partners. **Answer: D.**

**42.** Software is said to be open source if:

a) Its license specifies free usage and Modification.
b) It has no license.
c) Its source code can be accessed easily by users.
d) It can be distributed freely.

Open source software is software whose source code is available to users, who can read it and (under the licence) change it. Having no licence does not make software open source, and free distribution alone does not give access to the code. **Answer: C.**

**43.** In computer science, ________ is a well defined step by step method or procedure for solving a problem.

a) a syntax
b) an algorithm
c) an instruction
d) a solution

An algorithm is a well defined, finite sequence of steps that solves a problem. A syntax is a set of rules, an instruction is a single step, and a solution is the result. **Answer: B.**

**44.** EIS stands for:

a) Electronic Information System
b) Essential Information System
c) Executive Information System
d) Essential Intergrated Software.

EIS means Executive Information System, a system that gives senior managers summarised information for decision making. **Answer: C.**

**45.** The truth table below is for the ____ gate.

| INPUT X | OUTPUT out |
|---|---|
| 0 | 1 |
| 1 | 0 |

a) NOT
b) OR
c) AND
d) XOR

The gate has a single input and the output is always the opposite of the input (0 gives 1, 1 gives 0). This is the NOT gate; OR, AND and XOR all need two inputs. **Answer: A.**

**46.** ________ is the protocol that governs movement of data on the Internet.

a) HTML
b) Telnet
c) TCP/IP
d) XML

TCP/IP is the set of protocols (TCP splits data into packets and IP routes them) that governs the movement of data on the Internet. HTML and XML are markup languages, and Telnet is a remote login service. **Answer: C.**

**47.** An operating system that runs on a single computer and can accommodate different users at the same time is a:

a) single-user operating system.
b) multi-user operating system.
c) disk operating system.
d) peer to peer operating system.

A multi-user operating system lets several users work on the same computer at the same time. A single-user system serves one user, and a disk operating system is a name for an OS stored on disk. **Answer: B.**

**48.** Which of the following data types can have only two possible values?

a) Text.
b) Date.
c) Number.
d) Boolean.

A Boolean value is either true or false (yes or no, 1 or 0). Text, date and number can take many values. **Answer: D.**

**49.** Which of the following is a good password policy for an organization? Passwords should:

a) Be very long.
b) Never be changed.
c) Comprise about seven or eight characters that users can easily remember.
d) Be written and kept in a secret place in case the user forgets the password.

A good policy asks for passwords that are long enough to be hard to guess (seven or eight characters or more) yet easy to remember, so that users do not write them down. A password that is never changed or that is written down is a risk, and a very long password is hard to remember. **Answer: C.**

**50.** A ticket seller checks and allocates seats, then prints tickets for customers. What type of information system is the ticket seller using?

a) A data automation system.
b) A management information system.
c) An expert system.
d) A transaction processing system.

Checking seat availability, allocating a seat and printing a ticket is the day-to-day processing of a transaction (a booking). That is a transaction processing system. A management information system summarises data for managers and an expert system imitates a human expert. **Answer: D.**

**1.** When economic principles are developed from factual evidence, this method of economic reasoning is called

a) descriptive economics.

c) hypothesis testing.

Induction moves from particular facts and observations to a general principle or law. Deduction does the opposite: it starts from assumptions and derives conclusions logically. **3.** A market economy can result in

a) production ignoring externalities.
b) production not satisfying consumers' real wants.
c) shortages and surpluses of products.
d) reduced incentives lowering individual effort.

Private firms and consumers consider only private costs and benefits, so a market economy can produce too much of goods with external costs (pollution) and too little of goods with external benefits. B is not a feature of a market economy, where firms produce what consumers will pay for. C is corrected by the price mechanism, which clears shortages and surpluses. D describes a command economy, where incomes do not reward effort. **Answer: A.**

**4.** Which of the following will likely trigger a move from a command economy to a market economy?

b) Inflation resulting from the removal of price controls.
c) Low quality goods leading to low living standards.
d) Industrial unrest with frequent conflicts between workers and employers.

Command economies move towards the market when central planning fails to deliver: shortages, poor quality goods, little choice and low living standards. These failures push governments to introduce prices, competition and incentives. B is a consequence of liberalisation (removing price controls), not its cause. A and D are not typical causes of such a reform. **Answer: C.**

**5.** A security whose market price is the same as its nominal value is said to be

a) at par.
b) in equilibrium.
c) at zero rate.

A security (share or bond) quoted at its face (nominal) value is said to be **at par**. If the market price is above the nominal value it is at a premium, and below it, at a discount. **Answer: A.**

**6.** If the quantity of all factors used in a production process increased by 10% and production rose by 15%, there are

a) decreasing returns to scale.
b) increasing returns to scale.
c) decreasing returns to a variable factor.
d) increasing returns to a variable factor.

All factors are increased in the same proportion (10%), so this is a change of scale, not of one variable factor. Output rises by more (15% > 10%), so there are increasing returns to scale. Options C and D concern only one factor being varied while the others are fixed. **Answer: B.**

**7.** Providence and Son's Enterprise has a Capital structure composed of:

Preference shares = 80 million FCFA

If the company is lowly geared, the figure for its ordinary share capital might be

a) 20 million FCFA.
b) 400 million FCFA.
c) 40 million FCFA.
d) 120 million FCFA.

Gearing compares fixed-return capital (debentures and preference shares) with total capital. Here fixed-return capital is $40 + 80 = 120$ million FCFA. A company is **lowly geared** when fixed-return capital is a small part of total capital, so ordinary share capital must be much larger than 120 million. With 400 million, gearing is $120/(120+400) \approx 23\%$, which is low. With 20 million, it is $120/140 \approx 86\%$ (highly geared), with 40 million $75\%$ (highly geared), and with 120 million exactly $50\%$ (neutral, not low). **Answer: B.**

**8.** If an industry remains in an area long after the factors that attracted it have disappeared, this is known as

a) industrial location.
b) natural location advantage.
c) industrial inertia.
d) regional location advantages.

Industrial inertia (or geographical inertia) is the tendency of an industry to stay where it started even though the original advantages (raw materials, power, skilled labour) have gone, because of the sunk costs, skilled labour and supporting industries already in place. **Answer: C.**

**11.** Under which of the following circumstances would an increase in the price of good X result in a fall in the demand for good Y?

**15.** A shift of a demand curve to the left could be caused by

**16.** If a nationalised industry adopts the marginal costs pricing policy for its services when its average cost is declining, it will likely

a) make a loss.
b) break even.
c) make a profit.
d) not require state subvention.

When average cost is falling, marginal cost lies below average cost. Setting price equal to marginal cost therefore gives price below average cost, so each unit is sold at a loss and the industry makes a loss, which the state must cover by a subsidy (subvention). b) MR=MC
c) AR=AC

It therefore expands output up to the point where $AR = AC$, that is, where it just earns normal profit. $MR = MC$ is profit maximisation and $MR = 0$ is revenue maximisation, which stops earlier. **Answer: C.**

**19.** When consumers buy in the cheaper markets and sell in more expensive markets, this is known as

a) resale price maintenance.
b) seepage.
c) price discrimination.
d) penetrating pricing.

A discriminating seller keeps markets separate. **Seepage** (leakage) occurs when buyers in the cheap market resell the good in the dear market, which undermines the discrimination. b) each firm is a price maker.

In oligopoly there are few large firms, so each firm's decisions on price and output affect its rivals and provoke reactions. The firms are therefore mutually dependent. Differentiated products and price making are features of other structures too, and do not explain interdependence. **Answer: C.**

**22.** Normal profit is

b) the level of reward where MR = MC.

Normal profit is the minimum reward that keeps the entrepreneur in the industry. It is counted as a cost, so at normal profit total revenue equals total cost, that is, $AR = AC$. **24.** The market value of all goods and services produced by a country's resources regardless of where the resources are located is

a) Net National Product.
b) Gross National Product.
c) National Income.
d) Gross Domestic Product.

Output produced by a country's own resources wherever they are located (including net property income from abroad) is Gross National Product. GDP, by contrast, counts output produced inside the country's borders whoever owns the resources. NNP and national income are GNP minus depreciation (and indirect taxes for national income). **Answer: B.**

**25.** Why are adjustments made for financial services in the output method of measuring national income?

a) To eliminate the effect of stock appreciation.
b) To record all the interest paid by financial institutions.
c) To avoid double counting of interest paid and received by financial institutions.
d) To make adjustments for residual error.

Banks receive interest from borrowers and pay interest to depositors. The interest they receive is partly a payment for services to firms that is already counted in the value of their output, so adding it again would count the same value twice. An adjustment for financial services avoids this double counting. **Answer: C.**

b) 4,000 FCFA.
c) 2,000 FCFA.
d) 1,920 FCFA.

Real GDP in 2009 $= 480 \times 100/120 = 400$ billion FCFA (2005 prices). Per capita: $400 \times 10^9 / (250 \times 10^6) = 1{,}600$ FCFA. Option D (1,920) comes from dividing nominal GDP by the population and ignoring the deflator. **Answer: A.**

**27.** Which of the following would most likely be included in the measurement of Gross Domestic Product?

a) The output of second-hand goods.
b) Intermediate sales.
c) Legal Services.
d) Social security benefits.

GDP counts the value of final goods and services newly produced in the year. Legal services are a final service. Second-hand goods were counted when first produced, intermediate sales would double count, and social security benefits are transfer payments with no output. **Answer: C.**

**28.** If the MPC in a particular economy is 0.5 and the government increases its expenditure by 1,000 million FCFA, by how much will national income increase?

a) 1,000 million FCFA.
b) 2,000 million FCFA.
c) 3,000 million FCFA.
d) 500 million FCFA.

Multiplier $= 1/(1 - MPC) = 1/0.5 = 2$. Increase in national income $= 2 \times 1{,}000 = 2{,}000$ million FCFA. **Answer: B.**

**29.** If C = 1,500 million FCFA + 0,8Y (where C= consumption and Y = income) and intended investment is 500 million FCFA, then the equilibrium level of national income is

a) 20,000 million FCFA.
b) 24,000 million FCFA.
c) 15,000 million FCFA.
d) 10,000 million FCFA.

At equilibrium $Y = C + I = 1{,}500 + 0.8Y + 500$. So $0.2Y = 2{,}000$ and $Y = 10{,}000$ million FCFA. Check with the multiplier: autonomous spending $2{,}000 \times 1/(1-0.8) = 2{,}000 \times 5 = 10{,}000$. **Answer: D.**

**30.** Which of the following statements concerning the circular flow of income is true?

a) The factors of production are owned by households.
b) The factors of production are owned by firms.
c) Only interactions in the product market reflect the value of national income.
d) Only interactions in the factor market reflect the value of national income.

In the circular flow, households own the factors of production (labour, land, capital) and sell their services to firms in the factor market, receiving income. Firms own the goods produced. National income can be measured in both markets (as income, as expenditure or as output), so C and D are wrong. **Answer: A.**

**31.** Saving in an economy is equal to

a) saving by firms + saving by households.
b) GDP - government purchases.
c) private saving + public saving.
d) total final expenditure - consumption expenditure.

National saving is the sum of private saving (households and firms) and public saving (the government's budget surplus, taxes minus government spending). Option A leaves out public saving. B and D are not saving: $GDP - G$ still includes consumption and investment, and total final expenditure minus consumption equals $I + G + (X-M)$. **Answer: C.**

**32.** The value of the multiplier can fall because of

a) an increase in the marginal propensity to import.
b) a fall in the marginal propensity to save.
c) an increase in export.
d) an increase in government spending on goods and services.

The multiplier is $1/(MPS + MPT + MPM)$, the inverse of the marginal propensity to withdraw. A higher marginal propensity to import increases withdrawals, so the multiplier falls. A fall in MPS raises it, and extra exports or government spending are injections that raise income by the multiplier but do not change its value. **Answer: A.**

**33.** Question 33 is based on table 3, showing the T-account for a hypothetical commercial bank. The figures are in million FCFA.

Table 3

| Liabilities | | Assets | |
|---|---|---|---|
| Deposit | 1,000 | Cash | 100 |
| | | Loans | 900 |
| | 1,000 | | 1,000 |

What is the maximum amount of deposit this bank can make?

*Options as printed:* A) 800 million FCFA.   B) 1,000 million FCFA.   C) 9,000 million FCFA.   D) 10,000 million FCFA.

The cash ratio is $100/1{,}000 = 10\%$. With a 10% cash ratio, cash of 100 million FCFA supports at most $100/0.10 = 1{,}000$ million FCFA of deposits. The bank already holds deposits of 1,000, so it is fully loaned up and cannot create more. The printed question does not say whether it asks for total deposits (1,000, option B), for the extra credit created by a new deposit of 1,000 (9,000, option C) or for the total after such an expansion (10,000, option D), so the intended answer is B, the maximum total deposits supported by the cash held.

**Intended answer: B (1,000 million FCFA).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

**34.** In choosing a commodity to serve as money, the most important characteristic must be that it is

a) easily recognised.
b) portable.
c) durable.
d) generally acceptable.

Money is whatever is generally accepted in exchange for goods and services. Without general acceptability, no other quality (portability, durability, recognisability) makes a commodity money. **Answer: D.**

**35.** Question 35 is based on table 4 below.

Table 4

| Commodity | Expenditure 2005 (FCFA) | Price index 2005 | Price index 2007 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Drinks | 200 | 100 | 150 |
| Housing | 300 | 100 | 80 |
| Food | 500 | 100 | 120 |

The calculation of the weighted price index shows that between 2005 and 2007, the general price level rose by

a) 50%.
b) 16.6%.
c) 14%.
d) 5%.

The weights are the 2005 expenditures (200, 300, 500; total 1,000). Weighted index for 2007 $= (200 \times 150 + 300 \times 80 + 500 \times 120)/1{,}000 = (30{,}000 + 24{,}000 + 60{,}000)/1{,}000 = 114$. The base index is 100, so the general price level rose by 14%. A simple average of the three indices (116.7, giving 16.6%) ignores the weights. **Answer: C.**

**36.** A regressive tax can best be described as one which

*Options as printed:* A) increases with income.   B) imposes a greater burden on the poor.   C) redistributes income in favour of the poor.   D) decreases proportionately with income.

A regressive tax takes a larger proportion of income from low-income earners than from high-income earners, so its burden on the poor is greater. Option B states this in common words. Option D expresses the same idea (the tax rate falls as income rises) in different words. A tax that increases with income, or redistributes in favour of the poor, is progressive. Because B and D can both be defended, the intended answer is B, the usual textbook wording.

**Intended answer: B (imposes a greater burden on the poor).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

**37.** The hypothetical figures of a country's national debt are as follows:

National debt 1,400 million FCFA

External debt 560 million FCFA

Internal debt 840 million FCFA

What percentage of the national debt constitutes a real burden?

a) 60 %.
b) 40%.
c) 66 %.
d) 66.6%.

Internal debt is owed by citizens to citizens, so repayment only transfers income inside the country and imposes no real burden. External debt takes real resources out of the country when it is serviced and repaid, so it is the real burden: $560/1{,}400 \times 100 = 40\%$. A trap is to use the internal share, $840/1{,}400 = 60\%$. **Answer: B.**

**38.** What expression is used to describe a situation where a new loan is contracted to pay off the existing one to reduce interest rate?

a) Refinancing a debt.
b) Redeeming a debt.
c) Re-marketing a debt.
d) Replacing a debt.

Taking a new loan (usually at a lower interest rate) to repay an existing one is called **refinancing** (or conversion) of the debt. Redeeming means repaying the debt itself. **Answer: A.**

**39.** In year 1, a country's visible imports totalled 1,000 billion FCFA and its balance of trade was 500 billion FCFA. In year 2, its visible imports fell in value by 4 per cent. The balance of trade in year 2 was

a) 1,500 billion FCFA.
b) 540 billion FCFA.
c) 2,500 billion FCFA.
d) 960 billion FCFA.

Balance of trade $=$ visible exports $-$ visible imports. In year 1, $X - 1{,}000 = 500$, so exports were 1,500 billion FCFA. In year 2 imports $= 1{,}000 \times 0.96 = 960$ billion. Assuming exports are unchanged, balance of trade $= 1{,}500 - 960 = 540$ billion FCFA (surplus). **Answer: B.**

**40.** Which of the following people would be pleased by a devaluation of the FCFA everything being equal?

a) A Cameroonian tourist travelling to Europe.
b) A Cameroonian importer of Japanese cars.
c) A Spanish exporter of wine to Cameroon.
d) A German importer of Cameroon wood.

After a devaluation, the FCFA is worth less in foreign currency, so Cameroonian goods become cheaper for foreigners, and foreign goods and travel dearer for Cameroonians. The German importer of Cameroon wood pays fewer euros for the same wood. A, B and C are worse off: their purchases cost more FCFA, or the wine becomes dearer in Cameroon. **Answer: D.**

**41.** The adverse movement in the terms of trade means that

a) the volume of exports has fallen relative to the volume of imports.
b) the total value of exports has fallen relative to the total value of imports.
c) the average price of exports has fallen relative to the average price of imports.
d) the average price of imports has fallen relative to the average price of exports.

The terms of trade are $\frac{\text{index of export prices}}{\text{index of import prices}} \times 100$. They worsen (adverse movement) when export prices fall relative to import prices, so that more exports are needed to buy the same imports. Options A and B concern volumes and values, not prices, and D describes a favourable movement. **Answer: C.**

**42.** Arbitrage is the process where

a) exchange rates throughout the world are in equilibrium.
b) bills of exchange are discounted.
c) the central bank intervenes in the exchange market.
d) currencies are bought in one centre and immediately sold in another at a profit.

Arbitrage means buying a currency where it is cheap and selling it at once where it is dearer, taking the difference as profit. Its effect is to make exchange rates in different centres equal, but that is its result and not its definition (A). **Answer: D.**

**43.** The movement from any point inside to a point on the production possibilities curve is termed

a) actual growth.
b) potential growth.
c) economic development.
d) economic growth.

Moving from a point inside the curve (unused resources) to a point on it means that actual output rises by using existing resources more fully: this is **actual growth**. Potential growth is an outward shift of the curve itself, and economic development is a wider improvement in living standards. **Answer: A.**

**44.** When a country increases the stock of capital per worker, increasing labour productivity, this is called

a) capital consumption.
b) capital accumulation.
c) capital deepening.
d) capital widening.

Capital deepening means more capital per worker, which raises labour productivity. Capital widening is more capital in line with more workers (capital per worker unchanged). Capital accumulation is any increase in the capital stock, without saying whether it is per worker. **Answer: C.**

**45.** A recession as a phase of a business cycle is characterised by

a) an increase in investment.
b) falling government expenditure on benefits.
c) increasing inflationary pressures.
d) increasing stocks of unsold goods.

In a recession demand falls, so firms cannot sell all their output and stocks of unsold goods rise. Investment falls, inflationary pressure weakens, and government spending on unemployment benefits rises (automatic stabilisers), so A, B and C are wrong. **Answer: D.**

**46.** When the real source of money, which may be from illegal sources, is hidden, this is described as

a) money laundering.
b) hot money.
c) capital flight.
d) black money market.

**Money laundering** is disguising the illegal origin of money so that it appears to come from a legitimate source. Hot money is short-term funds moved between countries for interest or exchange-rate gains, and capital flight is the large-scale outflow of capital from a country. **Answer: A.**

**47.** When production is carried out on the basis of the order placed by the customers, this is known as

a) batch production.
b) job production.
c) flow production.
d) flow-line production.

In **job production** a single product is made to the customer's own specification (for example a bridge or a tailored suit). Batch production makes groups of identical items, and flow production is continuous mass production on a line. **Answer: B.**

**48.** The systematic procedure laid down by management concerning ordering, receiving, recording, issuing and accounting for stocks is known as

a) purchasing control.
b) stock control.
c) production control.
d) quality control.

Ordering, receiving, recording, issuing and accounting for stocks are the steps of **stock control** (inventory control). Purchasing control deals with buying, production control with scheduling production, and quality control with the standard of the product. **Answer: B.**

**49.** The best channel of distribution of a perishable good is:

a) wholesalers to consumers.
b) wholesalers to retailers then to consumers.
c) direct sales to consumers.
d) retailers to consumers.

A perishable good (fresh fish, fruit, milk) must reach consumers quickly, so the shortest channel, with no intermediaries, is best. Each intermediary adds time and the risk of spoilage. **Answer: C.**

**50.** A machine which has a life span of 2 years yields an annual income of 121,000 FCFA. If it costs 200,000 FCFA to buy it and the current rate of interest is 10 %, what is the net present value?

a) 20,000 FCFA.
b) 10,000 FCFA.
c) 79,000 FCFA.
d) 42,000 FCFA.

Discount each year's income at 10%: year 1: $121{,}000/1.1 = 110{,}000$; year 2: $121{,}000/1.1^2 = 100{,}000$. Present value of income $= 210{,}000$. $NPV = 210{,}000 - 200{,}000 = 10{,}000$ FCFA. The positive NPV says the machine is worth buying. **Answer: B.**
