In a randomly breeding human population, one person out of 1000 is albino. Calculate the approximate frequency of heterozygous breeding individuals in this population.

*Options as printed:* A) 2%   B) 1%   C) 44%   D) 25%

Albinism is recessive, so albinos have the genotype $aa$ and the Hardy-Weinberg equation applies: $q^2 = 1/1000 = 0.001$, so $q = \sqrt{0.001} \approx 0.0316$ and $p = 1 - q \approx 0.9684$. The frequency of heterozygotes is $2pq = 2 \times 0.9684 \times 0.0316 \approx 0.0612$, about 6 %. This value is not among the printed options (2 %, 1 %, 44 %, 25 %); 2 % (option A) would be obtained if one person in 10 000 were albino ($q = 0.01$, $2pq \approx 0.0198$). The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.
Hydrolysis of lipid molecules will yield:

A triglyceride is made of one glycerol molecule joined by ester bonds to three fatty acids. Hydrolysis by lipase breaks the ester bonds and releases fatty acids and glycerol. Amino acids come from proteins and glucose from carbohydrates. **Answer: B.**
In angiosperms, double fertilization results in a diploid zygote and a:

One male gamete fuses with the egg cell ($n + n$) to form the diploid zygote, which becomes the embryo. The second male gamete fuses with the two polar nuclei of the embryo sac ($n + n + n$) to form the triploid primary endosperm nucleus, which develops into the endosperm that nourishes the embryo. The pericarp is formed from the ovary wall and is not a product of fertilization. **Answer: D.**
A transgenic organism is characterized by the presence of:

A transgenic organism has received a gene from another species. This foreign gene is spliced into its DNA as recombinant DNA (DNA made of sequences from two sources). A plasmid is only a vector, restriction endonuclease is the enzyme used to cut DNA, and recombinant RNA is not the criterion. **Answer: B.**
An example of convergent evolution is:

Convergent evolution gives similar (analogous) structures with the same function in unrelated groups under similar selection pressures. Insect wings (chitinous outgrowths) and bird wings (modified forelimbs) are analogous. The bird wing and the pentadactyl limb of whales, and the appendix of man and the caecum of rodents, are homologous structures, which show divergent evolution. The coccyx and the horse's tail are also homologous. **Answer: A.**
wings of insects and wings of birds.
wings of birds and pentadactyl limbs of the whales.
appendix of man and the caecum of rodents.
coccyx of man and the tail of a horse.

In the fruit fly, grey body is dominant over black body and long wing over vestigial wing. The genes controlling these characters are linked. The following statistics was realized in a population of fruit fly when two parents homozygous for both characters were crossed and the offspring test crossed:

| Phenotype | Number |
|---|---|
| grey body, long wing | 1000 |
| black body, vestigial wing | 800 |
| black body, long wing | 206 |
| grey body, vestigial wing | 200 |

What is the crossover value of the recombinants produced?

The parental combinations are the two most numerous classes (grey long = 1000 and black vestigial = 800). The recombinants are the two small classes: black long = 206 and grey vestigial = 200, that is $206 + 200 = 406$. The total number of offspring is $1000 + 800 + 206 + 200 = 2206$. Crossover value $= \dfrac{406}{2206} \times 100 = 18.40\ \%$. **Answer: C.**

$\mathrm{Ca}^{2+}$ in living organisms:

(i) helps in muscle contraction.

(ii) is a component of bacterial cell wall.

(iii) helps in the transmission of impulses in nerve cells.

(iv) is a component of chlorophyll a.

(i) is correct: $\mathrm{Ca}^{2+}$ released from the sarcoplasmic reticulum binds troponin and starts the sliding of the filaments. (iii) is correct: the entry of $\mathrm{Ca}^{2+}$ into the presynaptic knob causes the release of neurotransmitter. (ii) is wrong: bacterial walls are made of peptidoglycan (calcium pectate is found in the middle lamella of plants). (iv) is wrong: chlorophyll contains magnesium. So (i) and (iii) are correct. **Answer: B.**

Which of the following is correct of glycolysis?

(i) It takes place in the mitochondrion.

(ii) It produces much of the ATP in tissue respiration.

(iii) It does not occur in bacterial cells.

(iv) It is the main process producing energy in yeast fermentation.

Glycolysis takes place in the cytoplasm, so (i) is wrong. It gives a net gain of only 2 ATP per glucose, whereas most ATP in tissue (aerobic) respiration comes from oxidative phosphorylation, so (ii) is wrong. Bacteria also use glycolysis, so (iii) is wrong. In alcoholic fermentation the only ATP produced comes from glycolysis (the later steps only regenerate NAD), so (iv) is correct. Only (iv) is correct. **Answer: D.**

Extinction of species can be prevented by:

(i) destroying the habitats.

(ii) not protecting the species.

(iii) increasing the use of bio-poisons.

(iv) controlling and reducing the impacts of modern agriculture.

Destroying habitats, leaving species unprotected and using more poisons all increase the risk of extinction. Controlling and reducing the harmful effects of modern agriculture (habitat clearing, pesticides, monoculture) helps to conserve species. Only (iv) is correct. **Answer: D.**

During the process of digestion in rodents:

(i) food is stored in the rumen.

(ii) upper incisors are absent.

(iii) the gizzard helps to grind food material.

(iv) mutualistic micro-organisms digest cellulose in the caecum.

The rumen belongs to ruminants (cattle, goats) and the absence of upper incisors (replaced by a horny pad) is also a ruminant feature, so (i) and (ii) are wrong. The gizzard is found in birds and earthworms, not in rodents, so (iii) is wrong. Rodents (and rabbits) have a large caecum in which symbiotic bacteria digest cellulose, so (iv) is correct. Only (iv) is correct. **Answer: D.**

The overall purpose of the Calvin cycle is to:

(i) generate molecules of ATP.

(ii) generate NADPH.

(iii) assist plants in tissue respiration.

(iv) build organic molecules.

The Calvin cycle (light-independent stage) uses the ATP and NADPH made in the light-dependent reactions to reduce carbon dioxide to triose phosphate and then to glucose and other organic molecules. It consumes ATP and NADPH, it does not generate them, and it has no role in respiration. Only (iv) is correct. **Answer: D.**

Kranz anatomy is:

(i) the biochemical pathway through which $\mathrm{C}_4$ plants carry out photosynthesis.

(ii) the arrangement of chloroplast-containing cells around the vascular bundles of the leaf.

(iii) a distinctive sheath of cells around the root hairs for absorption of water.

(iv) the arrangement of bundle sheath cells around the vascular bundles of the leaf.

Kranz (wreath) anatomy is a structural feature of $\mathrm{C}_4$ leaves: the vascular bundles are surrounded by a ring of bundle sheath cells that contain chloroplasts, and the mesophyll cells are arranged in turn around this ring. (ii) and (iv) describe this arrangement. (i) describes the $\mathrm{C}_4$ pathway, not the anatomy, and (iii) has nothing to do with leaves. So (ii) and (iv) are correct. **Answer: C.**

The molar of a human:

(i) has 4 or 5 cusps.

(ii) is used for tearing flesh.

(iii) is used for grinding and crushing of food.

(iv) is the last to appear in the milk dentition of humans.

A human molar is a broad tooth with 4 or 5 cusps (i), adapted for grinding and crushing food (iii). Tearing flesh is the work of the canines, so (ii) is wrong. The permanent molars have no predecessors and do not belong to the milk dentition (they appear after it, with the permanent teeth), so (iv) is wrong. Hence (i) and (iii) are correct. **Answer: B.**
The gametophyte in a moss, liverwort and fern:

In all land plants the gametophyte is the haploid generation that makes the gametes by mitosis. In mosses and liverworts it is the dominant, green plant held to the soil by rhizoids; in ferns it is a small independent heart-shaped prothallus. What all three groups share is that the gametophyte is haploid. The sporophyte is the diploid generation; option B (reduced) fits only the gametophyte of seed plants, and C and D are not true of all three groups (the moss gametophyte has multicellular rhizoids). **Answer: A.**
According to the fluid mosaic model, a plasma membrane is composed of:

In the fluid mosaic model (Singer and Nicolson) the membrane is a fluid bilayer of phospholipid in which protein molecules float like a mosaic: intrinsic (integral) proteins span the bilayer and extrinsic (peripheral) proteins lie on its surfaces. Hemicellulose and polysaccharides are not structural components of the plasma membrane. **Answer: C.**
When glomerular filtrate is produced in the kidney tubule, it moves from:

The filtrate leaves the Bowman's capsule and enters the proximal convoluted tubule (where glucose, amino acids and most of the water and salts are reabsorbed), then flows down the loop of Henle, then into the distal convoluted tubule and finally the collecting duct. The only option giving the right order is: proximal convoluted tubule to loop of Henle. **Answer: C.**

proximal convoluted tubule to collecting duct.
proximal convoluted tubule to loop of Henle.

Which of the following pairs of hormones work together so that sperms can be produced from spermatogonia?

Spermatogenesis in the seminiferous tubules needs two hormonal signals: FSH from the anterior pituitary, which acts on the Sertoli cells, and testosterone from the Leydig (interstitial) cells, which is produced under the control of LH (ICSH) and acts on the developing germ cells. So the pair that acts directly on the tubules is testosterone and FSH. LH alone only stimulates testosterone secretion and GnRH acts on the pituitary. (Options A and C are printed identically.) **Answer: D.**

How does the myelin sheath increase the speed of impulse transmission?

*Options as printed:* A) It restricts the potential difference to the Node of Ranvier.   B) It promotes a change in potential difference along an axon   C) It ensures that the ions are kept close to the axon membrane

The myelin sheath is a fatty insulating layer around the axon. Ions can cross the membrane only at the gaps in the sheath (the nodes of Ranvier), so the action potential (the change in potential difference) is restricted to the nodes and the impulse jumps from node to node by local circuits: this is saltatory conduction, which is much faster than the continuous spread along an unmyelinated axon. The answer expected is that the sheath restricts the depolarization to the nodes of Ranvier (the first printed option, A).

**Intended answer: A (It restricts the potential difference to the Node of Ranvier).**

The quantity of DNA in a mature human epithelial cell is $6.5 \times 10^{-12}$ g. The quantity of DNA in a mature red blood cell is:

A body cavity completely surrounded by tissue derived from the mesoderm that provides cushioning for internal organs is called:

A true coelom is a fluid-filled body cavity lined on all sides by mesoderm (the body wall and the gut are both covered by mesodermal tissue), which cushions and protects the organs. Which of these organisms has the largest number of chambers in its heart?

The shark has a two-chambered heart (one atrium and one ventricle), the amphibian has three chambers (two atria and one ventricle), and the typical reptile has three chambers (two atria and a partly divided ventricle). Birds, like mammals, have a four-chambered heart (two atria and two ventricles) which completely separates oxygenated and deoxygenated blood. The bird has the largest number of chambers. **Answer: C.**

In penicillin production, the fermentation process is described as:

Penicillin is a secondary metabolite: it is made after the rapid growth phase of the fungus Penicillium, when the nutrients (the carbon source and the precursor) are added gradually to the fermenter and the product is harvested at the end. This is a 'fed-batch' culture. In a continuous culture the medium is continually added and removed (as for single-cell protein), and downstream processing is the recovery and purification of the product after fermentation. **Answer: C.**
Some bacteria can effectively carry out metabolism in the presence or absence of oxygen. They are described as:

Facultative anaerobes can respire aerobically when oxygen is available and switch to fermentation or anaerobic respiration when it is absent (e.g. Escherichia coli). Strict aerobes need oxygen, strict (obligate) anaerobes cannot grow in oxygen, and 'fermentative microbes' only describes a type of metabolism. **Answer: D.**
Which of the following processes produce the maximum energy yield when one molecule of glucose is oxidized?

Per molecule of glucose, glycolysis gives a net 2 ATP, the Krebs cycle (including the oxidation of pyruvic acid) gives 2 ATP directly, and oxidative phosphorylation, in which the reduced NAD and FAD are reoxidized along the electron transport chain, gives about 26 to 28 of the 30 to 32 ATP formed. Oxidative phosphorylation therefore gives the maximum yield. **Answer: A.**
The enzyme cholinesterase which hydrolyses acetylcholine to choline acts on the:

After acetylcholine has crossed the synaptic cleft and stimulated the receptors, cholinesterase breaks it down to choline and ethanoic (acetic) acid in the synaptic cleft, so that the post-synaptic membrane is not stimulated continuously. The choline is then taken back into the presynaptic knob and resynthesized into acetylcholine. The enzyme acts in the cleft, where the transmitter is. **Answer: C.**

The set up below is a respirometer depicting an experiment to measure the rate of uptake of oxygen by wood louse. If after 30 mins the distance of the ascending and descending limbs of the manometer is 95.5 mm and the diameter of the bore of the capillary is 0.2 mm.

The rate of oxygen uptake by these eight wood lice is:

The carbon dioxide produced is absorbed by soda lime, so the movement of the manometer fluid measures the oxygen taken up. The volume of oxygen used is the volume of a cylinder of the capillary bore: $V = \pi r^2 h$ with $r = 0.1$ mm and $h = 95.5$ mm, so $V = \pi \times 0.1^2 \times 95.5 \approx 3.0\ \mathrm{mm}^3$. This was used in 30 minutes, so the rate is $3.0 / 30 = 0.1\ \mathrm{mm}^3/\mathrm{min}$. The value $3.0\ \mathrm{mm}^3/\mathrm{min}$ forgets to divide by the time. **Answer: B.**
A male with underdeveloped testes, breast development, subnormal intelligence and an abnormal karyotype is likely to have:

Klinefelter's syndrome (XXY, 47 chromosomes) gives a sterile male with small testes, some breast development (gynaecomastia), a tall body and often reduced intelligence. Down's syndrome is trisomy 21, Turner's syndrome (XO) affects females, and Huntington's disease is a dominant gene disease without an abnormal karyotype. **Answer: A.**

Which of the following tends to produce more organic material than it uses?

*Options as printed:* A) The shrub community.   B) The herb community.   C) The pine community.   D) The dense shrub community.

A community produces more organic material than it uses (production greater than community respiration, so that the P/R ratio is above 1) while it is still developing and biomass is accumulating. In an ecological succession the early communities have a high ratio of production to respiration, whereas the climax (such as a pine forest, with a large biomass to maintain) has a P/R ratio close to 1. Among the printed options the herb community, a young seral stage with rapid growth and little standing biomass to respire, is the intended answer, but shrub communities that are still closing their canopy also have P/R above 1, so the printed options do not give one unambiguous choice.

**Intended answer: B (The herb community).**

The solute potential of cells kept in pure water for two days is $-900$ kPa. The pressure potential of these cells is:

Cells kept in pure water until equilibrium is reached are fully turgid and have the same water potential as pure water: $\psi = 0$. Since $\psi = \psi_s + \psi_p$, the pressure potential is $\psi_p = \psi - \psi_s = 0 - (-900) = +900$ kPa. The pressure potential of a turgid cell is positive and equal in size to the solute potential. **Answer: C.**
The presence of a perivisceral cavity in the mesoderm of triploblastic multicellular organisms makes them to be called:

A perivisceral cavity (body cavity around the viscera) that is formed within the mesoderm and lined by it is a true coelom, and animals that have it are coelomates (annelids, molluscs, arthropods, vertebrates). Acoelomates have no body cavity, pseudocoelomates have a cavity not completely lined by mesoderm, and coelenterates are diploblastic. **Answer: C.**
Reverse transcriptase is used in genetic engineering do which of the following?

Reverse transcriptase is the enzyme of retroviruses that makes DNA from an RNA template. In genetic engineering it is used to make a copy of a gene (complementary DNA, cDNA) from its mRNA, which is easily isolated from the cells where the gene is active. The cDNA, which has no introns, can then be inserted into a plasmid vector and expressed in bacteria. **Answer: D.**

The number of moles of carbon dioxide ($\mathrm{CO_2}$) gas present in $44.8\ \mathrm{cm^3}$ at standard temperature and pressure (STP) (molar gas volume $= 22\,400\ \mathrm{cm^3}$) is given by:

Amount of gas $=$ volume of gas $\div$ molar gas volume. Here $n = \dfrac{44.8\ \mathrm{cm^3}}{22\,400\ \mathrm{cm^3\,mol^{-1}}} = 0.002\ \mathrm{mol}$. Option B uses $44.0$ (the molar mass of $\mathrm{CO_2}$) instead of the volume, C divides by the wrong quantity and D multiplies two volumes. **Answer: A.**
When the nuclide $^{239}_{93}\mathrm{Np}$ undergoes beta decay ($\beta^-$ decay) the nuclide produced is

In $\beta^-$ decay a neutron becomes a proton: the mass number stays the same ($239$) and the atomic number rises by one ($93 \rightarrow 94$): $^{239}_{93}\mathrm{Np} \rightarrow {}^{239}_{94}\mathrm{X} + {}^{0}_{-1}e + \bar\nu$. Element 94 is plutonium (Pu), so the product is $^{239}_{94}\mathrm{Pu}$. Option C is the only one with mass number $239$ and atomic number $94$; its symbol is printed 'Pa' (protactinium is $Z = 91$), which is a misprint for Pu. A and B have $Z = 92$, D has $Z = 93$ and a different mass number. **Answer: C.**

$Z = 25$ is manganese: $[\mathrm{Ar}]\,3d^5\,4s^2$. Transition metals lose their $4s$ electrons first, so $\mathrm{Mn^{2+}}$ is $[\mathrm{Ar}]\,3d^5\,4s^0$. A is the neutral atom. **Answer: B.**

Given that the standard enthalpies of formation in $\mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}}$ of $\mathrm{CO(g)}$, $\mathrm{CO_2(g)}$ and $\mathrm{H_2O(g)}$ are respectively $-110$, $-394$ and $-242$. For the elements across period 2 of the Periodic Table, lithium (Li) to neon (Ne)

Which of the following bond type accounts for the reaction between boron trifluoride and ammonia?

$\mathrm{BF_3}$ is electron-deficient (6 electrons around B) and $\mathrm{NH_3}$ has a lone pair on N. The lone pair is donated into the empty orbital of boron, giving $\mathrm{F_3B{\leftarrow}NH_3}$: a dative covalent bond. **Answer: C.**

Select the compound which forms methanol on warming with dilute NaOH solution. (Printed structures: A $\mathrm{CH_3CH_2COCH_2CH_3}$; B $(\mathrm{CH_3})_2\mathrm{CHCOOCH_3}$; C $(\mathrm{CH_3})_2\mathrm{CHCH(OH)CH_3}$; D $(\mathrm{CH_3})_2\mathrm{CHCHO}$.)

Methanol is released only by alkaline hydrolysis of an ester whose alcohol part is $\mathrm{CH_3O{-}}$. B is methyl 2-methylpropanoate: $(\mathrm{CH_3})_2\mathrm{CHCOOCH_3} + \mathrm{NaOH} \rightarrow (\mathrm{CH_3})_2\mathrm{CHCOONa} + \mathrm{CH_3OH}$. A (a ketone), C (an alcohol) and D (an aldehyde) do not react with dilute NaOH to give methanol. **Answer: B.**

In an experiment to determine the relative molecular mass of ethanoic acid in an organic solvent, 120 was obtained instead of the expected value of 60. What could be the explanation for this phenomenon?

A measured $M_r$ of $120 = 2 \times 60$ means that two molecules behave as one particle. In a non-polar organic solvent (and in the vapour), ethanoic acid molecules pair through two hydrogen bonds between their $\mathrm{{-}COOH}$ groups, forming dimers. Dissociation (C) would give a value lower than $60$, not higher. **Answer: D.**
Vapours of volatile liquids deviate from ideal gas behavior.
Ethanoic acid decomposes to methane and carbon dioxide.
Ethanoic acid vapour exists in the form of the dimers.

When the compound represented by the structural formula $\mathrm{C_6H_5{-}O{-}CHO}$ (phenyl methanoate: a benzene ring bonded to $\mathrm{O{-}C(=O){-}H}$) is warmed with aqueous solution of dilute sodium hydroxide, the most likely products formed are

The ester link $\mathrm{HCOO{-}C_6H_5}$ is hydrolysed by hydroxide into the alcohol-type part (phenol, from the $\mathrm{C_6H_5{-}O}$ side) and the acid part, which in alkaline solution is present as its sodium salt: $\mathrm{HCOOC_6H_5} + \mathrm{NaOH} \rightarrow \mathrm{HCOONa} + \mathrm{C_6H_5OH}$. Free methanoic acid (B) cannot exist in alkali; A and D name products (benzoic acid, methanol) that do not come from this ester. **Answer: C.**
The two nuclei in the hydrogen molecule ion ($\mathrm{H_2^+}$) are held together by

$\mathrm{H_2^+}$ contains two protons and one electron. The two nuclei repel each other; they are held together because the single electron's charge cloud lies between them and attracts both nuclei: this is a (one-electron) covalent bond, i.e. mutual sharing of the electron charge cloud. There are no ions of opposite charge (A), and C is wrong because the nuclei are not attracted to each other. **Answer: D.**
electrostatic attraction between the two hydrogen atoms.
mutual sharing of the electron charge cloud.
The acidity constant of propanoic acid is $1.26 \times 10^{-5}$. What is the pH of a $0.1\ \mathrm{M}$ solution of this acid?

For a weak acid, $[\mathrm{H^+}] = \sqrt{K_a c} = \sqrt{1.26 \times 10^{-5} \times 0.1} = 1.12 \times 10^{-3}\ \mathrm{M}$, so $\mathrm{pH} = -\log(1.12 \times 10^{-3}) = 2.95$. A is the pH of a $0.1\ \mathrm{M}$ strong acid. **Answer: D.**
Which of the following statements is true?

The larger the cation down a group, the less it polarises the carbonate ion, so the carbonates are harder to decompose: thermal stability increases down both groups. A is false ($\mathrm{BeO}$ is amphoteric). B is the wrong way round (Group 2 sulphate solubility decreases down the group). D is false (beryllium does not react with water). **Answer: C.**
All oxides of the s-block elements are basic.
The solubility of Group 1 sulphates decreases down the group while that of Group 2 sulphates increases down the group.
The thermal stability of the carbonates of the s-block elements increases down both Groups 1 and 2.
Beryllium and magnesium both react with water to form basic hydroxides.
Which of the following steps is unlikely to occur in the chlorination of methane?

Free radical substitution: initiation $\mathrm{Cl_2} \rightarrow 2\mathrm{Cl^\bullet}$ (B), propagation $\mathrm{CH_4} + \mathrm{Cl^\bullet} \rightarrow \mathrm{CH_3^\bullet} + \mathrm{HCl}$ (D) then $\mathrm{CH_3^\bullet} + \mathrm{Cl_2} \rightarrow \mathrm{CH_3Cl} + \mathrm{Cl^\bullet}$ (C). There is no hydrogen gas in the mixture and the $\mathrm{H{-}H}$ bond is not broken: A is unlikely. **Answer: A.**

Two pure liquids, S and T, which form an ideal mixture, have vapour pressures $12.9\ \mathrm{kPa}$ and $26.8\ \mathrm{kPa}$ respectively at $25\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$. What is the vapour pressure of a mixture containing $2.0$ moles of S and $1.0$ mole of T and $25\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$.

Raoult's law: $x_S = \tfrac{2}{3}$, $x_T = \tfrac{1}{3}$. $P = \tfrac{2}{3}(12.9) + \tfrac{1}{3}(26.8) = 8.60 + 8.93 = 17.5\ \mathrm{kPa}$. A just adds the two vapour pressures; D is the mean of the two with equal weights. **Answer: C.**
Which of the following is the product formed when acidified sodium dichromate(VI) oxidises propan-2-ol (2-propanol)?

Propan-2-ol is a secondary alcohol: oxidation gives a ketone, propanone, $(\mathrm{CH_3})_2\mathrm{CO}$, which resists further oxidation. Propanal and propanoic acid come from the primary alcohol propan-1-ol; methoxyethane is an ether. **Answer: B.**
In which of the following solutions will the reaction with $1.0\ \mathrm{g}$ $\mathrm{CaCO_3}$ be fastest?

The rate depends on the concentration of $\mathrm{H^+}$, not on the volume of acid. $\mathrm{HCl}$ and $\mathrm{HNO_3}$ are fully ionised: C has $[\mathrm{H^+}] = 2.0\ \mathrm{M}$, B $1.0\ \mathrm{M}$, D $0.5\ \mathrm{M}$. For sulphuric acid only the first ionisation is complete; the second ($\mathrm{HSO_4^-} \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{H^+} + \mathrm{SO_4^{2-}}$, $K_a \approx 0.01$) is only slight, so $[\mathrm{H^+}]$ in $1.0\ \mathrm{M}$ $\mathrm{H_2SO_4}$ is only about $1.0\ \mathrm{M}$ (not $2.0$), and the insoluble $\mathrm{CaSO_4}$ formed also coats the carbonate. The fastest reaction is with C. $1.0\ \mathrm{g}$ $\mathrm{CaCO_3}$ ($0.01\ \mathrm{mol}$) needs $0.02\ \mathrm{mol}$ $\mathrm{H^+}$, which every option supplies in excess. **Answer: C.**
A sample of oxygen gas contains $^{16}\mathrm{O}$ and $^{18}\mathrm{O}$. The peaks in the mass spectrum of the oxygen sample would be at mass numbers

Oxygen gas is $\mathrm{O_2}$. In the spectrometer the molecules give molecular ions $^{16}\mathrm{O}{-}^{16}\mathrm{O}^+$ ($32$), $^{16}\mathrm{O}{-}^{18}\mathrm{O}^+$ ($34$) and $^{18}\mathrm{O}{-}^{18}\mathrm{O}^+$ ($36$), and fragmentation gives the atomic ions $^{16}\mathrm{O}^+$ ($16$) and $^{18}\mathrm{O}^+$ ($18$). The mixed molecule at $34$ is the one most easily forgotten (option C). **Answer: D.**
One property of a buffer solution, prepared from a weak acid and its sodium salt is that

Adding the sodium salt supplies the conjugate base, which suppresses the ionisation of the acid ($\mathrm{HA} \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{H^+} + \mathrm{A^-}$ shifts left), so $[\mathrm{H^+}]$ falls and the pH rises above that of the acid alone. B is false because a buffer resists only small additions (its capacity is limited) and D is false (the pH depends on $pK_a$ and the ratio salt/acid). **Answer: C.**
its pH is less than the pH of the original acid
its pH is unaffected by the addition of any quantity of $\mathrm{H^+}$ ions
its pH is greater than the pH of the original acid
Which of the following species is trigonal bipyramidal?
Five bonding pairs and no lone pair give a trigonal bipyramid: $\mathrm{PCl_5}$. The other three species have four bonding pairs and no lone pair, so they are tetrahedral. **Answer: C.**
An oxidizing agent is a species that
An oxidising agent takes electrons from another species and is itself reduced (its oxidation number decreases). A, C and D describe a reducing agent. **Answer: B.**
has an increase in oxidation state
The half-life of radioactive $^{233}_{91}\mathrm{Pa}$ is $28$ days. How many days will it take for the radioactivity to fall to one-eighth of the initial value?
$\tfrac{1}{8} = (\tfrac{1}{2})^3$, so three half-lives are needed: $3 \times 28 = 84$ days. **Answer: B.**
In the production of sulphuric acid, the sulphur trioxide in the Contact process is

Dissolving $\mathrm{SO_3}$ directly in water is violent and forms a corrosive acid mist, so it is not done. In the Contact process the gas is passed into concentrated (about 98 %) sulphuric acid, which absorbs it to form oleum, $\mathrm{H_2S_2O_7}$: $\mathrm{SO_3} + \mathrm{H_2SO_4} \rightarrow \mathrm{H_2S_2O_7}$; the oleum is then diluted with water to give sulphuric acid. Liquefying under pressure (D) is not part of the process. **Answer: C.**
dissolved in oleum or fuming sulphuric acid

What colour would be observed when iron(III) chloride is added to the following equilibrium reaction? $\mathrm{Fe^{3+}(aq)} + 3\mathrm{CNS^-(aq)} \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{Fe(CNS)_3(aq)}$ (pale yellow, colourless, blood red)

Adding $\mathrm{FeCl_3}$ increases $[\mathrm{Fe^{3+}}]$. By Le Chatelier's principle the equilibrium shifts to the right to use up the extra ion, forming more $\mathrm{Fe(CNS)_3}$: the blood-red colour deepens. **Answer: B.**

Select the compound which is optically active from the list below. (Printed structures: A $\mathrm{CH_3CH_2COCH_2CH_3}$; B $(\mathrm{CH_3})_2\mathrm{CHCOOCH_3}$; C $(\mathrm{CH_3})_2\mathrm{CHCH(OH)CH_3}$; D $(\mathrm{CH_3})_2\mathrm{CHCHO}$.)

A compound is optically active if it has a chiral carbon (four different groups). In C, the carbon bearing the $\mathrm{OH}$ has $\mathrm{H}$, $\mathrm{OH}$, $\mathrm{CH_3}$ and $\mathrm{CH(CH_3)_2}$: four different groups (3-methylbutan-2-ol). In A, B and D there is no carbon with four different groups (the $\mathrm{CH}$ in B and D carries two identical methyl groups). **Answer: C.**
Which of the following statements is true for a pair of miscible liquids whose mixture shows negative deviation from Raoult's Law?

Negative deviation means the A-B attractions are stronger than A-A and B-B: molecules escape less easily, so the vapour pressure is lower than Raoult's law predicts (A). The mixing is exothermic (temperature rises, so B is false), the volume decreases (D is false) and the forces are strengthened, not broken (C). **Answer: A.**
Slight drop in temperature is observed when the liquids are mixed.
The total volume of the mixture is increased.

Given a cell composed of the following half-cells: $\mathrm{I_2(aq), 2I^-(aq)/Pt}$ $E^\circ = +0.544\ \mathrm{V}$; $\mathrm{Fe^{3+}(aq), Fe^{2+}(aq)/Pt}$ $E^\circ = +0.770\ \mathrm{V}$. Which of the following species is the strongest reducing agent?

The reduced species of the couple with the lower (less positive) $E^\circ$ is the stronger reducing agent. $E^\circ(\mathrm{I_2/I^-}) = +0.544\ \mathrm{V} < E^\circ(\mathrm{Fe^{3+}/Fe^{2+}}) = +0.770\ \mathrm{V}$, so $\mathrm{I^-}$ gives up electrons more readily than $\mathrm{Fe^{2+}}$. $\mathrm{I_2}$ and $\mathrm{Fe^{3+}}$ are oxidising agents. **Answer: D.**
A possible isomer of buta-1,3-diene (1,3-butadiene), $\mathrm{CH_2{=}CH{-}CH{=}CH_2}$ is

Buta-1,3-diene is $\mathrm{C_4H_6}$; an isomer must have the same molecular formula. Butyne is $\mathrm{C_4H_6}$ (e.g. but-1-yne, but-2-yne). Cyclobutane and butene are $\mathrm{C_4H_8}$ and cyclobutadiene is $\mathrm{C_4H_4}$. **Answer: C.**
The reaction $\mathrm{H_2O} + \mathrm{NH_3} \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{NH_4OH}$ could be classified as

$\mathrm{NH_3}$ accepts a proton from water ($\mathrm{NH_3} + \mathrm{H_2O} \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{NH_4^+} + \mathrm{OH^-}$): a Bronsted-Lowry acid-base reaction. No oxidation numbers change, so it is not redox or disproportionation. **Answer: C.**
For the Group 14 (Group IV) elements C to Pb;

The bonds from hydrogen to the element get longer and weaker down the group, so the thermal stability of the hydrides $\mathrm{CH_4} > \mathrm{SiH_4} > \mathrm{GeH_4} > \mathrm{SnH_4} > \mathrm{PbH_4}$ decreases: D is true. A is false (the $+2$ state becomes more stable down the group: inert pair effect). B is false ($\mathrm{CCl_4}$ does not hydrolyse, having no available $d$ orbitals). C is not correct either, since $\mathrm{PbO_2}$ is amphoteric. **Answer: D.**
The stability of +2 oxidation state decreases down the group
All the tetrachlorides hydrolyze in water to give acidic solutions
PbO is amphoteric while $\mathrm{PbO_2}$ is acidic
The stability of the tetrahydrides decreases down the group

K, L and M are elements in the same short period of the Periodic Table. The oxide of K is a giant molecule, the oxide of L is a simple molecular and the oxide of M is ionic. Arrange the elements in increasing atomic number.

Across a short period the oxides change from ionic (metals, left: e.g. $\mathrm{Na_2O}$, $\mathrm{MgO}$) through giant covalent ($\mathrm{SiO_2}$, middle) to simple molecular ($\mathrm{P_4O_{10}}$, $\mathrm{SO_2}$, right). In order of increasing atomic number: M (ionic), K (giant), L (simple molecular). **Answer: B.**
Which of the following gases has the highest volume at STP? (RAM: He = 4; O = 16; Cl = 35.5; N = 14)

At STP equal amounts of gas occupy equal volumes. Helium is monatomic: $4.0\ \mathrm{g} \div 4 = 1.0\ \mathrm{mol}$. The others are diatomic gases: $\mathrm{N_2}$ $14.0/28 = 0.50\ \mathrm{mol}$, $\mathrm{O_2}$ $16.0/32 = 0.50\ \mathrm{mol}$, $\mathrm{Cl_2}$ $35.5/71 = 0.50\ \mathrm{mol}$. Helium has the largest amount, hence the largest volume. **Answer: A.**

Which of the following compounds will give a yellow precipitate when reacted with a solution of potassium iodide (KI) and sodium hypochlorite (NaOCl)?

1. $\mathrm{CH_3CH_2OH}$
2. $\mathrm{CH_3CHO}$
3. $\mathrm{C_6H_5COCH_3}$

KI with NaOCl generates iodine/hypoiodite, i.e. the iodoform test. It gives yellow $\mathrm{CHI_3}$ with compounds containing $\mathrm{CH_3CO{-}}$ or $\mathrm{CH_3CH(OH){-}}$. Ethanol (1) is oxidised to ethanal, ethanal (2) has $\mathrm{CH_3CO{-}H}$, and phenylethanone (3) has $\mathrm{CH_3CO{-}C_6H_5}$: all three are positive. **Answer: A.**

From the following data: $\mathrm{Zn^{2+}(aq)/Zn(s)}$ $E^\circ = -0.76\ \mathrm{V}$; $\mathrm{Fe^{3+}(aq)/Fe^{2+}(aq)}$ $E^\circ = -0.77\ \mathrm{V}$ (as printed). It can be deduced that

1. The standard emf for the cell $\mathrm{Zn(s)/Zn^{2+}(aq)\,||\,Fe^{3+}(aq)/Fe^{2+}(aq)/Pt}$ is $-1.54\ \mathrm{V}$
2. Zinc is a more powerful reductant than $\mathrm{Fe^{2+}(aq)}$
3. $\mathrm{Fe^{3+}(aq)}$ can oxidized Zinc under standard condition

*Options as printed:* A) 1, 2 and 3 are all correct   B) 1 and 2 only are correct   C) 2 and 3 only are correct   D) 3 only is correct

The printed $E^\circ(\mathrm{Fe^{3+}/Fe^{2+}}) = -0.77\ \mathrm{V}$ is a misprint: the correct value is $+0.77\ \mathrm{V}$ (the same couple is given as $+0.770\ \mathrm{V}$ in question 31). With $+0.77\ \mathrm{V}$: statement 1: $E^\circ_{cell} = E^\circ_{right} - E^\circ_{left} = +0.77 - (-0.76) = +1.53\ \mathrm{V}$, not $-1.54\ \mathrm{V}$: false. Statement 2: $\mathrm{Zn}$ ($E^\circ = -0.76$) is a much stronger reductant than $\mathrm{Fe^{2+}}$ ($+0.77$): true. Statement 3: $E^\circ_{cell} > 0$, so $\mathrm{Fe^{3+}}$ oxidises zinc: true. Statements 2 and 3 only. With the printed $-0.77\ \mathrm{V}$ the three statements would all be false (cell emf $-0.01\ \mathrm{V}$), which no option offers.

**Intended answer: C (2 and 3 only are correct).**

The anomalous behavior of lithium (Li) in group I can be attributed to:

1. its high electropositivity
2. its small size
3. the ability of $\mathrm{Li^+}$ ions to polarize small anions like $\mathrm{N^{3-}}$

Lithium differs from the rest of Group 1 because the $\mathrm{Li^+}$ ion is very small with a high charge density (2: true), so it strongly polarises anions such as $\mathrm{N^{3-}}$ (3: true, $\mathrm{Li_3N}$ forms; compare $\mathrm{Li_2CO_3}$ decomposing easily). High electropositivity (1) is a property of all Group 1 metals and does not explain the anomaly. **Answer: C.**

Which of the following pairs of compounds will form an ideal mixture?

1. $\mathrm{CHCl_3}$ and $\mathrm{CH_3COCH_3}$
2. $\mathrm{H_2O}$ and $\mathrm{HNO_3}$
3. benzene and methylbenzene (printed as their structural formulae)

An ideal mixture needs A-B forces equal to A-A and B-B forces. Trichloromethane/propanone (1) form hydrogen bonds with each other and show negative deviation; water/nitric acid (2) also strongly attract each other (negative deviation). Benzene and methylbenzene (3) are similar non-polar molecules with the same type of van der Waals forces and give an ideal mixture. **Answer: D.**

The graph of boiling point against hydrides of Group 14, 15, 16, 17 (Group IV, V, VI, VII) reveals that:

1. The boiling points of the hydrides of the Group 14 element increases down the group due to increase in van der waal's forces.
2. The boiling points of the first members of the hydrides of Group 15, 16 and 17 have abnormally high boiling points because their molecules are held by hydrogen bonds.
3. The boiling points of the hydrides of Group 17 decrease down the group due to decrease in the strength of the hydrogen bonds.

1 is true: the Group 14 hydrides are non-polar and their boiling points rise as the molecules get larger (stronger van der Waals forces). 2 is true: $\mathrm{NH_3}$, $\mathrm{H_2O}$ and $\mathrm{HF}$ have unusually high boiling points because of hydrogen bonding. 3 is false: after $\mathrm{HF}$ (hydrogen-bonded, highest), the boiling points of $\mathrm{HCl}$, $\mathrm{HBr}$ and $\mathrm{HI}$ increase down the group, because van der Waals forces increase; the trend is not a uniform decrease. 1 and 2 only. **Answer: B.**

The two isomers corresponding to the molecular formula $\mathrm{C_3H_6O_2}$

1. can be distinguished using $\mathrm{PCl_5}$
2. are functional group isomers
3. will undergo condensation reaction

*Options as printed:* A) 1, 2 and 3 are all correct   B) 1 and 2 only are correct   C) 2 and 3 only are correct   D) 3 only is correct

The printed question does not say which two isomers are meant, so the intended pair has to be inferred: propanoic acid $\mathrm{CH_3CH_2COOH}$ and methyl ethanoate $\mathrm{CH_3COOCH_3}$ are the usual pair. 1: $\mathrm{PCl_5}$ reacts with the acid (misty fumes of $\mathrm{HCl}$) but not with the ester: true. 2: an acid and an ester are functional group isomers: true. 3: only the acid undergoes a condensation reaction (esterification with an alcohol); the ester does not: not true of both isomers. 1 and 2 only.

**Intended answer: B (1 and 2 only are correct).**

The Rutherford gold-foil experiment led to the discovery of

1. The electron
2. The neutron
3. The position and properties of the nucleus

The electron was discovered by J. J. Thomson (cathode rays) and the neutron by Chadwick. In the gold-foil experiment most alpha particles passed through but a few were strongly deflected, showing a small, dense, positively charged nucleus at the centre of the atom. 3 only. **Answer: D.**

Phenylamine ($\mathrm{C_6H_5NH_2}$) is a brown liquid.

1. It is insoluble in water but soluble in dilute acids
2. It will react with bromine water to give a white precipitate
3. It can be separated from the reaction mixture when prepared by reduction of nitrobenzene by steam distillation

1 is true: the large phenyl group makes it insoluble in water, but the amine group is protonated by dilute acid to give the soluble $\mathrm{C_6H_5NH_3^+}$ salt. 2 is true: the ring is strongly activated and gives a white precipitate of 2,4,6-tribromophenylamine. 3 is true: phenylamine is volatile in steam and immiscible with water, so it can be steam distilled from the mixture. All three. **Answer: A.**

Which of the following group 14 (Group IV) element/compounds have giant covalent lattices?

1. $\mathrm{SiO_2}$
2. Ge
3. $\mathrm{SnO_2}$

$\mathrm{SiO_2}$ (1) has a giant covalent lattice and germanium (2) has the same diamond-type giant covalent structure. $\mathrm{SnO_2}$ (3) is a metal oxide with the rutile structure, usually described as a giant ionic lattice (it is not classed as giant covalent at this level). 1 and 2 only. **Answer: B.**

The solubility of ionic compounds depends on

1. the strength of the electrostatic attraction between the oppositely charged ions
2. hydration energy
3. the sizes of the ions

Dissolving requires the lattice energy (electrostatic attraction between ions, 1) to be compensated by the hydration energy (2); both depend on the sizes and charges of the ions (3). All three. **Answer: A.**

**First statement:** Chlorination of methyl benzene in UV light proceeds via free radical substitution

**Second statement:** Methyl benzene is oxidized to benzoic acid by $\mathrm{H^+/KMnO_4(aq)}$

First: true. In UV light, chlorine radicals substitute a hydrogen of the $\mathrm{CH_3}$ side chain by a free radical mechanism. Second: true, hot acidified $\mathrm{KMnO_4}$ oxidises the side chain to $\mathrm{C_6H_5COOH}$. The oxidation does not explain why UV light gives free radical substitution, so the second statement is not an explanation. **Answer: B.**
Both statements are true and the second statement is a CORRECT explanation of the first statement.
Both statements are true and the second statement is NOT a CORRECT explanation of the first statement.
The first statement is true, but the second statement is false.
The first statement is false, but the second statement is true.

**First statement:** The hydrogen atom shows only one series of spectral lines

**Second statement:** The hydrogen atom contains only one electron

First: false. The hydrogen atom shows several series (Lyman in the UV, Balmer in the visible, Paschen, ...), each for transitions to a different lower level. Second: true, hydrogen has one electron. **Answer: D.**

**First statement:** All d-block elements are transition metals

**Second statement:** Transition metals and compounds function as catalyst because they contain available empty d-orbital's

First: false. A transition element forms at least one ion with a partly filled $d$ subshell; scandium ($\mathrm{Sc^{3+}}$, $3d^0$) and zinc ($\mathrm{Zn^{2+}}$, $3d^{10}$) are d-block elements but not transition elements. Second: true, the available $d$ orbitals (and variable oxidation states) allow transition metals to act as catalysts. **Answer: D.**
Both statements are true and the second statement is a CORRECT explanation of the first statement.
Both statements are true and the second statement is NOT a CORRECT explanation of the first statement.
The first statement is true, but the second statement is false.
The first statement is false, but the second statement is true.

**First statement:** Ethoxyethane has a lower boiling point than butan-1-ol (1-butanol).

**Second statement:** Butan-1-ol (1-butanol) molecules are held by hydrogen bonds which are stronger than van der waal's forces of attraction in ethoxyethane.

First: true ($34.6\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$ against $117\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$). Second: true: butan-1-ol has an $\mathrm{O{-}H}$ group and forms hydrogen bonds, while the ether has none (only van der Waals and weak dipole forces). The stronger intermolecular forces in the alcohol are exactly why its boiling point is higher: a correct explanation. **Answer: A.**
Both statements are true and the second statement is a CORRECT explanation of the first statement.

State the property which is used to classify elements into groups of the Periodic Table.

Elements in the same group have the same number of electrons in their outer (valence) shell, and this is why they have similar chemical properties. The number of shells gives the period, and the number of protons (atomic number) gives the order of the elements. **Answer: C.**
A substance whose aqueous or molten form conducts electricity is called:

An electrolyte is a compound that conducts electricity when molten or dissolved in water, because its ions are free to move, and it is decomposed in the process. A metal is a conductor but conducts as a solid. Non-conductors and insulators never conduct. **Answer: D.**
Fractional distillation of liquid air is used to obtain:

Air is cooled until it is liquid (water vapour and carbon dioxide are removed first), then warmed slowly. The components boil off at different temperatures: nitrogen (b.p. $-196\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$) first, then argon and oxygen ($-183\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$). Hydrogen is not a component of air. **Answer: D.**
An element X has atomic symbol ${}^{23}_{11}X$. How many neutrons are found in the nucleus of X?
Number of neutrons = mass number $-$ atomic number $= 23 - 11 = 12$. The distractors are the mass number (23), the atomic number (11) and their sum (34). **Answer: C.**
Which of the following metals is extracted by electrolysis?

Aluminium is high in the reactivity series, so carbon cannot reduce its oxide: it is extracted by the electrolysis of molten aluminium oxide (alumina) dissolved in molten cryolite. Iron and zinc are extracted by reduction with carbon or carbon monoxide in a furnace; copper is obtained by roasting its ores and is then refined by electrolysis, but it is not extracted by electrolysis. **Answer: B.**

Which of the following structures represents 1,2-dibromopropane?

![Structural formulae A to D (question 6)](/media/figures/cm/gce-ol-chemistry-2017-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_1.webp)

*Options: the structures A, B, C and D in the figure.*

1,2-Dibromopropane is propane ($\mathrm{CH_3CH_2CH_3}$) with one bromine atom on carbon 1 and one on carbon 2: $\mathrm{CH_2BrCHBrCH_3}$. Reading each structure: **A** has Br on carbons 1 and 3 (1,3-dibromopropane); **B** has three Br atoms (one on C1, two on C2); **C** has one Br on C1 and one Br on C2, and C3 is $\mathrm{CH_3}$, which is 1,2-dibromopropane; **D** has two Br atoms on the same carbon C1 (1,1-dibromopropane). **Answer: C.**
A halogen that is used in making toothpaste is:

Fluoride (from fluorine, a Group 7 element) is added to toothpaste as sodium fluoride or sodium monofluorophosphate, because it strengthens tooth enamel and reduces decay. Chlorine is used to treat water, iodine as an antiseptic and bromine in making some dyes and fumigants. (The word "Chloride" in option A is an ion and not a halogen element.) **Answer: C.**

*Questions 8-10 concern the following experiment.* $20\ \mathrm{cm^3}$ of $2\ \mathrm{M}$ $\mathrm{NaOH}$ is quickly mixed with $20\ \mathrm{cm^3}$ of $2\ \mathrm{M}$ $\mathrm{H_2SO_4}$ in a plastic cup. The temperature changes from $25.2\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$ to $38\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$.

8. Which one of the following describes the above reaction?

*Options as printed:* A) Neutralization reaction   B) Exothermic reaction   C) Precipitation reaction   D) Acid-base reaction

The temperature of the mixture rises from $25.2\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$ to $38\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$, so heat is given out to the surroundings: the reaction is **exothermic**. Select a substance whose bonding involves the formation of ions.

Sodium chloride is formed when a sodium atom gives one electron to a chlorine atom, giving $\mathrm{Na^+}$ and $\mathrm{Cl^-}$ ions (ionic bonding). Ammonia, hydrogen and nitrogen are covalent molecules in which atoms share electrons. **Answer: D.**
Why do farmers apply fertilizers to their farms?

Crops take nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium out of the soil. Fertilizers (for example $\mathrm{NH_4NO_3}$, $\mathrm{(NH_4)_2SO_4}$, NPK mixtures) put these plant nutrients back so that crops grow well. Their purpose is not to change the pH of the soil, and sulphates are not the main nutrients replaced. **Answer: C.**

Determine the empirical formula of the compound when $0.6\ \mathrm{g}$ of carbon combines with $1.6\ \mathrm{g}$ of sulphur.

Moles of C $= 0.6 \div 12.0 = 0.05$; moles of S $= 1.6 \div 32.0 = 0.05$. The mole ratio $\mathrm{C} : \mathrm{S} = 0.05 : 0.05 = 1 : 1$, so the empirical formula is $\mathrm{CS}$. The components of a mixture are not chemically combined, so they keep their own properties and can be separated by physical methods (filtration, distillation, using a magnet, a separating funnel...). Identify the products formed when solid magnesium nitrate is strongly heated.

Nitrates of metals in the middle of the reactivity series (such as magnesium) decompose on strong heating to the metal oxide, brown nitrogen dioxide gas and oxygen: $2\mathrm{Mg(NO_3)_2} \rightarrow 2\mathrm{MgO} + 4\mathrm{NO_2} + \mathrm{O_2}$. Caesium (Cs) and sodium (Na) are found in Group 1 of the Periodic Table. Write the formula of the oxide of caesium.

Caesium is in Group 1 like sodium, so it forms the $\mathrm{Cs^+}$ ion. The oxide ion is $\mathrm{O^{2-}}$, so two $\mathrm{Cs^+}$ ions balance one $\mathrm{O^{2-}}$ ion: the formula is $\mathrm{Cs_2O}$, like $\mathrm{Na_2O}$. **Answer: A.**
An organic liquid, W, has no effect on litmus. On addition of a few crystals of phosphorus pentachloride to the liquid, white fumes are evolved. W could be:

Phosphorus pentachloride is the test for the $-\mathrm{OH}$ group: it reacts with an alcohol to give steamy white fumes of hydrogen chloride, e.g. $\mathrm{CH_3CH_2OH} + \mathrm{PCl_5} \rightarrow \mathrm{CH_3CH_2Cl} + \mathrm{POCl_3} + \mathrm{HCl}$. Which of the following processes DOES NOT involve the large scale use of limestone?

Limestone ($\mathrm{CaCO_3}$) is heated to make quicklime ($\mathrm{CaO}$), added to the blast furnace to remove silica as slag, and heated with clay to make cement. Soap is made from fats or oils and sodium hydroxide, so it does not use limestone. **Answer: D.**
Which of the following natural processes is catalyzed by light?

In photosynthesis, green plants use light energy (absorbed by chlorophyll) to change carbon dioxide and water into glucose and oxygen: $6\mathrm{CO_2} + 6\mathrm{H_2O} \rightarrow \mathrm{C_6H_{12}O_6} + 6\mathrm{O_2}$. When $2.0\ \mathrm{g}$ each of powdered diamond and graphite are burnt in excess air:

Diamond and graphite are both pure carbon (allotropes), so $2.0\ \mathrm{g}$ of each contains the same number of moles of carbon: $2.0 \div 12 = 0.167\ \mathrm{mol}$. Each mole of carbon gives one mole of $\mathrm{CO_2}$ ($\mathrm{C} + \mathrm{O_2} \rightarrow \mathrm{CO_2}$), so the same volume of carbon dioxide is produced. A gas occupies a volume of $211\ \mathrm{cm^3}$ at $18\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$. What volume will it occupy at $28\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$?

Assuming a fixed pressure and amount of gas, Charles's law gives $V_1/T_1 = V_2/T_2$ with temperatures in kelvin ($0\ ^\circ\mathrm{C} = 273\ \mathrm{K}$): $T_1 = 291\ \mathrm{K}$, $T_2 = 301\ \mathrm{K}$. $V_2 = 211 \times 301/291 = 218.3\ \mathrm{cm^3}$. The gas expands when heated, so $V_2 > 211$ (B is wrong), and using $^\circ\mathrm{C}$ instead of kelvin gives a very different answer. **Answer: A.**

Catalytic oxidation or reduction is used in the manufacture of the following heavy chemicals EXCEPT:

Ammonia is made by the Haber process (nitrogen and hydrogen over an iron catalyst), nitric acid by the Ostwald process (oxidation of ammonia on platinum) and sulphuric acid by the Contact process (oxidation of $\mathrm{SO_2}$ over $\mathrm{V_2O_5}$). $\mathrm{Cu^{2+}}$ ions give a pale blue gelatinous precipitate of copper(II) hydroxide with $\mathrm{NaOH}$, insoluble in excess. $\mathrm{Fe^{2+}}$ gives a green precipitate, $\mathrm{Fe^{3+}}$ a red-brown one, and copper(I) compounds (rarely found in solution) give a yellow or orange precipitate. **Answer: A.**

A student got stung by bees on campus, sodium hydrogen carbonate was used in treating this bee sting. What chemical substance is found in bee sting?

What is the major effect of sulphur dioxide emission into the atmosphere?

Two elements, X and Y have electronic configurations 2, 4 and 2, 8, 7 respectively. Identify the bond type in a compound formed between X and Y.

How many Faradays of electricity will be needed to pass through a solution in which $5.5\ \mathrm{A}$ of electricity are allowed to run through for $1$ hour?

Dry ice (Cardice) is a refrigerant that sublimes. The particles that make up dry ice are:

A foreigner can acquire Cameroonian citizenship by ...

A foreigner who meets the conditions set by law (for example a period of residence in the country) and applies for it can be granted Cameroonian nationality. Which of the following is a right of a citizen?
