*SECTION V - directions as printed, summarised:* Each question consists of four lettered headings A, B, C, D. Select the heading which is closely related to the description which follows.

A carbohydrate digesting enzyme
Ptyalin (salivary amylase) digests starch to maltose. Rennin and pepsin digest protein in the stomach and trypsin digests protein in the small intestine. **Answer: B.**
Edaphic factors are the properties of the soil (pH or acidity, water content, minerals, texture). Temperature, light and pressure are climatic factors. **Answer: D.**

Genes are located along the chromosomes, which therefore carry them. Genotype and phenotype are the genetic make-up and the observable features, and 'recessive' describes an allele that is masked. **Answer: B.**
Made up of organisms of the same species.

A population is all the organisms of one species living in an area. A community has many species, an ecosystem is the community plus its environment, and the biosphere is all the places on Earth where life exists. **Answer: C.**

Antibodies are made by lymphocytes, a type of leucocyte (white blood cell). Platelets help clotting, plasma is the liquid that carries substances (it carries antibodies but does not make them), and erythrocytes (red cells) carry oxygen. **Answer: D.**

The synovial membrane lining the joint capsule secretes synovial fluid, which lubricates the joint. Cartilage reduces friction and absorbs shocks, ligaments join bone to bone, and bone provides support. **Answer: A.**
Deficiency of this vitamin results in bleeding gums.

Lack of vitamin C (ascorbic acid) causes scurvy, with bleeding gums and slow healing of wounds. Vitamin D deficiency causes rickets, vitamin A deficiency causes night blindness and vitamin B deficiency causes beriberi (B1) or other disorders. **Answer: B.**

The habitat is the place where an organism lives (for example a pond for a frog). An ecosystem and a community are larger units containing many species, and the environment is all the surroundings. **Answer: D.**
Its destruction will interrupt movement of water in plants.

Water and mineral salts move up the plant in the xylem vessels. The phloem carries manufactured food, cambium is a tissue that makes new xylem and phloem, and the cortex is a storage and support tissue. **Answer: B.**
Deficiency of iodine in the diet will lead to its malfunctioning.
Iodine is needed to make thyroxine, the hormone of the thyroid gland. Without iodine the gland enlarges to form a goitre and works badly. The other glands do not need iodine. **Answer: A.**

*SECTION VI - directions as printed, summarised:* This group of questions deals with biological situations. Select the best answer for each question.

Given that black fur is dominant over grey fur in mice, which of the options is the result of crossing a heterozygous black mouse and a grey mouse?

Let B = black (dominant) and b = grey (recessive). The heterozygous black mouse is Bb and the grey mouse is bb. Gametes: B or b from the first parent, only b from the second. Offspring: Bb (black) and bb (grey) in the ratio 1 : 1, so half the offspring are black. **Answer: C.**
In testing a leaf for starch, the leaf is first boiled in water to

Boiling in water kills the leaf cells at once, so all chemical reactions and enzyme action stop and the starch present is preserved (it can no longer be changed to sugar or used); it also breaks the cell membranes so that the iodine can enter. Option C is wrong because boiling destroys (denatures) the enzymes, not just slows them, and D is the opposite of what happens. Softening is only a secondary effect. **Answer: B.**
To speed up the conversion of glucose to starch.
At the start of seed germination, water

A dry seed has very little water. When the seed absorbs water, its enzymes are activated and start to digest the stored food (starch, protein, fat) into soluble substances that are carried to the embryo. The testa splits because of swelling, but that is a later effect, the micropyle is only the small pore for water entry, and food is produced by the enzymes from stored reserves, not by the water itself. **Answer: A.**
A drop in dry mass of a seed occurs at the beginning of germination due to

Before the seedling has leaves, it cannot photosynthesise. It respires, using up stored food (and releasing carbon dioxide and water), so the dry mass falls. Water evaporation does not change dry mass (water has been removed), and the digestion of reserves only changes insoluble food into soluble food without losing mass. **Answer: B.**
Maize plants interspersed with leguminous plants will look greener because

Leguminous plants (beans, groundnuts) have root nodules with nitrogen-fixing bacteria (Rhizobium) that turn atmospheric nitrogen into nitrates in the soil. Maize uses nitrates to make proteins and chlorophyll, so it is greener. Shade, less water loss and more water are not effects of legumes on maize. **Answer: D.**
The leguminous plants give shed to the maize.
The leguminous plants reduce water loss.
The leguminous plants make more water available to the maize.
The leguminous plants increase the nitrogen content of the soil.
The percentage of carbon dioxide, in expired air is more than that in inspired air

Carbon dioxide is a waste product of cell respiration in the tissues. The blood carries it to the lungs, where it diffuses into the alveoli and is breathed out, so expired air has about 4% against 0.04% in inspired air. B is false because the lungs do not produce carbon dioxide; C and D are not the reason. **Answer: A.**
It is produced in tissue respiration.
Much carbon dioxide is produced in the lungs.
It is not useful in the body.
Roofs of houses in industrial areas are often corroded due to,

Factories release sulphur dioxide and nitrogen oxides. These dissolve in rain water to form acid rain, which corrodes metal roofs. The cause is therefore the chemicals dissolved in the atmosphere (C). Smoke itself (soot) is not the corroding agent, and rain alone or poor material would not explain why industrial areas are particularly affected. **Answer: C.**
Presence of dissolved chemicals in the atmosphere.
The wilting of a newly transplanted well watered seedling on a sunny day is due to

A transplanted seedling has lost many root hairs, so it takes up little water, while on a sunny day the leaves lose water quickly by transpiration. Loss exceeds uptake, the cells lose turgor and the plant wilts. Light intensity and temperature act only through the rate of transpiration. **Answer: D.**
High rate of transpiration and little water uptake.
Bread left on the kitchen window for two days moulds due to

Mould is a fungus (Mucor, Rhizopus). Spores from the air land on the moist, starchy bread and germinate into hyphae that digest the bread. Bacteria and viruses do not make a furry mould, and moisture absorption alone does not produce mould. **Answer: A.**
Growth of fungal spores from the air.
Absorption of moisture from the air.

![Graph of rate of reaction against temperature: the rate rises from a low value to a maximum and then falls sharply at high temperature (Question 50). Axes have no numerical scale. Redrawn from the printed graph.](/media/figures/cm/gce-ol-biology-2016-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_4.webp)

From the graph above showing the effect of temperature on the rate of enzyme controlled reaction, which of the following is true

The rate rises with temperature up to an optimum, then falls steeply, because the high temperature changes the shape of the enzyme (denaturation) and the active site no longer fits the substrate. A is false (the rate falls after the optimum) and B is false (at very high temperatures the enzyme does not work). D is also true as an observation, but C gives the explanation and is the best answer. **Answer: C.**
Increase in temperature always increases the rate of reaction.
Enzymes are active at all temperatures.
Enzymes are denatured at very high temperatures.
Enzymes are inactive at very high temperatures.
Which of the following factors increase the rate of a reaction?

A rise in temperature gives more molecules an energy at least equal to the activation energy and increases the collision frequency, so the rate increases. A higher activation energy (C) or a lower concentration of reactants (D) lowers the rate, and pressure (B) only matters for gases and is not a general factor. **Answer: A.**

Radioactive isotopes can be used to calculate the age of materials because their decay rates are

*Options as printed:* A) dependent on the conditions of a reaction   B) unstable   C) constant   D) dependent on the amount of material present

Dating relies on the fact that the half-life, the decay constant of a radioisotope, is fixed and is not changed by temperature, pressure or chemical combination (A is false). Because the decay constant is constant, the fraction left after a time $t$ is known and the age can be calculated. The intended key is C; note that the activity itself is proportional to the number of nuclei present (D), which makes the item debatable.

**Intended answer: C (constant).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.
An organic compound gives a positive test with Tollen's reagent (ammoniacal silver nitrate). This implies that the compound

Tollens' reagent is reduced to a silver mirror by aldehydes (which are oxidised to carboxylic acids); ketones (A) and carboxylic acids (D) do not react. A positive test does not tell whether the aldehyde is aromatic or aliphatic, so B is too specific: the compound can be an aliphatic aldehyde. **Answer: C.**

A sample of hydrocarbon on complete combustion gave 1.32 g of carbon dioxide and 0.72 g of water. What would be the empirical formula of the hydrocarbon given the following relative atomic masses: H = 1.0; C = 12.0?

$n(\mathrm{CO_2}) = 1.32/44 = 0.030$ mol, so $n(\mathrm{C}) = 0.030$ mol. $n(\mathrm{H_2O}) = 0.72/18 = 0.040$ mol, so $n(\mathrm{H}) = 0.080$ mol. Ratio $\mathrm{C:H} = 0.030:0.080 = 3:8$, so the empirical formula is $\mathrm{C_3H_8}$. **Answer: D.**
Which of the following compounds is most ionic?

Ionic character is greatest when the cation has a large radius and low polarising power and the anion is small and hard to polarise. $\mathrm{Ba^{2+}}$ is the largest cation and $\mathrm{Cl^-}$ the smallest anion of the choices, so $\mathrm{BaCl_2}$ is the most ionic (Fajans' rules). $\mathrm{BaI_2}$ and $\mathrm{CaBr_2}$ contain more polarisable anions, $\mathrm{CaCl_2}$ a more polarising cation. **Answer: A.**
Calculate the pH of a 0.1 mol dm$^{-3}$ solution of a fully dissociated tribasic acid.

A fully dissociated tribasic acid releases three $\mathrm{H^+}$ per molecule, so $[\mathrm{H^+}] = 3 \times 0.1 = 0.3\ \mathrm{mol\,dm^{-3}}$ and $\mathrm{pH} = -\log_{10} 0.3 = 0.52 \approx 0.5$. Option D ($\mathrm{pH} = 1$) would be for a 0.1 M monobasic acid. **Answer: C.**
When a hydroxyl compound is treated with hot acidified potassium permanganate, the final oxidation product gives a positive iodoform test. What would be the likely formula of the hydroxyl compound?

The iodoform test needs the group $\mathrm{CH_3CO{-}}$ (or $\mathrm{CH_3CH(OH){-}}$). Oxidising $\mathrm{CH_3CH(OH)C_2H_5}$ (butan-2-ol) gives butanone $\mathrm{CH_3COC_2H_5}$, which contains $\mathrm{CH_3CO{-}}$ and is positive. Propan-1-ol (A) gives propanal or propanoic acid, 1-phenylpropan-1-ol (C) gives $\mathrm{C_6H_5COC_2H_5}$ with no methyl ketone group, and phenol (D) is not oxidised to a carbonyl compound. **Answer: B.**
Which of the following compounds will form hydrogen bonds?

Hydrogen bonding needs H bonded to a very electronegative small atom (F, O or N) and a lone pair on a neighbouring molecule. Only HF qualifies; $\mathrm{CHCl_3}$, $\mathrm{PH_3}$ and $\mathrm{SiH_4}$ have only weak dipole or van der Waals forces. **Answer: A.**
Iodine has a half-life of 8.07 days. What fraction of a sample of iodine-131 will be left after 16.14 days?
$16.14/8.07 = 2$ half-lives, so the fraction left is $(1/2)^2 = 1/4$. **Answer: B.**

Give the product of the following reaction.

Benzenediazonium chloride ($\mathrm{C_6H_5N_2^+Cl^-}$) is treated with $\mathrm{CuCN/KCN}$ ($\rightarrow$ ?).

The options are structures of a benzene ring carrying a single substituent: A ($-\mathrm{N_2CN}$), B ($-\mathrm{Cu_2Cl}$), C ($-\mathrm{CN}$), D ($-\mathrm{KN_2}$, as printed).

This is the Sandmeyer reaction: a copper(I) salt replaces the diazonium group, which leaves as $\mathrm{N_2}$. With $\mathrm{CuCN/KCN}$ the product is benzonitrile: $\mathrm{C_6H_5N_2^+Cl^-} + \mathrm{CuCN} \rightarrow \mathrm{C_6H_5CN} + \mathrm{N_2} + \mathrm{CuCl}$. The other structures are not formed. **Answer: C.**
What is the colour observed in a flame test to indicate the presence of copper(II) ions in a compound?
Copper(II) compounds give a blue-green flame. Apple green is typical of barium, so B is a trap. **Answer: D.**
How many isomers are in the compound with molecular formula $\mathrm{C_2H_4Cl_2}$?
The two structural isomers are 1,1-dichloroethane $\mathrm{CH_3CHCl_2}$ and 1,2-dichloroethane $\mathrm{ClCH_2CH_2Cl}$. Neither is optically active. **Answer: B.**
Choose the species with a trigonal planar shape.

$\mathrm{BF_3}$ has three bonding pairs and no lone pair on boron (3 regions of electron density), so it is trigonal planar. $\mathrm{NH_4^+}$ is tetrahedral and $\mathrm{NH_3}$, $\mathrm{H_3O^+}$ are trigonal pyramidal (one lone pair). **Answer: B.**
In the same period of the Periodic Table the atomic radii are largest for elements of group:

Across a period the nuclear charge increases while the shielding stays almost constant, so the radius decreases. Group 1 elements, at the start of the period, have the largest atomic radii. **Answer: A.**
Which of the following pairs of liquids when mixed would give a higher boiling point than that predicted by Raoult's law?

A boiling point higher than predicted means a lower vapour pressure than predicted: a negative deviation from Raoult's law, caused by A-B attractions stronger than A-A and B-B. Nitric acid and water form strong hydrogen bonds and ion-dipole attractions (and give a maximum-boiling azeotrope). Propanol and ethanol are almost ideal, propane and tetrachloromethane are non-polar (nearly ideal) and hexane and water are immiscible. **Answer: C.**
The reaction between ethanoyl chloride and the hydroxide ion to give an acid is classified as:

$\mathrm{OH^-}$ is a nucleophile that attacks the $\delta+$ carbon of $\mathrm{CH_3COCl}$ and replaces $\mathrm{Cl^-}$ (addition-elimination): $\mathrm{CH_3COCl} + \mathrm{OH^-} \rightarrow \mathrm{CH_3COOH} + \mathrm{Cl^-}$. The net result is substitution of Cl by OH by a nucleophile. **Answer: C.**
In the titration of ammonia solution with ethanoic acid solution, the endpoint can best be determined by using

A weak base against a weak acid gives no sharp pH jump at the equivalence point, so no simple indicator changes colour sharply (phenolphthalein suits weak acid/strong base, methyl orange strong acid/weak base). A pH meter follows the gradual change and shows the end point from the pH-volume curve. **Answer: D.**
The standard redox potentials for copper and silver electrodes are +0.34 V and +0.80 V respectively. What cell emf will be obtained when the two half-cells are coupled?

$E^\circ_{cell} = E^\circ_{(\text{positive})} - E^\circ_{(\text{negative})} = +0.80 - (+0.34) = +0.46\ \mathrm{V}$ (silver is the positive electrode). The emf of a feasible cell is positive, so B and D are excluded; C adds the potentials. **Answer: A.**

The enthalpy change for the equilibrium reaction, $2\mathrm{NO(g)} + \mathrm{O_2(g)} \rightleftharpoons 2\mathrm{NO_2(g)}$ is $-113\ \mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}}$. The proportion of $\mathrm{NO_2(g)}$ in the equilibrium mixture could be increased by

By Le Chatelier's principle, raising the pressure favours the side with fewer gas moles (3 mol on the left, 2 mol on the right), so more $\mathrm{NO_2}$. Raising the temperature favours the endothermic (reverse) direction for this exothermic reaction (A), added $\mathrm{N_2}$ at constant volume does not change the partial pressures (B) and a catalyst does not change the position (D). **Answer: C.**
increasing the pressure of the system

Which of the following statements is true about 2-hydroxypropanoic acid?

*Options as printed:* A) Is optically inactive   B) Reacts with $\mathrm{PCl_5}$ to form steamy white fumes of HCl   C) Decolourizes acidified $\mathrm{KMnO_4}$ solution   D) Is an amino acid

2-Hydroxypropanoic acid (lactic acid) is $\mathrm{CH_3CH(OH)COOH}$. It has a chiral carbon so it is optically active (A false) and it is not an amino acid (D false). It contains $-\mathrm{OH}$ and $-\mathrm{COOH}$ groups, so it reacts with $\mathrm{PCl_5}$ giving steamy fumes of HCl (B true). Its secondary alcohol group is also oxidised by hot acidified $\mathrm{KMnO_4}$ to $\mathrm{CH_3COCOOH}$ with decolourisation (C true as well), so the item has two defensible answers; B is the more likely intended key.

**Intended answer: B (Reacts with $\mathrm{PCl_5}$ to form steamy white fumes of HCl).**

The graph below represents the graph of first ionization energy against atomic number for some elements across period 2 and 3 of the Periodic Table. The elements S, T, U, V or W shown on the graph are not the usual symbols of the elements.

![Figure (Q21): first ionisation energy against atomic number for elements across periods 2 and 3, with points S, T, U, V and W labelled.](/media/figures/cm/gce-al-chemistry-2016-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_1.webp)

Which of the elements represents an alkali metal?

Reading the graph from the left: the points correspond to Be, B (S), C, N, O (T), F, Ne (U), Na (V), Mg and Al (W). The first ionisation energy is highest for the noble gas U (end of period 2) and falls sharply to the lowest value for the next element, the alkali metal Na, which is V. S is boron (dip after Be), T is oxygen (dip after N) and U is neon. **Answer: D.**
Propene, $\mathrm{CH_3CHCH_2}$ and ethanal, $\mathrm{CH_3CHO}$ react with cyanide ion by different mechanisms. This can be explained in terms of the general principle that

The C=O carbon is $\delta+$ (oxygen is more electronegative), so nucleophiles such as $\mathrm{CN^-}$ attack it readily (nucleophilic addition). The C=C bond is electron rich and is attacked by electrophiles, not by nucleophiles. **Answer: D.**
Nucleophiles attack a C = C carbon bond more readily than a C = O carbon bond
Electrophiles attack a C = O carbon bond more readily than a C = C carbon bond
Both nucleophiles and electrophiles attack a C = O carbon bond more readily than a C=C carbon bond
Nucleophiles attack a C = O carbon bond more readily than a C = C carbon bond
Select the s-block element which would not give a hydroxide when reacted with water at room temperature.

Sodium, lithium and calcium react with cold water giving $\mathrm{NaOH}$, $\mathrm{LiOH}$ and $\mathrm{Ca(OH)_2}$. Magnesium does not react appreciably with cold water because the protective, sparingly soluble $\mathrm{Mg(OH)_2}$ layer stops the reaction (it reacts with steam to give the oxide). **Answer: B.**
Three oxides have the structures: giant molecular, intermediate between giant molecular and giant ionic and giant ionic. These oxides could be respectively

$\mathrm{SiO_2}$ is a giant molecular (covalent) lattice; $\mathrm{GeO_2}$ is intermediate between covalent and ionic; $\mathrm{SnO}$ is largely ionic. In A and B, $\mathrm{CO_2}$ is a simple molecular oxide, and in D $\mathrm{GeO}$ is not giant molecular while $\mathrm{SnO_2}$ and $\mathrm{PbO_2}$ are not both giant ionic. The ordering in C follows the increase in metallic character down Group 14. **Answer: C.**
Alkanes do not undergo many chemical reactions. This is because they are

Alkanes contain only strong, non-polar C-C and C-H single bonds (C and H have almost the same electronegativity) and no $\pi$ bond. They are saturated and have no sites of high or low electron density attacked by nucleophiles or electrophiles, so they are unreactive. Options A and C contain "neutral", which is not a structural reason, and B is false because alkanes are non-polar. **Answer: D.**
The concentration (mol dm$^{-3}$) of nitrate ions in a mixture of 10 cm$^3$ of 0.02 mol dm$^{-3}$ $\mathrm{Ca(NO_3)_2}$ and 15 cm$^3$ of 0.30 mol dm$^{-3}$ $\mathrm{NaNO_3}$ is

$n(\mathrm{NO_3^-})$ from $\mathrm{Ca(NO_3)_2} = 2 \times 0.02 \times 0.010 = 4.0 \times 10^{-4}$ mol; from $\mathrm{NaNO_3} = 0.30 \times 0.015 = 4.5 \times 10^{-3}$ mol. Total $= 4.9 \times 10^{-3}$ mol in $25\ \mathrm{cm^3}$, so $[\mathrm{NO_3^-}] = 4.9\times10^{-3}/0.025 = 0.196\ \mathrm{mol\,dm^{-3}}$. **Answer: A.**

The standard enthalpies of formation of ethyne, $\mathrm{C_2H_2}$, carbon dioxide, $\mathrm{CO_2}$ and water, $\mathrm{H_2O}$, are $+227.06$, $-394.07$ and $-286.26\ \mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}}$ respectively. What is the enthalpy change of the reaction for 1 mole of ethyne?

$2\mathrm{C_2H_2(g)} + 5\mathrm{O_2(g)} \rightleftharpoons 4\mathrm{CO_2(g)} + 2\mathrm{H_2O(l)}$

For the equation as written: $\Delta H = [4(-394.07) + 2(-286.26)] - [2(+227.06)] = -1576.28 - 572.52 - 454.12 = -2602.92\ \mathrm{kJ}$. This is for 2 mol of ethyne, so for 1 mol: $-2602.92/2 = -1301.46\ \mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}}$. B has the wrong sign; the values in C and D (printed unclearly) are not obtained. **Answer: A.**
The change in the oxidation state of the vanadium atom when $\mathrm{VO^{2+}}$ is converted into $\mathrm{VO_2^+}$ is

For the reaction sequence below, aniline ($\mathrm{C_6H_5NH_2}$) is converted by reagent (i) into $\mathrm{C_6H_5NHCOCH_3}$ (phenylethanamide); this is treated with conc. $\mathrm{HNO_3}$ / conc. $\mathrm{H_2SO_4}$ to give 4-nitrophenylethanamide ($\mathrm{O_2N{-}C_6H_4{-}NHCOCH_3}$), and reagent (ii) then gives 4-nitroaniline ($\mathrm{O_2N{-}C_6H_4{-}NH_2}$).

The reagents (i) and (ii) are respectively

Step (i) protects the amine group by acylation with ethanoyl chloride, $\mathrm{CH_3COCl}$, giving the amide (this also stops oxidation of the ring by nitric acid and directs nitration to the 4-position). After nitration, step (ii) removes the protecting group by acid hydrolysis, $\mathrm{H_2O/H^+}$ (heat), to give 4-nitroaniline. Ethanoic acid (B) is too unreactive, ethanamide (C) and propanone (D) do not acylate the amine. **Answer: A.**
The first four successive ionization energies of an element X in kJ mol$^{-1}$ are 900, 1758, 14905 and 15100. From the values it can be predicted that the element has

There is a very large jump between the second (1758) and third (14905) ionisation energies: the third electron is removed from an inner, closer shell. So two electrons are in the outermost shell (X is in Group 2, e.g. beryllium, whose first IE is 900 kJ mol$^{-1}$). **Answer: C.**
three electrons in its outermost shell
one electron in its outermost shell
two electrons in its outermost shell
four electrons in its outermost shell

An organic compound has the molecular formula, $\mathrm{C_8H_8O}$. It produces an orange precipitate when reacted with 2,4-dinitrophenylhydrazine (2,4-DNPH) and gives a silver mirror with Tollen's reagent. What is the name of the compound?

The orange precipitate shows a carbonyl group and the silver mirror shows an aldehyde. Phenylethanal, $\mathrm{C_6H_5CH_2CHO}$, is $\mathrm{C_8H_8O}$. Phenylpropanal is $\mathrm{C_9H_{10}O}$, octanal is $\mathrm{C_8H_{16}O}$ and phenylethanone $\mathrm{C_6H_5COCH_3}$ (also $\mathrm{C_8H_8O}$) is a ketone, which gives no silver mirror. **Answer: A.**

Calculate the relative atomic mass (RAM) of an element, X, whose mass spectrometer's trace shows isotopes with the following percentage abundances: $^{24}\mathrm{X}$ (78.3%), $^{25}\mathrm{X}$ (10.8%) and $^{26}\mathrm{X}$ (10.9%)

What is the general name given to the following reaction?

Fat/oil + Alkali $\rightarrow$ Soap + glycerol
Alkaline hydrolysis of a fat or oil (an ester of propane-1,2,3-triol) gives the sodium or potassium salt of the fatty acid (soap) and glycerol: this is saponification. **Answer: B.**

Consider the reactions represented by equations below:

I. $4\mathrm{NaClO_3(s)} \rightarrow 3\mathrm{NaClO_4(s)} + \mathrm{NaCl(s)}$

II. $3\mathrm{Cu(s)} + 8\mathrm{HNO_3(aq)} \rightarrow 3\mathrm{Cu(NO_3)_2(aq)} + 2\mathrm{NO(g)} + 4\mathrm{H_2O}$

III. $2\mathrm{NO_2(g)} + \mathrm{H_2O(l)} \rightarrow \mathrm{HNO_3(aq)} + \mathrm{HNO_2(aq)}$

Which of the reactions involve disproportionation?

Disproportionation is a reaction in which the same element is simultaneously oxidised and reduced. I: Cl goes from $+5$ ($\mathrm{ClO_3^-}$) to $+7$ ($\mathrm{ClO_4^-}$) and to $-1$ ($\mathrm{Cl^-}$): yes. II: Cu goes from 0 to $+2$ (oxidised) and N from $+5$ to $+2$ (reduced), two different elements: no. III: N goes from $+4$ ($\mathrm{NO_2}$) to $+5$ ($\mathrm{HNO_3}$) and $+3$ ($\mathrm{HNO_2}$): yes. So I and III. **Answer: C.**
James Chadwick discovered the neutron in 1932 (Thomson the electron, Rutherford the nucleus and the proton). **Answer: C.**

The element with electronic configuration $[\mathrm{Ar}]\,3d^{10}4s^24p^2$ is

1. a typical metal
2. in Group 14 (Group IV) of the Periodic Table
3. in period 4 of the Periodic Table

The configuration with 14 electrons beyond argon (18) gives $Z = 32$, germanium. The outer shell is $n = 4$, so it is in period 4 (3 true), and it has four outer electrons ($4s^24p^2$), so it is in Group 14 (2 true). Germanium is a metalloid (semi-metal), not a typical metal (1 false). **Answer: C.**

On combustion, it is found that 0.46 g of compound Y gives 0.88 g $\mathrm{CO_2}$ and 0.54 g $\mathrm{H_2O(g)}$. Given the relative atomic masses: H = 1.0; C = 2.0; O = 16.0, what would be the structural formula of compound Y?

1. $\mathrm{CH_3CHO}$
2. $\mathrm{CH_3CH_2OH}$
3. $\mathrm{CH_3OCH_3}$

The printed value C = 2.0 is a misprint for 12.0 and is replaced by 12.0. $n(\mathrm{C}) = 0.88/44 = 0.020$ mol (0.24 g); $n(\mathrm{H}) = 2 \times 0.54/18 = 0.060$ mol (0.060 g); mass of O $= 0.46 - 0.24 - 0.06 = 0.16$ g, $n(\mathrm{O}) = 0.010$ mol. Ratio $\mathrm{C:H:O} = 2:6:1$, so Y is $\mathrm{C_2H_6O}$ ($M = 46$). Ethanol (2) and methoxymethane (3) both have this formula; ethanal ($\mathrm{C_2H_4O}$, 1) does not. **Answer: C.**

A compound of structural formula, $\mathrm{NH_2CH_2CO_2H}$ can be obtained:

1. from the hydrolysis of ethanenitrile (acetonitrile)
2. by the action of ammonia on 2-chloroethanoic acid
3. from the hydrolysis of protein

The compound is glycine (aminoethanoic acid). Hydrolysis of ethanenitrile gives ethanoic acid, $\mathrm{CH_3COOH}$, with no amino group (1 false). Ammonia substitutes the chlorine of $\mathrm{ClCH_2COOH}$ giving $\mathrm{H_2NCH_2COOH}$ (2 true), and glycine is one of the amino acids released by hydrolysis of proteins (3 true). **Answer: C.**

Select the statement(s) which is/are true of the organic compound that has the following structure:

$\mathrm{CH_3{-}CH(CH_3){-}CH(Cl){-}CH_2{-}COOCH_3}$ (the methyl group is attached to the second carbon from the left and the chlorine to the third carbon, as printed)

1. The subsituents are chloro, methyl and hydrogen groups
2. It is a carbonyl compound
3. The chloro and methyl groups are in positions 3 and 4 respectively on the parent chain

*Options as printed:* A) 1, 2 and 3 are all correct   B) 1 and 2 only are correct   C) 2 and 3 only are correct   D) 3 only is correct

The compound is methyl 3-chloro-4-methylpentanoate. Numbering from the ester carbon (C1): C2 is $\mathrm{CH_2}$, C3 bears Cl, C4 bears $\mathrm{CH_3}$ and C5 is the end methyl, so statement 3 is true. Statement 1 is false because hydrogen is not a substituent (the substituents are chloro and methyl, plus the ester). Statement 2 is debatable: the ester contains a C=O group but "carbonyl compound" is normally used for aldehydes and ketones. The intended key is D.

**Intended answer: D (3 only is correct).**

Which of the following will react with transition metals to form complex ions in which the ligand is bidentate?

1. Aminoethanoic acid, $\mathrm{H_2NCH_2CO_2H}$
2. Ethanedioic acid, $\mathrm{H_2C_2O_4}$
3. Ethane-1,2-diammine, $\mathrm{H_2NCH_2CH_2NH_2}$

A bidentate ligand donates two lone pairs from two different atoms. Aminoethanoate (as glycinate) bonds through N and O; ethanedioate (oxalate) through two O atoms; ethane-1,2-diamine ('en') through its two N atoms. All three are bidentate. **Answer: A.**

What type of bond(s) exists in sodium tetrahydridoborate or sodium borohydride, $\mathrm{NaBH_4}$?

1. Ionic bonds
2. Covalent bonds
3. Hydrogen bonds

$\mathrm{NaBH_4}$ consists of $\mathrm{Na^+}$ and $\mathrm{BH_4^-}$ ions: ionic bonding between them (1 true) and covalent B-H bonds inside the tetrahedral anion (2 true, one being dative). There is no H bonded to F, O or N, so no hydrogen bonds (3 false). **Answer: B.**

Given the following redox potentials:

| Electrode | $E^\circ$ (V) |
|---|---|
| $\tfrac12\mathrm{I_2(aq)}/\mathrm{I^-(aq)}$ | +0.54 |
| $\mathrm{Fe^{3+}(aq)}/\mathrm{Fe^{2+}(aq)}$ | +0.77 |
| $\tfrac12\mathrm{Br_2(aq)}/\mathrm{Br^-(aq)}$ | +1.07 |
| $\tfrac12\mathrm{Cl_2(aq)}/\mathrm{Cl^-(aq)}$ | +1.36 |

Which of the following statements may likely be made?

1. $\mathrm{I^-(aq)}$ is likely to reduce $\mathrm{Fe^{3+}(aq)}$ to $\mathrm{Fe^{2+}(aq)}$
2. $\mathrm{Fe^{2+}(aq)}$ is likely to reduce $\tfrac12\mathrm{Cl_2(aq)}$ to $\mathrm{Cl^-(aq)}$
3. $\mathrm{Br^-(aq)}$ is likely to reduce $\mathrm{Fe^{3+}(aq)}$ to $\mathrm{Fe^{2+}(aq)}$

A reaction is feasible when the couple with the more positive $E^\circ$ is the oxidising agent. 1: $\mathrm{Fe^{3+}}$ (+0.77) oxidises $\mathrm{I^-}$ (+0.54): $E_{cell} = +0.23$ V, feasible (true). 2: $\mathrm{Cl_2}$ (+1.36) oxidises $\mathrm{Fe^{2+}}$, so $\mathrm{Fe^{2+}}$ reduces $\mathrm{Cl_2}$ ($E_{cell} = +0.59$ V): true. 3: $\mathrm{Fe^{3+}}$ (+0.77) is a weaker oxidant than $\mathrm{Br_2}$ (+1.07), so $\mathrm{Br^-}$ cannot reduce $\mathrm{Fe^{3+}}$ ($E_{cell} = -0.30$ V): false. Statements 1 and 2 only. **Answer: B.**

The diagram below shows the Maxwell-Boltzmann energy distribution curves for molecules of a gas under two sets of conditions, X and Y. Which of the following statement(s) is/are correct?

![Figure (Q43): Maxwell-Boltzmann energy distribution curves X and Y (number of molecules with given energy against energy).](/media/figures/cm/gce-al-chemistry-2016-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_2.webp)

1. An increase in temperature is required to produce curve Y from X
2. The total area under the curve X represents the total number of molecules of the gas
3. The total area under curve X is the same as that under curve Y

Curve Y has a lower, broader peak displaced to higher energy and a longer tail than X: this is the effect of a higher temperature, so 1 is true. The area under a distribution curve equals the total number of molecules (2 true), and as the same sample of gas is used for X and Y the two areas are equal (3 true). **Answer: A.**

In which of the following reaction(s) will $\Delta H$ be positive?

1. $\mathrm{O^+(g)} + e \rightarrow \mathrm{O(g)}$
2. $\mathrm{O(g)} + e \rightarrow \mathrm{O^-(g)}$
3. $\mathrm{O^-(g)} + e \rightarrow \mathrm{O^{2-}(g)}$

1 is the reverse of the first ionisation of oxygen, so it is exothermic ($\Delta H < 0$). 2 is the first electron affinity of oxygen, exothermic ($-141\ \mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}}$). 3 is the second electron affinity: the electron is added to a negative ion and has to overcome repulsion, so it is endothermic ($\Delta H > 0$). Only 3 is positive. **Answer: D.**

Which of the following compounds would react with acidified potassium dichromate solution on warming?

1. $\mathrm{(CH_3)_3COH}$
2. $\mathrm{CH_3OH}$
3. $\mathrm{(CH_3)_2CHOH}$

Primary and secondary alcohols are oxidised by warm acidified $\mathrm{K_2Cr_2O_7}$ (orange to green): methanol (2) gives methanal / methanoic acid and propan-2-ol (3) gives propanone. 2-Methylpropan-2-ol (1) is tertiary and has no H on the carbon carrying OH, so it is not oxidised under these conditions. **Answer: C.**

Which of the following statement(s) is/are correct concerning Group 17 (Group VII) elements?

1. They will all disproportionate when reacted with a cold dilute solution of sodium hydroxide
2. The melting and boiling temperatures of the hydrides increase down the group
3. Their ionic radii are larger than those of their atomic radii

3 is true: each halogen atom gains an electron to form $\mathrm{X^-}$, which has the same nuclear charge but more electron repulsion, so the ion is larger. 1 is false: fluorine does not disproportionate (it cannot have a positive oxidation state, it gives $\mathrm{F^-}$ and $\mathrm{OF_2}$ or $\mathrm{O_2}$). 2 is false: HF has the highest boiling point of the hydrogen halides because of hydrogen bonding, so the trend is not regular. Only 3. **Answer: D.**

**First statement:** An aqueous solution of ammonium chloride $\mathrm{NH_4Cl(s)}$ is likely to have a pH greater than 7

**Second statement:** An equimolar mixture of ammonia and ammonium chloride solution functions as a buffer

First: false. $\mathrm{NH_4^+}$ is the conjugate acid of a weak base and hydrolyses, $\mathrm{NH_4^+ + H_2O \rightleftharpoons NH_3 + H_3O^+}$, so the solution is acidic (pH below 7). Second: true, a weak base with its salt resists changes in pH. So the first is false and the second true. **Answer: D.**

First: false. Manganese shows the widest range (+2 to +7), chromium shows mainly +2, +3 and +6. Second: true, $\mathrm{Cr^{3+}}$ (aq) is green (violet-green) and $\mathrm{Cr(VI)}$ as dichromate is orange. **Answer: D.**

**First statement:** Nitrogen gas is relatively unreactive towards other substances

**Second statement:** The nitrogen to nitrogen bond dissociation energy is very high.

First: true. Second: true, the $\mathrm{N{\equiv}N}$ triple bond has a bond energy of about $944\ \mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}}$. A great amount of energy is needed to break it, which is exactly why nitrogen is unreactive, so the second statement is the correct explanation. **Answer: A.**

The most appropriate method to separate a mixture of coloured pigments is by:

Coloured pigments (dyes) differ in how strongly they are carried along a paper by a solvent, so they are separated by paper chromatography. Sublimation only separates a solid that sublimes, distillation separates liquids by boiling point, and filtration separates an insoluble solid from a liquid. **Answer: A.**
Which of the following is most easily compressible?

In a gas the particles are far apart with large empty spaces between them, so the particles can be pushed closer together. In a solid they are packed tightly and in a liquid they are close together, so neither can be compressed easily. **Answer: C.**
What type of bonding is present in aluminium?
Aluminium is a metal: its atoms give up their outer electrons to form a lattice of positive ions held together by a sea of delocalised electrons. This is metallic bonding. **Answer: B.**
Which of the following particles account for electrical conductivity in electrolytes?

In an electrolyte (molten or dissolved ionic compound) the current is carried by mobile positive and negative ions. Electrons carry the current in metals, not in electrolytes, and molecules and atoms are uncharged. **Answer: C.**
Which of the following reactions will be the fastest?

The rate increases with a higher concentration of the acid and with a larger surface area of the solid. Powdered zinc has a much larger surface area than granular zinc, and 2 M HCl is more concentrated than 1 M HCl, so 5 g of powdered zinc with 20 cm$^3$ of 2 M HCl is the fastest. The other options have a lower concentration, a smaller surface area, or both. **Answer: A.**

How many neutrons are there in an atom of $^{31}_{15}\mathrm{P}$?
Number of neutrons = mass number $-$ atomic number $= 31 - 15 = 16$. A common mistake is to give 31 (the nucleon number) or 15 (the number of protons). **Answer: C.**
Which of the following acids has a basicity of one?

The basicity of an acid is the number of hydrogen ions (replaceable hydrogen atoms) one molecule gives in water. $\mathrm{H_2CO_3}$, $\mathrm{H_2SO_3}$ and $\mathrm{H_2SO_4}$ are dibasic. Methanoic acid, $\mathrm{HCOOH}$, only ionises its carboxyl hydrogen ($\mathrm{HCOOH \rightleftharpoons H^+ + HCOO^-}$), so its basicity is one; the hydrogen bonded to carbon does not ionise. **Answer: B.**
The reaction $2\mathrm{FeCl_2} + \mathrm{Cl_2} \rightarrow 2\mathrm{FeCl_3}$ is a redox reaction. Identify the oxidized species in this reaction.

Iron goes from oxidation number $+2$ in $\mathrm{FeCl_2}$ to $+3$ in $\mathrm{FeCl_3}$: it loses an electron, so $\mathrm{FeCl_2}$ is oxidized (and is the reducing agent). Chlorine goes from 0 to $-1$ so $\mathrm{Cl_2}$ is reduced. Option A names both reactants together, which cannot be right as one of them is reduced. **Answer: C.**

The component of air used in fire extinguishers is:

Carbon dioxide is denser than air and does not support combustion, so it smothers a fire by keeping oxygen away from the burning material. Oxygen would feed a fire, and nitrogen is not used for this purpose in an ordinary fire extinguisher. **Answer: C.**

The reaction $\mathrm{A} + \mathrm{B} \rightarrow \mathrm{C} + \mathrm{D}$ is represented in an energy level diagram.

![Energy level diagram, A + B to C + D (question 14)](/media/figures/cm/gce-ol-chemistry-2016-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_2.webp)

In the diagram the products $\mathrm{C + D}$ are at a higher heat content than the reactants $\mathrm{A + B}$, so heat is taken in from the surroundings: the reaction is endothermic ($\Delta H$ positive). The diagram does not show whether the reaction is feasible or spontaneous. **Answer: B.**
Which of the following reactions is common with alcohols?

Alcohols react with carboxylic acids, in the presence of an acid catalyst, to form esters and water: this is esterification. Substitution and addition are typical of alkanes and alkenes, and hydrolysis is the splitting of an ester, not a typical reaction of an alcohol. **Answer: C.**
A flame test on a metallic salt produces a blue colour and its solution with acidified silver nitrate produces a yellow precipitate. This salt would be:

The blue (blue-green) flame colour points to a copper salt (iron compounds give no characteristic blue flame). The yellow precipitate with acidified silver nitrate is silver iodide, so the anion is iodide, whereas bromide gives a cream precipitate. This leaves a copper iodide. Of the two printed, copper(I) iodide is the stable compound (copper(II) iodide is unstable and decomposes to copper(I) iodide and iodine), so the answer is copper(I) iodide. **Answer: A.**
What mass of sodium hydroxide is required to prepare 500 cm$^3$ of a 0.1 M solution?

Moles of NaOH $= 0.1\ \mathrm{mol\ dm^{-3}} \times 0.500\ \mathrm{dm^3} = 0.05\ \mathrm{mol}$. Molar mass of NaOH $= 23.0 + 16.0 + 1.0 = 40.0\ \mathrm{g\ mol^{-1}}$. Mass $= 0.05 \times 40.0 = 2\ \mathrm{g}$. A common mistake is to use 1000 cm$^3$ instead of 500 cm$^3$, which gives 4 g. **Answer: C.**
Explain why sulphur trioxide is not usually dissolved directly in water to produce sulphuric acid.

In the Contact process $\mathrm{SO_3}$ is not added to water because the reaction $\mathrm{SO_3 + H_2O \rightarrow H_2SO_4}$ is so violently exothermic that it produces a fine acid mist (spray) which is difficult to condense and handle. Instead $\mathrm{SO_3}$ is dissolved in concentrated sulphuric acid to give oleum, which is then diluted with water. The statements in B, C and D are false: $\mathrm{SO_3}$ is very soluble in water, and the acid formed is strong. **Answer: A.**

The nitrates of sodium and potassium are the only common ones that decompose on heating to the nitrite and oxygen: $2\mathrm{NaNO_3} \rightarrow 2\mathrm{NaNO_2} + \mathrm{O_2}$. The nitrates of iron and magnesium give the oxide, nitrogen dioxide and oxygen, and silver nitrate gives silver, nitrogen dioxide and oxygen. **Answer: C.**

Iron is a transition metal: $\mathrm{Fe^{2+}}$ is pale green and $\mathrm{Fe^{3+}}$ is yellow-brown in solution. The ions of magnesium, sodium and silver are colourless. **Answer: A.**

From the given structure of the polymer, polystyrene, deduce the formula of the monomer styrene.

The polymer chain is: $-\mathrm{CH_2-CH(C_6H_5)-CH_2-CH(C_6H_5)-CH_2-CH(C_6H_5)-}$ (carbon backbone, with hydrogen atoms and a phenyl group $\mathrm{C_6H_5}$ on alternate carbon atoms).

An addition polymer is made from monomers with a carbon-carbon double bond, which opens up to join the units. The repeating unit is $-\mathrm{CH_2-CH(C_6H_5)-}$, so the monomer is $\mathrm{CH_2{=}CHC_6H_5}$ (phenylethene, styrene). The only option with this atom count is A, printed as $\mathrm{CH_2CHC_6H_5}$ (the double bond sign is missing in the print). Option D has two hydrogens more ($\mathrm{CH_3CHC_6H_5}$, no double bond) and so cannot polymerise. **Answer: A.**
The method employed by oil companies to separate petroleum into its different components is:

Crude oil (petroleum) is a mixture of hydrocarbons with different boiling points. It is separated in a fractionating column by fractional distillation, which gives petrol, kerosine, diesel and so on. Simple distillation cannot separate liquids with close boiling points. **Answer: D.**

Ethanol loses a molecule of water to give ethene: $\mathrm{C_2H_5OH \rightarrow C_2H_4 + H_2O}$ (heated with concentrated sulphuric acid or over alumina). The removal of water is dehydration, not dehydrogenation (which removes hydrogen). **Answer: C.**

Ethene adds hydrogen to become ethane: $\mathrm{C_2H_4 + H_2 \rightarrow C_2H_6}$ (nickel catalyst, about 150 $^\circ$C). Adding hydrogen to a double bond is hydrogenation. **Answer: B.**

What role does ammonia play in the following reaction?

$3\mathrm{CuO(s)} + 2\mathrm{NH_3(g)} \rightarrow 3\mathrm{Cu(s)} + \mathrm{N_2(g)} + 3\mathrm{H_2O(l)}$

Copper(II) oxide is reduced to copper (it loses oxygen), and the nitrogen of ammonia goes from $-3$ in $\mathrm{NH_3}$ to 0 in $\mathrm{N_2}$, so ammonia is oxidized. A substance that is itself oxidized while reducing something else is a reducing agent. **Answer: B.**

32. Which of the elements below exhibit allotropy?

2. Sulphur
3. Calcium

Allotropy is the existence of an element in different forms in the same physical state. Sulphur (rhombic and monoclinic) and carbon (diamond, graphite, fullerenes) show it. Chlorine (only $\mathrm{Cl_2}$) and calcium (a metal) do not. **Answer: C.**

33. An aqueous solution of HCl:

2. Is weakly acidic
3. Is strongly acidic
4. Is an oxidizing agent

HCl ionises completely in water, so the solution is a strong acid (3 true, 2 false) and turns blue litmus red (1 true). Hydrochloric acid is not described as an oxidizing agent at this level (4 is taken as false), so only 1 and 3 are correct, which is option B. **Answer: B.**
All the alkali metals form ions with charge:
The alkali metals (group I) have one electron in the outer shell and lose it to form $\mathrm{M^+}$ ions. **Answer: C.**
How many Faradays of electricity are passed through a solution if 6.5 amperes of current flow for one hour?
Charge $Q = It = 6.5 \times 3600 = 23400\ \mathrm{C}$. Number of Faradays $= 23400 \div 96000 = 0.24375 \approx 0.24\ \mathrm{F}$. Options C and D wrongly use the charge in coulombs. **Answer: A.**
Which of the following compounds is most suitable for testing alcohols?

Phosphorus pentachloride reacts with an alcohol (containing $-\mathrm{OH}$) giving steamy white fumes of hydrogen chloride: $\mathrm{C_2H_5OH + PCl_5 \rightarrow C_2H_5Cl + POCl_3 + HCl}$. The other compounds are not the usual test (phosphorus(V) oxide is a drying agent). **Answer: D.**
Which of the equations below represents a possible displacement reaction?

A more reactive halogen displaces a less reactive halogen from its salt. Reactivity decreases down the group: $\mathrm{F_2 > Cl_2 > Br_2 > I_2}$. Chlorine displaces bromine from sodium bromide: $\mathrm{Cl_2 + 2NaBr \rightarrow 2NaCl + Br_2}$ (option C). In A and B a less reactive halogen would have to displace a more reactive one, and in D chlorine would have to displace the more reactive fluorine. **Answer: C.**
An atom of an element X (where X is not the usual symbol) has electronic configuration of 2, 8, 1. Which of the following is true about X?

The electrons total $2 + 8 + 1 = 11$, so the neutral atom has 11 protons and 11 electrons (this is sodium). One outer electron means group I (not II), the atom forms positive ions by losing ONE electron (not two), and it does not form negative ions. **Answer: B.**

An element A forms an ion $\mathrm{A^{2-}}$. Select the formula of the compound which A forms with hydrogen.

A forms a 2- ion, so its valency is 2, and hydrogen has valency 1. Two hydrogen atoms combine with one atom of A: $\mathrm{H_2A}$, written as $\mathrm{AH_2}$ in option C (like $\mathrm{H_2S}$ or $\mathrm{H_2O}$). **Answer: C.**
Which of the following will dissolve in water to form a strong electrolyte?

A strong electrolyte ionises completely in water. Hydrogen chloride dissolves in water to give hydrochloric acid, which is fully ionised ($\mathrm{HCl \rightarrow H^+ + Cl^-}$). Ethanol, sugar and carbon tetrachloride do not ionise (carbon tetrachloride does not even dissolve). **Answer: D.**
Which of the following substances contains the highest percentage by mass of nitrogen?

Percentage of N by mass: $\mathrm{NH_4NO_3}$ ($M = 80$): $28/80 = 35.0\%$; $\mathrm{(NH_4)_2SO_4}$ ($M = 132$): $28/132 = 21.2\%$; $\mathrm{NH_3}$ ($M = 17$): $14/17 = 82.4\%$; $\mathrm{KNO_3}$ ($M = 101$): $14/101 = 13.9\%$. The highest is ammonia (a typical mistake is to pick $\mathrm{NH_4NO_3}$ because it has two nitrogen atoms). **Answer: C.**
What volume of carbon dioxide will be formed when 20 g of calcium carbonate is decomposed on heating?

$\mathrm{CaCO_3 \rightarrow CaO + CO_2}$. Molar mass of $\mathrm{CaCO_3} = 40.0 + 12.0 + 3 \times 16.0 = 100\ \mathrm{g\ mol^{-1}}$. Moles $= 20 \div 100 = 0.2\ \mathrm{mol}$. One mole of $\mathrm{CaCO_3}$ gives one mole of $\mathrm{CO_2}$, so volume $= 0.2 \times 24000 = 4800\ \mathrm{cm^3}$. **Answer: C.**
Select from the following the correct order of increasing reactivity of the halogens.

Reactivity of the halogens decreases down group VII, so it increases going up the group: iodine $<$ bromine $<$ chlorine $<$ fluorine. Option C gives this order; option A is the order of decreasing reactivity. **Answer: C.**
Which of the following is the formula for Lime?

Lime (quicklime) is calcium oxide, CaO, made by heating limestone. Calcium hydroxide, $\mathrm{Ca(OH)_2}$, is slaked lime (limewater when dissolved), sodium hydroxide is caustic soda and $\mathrm{Na_2CO_3}$ is washing soda. **Answer: A.**
Why is the anode in the extraction of aluminium replaced continually?

The anodes are made of carbon (graphite). At the anode, oxygen is released at about 950 $^\circ$C and burns the carbon to give carbon dioxide: $\mathrm{C + O_2 \rightarrow CO_2}$. The anode is gradually used up and so has to be replaced. **Answer: D.**

Which reason justifies why the Aluminium plant in Cameroon is located at Edea?

The extraction of aluminium by electrolysis needs very large quantities of cheap electricity. At Edea the hydroelectric dams on the Sanaga river supply this power, so the plant is sited there. **Answer: D.**

Which of the following has the highest number of molecules?

For equal masses, the number of molecules is greatest for the substance with the smallest molar mass ($n = m/M$). Molar masses: $\mathrm{H_2O}$ 18, $\mathrm{HCl}$ 36.5, $\mathrm{CO_2}$ 44, $\mathrm{CO}$ 28. So 5 g of $\mathrm{H_2O}$ is $5/18 = 0.28\ \mathrm{mol}$, the largest (HCl 0.14 mol, $\mathrm{CO_2}$ 0.11 mol, CO 0.18 mol). **Answer: A.**
Which one of the following produces oxygen when heated?

Potassium chlorate decomposes on heating to give oxygen: $2\mathrm{KClO_3} \rightarrow 2\mathrm{KCl} + 3\mathrm{O_2}$. Calcium carbonate gives carbon dioxide and calcium oxide, and sodium carbonate and potassium carbonate are not decomposed by heat in a Bunsen flame. **Answer: C.**
An unknown gas, X, rekindles a glowing splint, while gas Y turns lime water milky. The formulae of the gases X and Y respectively would be:

A gas that rekindles a glowing splint is oxygen, $\mathrm{O_2}$. A gas that turns limewater milky is carbon dioxide, $\mathrm{CO_2}$. Carbon monoxide has no effect on limewater, and nitrogen and nitrogen dioxide do not fit the tests. **Answer: B.**
Which of the following pair of ions will cause hardness in water?
Hardness in water is caused by dissolved calcium and magnesium ions, $\mathrm{Ca^{2+}}$ and $\mathrm{Mg^{2+}}$, which form scum with soap. Sodium and potassium ions do not. **Answer: D.**
Citizenship of a country can be acquired through the following methods **except:**

Citizenship is acquired by birth (to Cameroonian parents or on the territory, as the law provides), by marriage to a citizen and by naturalization, which is granted by the State after an application. Loyalty is a duty that a citizen shows towards the country, not a legal way of acquiring citizenship.

**Answer: B.**
The original members of a typical Cameroonian home are...

A home (nuclear family) is first formed by the father and the mother, who are the parents; children, and later other relatives, join them. Uncles, cousins and in-laws belong to the extended family.

**Answer: A.**
Which of the following elements can lay the foundation for a strong and united family?

Love brings understanding, care and forgiveness, which keep family members together. Pride, greed and intolerance divide people and weaken the family.

**Answer: C.**

The marriage of one man to two or more wives is called...

Monogamy is marriage between one man and one woman, and polyandry is the marriage of one woman to several husbands. Planting of young trees where trees had once existed and were cut down is known as...

Decentralisation and the creation of administrative units close to the population make it easier and faster for people to obtain services and papers, and easier for the State to manage local affairs. The aim is therefore to ease administration.

Cocaine, opium and marijuana (cannabis) are illegal narcotic drugs. Whisky is an alcoholic drink whose sale is regulated but not banned.

Which Constitution introduced the Senate as a new organ in the legislature?

The Constitution of 18 January 1996 provided for a second chamber of Parliament, the Senate, in addition to the National Assembly. Earlier constitutions had a National Assembly only (a one-chamber legislature).

The government protects consumers by making laws that control prices, quality and weights and measures and punish fraud. Higher taxes do not protect consumers (they usually raise prices).

The social security scheme in Cameroon that takes care of retired persons is called....

The National Social Insurance Fund (CNPS) pays an old age pension to workers who have retired. Family allowances are for children, accident benefits are for work injuries and housing allowances help with rent.

Tax evasion is the illegal refusal to pay tax. The State collects less money, so government revenue falls; this may later force it to spend less, but the first effect is the reduction of revenue.

The Universal Declaration of Human Rights was adopted in...

The United Nations General Assembly adopted the Universal Declaration of Human Rights on 10 December 1948 (the UN itself was created in 1945).

Child labour, child trafficking and child molestation are abuses of the rights of the child. Child delinquency is a child's own anti-social behaviour (a youth problem), not a violation of the child's rights by others.

The organization which plays an important role in the protection of Human rights and freedoms around the world is....

Amnesty International is the non-governmental organisation known for defending human rights worldwide. The ICJ settles disputes between states, the WHO deals with health and the ILO with work.

The United Nation flag shows two olive branches surrounding a map of the world. This signifies that the U.N.O. is ...

Working for peace through out the world

The following are the consequences of bad governance **except**:

Transparency in the management of resources

Domestic violence takes place inside the home, between members of the household (for example between spouses or against children), so it is a home based conflict.

**Answer: A.**
Which is the proper appellation for men and women with equal rights and opportunities?

Gender equality means that men and women have the same rights and opportunities. Empowerment gives power to a group, a stereotype is a fixed idea and discrimination is unfair treatment.

**Answer: B.**
The following is **not** an obstacle to women participation in the electoral process.

Lack of money, intimidation and lack of self confidence hold women back from taking part in elections. The mass media can help women by informing and sensitising the public, so it is not an obstacle.

A person who has been forced to leave his country of origin because of wars is called...

Application software most suitable for doing automatic calculations as data changes is:

A spreadsheet recalculates its formulas automatically whenever the data in the cells they refer to changes. A word processor handles text, a DBMS stores and queries records, and presentation software builds slides. **Answer: A.**
WWW stands for World Wide Web, the system of linked web pages accessed over the Internet. **Answer: B.**
The installation of a newer version of software is referred to as:

Replacing an installed program by a newer version is an upgrade. Updating usually means applying small patches to the same version, and downloading or uploading only describe copying files. **Answer: C.**
A central device is used to connect the machines in a ________ network.

In a star network every machine is connected to a central device (hub or switch). A bus uses one shared cable, a ring connects machines in a closed loop and a mesh links machines directly to each other. **Answer: B.**
________ is a temporary storage area in the CPU for input/output operations.

A buffer is a temporary storage area that holds data while it is moved between the processor and input/output devices of different speeds. A register is also a small storage area in the CPU, but it holds data and instructions being processed, not data waiting for input/output. A USB key is permanent secondary storage. **Answer: B.**
A graphical representation of an algorithm is known as:
A flow chart shows the steps of an algorithm with standard symbols joined by arrows. Pseudocode is a text description of an algorithm, not a graphic. **Answer: A.**
Data and programs that are not currently in use by the computer are stored in ________
Data and programs that are not being used are kept permanently in secondary storage (hard disk, flash disk, DVD). Main memory only holds what is currently being processed. **Answer: D.**
Step-by-step instructions that run on a computer are called ________.
A program is a set of step-by-step instructions that a computer runs. **Answer: C.**
Software used to access the WWW is called a (an) ________.
A web browser (for example Firefox or Chrome) is the software used to view web pages. Mozilla is the name of one organisation and its products, not the name of the kind of software. **Answer: C.**
Making illegal copies of copyrighted software is known as ________.
Copying copyrighted software without permission is software piracy. **Answer: D.**
The most appropriate software to use to deliver a lesson in a classroom is:
Presentation software lets a teacher show a lesson as a sequence of slides to the whole class. **Answer: D.**
The meaning of SMS as used in mobile communication is:
SMS stands for Short Messaging Service (text messages sent between phones). **Answer: A.**
An electronic pathway through which the processor communicates with other parts of a computer system is a ________.
A bus is a set of electronic pathways (wires on the motherboard) that carries data, addresses and control signals between the processor and other components. **Answer: C.**
Which one of the following is a valid address for a website?

A valid web address starts with the protocol followed by a colon and two slashes (http://), then the domain name ending with the domain extension (.com). Option A is the only one in this form. B and D misplace or omit the colon, and C puts the extension .com in the middle of the name. **Answer: A.**
What type of license agreement is an individual automatically agreeing to when they purchase software?

An individual buyer of software automatically accepts the end-user license agreement (EULA), which allows use by that one user under stated conditions. Multi-user, website and business licenses are bought separately by organisations. **Answer: A.**
A field which uniquely identifies records in a database table is referred to as:

The primary key is the field whose value is different for every record, so it identifies each record uniquely. A foreign key is a field that refers to the primary key of another table. 'Identify key' and 'Identity key' are not database terms. **Answer: D.**
Which one of the following helps to create a good ergonomic working environment?

Protecting computer monitors from reflections and glare by correcting positioning.
Protecting data in the computer by using effective anti-virus.
Making sure the voltage regulators of your computer uses the right voltage.
Making regular backup of sensitive data.
Software that converts a program one statement at a time into machine language just before the statement is executed is:
An interpreter translates and runs a program one statement at a time. A compiler translates the whole program before it runs, and an assembler translates assembly language. **Answer: C.**
Which of the following is an example of a declarative language?

A declarative language states WHAT result is wanted, not the steps to get it. SQL queries (SELECT ... WHERE ...) are declarative. C++, Java and Pascal are procedural or object-oriented languages. **Answer: A.**

|---|---|---|

| 0 | 1 | 1 |
| 1 | 0 | 1 |

Guidelines for the use of the Internet is referred to as:

Netiquette (network etiquette) is the set of guidelines for good behaviour when using the Internet. A code of ethics is a general professional code and cyber law is legislation, which is enforced by the state. **Answer: B.**
If you DO NOT want your data to be read while being sent over the Internet, then you need to:

Encryption scrambles the data so that only someone with the key can read it, even if it is intercepted. A firewall filters network traffic but does not hide the content of data in transit, and decrypting is the reverse operation. **Answer: B.**

A critical task lies on the critical path: any delay in it delays the whole project. **Answer: C.**
Which of the following structured (or compound) data types can be used to store a collection of test scores of ALL the students in a class?
An array stores a collection of values of the same type under one name, so it can hold all the scores. Real, Integer and String are simple types holding one value. **Answer: C.**
How many nibbles are there in 4 bytes?
1 byte = 8 bits and 1 nibble = 4 bits, so 1 byte = 2 nibbles. Then $4 \times 2 = 8$ nibbles. 32 is the number of bits, not nibbles. **Answer: C.**
EBCDIC means Extended Binary Coded Decimal Interchange Code, an 8-bit character code used on IBM mainframes. **Answer: B.**

Extended Binary Coded Decimal Interchange Code

Which of the following is an example of an impact printer?
An impact printer forms characters by striking an inked ribbon against the paper. The dot matrix printer does this with pins. Laser, ink jet and thermal printers are non-impact. **Answer: C.**
Another name for secondary storage is

Secondary storage is also called auxiliary (or backing) storage. Primary storage and memory both mean main memory. Disk storage is only one example of secondary storage, not another name for it. **Answer: D.**
A collection of related web pages is a
A website is a collection of related web pages kept under one domain name. A web document is a single page. **Answer: C.**
The process of converting digital signals to a form suitable for transmission over a telephone line is called:
A telephone line carries analogue signals, so a modem modulates the digital signal into an analogue one. The reverse operation, at the receiver, is demodulation. **Answer: A.**
The first major computer network was:
ARPANET, developed in the late 1960s for the US Department of Defense, was the first major computer network and the ancestor of the Internet. **Answer: D.**
A ________ is a communication network that covers a large geographical area such as a country.
A Wide Area Network (WAN) covers a large area such as a country or the world. A LAN covers a building, a MAN a city and a PAN the space around one person. **Answer: C.**
________ is a protocol for transfering files over the Internet.
FTP (File Transfer Protocol) is used to transfer files between computers. HTTP transfers web pages, an ISP is a company that provides Internet access and a URL is a web address. **Answer: B.**
Buying and selling over the internet is also known as
Electronic commerce (e-commerce) means buying and selling goods and services over the Internet. **Answer: C.**
________ is a set of rules that governs the transmission of signals across devices in a network.
A protocol is a set of rules for communication between devices. A topology is the layout of the network. **Answer: A.**
People who manage and manipulate the development of information systems are referred to as ________.
System analysts study the needs of an organisation and manage the development of its information system. Programmers only write the code. **Answer: C.**
What is the decimal equivalent of the binary number 11011?
In which phase of the system development life cycle are interviews and questionnaires used?
Interviews and questionnaires are fact-finding techniques used in the analysis phase to collect information about the existing system and the users' needs. **Answer: B.**
Simulation software imitates a real situation (a flight, a chemical reaction, traffic) so that it can be studied or practised safely. **Answer: C.**
designed to solve real life problems
designed to imitate a real life situation

Bluetooth connections between two or more devices is an example of a ________ network
Bluetooth links devices within a few metres around a person: this is a Personal Area Network (PAN). **Answer: A.**
The main role of a repeater in a network is to:
A signal weakens over distance. A repeater receives it and regenerates (amplifies) it so it can travel further. Choosing the best path is the job of a router. **Answer: A.**
Select the best path for a packet across networks
Provide an error free connection between two network segments
Ensure that two network have a repeated set of signals
If the ASCII code for letter b in binary is 01100010, then the ASCII code for letter d in binary is?
The letters are coded in alphabetical order, so d is two codes after b: $01100010_2 + 2 = 01100100_2$ ($98 + 2 = 100$). **Answer: D.**
A webcam sends pictures and video into the computer, so it is an input device. **Answer: B.**

Questions 46 to 48 concern Spreadsheet Applications.

A pre-programmed formula is called ________.
A function (such as SUM or AVERAGE) is a pre-programmed formula built into a spreadsheet. **Answer: A.**

Questions 46 to 48 concern Spreadsheet Applications.

A column header is described as:

The header of a column of data names what the column contains, so it is the field name. It is not a value or a formula, and a cell address is a column letter combined with a row number. **Answer: A.**

Which of the following is a correct cell address?

A (an) ________ is a pictorial representation of a command or task that is used in GUIs
An icon is a small picture that represents a program, file or command in a graphical user interface. **Answer: C.**

In the system analysis phase the analyst gathers data on the existing system and examines it carefully to define the requirements. The preliminary investigation only checks whether the problem is worth solving (feasibility). **Answer: B.**
Money whose face value is greater than the value of its metal content is known as:

Token money (coins such as 25 or 50 FCFA pieces) is legal tender whose face value is higher than the value of the metal it contains. Standard money has a face value equal to its metal content, paper money has almost no intrinsic value and is not made of metal, and near money (bills, bonds) is not legal tender. **Answer: B.**
Industries producing commodities that are fragile are better located:

Near the source of raw materials
When net migration is positive, it implies that:

Rural urban migrants are greater than urban rural migrants
Co-operative societies that buy and retail goods to members are:

A consumers' co-operative buys goods in bulk and sells them to its members at fair prices. Thrift and loan societies lend money, producers' societies help members to produce, and marketing societies sell members' products. **Answer: D.**
Which of the following documents give a public limited company the right to commence business?

Any addition to the stock of capital is known as:

Gross investment is total spending on new capital goods, part of which only replaces worn-out capital (depreciation). Net investment = gross investment - depreciation, and it is the real addition to the stock of capital. 'Real' and 'true' investment are not standard terms. **Answer: A.**
The economic concept of choice is as a result of:

People must choose because resources are scarce while wants are unlimited: if resources were not scarce, nothing would have to be given up. How is an economic good similar to a free good?

Both economic goods and free goods satisfy human wants, that is, they give utility. Only economic goods are scarce and carry a price; free goods (such as air) are free gifts of nature and have no price. So B, C and D are false for at least one of them. **Answer: A.**
Both are scarce relative to demand
Both are free gifts of nature
Both command a price in the market

Study the table illustrating the utility pattern of a consumer of palm wine.

| Number of cups of palm wine | Total utility (in utils) |
|---|---|
| 1 | 10 |
| 2 | 19 |
| 3 | 24 |

What is this consumer's marginal utility when he consumes 2 cups of palm wine?

Marginal utility is the change in total utility caused by consuming one more unit: MU of the 2nd cup = $TU_2 - TU_1 = 19 - 10 = 9$ utils. The value 5 is the marginal utility of the 3rd cup ($24 - 19$). **Answer: B.**
The practice of mono-cropping over a large piece of land is known as:

Growing a single crop (such as banana, rubber or oil palm) on a very large area is plantation farming. Subsistence farming produces mainly for the family's own use, and commercial farming is a wider term (production for sale) that does not imply one crop on a large estate. **Answer: C.**
The population of a country is 16 million people and the working population which is 47.5% is effectively employed. What is the number of unemployed?

When total output is increasing at increasing rate, the return to variable factors is:

If each extra unit of the variable factor adds more to total output than the previous one, total output grows faster and faster, which means increasing returns. Constant returns give a constant rate of increase, decreasing returns a slower rate, and negative returns make total output fall. **Answer: B.**
The main aim of backward vertical integration is to:

Backward vertical integration means a firm takes over a firm at an earlier stage of production (its supplier), so as to be sure of regular and cheaper raw materials. Acquiring outlets or retail shops (A, D) is forward integration. **Answer: C.**
Secure the supply of raw materials

This question is based on the diagram showing cost of production.

![Cost curves: total cost TC rising from 1,000 FCFA, flat fixed cost FC at 1,000 FCFA, and the gap VC between them at an output of 60 pens where TC is 3,000 FCFA (Question 14).](/media/figures/cm/gce-ol-economics-2016-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_1.webp)

When output is 60 pens, the variable cost is:

At 60 pens, total cost (TC) = 3,000 FCFA (the dotted line) and fixed cost (FC) = 1,000 FCFA. Variable cost is the gap between TC and FC: $VC = TC - FC = 3{,}000 - 1{,}000 = 2{,}000$ FCFA. The value 3,000 FCFA (D) is the total cost, and 1,000 FCFA (A) is the fixed cost. **Answer: B.**

Which letter represents the destruction of utilities?

Utility is destroyed when a good is finally consumed, because the good is used up and no longer satisfies wants. This happens at the last stage, the consumers (D). Stages A, B and C create utility (raw materials, form utility, place and time utility). **Answer: A.**
To which of the following trade bloc does Cameroon belong?

When the government uses taxation to regulate the economy, she is using what policy?

Fiscal policy is the use of government spending and taxation to influence the economy. Monetary policy uses the money supply and interest rates, and 'physical policy' is not an economic policy term. **Answer: B.**
Which name would you give to trade among CEMAC member states?
CEMAC has several member countries, so trade among them involves more than two countries: it is multilateral trade. Bilateral trade is between two countries only. **Answer: D.**

Calculate the terms of trade for 2011.

A country registered 200,000 emigrants and 500,000 immigrants in 2012. Net migration is:
Net migration = immigrants - emigrants = $500{,}000 - 200{,}000 = +300{,}000$. Option C adds the two figures instead of subtracting, and the negative values reverse the order. **Answer: A.**
Which of the following is a feature of developed countries?

Developed countries have a high standard of living (high income per head, good health and education). A high dependency ratio, high birth rate and high unemployment are typical of developing countries. **Answer: C.**
What will determine the exchange rate for any currency if we have a free floating exchange rate?

Under a free floating system the central bank does not fix the rate: the price of a currency is set by the interaction of the demand for it and the supply of it on the foreign exchange market. Demand alone or supply alone cannot fix a price. **Answer: C.**

A commercial bank operating with a cash ratio of 10% received bank deposits of 10,000,000 FCFA. Which amount will it keep as cash reserves?
Cash reserve = cash ratio $\times$ deposits = $0.10 \times 10{,}000{,}000 = 1{,}000{,}000$ FCFA. The 9,000,000 FCFA of option D is the amount available for lending. **Answer: A.**
Which function of money enables the state to collect taxes from individuals?

Taxes are collected in money because money is generally accepted by everybody as payment: it works as a medium of exchange, so the state does not need to collect taxes in goods. 'One way payment' is not a function of money. **Answer: D.**
A cocoa producer in Cameroon sells his cocoa in Britain for 12,000 FCFA while in Cameroon, he sells it at 15,000 FCFA. How can this be best described?

Dumping is the sale of goods abroad at a price lower than the price charged on the home market. Here the export price (12,000 FCFA) is lower than the home price (15,000 FCFA). Devaluation and revaluation are changes in the value of a currency, and black marketing is illegal trading. **Answer: A.**
Excise duties are taxes on goods produced and consumed inside the country (home-made goods such as beer or tobacco). Taxes on imports are customs duties (C). **Answer: B.**
Taxes on home made goods and services
Taxes on imported goods and services
Which of the following factors can affect the demand for a commodity?

Hire purchase and other credit facilities let consumers buy more of a good than their current income allows, so they raise the demand for it: they are a determinant of demand. The size of stock available concerns supply, while the degree of necessity and the number of uses influence how elastic demand is rather than the level of demand. **Answer: A.**

The holding of money to take care of any eventual sickness in the family is known as:

People keep money for unexpected events such as sickness or accidents: this is the precautionary motive for demanding money. The transactions motive is for planned daily spending, and the speculative motive is to profit from changes in bond prices or interest rates. **Answer: B.**
In which market does the buying and selling of the FCFA takes place?
Buying and selling one currency against another (FCFA against dollars, euros...) takes place in the foreign exchange market. **Answer: D.**
Which of the following types of agriculture is involve in the cultivation of foodstuff mainly for family consumption?

Peasant farming is small-scale farming in which families grow food crops mainly for their own consumption. Plantation and commercial agriculture produce mainly for sale, and arable farming only means growing crops (as opposed to rearing animals). **Answer: C.**
A population in which a greater proportion is made up of old people can be described as:

When old people form a large share of the population, few babies are born and few young people enter the labour force, so the population is declining (ageing). Sparse population refers to low density, underpopulation to too few people for the resources, and an expanding population has many young people. **Answer: D.**
The weekly incomes of five (5) sons are as: 2,500 FCFA, 3,000 FCFA, 3,500 FCFA, 4,000 CFA and 4,500 FCFA. Calculate the mean weekly income.
Mean = sum / number of values = $\frac{2500 + 3000 + 3500 + 4000 + 4500}{5} = \frac{17500}{5} = 3{,}500$ FCFA (this is also the middle value). **Answer: B.**
A negative income elasticity of demand suggest that the commodity is:

Income elasticity of demand is negative when demand falls as income rises: this is the behaviour of an inferior good. Normal goods have a positive income elasticity, and Veblen goods / goods of ostentation are luxuries bought for show, with a positive income elasticity. **Answer: A.**
Paul has 400,000 FCFA and he sets aside 120,000 FCFA to buy bread. If a loaf of bread sells at 300 FCFA, what quantity of bread will he buy?
Only the money set aside is spent on bread: $\frac{120{,}000}{300} = 400$ loaves. Dividing the whole 400,000 FCFA by 300 would give 1,333 loaves, which is not an option. **Answer: D.**
In which market structure are firms said to be "price takers"?

In perfect competition there are very many small firms selling a homogeneous product, so no single firm can influence the market price: it must accept (take) the price set by the market. A monopoly is a price maker. **Answer: C.**
What is the main function of an entrepreneur?

The entrepreneur organises the other factors of production and, above all, bears the risk of the business: he accepts that he may make a loss as well as a profit. Providing capital belongs to the capitalist, and insurance companies, not the entrepreneur, insure against risks. **Answer: D.**
Which taxation system may help to reduce the gap between the rich and the poor?

In a progressive tax system the rate rises with income, so the rich pay a larger percentage of their income than the poor, which reduces inequality. Flat-rate and proportional taxes take the same percentage from everybody, and a regressive tax takes a larger percentage from the poor. **Answer: A.**
If government expenditure is 42 billion FCFA and her revenue stands at 40 billion FCFA. This type of budget is called:
Expenditure (42 billion) is greater than revenue (40 billion), so the government spends $42 - 40 = 2$ billion FCFA more than it earns: this is a budget deficit. **Answer: C.**
Another name for fixed costs is

Which type of production is a musician involved in, when entertaining his fans?

A musician who entertains his fans provides a service, and the production of services is tertiary production. Primary production extracts natural resources (farming, mining), and direct production means producing for one's own use rather than for others. **Answer: C.**
Peter changes his job from a cook to a bus driver. This is an example of:

Occupational mobility is the ease with which a worker changes from one kind of job to another (cook to bus driver). Geographical mobility is a change of place of work. Economic planning in Cameroon is necessary in order to:

The main aim of economic planning is to set targets and share resources among regions and sectors so that the whole country develops in a balanced way. Improving trade and attracting investment are only means or side effects. **Answer: D.**

A commercial bank earns most of its income from the interest charged on loans and advances, which is higher than the interest it pays on deposits. Accepting deposits and issuing cheques are services that bring little or no profit. **Answer: C.**
The integrating factor for the differential equation $x\dfrac{dy}{dx}+4y=\dfrac{e^{x}}{x}$ is

Write the equation in standard form $\dfrac{dy}{dx}+P(x)y=Q(x)$ by dividing by $x$:

$$\dfrac{dy}{dx}+\dfrac{4}{x}y=\dfrac{e^{x}}{x^{2}}.$$

The integrating factor is $e^{\int P\,dx}=e^{\int 4/x\,dx}=e^{4\ln x}=x^{4}$ (for $x>0$). Multiplying by $x^4$ gives $\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(x^{4}y\right)=x^{2}e^{x}$, which can be integrated directly. The traps are to use $4x$ or $e^{4x}$ (integrating the coefficient $4$ instead of $4/x$) or to forget to divide by $x$ first. **Answer: C.**

$\dfrac{x^{2}}{x^{2}-4}$ expressed in partial fractions, where $P$, $Q$ and $R$ are real constants is

$$\dfrac{x^{2}}{x^{2}-4}=1+\dfrac{4}{x^{2}-4}=1+\dfrac{1}{x-2}-\dfrac{1}{x+2},$$

that is $P=1$, $Q=-1$, $R=1$ in the form $P-\dfrac{Q}{x-2}-\dfrac{R}{x+2}$ (sympy confirms $1+\frac1{x-2}-\frac1{x+2}$). Option A has no constant term, and options C and D contain $(x-2)^2$, a repeated factor that is not in the denominator. **Answer: B.**
If $f(x)=3\cosh2x-1$, then the minimum value of $f(x)$ is

If $P$ and $Q$ are statements, then $\sim(P\Rightarrow Q)\equiv$

$x=at^{2}$, $y=2at$, $a\in\mathbb{R}$, are the parametric equations of a curve where $t$ is the parameter. The length of the arc for $0\le t\le1$ is given by

The arc length of a parametric curve is $s=\displaystyle\int\sqrt{\left(\dfrac{dx}{dt}\right)^{2}+\left(\dfrac{dy}{dt}\right)^{2}}\,dt$. Here $\dfrac{dx}{dt}=2at$ and $\dfrac{dy}{dt}=2a$, so

$$\sqrt{4a^{2}t^{2}+4a^{2}}=2a\sqrt{1+t^{2}}\qquad(a>0),$$

and $s=2a\displaystyle\int_0^1\sqrt{1+t^{2}}\,dt$. The sum (not the difference) of the squares appears under the root, which rules out D, and the square root cannot be dropped, which rules out C. **Answer: B.**
The polar equation of the curve $x^{2}+y^{2}=2x$ is

The rate of decay of cells in a certain culture is directly proportional to the number $n$ of cells present at time $t$. Treating $n$ as a continuous variable, $k$ a positive constant, then $n$ satisfies the differential equation

A particle $P$ moves on the curve with equation $r=ae^{\theta}$ with constant angular speed $\omega$. The transverse component of acceleration of $P$ is
