A **weight-losing (bulk-reducing) industry** loses a lot of weight in processing (for example cement, sugar, timber, mining), so it saves transport costs by locating near the raw materials. A weight-gaining industry (A) locates near the market, and a footloose industry (B) can be located almost anywhere. **Answer: D.**
The main hindrance to large scale farming in villages is:

In most villages land is held under customary **land tenure systems**: it is inherited, shared among family members and split into very small plots, so a farmer cannot easily gather a large area. This is the main obstacle to large-scale farming. Soil infertility and rural exodus (A, D) matter but are not the main hindrance. **Answer: B.**
A negative income elasticity of demand suggests that the good is:

Income elasticity of demand (YED) is the percentage change in quantity demanded divided by the percentage change in income. A **negative** YED means that demand falls when income rises, which is the definition of an **inferior good** (for example cassava or second-hand clothes). A normal good (A) has positive YED. **Answer: C.**
A new HP computer in Japan costs 1,000 Euros. The exchange rate between Euros and CFA Francs is 1 Euro = 655CFAF. How much will a Cameroonian need in order to buy this computer?
Price in FCFA $= 1{,}000 \times 655 = 655{,}000$ FCFA. The Cameroonian pays in his own currency, so the answer is in FCFA, not in Euros (A, C). **Answer: B.**
Which one of the following instruments involve the buying and selling of securities to the public?

**Open market operations** are the buying and selling of government securities (treasury bills and bonds) by the central bank to the public in order to change the amount of money in circulation. The cash ratio (A) fixes the cash banks must hold, and moral suasion (D) is persuasion without any buying or selling. **Answer: B.**
Assume that the cash ratio of a single bank is 20% and its total deposit is 1,500,000 FCFA. Calculate how much the bank has to keep to meet up with her customers' demand?
Cash to keep in reserve $= 20\% \times 1{,}500{,}000 = 0.2 \times 1{,}500{,}000 = 300{,}000$ FCFA. The remaining $1{,}200{,}000$ FCFA (A) can be lent out. **Answer: C.**

Which one of the following diagrams represents a contraction of the demand curve?

![Four demand diagrams A to D: A and C show an arrow along a single curve D (up and down), B shows a shift from D to D1 to the right, D shows a shift from D to D1 to the left (Question 43). Redrawn from the scan.](/media/figures/cm/gce-ol-economics-2015-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_4.webp)

A **contraction** of demand is a movement **up along the same demand curve**: the price rises and the quantity demanded falls. Diagram A shows the arrow moving up the curve. Diagram C is an extension (movement down the curve), diagram B is an increase in demand (shift to the right) and diagram D is a decrease in demand (shift to the left). **Answer: A.**

The following table shows the cost structure of a firm:

| Output (in units) | 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Total costs (in FCFA) | 5,000 | 7,500 | 12,000 | 21,000 | 32,000 |

The marginal cost of producing the 3rd unit of output is:

Marginal cost of the 3rd unit $= TC_3 - TC_2 = 21{,}000 - 12{,}000 = 9{,}000$ FCFA. Option B is $TC_4 - TC_3 = 11{,}000$ (the marginal cost of the 4th unit), option A is $TC_2 - TC_0 = 7{,}000$ (the cost of the first two units together), and option D is $(21{,}000 - 5{,}000) / 3 \approx 5{,}333$, the average variable cost of 3 units, not the marginal cost. **Answer: C.**
All indirect taxes are regressive because:

An indirect tax is a fixed percentage of the **price** of a good, whatever the buyer's income. Rich and poor pay the same amount on the same good, so the tax takes a **larger share of a poor person's income** than of a rich person's: it is regressive. Option C describes a progressive tax, and B and D do not describe how indirect taxes work. **Answer: A.**
Higher and lower income levels pay the same percentage of price in taxation
The poor pay a lesser amount than the rich
As income increases a higher proportion is paid
Higher income brackets pay smaller amounts as taxes

Study the nature of the set up of the authorized capital of a private company and answer the question that follows:

1,000 Ordinary shares at 5,000 FCFA each

1,000 Preference shares at 10,000 FCFA each

500 debentures at 25,000 FCFA each

What is the monetary value of debentures?

Value of debentures $= 500 \times 25{,}000 = 12{,}500{,}000$ FCFA, that is **12.5 million FCFA**. Option A ($1{,}000 \times 5{,}000$) is the ordinary shares and option C ($1{,}000 \times 10{,}000$) the preference shares. **Answer: B.**

Sunk capital (fixed capital that cannot be transferred) is capital invested in an asset that has **one specific purpose** and cannot be used for anything else without a great loss, for example a railway line or a mine shaft. Capital that can be used for any purpose (A) is called circulating or liquid capital. **Answer: D.**
Capital which can be used for any purpose
Capital used to satisfy any personal savings
Capital used to satisfy specific personal saving
Capital which has a specific purpose
Which financial institution is charged with the responsibility of issuing new bank notes and coins into circulation?

The sole right to issue notes and coins belongs to the **central bank** (here the Bank of Central African States, BEAC). The Treasury (A) manages government accounts and commercial banks (D) only receive and lend out deposits. **Answer: C.**

In managing his restaurant, John made a weekly budget of 180,000 FCFA. Of this amount, he allocates 90,000 FCFA for bread for breakfast. If a loaf of bread costs 300 FCFA, how many loaves of bread will he buy per week.
Only the amount allocated to bread is used: number of loaves $= \dfrac{90{,}000}{300} = 300$ loaves. Option A ($180{,}000 / 300$) wrongly uses the whole budget. **Answer: B.**
Give another name for variable costs of production

Variable costs change with output (raw materials, direct labour). They are also called **prime costs** (direct costs). Overhead and supplementary costs (B, D) are the fixed costs that do not change with output, and sunk costs (C) are costs that cannot be recovered. **Answer: A.**
Which of these statements of scale is the correct conversion of the ratio scale 1:25000?

The ratio 1:25 000 means 1 cm on the map is 25 000 cm on the ground. 25 000 cm = 250 m = 0.25 km = $\frac{1}{4}$ km. A wrong choice such as $\frac{1}{2}$ km comes from dividing by 50 000 instead.

**Answer: C.**
Which of these statements is NOT true about Eastings?

Eastings are the vertical grid lines. They link the north and south edges of the map, and their values increase towards the east, so they are numbered from West to East. Statement D is therefore false: the numbering is not from North to South.

**Answer: D.**
They run vertically on the map
They link the North and South of the map
They are numbered from North to South
Which group of features will indicate that a settlement renders administrative functions?

Administrative functions are those of government and public order. A post office, a city hall, army headquarters and a prison are all run by the State or the council. Group A shows commercial functions, B recreational and cultural functions, and C a mixture of educational, religious and industrial features.

**Answer: D.**
Parking, gardens, ancient monument, sport centre
Post office, city hall, army headquarters, prison
Which of the following map scales is the smallest?

The smaller the fraction, the smaller the scale. $\frac{1}{150\,000}$ is smaller than $\frac{1}{100\,000}$, $\frac{1}{50\,000}$ and $\frac{1}{5\,000}$. A small scale shows a large area with little detail. A common mistake is to call 1:5,000 the smallest because 5,000 looks like the smallest number.

**Answer: D.**
An Ordnance Survey map has a scale of 1/100,000. If the distance between two measured points is 32 cm, what will be the actual distance?

Actual distance = map distance × scale denominator = $32 \times 100\,000 = 3\,200\,000$ cm. Convert to kilometres: $3\,200\,000 \div 100\,000 = 32$ km (1 km = 100 000 cm). So 1 cm on this map is 1 km, and 32 cm is 32 km.

**Answer: B.**
If the time is 1.00 pm in London (Longitude 0°), what will be the time at a place located 75°W?

The Earth turns $15^\circ$ per hour. Difference = $75 \div 15 = 5$ hours. A place west of Greenwich is behind in time, so we subtract: 1.00 pm − 5 h = 8.00 am. Adding 5 hours (6.00 pm) is the usual error.

**Answer: C.**
The earth's movement from west to east on its axis in an anti-clockwise direction is known as:

Rotation is the spinning of the Earth on its axis, from west to east (anticlockwise when seen from above the North Pole), once in about 24 hours; it causes day and night. Revolution is the yearly movement around the Sun.

**Answer: A.**
All of the following are proofs of the earth's spherical shape EXCEPT:

Aerial and satellite photographs show a curved horizon, sunrise and sunset happen at different times in different places, and a ship disappears hull first over the horizon. The changing length of day and night is caused by the tilt of the Earth's axis and its revolution round the Sun, not by its shape, so it is not a proof of sphericity.

**Answer: C.**
Variations in lengths of day and night
The downward movement of water from the surface of the earth into the soil is:

Infiltration is the downward movement of water from the surface into the soil. Stem flow and drip flow happen on vegetation (interception), and base flow is groundwater feeding a river.

**Answer: B.**
Which of the following is an input into a drainage basin?

Inputs are the water entering the system: precipitation (rain, snow, hail). Interception, infiltration and throughflow are stores or transfers inside the basin.

**Answer: B.**
Lines drawn on weather maps joining places of equal mean air temperature:

Isotherms join places with the same temperature. Isonephs join equal cloud cover, isohyets equal rainfall and isobars equal pressure.

**Answer: D.**
The trend of continuous increase in world temperatures in the atmosphere in the 20th century is called:

A continuous rise in the average temperature of the atmosphere is global warming. The greenhouse effect is the mechanism that traps heat, and climate change is a wider term that also covers changes in rainfall and winds, so it is not the best answer.

**Answer: C.**
Air that cannot hold more water vapour is said to be:

Air that has reached the maximum amount of water vapour it can hold at its temperature is saturated (relative humidity 100%, dew point reached). Humid only means that it contains much vapour.

**Answer: B.**
Which of these activities is most likely to increase environmental disturbances?

Burning garbage releases smoke and harmful gases and adds to air pollution and global warming. Recycling water, cleaning rivers and planting trees protect the environment.

**Answer: C.**
Which of the following aspects is most likely to check flooding?

Trees intercept rain and their roots increase infiltration, so less water reaches the rivers quickly: afforestation reduces flooding. Heavy precipitation, urbanisation (concrete surfaces, fast run-off) and deforestation all increase it.

**Answer: D.**
Which of these is NOT a means of adaptation of plants in the tropical desert biome?

Desert plants have long tap roots, thick seed coats and succulent stems to find and store water and resist heat. Large buttress roots are found in tropical rainforest trees, which are tall and shallow-rooted, so C is not a desert adaptation.

**Answer: C.**
Long tap roots to absorb groundwater
Thick seed coats to protect it from intense heat
Large buttress roots to support trees
Thick succulent stems to store water
Which of the following is associated with vegetation of the tropical rain forest?

The tropical rainforest is made of evergreen trees arranged in layers (emergent, canopy, understorey, shrub and ground layers). Tall grass with scattered trees is savanna, and conical branches belong to coniferous forests. A is partly true of rainforest trees, but C is the best defining feature.

**Answer: C.**
The most abundant soil material produced by wind action in arid areas is:

Wind erodes by deflation and abrasion and carries sand, the commonest material in deserts (dunes and sand sheets). Silt forms loess, and clay and loam are not the main product of wind action in arid areas.

**Answer: C.**
What type of soil is found in the coniferous forest ecosystem?

Cold, wet climates with acid needle litter leach the soil strongly and form podzols under coniferous (taiga) forests. Brown earth belongs to deciduous forests and chernozem to temperate grasslands.

**Answer: A.**
Which of the following is not an intrusive volcanic feature?

Intrusive features form when magma cools underground: dyke, batholith, laccolith, sill. A volcanic cone is built on the surface by lava and ash, so it is extrusive.

**Answer: C.**
An underground feature in a limestone area is?

A cave is a hollow dissolved under the ground. Doline, uvala and polje are surface depressions (small, medium and large).

**Answer: A.**
All of these statements are stages in the formation of barchans EXCEPT:

A barchan starts when sand collects around an obstacle, grains are carried up the windward face and slide down the slip face, and eddies at the sides push sand forward to form the horns. Blasting of sand against rock is abrasion, which erodes rock (for example mushroom rocks); it is not a stage of barchan formation.

**Answer: C.**
Sand moves slowly forward as sand grains are carried up the wind face
Sand is blasted against the rock
Eddies push sand forward to form horns
Which of the following is the correct sequence of occurrence of the denudation process?

Rock is first broken down by weathering, then the loose material is removed and transported by erosion, and finally dropped as deposition. Deposition cannot come before the material has been weathered and eroded.

**Answer: A.**

Which of the following is important in the formation of deltas?

*Options as printed:* A) Weak currents at the mouth of the river   B) Saline water with strong currents   C) Fast flow at the mouth of the river   D) Slow silting at the mouth of the river

Deltas form where a river carrying a large load of sediment enters a calm, shallow sea or lake, where waves, tides and currents are too weak to remove the deposits. Strong currents (B) and fast flow (C) would carry the load away. Option D is vaguely worded (silting is a result, not a condition), so the question is ambiguous between A and D.

**Intended answer: A (Weak currents at the mouth of the river).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.
Which process involves the movement of material along the beach?

Longshore drift is the zigzag movement of sand and pebbles along a beach: waves push material up the beach at an angle (swash) and the backwash returns it straight down. The other terms are not standard processes.

**Answer: B.**
Which of the following is a MAJOR cause of air pollution?

Smoke from vehicles, factories and bush burning carries gases and fine particles and is a major source of air pollution. Vapour, moisture and heat are not pollutants in themselves.

**Answer: D.**
Release of vapour into the atmosphere
Release of heat into the atmosphere
Release of moisture into the atmosphere
Release of smoke into the atmosphere
Which of the following is a consequence of global warming?

Higher temperatures melt polar ice sheets and glaciers, which raises sea level. A fall in sea level is the opposite of what happens, crop yields generally fall in many regions, and urban decay is unrelated.

**Answer: B.**
All of the following are indicators of development EXCEPT:

Standard indicators of development are the number of patients per doctor (health care), the literacy rate (education) and the energy consumed per person (industrial and economic level). The number of children per family is a family size figure and is not one of the usual indicators.

**Answer: C.**
The most important factor that favours the creation of a Multipurpose River Development Project is:

A multipurpose project (dam for electricity, irrigation, flood control) depends first on the physical site: a river with a regular, reliable flow all year, to fill the reservoir and run the turbines. Capital, labour and demand are also needed but can be obtained from elsewhere, while the river cannot.

**Answer: C.**
The regular flow of a river

Intensive farming involves all of the following EXCEPT:

*Options as printed:* A) Use of glass houses   B) Irrigation   C) Monoculture   D) Use of fertilizer

Intensive farming puts large inputs of capital and labour on a small area to get high yields: glasshouses, irrigation and fertilizers are typical. Monoculture (one crop on a large area year after year) is usually linked to extensive or plantation farming, so it is the intended odd one out, although intensive farms can also grow a single crop.

**Intended answer: C (Monoculture).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.
The agricultural system which involves the cutting and burning of vegetation for 2 to 3 years and abandoning of the land completely by the farmer when the soil loses fertility is:

In shifting cultivation the farmer clears and burns a plot, farms it for 2 to 3 years, then abandons it completely and moves to a new plot. In bush fallowing the farmer returns to the same plot after a rest period. Nomadic herding concerns animals, and crop rotation keeps the land in use.

**Answer: C.**
Which term best describes planting of trees where no forest had existed?

Afforestation is planting trees on land that was not forest before. Reforestation replants an area where forest was cut down, and deforestation is the clearing of forest.

**Answer: C.**
Which of the following energy resources is renewable?

Hydro-electric power comes from flowing water, which is replaced by rainfall. Coal, natural gas and petroleum are fossil fuels that take millions of years to form and are non-renewable.

**Answer: C.**
Which of the following is the leading producing area of crude oil in the world?

The Middle East (Saudi Arabia, Iran, Iraq, Kuwait, United Arab Emirates) has the largest reserves and output of crude oil in the world. The Gulf of Guinea, the Gulf of Mexico and the North Sea are important but smaller.

**Answer: C.**
Which of the following phrases best describes fishing done in rivers and lakes?

Inland fishing is done in fresh water: rivers, lakes and ponds. Coastal and offshore fishing take place in the sea, near the coast or farther out.

**Answer: A.**
Accessibility to large urban centres is an important factor in the dairy industry because of:

Fresh milk and other dairy products spoil quickly, so dairy farms are located close to large towns, which are also the main market, to deliver them quickly. The other options do not give a reason for the location.

**Answer: B.**
Easy movement to the city centre
A more thirsty dense urban population
More milk factories located in urban centres
The greatest invention of the beef industry to secure a global market is:

Refrigeration (refrigerated ships and trains from the 1870s) allowed meat to be stored and exported over long distances without spoiling, opening global markets. Canning exists but is secondary, and glass houses are for crops.

**Answer: B.**
Tourism can best be defined as:

Tourism is travel for leisure to a place outside one's home which includes at least one night's stay. A visit to a foreign country is only one case, and a day visit or a work visit is not tourism in this definition.

**Answer: C.**
A visit to a foreign country
A visit for leisure which includes a night stay
A visit for work that involves a night stay
In modern times, the transportation of Petroleum products from one place to another is done by:

Pipelines carry crude oil, petrol and gas over long distances cheaply and safely, continuously and with low running costs. Canals, cableways and containers are not suited to bulk liquids.

**Answer: D.**
Which of the following is NOT a member of the trade bloc ECOWAS?

ECOWAS is the Economic Community of West African States. Cote d'Ivoire, Nigeria and Niger are West African members, while the Republic of Congo is in Central Africa.

**Answer: B.**
If the surface area of a place is 475, 000 km² and its total population is 16,000,000. What is the population density of the area?

Population density = population ÷ area = $\frac{16\,000\,000}{475\,000} = 33.68 \approx 34$ persons per km². Option D (03.4) is not 34.

**Answer: C.**
All of the following are positive checks to population growth given by Malthus EXCEPT:

For Malthus the positive checks raise the death rate: disease, war and famine. Early marriage would increase births, and delayed marriage (moral restraint) is a preventive check, so C is the exception.

**Answer: C.**
When a town expands and merges with the surrounding villages or towns, the resultant settlement is called:

A conurbation is a continuous built-up area formed when towns grow and merge (for example the Ruhr or Greater Manchester). A megalopolis is a chain of conurbations, and a megacity or millionaire city is defined by population size, not by merging.

**Answer: D.**
Which of the following farming is near large cities?

Market gardening grows perishable vegetables, fruit and flowers close to large cities, which supply the market and the transport. Ranching, plantations and bush fallowing need large areas of cheaper land away from towns.

**Answer: C.**

Global warming is the rise in the average temperature of the Earth's atmosphere. A rising sea level is a consequence, more greenhouse gases are a cause, and the ozone hole is a different problem.

**Answer: B.**
The hole in the Ozone layer
Which of the following is a major cause of land pollution in most towns in Cameroon?

Most Cameroonian towns have few big industries or mines, but households produce large amounts of rubbish (plastic, food waste) that is dumped in open spaces and drains. Domestic waste is therefore the main cause.

**Answer: A.**
Cameroon is often referred to as "Africa in miniature" because:

Cameroon has many of the physical and human features of the whole continent: forest, savanna, mountains, coast, desert edge, many ethnic groups and several religions. B states this general idea. C is too narrow and not exact (Cameroon has no Mediterranean climate), and A and D are wrong or too partial.

**Answer: B.**
She speaks all languages in Africa
Most of what is present in Africa is found in Cameroon
She cuts across all climates of Africa
She is a Muslim and Christian country
In which major climatic region does the northern part of Cameroon belong to?

Northern Cameroon (Adamawa, North and Far North) has the tropical (Sudan type) climate, with one long dry season and a short rainy season. Equatorial climate is in the south, and there is no true desert or temperate climate in the north.

**Answer: C.**
Which one of these falls under invisible trade?

Invisible trade is the trade in services that cannot be seen or touched, such as insurance, banking, tourism and transport. Cocoa, petroleum and timber are visible goods.

**Answer: C.**
A major tourist's attraction in the Far North region of Cameroon is the:

Waza National Park, in the Far North region, is famous for elephants, lions, giraffes and antelopes. Campo and Korup are in the South and South West (rainforest), and Dja is in the East.

**Answer: C.**
Which of the following missionary bodies showed interest in British annexation of Cameroon before 1884?

The English Baptist Missionary Society, working on the coast since Joseph Merrick (1843) and Alfred Saker (1845), had close ties with Britain. Its missionaries and the Douala chiefs repeatedly asked Britain to annex the coast, and Saker was ready to accept British rule. The American Presbyterians came in 1879 and the Basel Mission (Swiss-German) in 1886, and the Catholic Pallottines arrived in 1890, all after the annexation question was settled or without a British interest. **Answer: A.**
The Douala chief who opposed the signing of the Germano-Duala treaty was...

The treaty of July 1884 was signed by Kings Bell and Akwa. Lock Priso (Bele Bele), chief of Hickory Town (Bonaberi) across the Wouri, refused German rule, and a German force destroyed his town in December 1884. King Pass All was another chief who signed. **Answer: C.**
Which of these Coastal towns was founded by British missionaries in 1858?

Alfred Saker of the English Baptist Missionary Society founded Victoria (now Limbe) in 1858 as a settlement for freed slaves and Christian converts. Douala, Kribi and Tiko were African or trading settlements. **Answer: B.**
Who of the following German officials was a signatory to the Germano-Duala treaty of July 1884?

Gustav Nachtigal, the German imperial commissioner, reached the Cameroon coast in July 1884 and concluded the treaties with the Douala kings (the treaty is dated 12 July, with the Woermann agents Schmidt and Voss also involved). Hans Dominik and Eugen Zintgraff were later explorers and officers in the interior, and Emile Schulze is not linked to the treaty. **Answer: C.**
The German colonial Governor who convened an important conference on educational reforms in Cameroon in 1907 was...

Theodor Seitz became Governor in 1907 and called the conference of missions and administration on education in 1907, which led to the education reforms and the 1910 school regulations (more German taught, state control of mission schools). Von Puttkamer (1895-1907), Gleim (1910-1912) and Ebermaier (1912-1914) were other governors and are not tied to the conference. **Answer: C.**
In which of the following towns did the British remain in control after the German annexation of Cameroon until 1887?

After 1884 the British kept the Victoria-Bimbia area, where the Baptist settlement and British interests were, until Britain ceded it to Germany in 1887. Buea and Douala were never British, and Bimbia was part of the same area, but Victoria was the centre of British control. **Answer: A.**

Which of the following African territories supplied the Allies with troops during their invasion of Cameroon in the 1910s?

*Options as printed:* A) Egypt   B) The Gambia   C) The Gold Coast   D) Kenya

The Allied invasion of German Kamerun in 1914-1916 used mainly British West African Frontier Force units from Nigeria and the Gold Coast, plus French troops from French Equatorial Africa and Belgian troops from the Congo. Egypt and Kenya were not involved. The Gambia is also reported to have sent a company, so the key is not certain.

**Intended answer: C (The Gold Coast).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.
Select the world power that fought against the Germans in Cameroon during the 1914 - 1916 war...

Britain, France and Belgium fought the Germans in Cameroon in 1914-1916. Belgium contributed troops from the Belgian Congo. Portugal entered the war only in 1916 and did not fight in Cameroon, Spain was neutral (Spanish Guinea received fleeing German troops in 1916), and the U.S.A. joined the war in 1917 and fought in Europe. **Answer: D.**
Which of the reasons below explains why the Cameroons was administered as an integral part of Nigeria from 1922?

When the League of Nations gave Britain the mandate over the British Cameroons in 1922, the mandate agreement (Article 9) allowed Britain to administer the territory as an integral part of neighbouring Nigeria. This was a legal permission from the League, not a request by the Cameroonians, and it was not a reward for rescuing the territory. **Answer: B.**
The territory was rescued by Britain during world war 1
The League of Nations permitted Britain to do so.
Britain feared interference of French officials from French Cameroon
British Southern Cameroons requested its integration with Nigeria.
On which institution did the Indirect Rule System in Cameroon depend for its successful implementation?

Indirect rule worked through the Native Authority, that is the traditional chief or council recognised and supervised by British officials, who collected taxes, kept order and judged cases. Native Courts, Native Treasuries and Native Authority schools were organs set up under the Native Authority, so the system depended first on the Native Authorities. **Answer: A.**
Which of the following pairs of French Colonial Policies was abandoned in 1946 as a result of the Brazzaville Conference?

The Brazzaville Conference of 1944 recommended the end of the indigenat (a set of special punishments applied to Africans) and of forced labour (prestation). Both were abolished in 1946. Assimilation was not abandoned then, and la mise en valeur (economic development of the colonies) was continued. **Answer: C.**
Corvee and la mise en Valeur.
Prestation and la mise en Valuer.
An important political reform introduced in French Cameroon as a result of the Brazzaville Conference of the 1940s was...

After Brazzaville, France gave its territories representative bodies. In French Cameroon the Representative Assembly (ARCAM) was created in 1946. The post of Prime Minister came only in 1957, abolition of forced labour was a social and labour reform and not an institution, and the electoral college stayed double (separate colleges for French citizens and Africans). **Answer: B.**
Introduction of Post of Prime Minister.
Introduction of the Cameroon Representative Assembly (ARCAM).
Introduction of a single electoral college.
What was the positive effect of World War II on Cameroonians?

The war made Cameroonians aware of their rights (contact with Free French and political ideas, soldiers back from the war, the Atlantic Charter), so nationalism grew after 1945. German planters and institutions were removed after World War I, and loss of lives and property was a negative effect. **Answer: A.**
Which Legislative Assembly came into being in French Cameroon in 1957 as a result of the 1956 elections?

The loi-cadre (Defferre law) of 1956 led to the elections of December 1956 and to the Legislative Assembly of Cameroon (ALCAM, Assemblee Legislative du Cameroun) in 1957, which chose the first Prime Minister, Andre-Marie Mbida. ARCAM (1946) and ATCAM (1952) were earlier assemblies, and RACAM does not exist. **Answer: A.**
In which of these Conferences was a petition submitted by Dr Endeley to the Lyttelton Commission requesting a Regional Status?

Dr E.M.L. Endeley and the Southern Cameroons delegation went to the London constitutional conference of 1953, chaired by the Colonial Secretary Oliver Lyttelton, and asked for a separate Region for the Southern Cameroons. The Mamfe conference of 1959 dealt with the plebiscite and the London conference of 1957 gave Southern Cameroons quasi-federal status. **Answer: A.**
In which of these towns in British Southern Cameroon was a meeting held to discuss the plebiscite issue in 1959?

The Mamfe Conference of 1959 brought together the Southern Cameroons political leaders (KNDP, KNC and others) to discuss the plebiscite questions proposed by the UN. Buea was the capital, and the other towns hosted different meetings. **Answer: C.**

Question 17 is based on this extract of a speech made by a prominent French Cameroon Political leader in the 1960s. "... Today, Cameroon is free and independent...." Identify the author of the speech above.

On 1 January 1960 the Prime Minister, Ahmadou Ahidjo, proclaimed the independence of French Cameroon, and he became the first President. Mbida was Prime Minister in 1957-1958 and Assale in 1958-1960 (both before independence), and Moumie, the UPC leader, opposed Ahidjo. **Answer: B.**
Select the date French Cameroon achieved its independence.

French Cameroon became independent on 1 January 1960. 11 February 1961 was the plebiscite date, and 1 October 1961 was the reunification day when Southern Cameroons joined the Republic of Cameroon. **Answer: A.**
In which Conference did the leaders of the British Southern Cameroons meet for re-unification talks with the Republic of Cameroon?

The Foumban Constitutional Conference of 17-21 July 1961 brought Ahidjo's government and the Southern Cameroons delegation (Foncha, Muna, Jua and others) together to discuss the constitution of the Federal Republic. The Bamenda All-Party Conference (June 1961) was a meeting between Southern Cameroons parties to prepare their position. **Answer: D.**
Which of the following West Cameroon Political leaders occupied the twin posts of Prime Minister of West Cameroon and Vice President of the Federal Republic from 1968 to 1972?

S.T. Muna succeeded A.N. Jua as Prime Minister of West Cameroon in 1968 and at the same time held the post of Vice President of the Federal Republic until 1972. Foncha was Vice President of the Federal Republic from 1961 to 1970, Jua was Prime Minister in 1965-1968, and Endeley was the first Southern Cameroons Premier. **Answer: B.**
In which year did the franc C.F.A replace the Pound Sterling in West Cameroon?

West Cameroon used the Nigerian pound until the federal government introduced the CFA franc as the single currency of the Federation, which happened in 1962 (the Bank of West Africa notes were withdrawn). The other years are distractors. **Answer: A.**
The date 20th May 1972 is important in the political history of Cameroon because it marked....

On 20 May 1972 a referendum approved President Ahidjo's proposal and the Federal Republic became the United Republic of Cameroon, a unitary state. Independence was 1 January 1960, reunification 1 October 1961, and the Federal Republic was born in 1961. **Answer: C.**
re-unification Day of the two Cameroons
birth of the Unitary State of Cameroon
birth of the Federal Republic of Cameroon
All of the following events took place in Cameroon under President Paul Biya except the...

Under Biya the University of Buea (1992), the entry into the Commonwealth (1995) and the creation of ten provinces (1983 reorganisation) took place. The Unitary State was established in 1972 under President Ahidjo. **Answer: C.**
creation of an Anglo-Saxon University in Buea.
admission of Cameroon into the Common Wealth.
In which year did Cameroon become a full member of the Common Wealth and la Francophonie?

Cameroon was admitted into the Commonwealth at the Auckland summit in November 1995, and this is the date taught for its full membership of both organisations. 1980, 1985 and 1990 are distractors. **Answer: D.**
Cameroon is a member of the following organisations except...

Cameroon belongs to CEMAC (Central African Economic and Monetary Community), the Lake Chad Basin Commission and the African Union, but it is a member of ECCAS in Central Africa, not of ECOWAS, which is a West African grouping. **Answer: C.**
The European Monarch whose activities in the Congo basin led to the summoning of the Berlin Conference of 1884-1885 was...

King Leopold II of Belgium financed Stanley's treaties and the International African Association in the Congo basin, which alarmed Britain, France and Portugal and led Bismarck to call the Berlin Conference. The other names are not monarchs linked to the Congo. **Answer: D.**

Question 27 is based on this description of an African resistance leader in the 1890s. "He displayed bravery against the French imperialists and earned for himself the title 'Black Napoleon Bonaparte' of the Sudan ...." Identify the resistant African leader above

Samori Toure built the Mandinka (Wassoulou) empire and fought the French for about sixteen years until his capture in 1898, which earned him the name of the Napoleon of the Sudan. Menelik II defeated Italy at Adowa (1896), Prempeh was the Asante king, and Jaja ruled Opobo. **Answer: B.**
In the course of the scramble for Africa, Fashoda incident of 1898 was the scene of colonial rivalry between....

At Fashoda on the Upper Nile, the French expedition of Marchand met the British force of Kitchener in 1898. France withdrew, and the crisis ended with the 1899 agreement that separated the French and British spheres. **Answer: A.**
Which British colonial policy was friendly towards African traditional rulers and institutions?

Indirect rule used the traditional rulers and their institutions as local government under British supervision. Assimilation and association were French policies, and paternalism was applied by the Belgians. **Answer: D.**
In which African territory was the colonial policy of paternalism largely practised?

Paternalism, treating Africans like children who needed guidance, was the Belgian policy in the Belgian Congo (with the Church and companies providing education and health). Guinea Bissau was Portuguese, and Senegal was French (assimilation). Rwanda was also Belgian, but the Congo is the typical example. **Answer: A.**

The First World War was fought in the following African territories except...

*Options as printed:* A) Tanganyika.   B) Togoland.   C) Mozambique.   D) South West Africa.

The intended answer is Mozambique, a Portuguese colony, whereas Tanganyika (German East Africa), Togoland and South West Africa were German colonies attacked by the Allies. Fighting did however reach Mozambique in 1917-1918 (German forces crossed into it), so the question is not clear.

**Intended answer: C (Mozambique).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.
The African Statesman often associated with Pan African movement in the 1940s and 1950s and gained independence for his country in the 1950s was ...

Kwame Nkrumah took part in the 1945 Pan-African Congress in Manchester and led the Gold Coast to independence as Ghana in 1957. Garvey and Du Bois were Pan-Africanists outside Africa who did not lead independence, and Kenya became independent only in 1963 under Kenyatta. **Answer: B.**
African nationalism may be defined as...

African nationalism was the movement of Africans against colonial rule to regain self-government and independence. It was not racial hatred, and neo-colonialism is a feature of the period after independence. **Answer: C.**
African hatred for the white race.
African reluctance to accept European policies
African opposition to European colonial rule
African hatred and rejection of neo-colonial tendencies.
Which Pan-African leader convened The All-Africa Peoples' Conference in December 1958?

Kwame Nkrumah called the All-African Peoples' Conference in Accra in December 1958, after Ghana's independence, to unite the African liberation movements. Senghor, Houphouet-Boigny and Sekou Toure were French West African leaders. **Answer: B.**
These Southern African Liberation Movements, FRELIMO and MPLA, were very important in decolonisation of the Portuguese colonies of ...

FRELIMO (Front for the Liberation of Mozambique) fought Portugal in Mozambique and the MPLA (Popular Movement for the Liberation of Angola) fought in Angola, until independence in 1975. Rhodesia, South Africa, Tanzania, Uganda and South West Africa were not Portuguese colonies. **Answer: A.**
The French West African nationalist leader who formed the RDA, served as Minister in the 4th French Republic and led Cote d'Ivoire to independence in 1960 was...

Felix Houphouet-Boigny founded the Rassemblement Democratique Africain (RDA) in 1946, was a minister in French governments and became the first President of Cote d'Ivoire in 1960. Sekou Toure led Guinea (1958), Blaise Diagne was a Senegalese deputy earlier, and Nyerere led Tanganyika. **Answer: A.**
In which African country did a civil war breakout, following the attainment of independence that led to the death of a U.N Secretary General on a peace keeping mission?

The Congo (now the Democratic Republic of Congo) fell into civil war after independence in 1960 (Katanga secession). UN Secretary General Dag Hammarskjold died in a plane crash in September 1961 on his way to talks in the Congo conflict. **Answer: D.**
Which of the following Angolan Political Movements formed the first government when Angola achieved independence from Portugal in 1957?

The MPLA under Agostinho Neto proclaimed independence in Luanda in 1975 and formed the first government. SWAPO is a Namibian movement, and the FNLA and UNITA were rival Angolan movements. The date 1957 in the question is a misprint for 1975. **Answer: A.**
Which South African Racist President released Nelson Mandela from prison in 1990?
President F.W. de Klerk lifted the ban on the ANC and freed Mandela on 11 February 1990. Verwoerd (killed in 1966), Vorster and P.W. Botha were earlier apartheid leaders. **Answer: C.**
All the following African countries were founding members of the OAU in 1963 except...
The OAU was founded in Addis Ababa in May 1963 by 32 independent states, including Nigeria, Senegal and Libya. Zimbabwe became independent only in 1980 and joined later. **Answer: D.**
The European Statesman who dominated European diplomacy in the 1870s and 1880s was...

Otto von Bismarck, Chancellor of Germany, built the alliance system (Dreikaiserbund, Dual Alliance, Triple Alliance) that isolated France and dominated European diplomacy after 1871. Metternich belonged to the early nineteenth century, Guizot was a French minister in the 1840s, and Francis I was a sixteenth century king. **Answer: B.**
Which important agreement between France and Russia in 1892 signalled the end of German isolation of France in Europe?

The Franco-Russian (Dual) Alliance, agreed in 1892 and ratified in 1894, ended Bismarck's isolation of France. The Entente Cordiale (Britain-France) is of 1904, and the Triple Alliance (Germany, Austria-Hungary, Italy) was of 1882. **Answer: D.**
The following were reasons for the outbreak of the First World War except...

The assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand (the question writes 'Frank'), naval rivalry between Britain and Germany and colonial rivalry were causes. The collapse of the German Empire in 1918 was a result of the war. **Answer: B.**
The collapse of the German Empire.
The Peace treaty signed between the Allies and Austria at the end of the First World War was...
The Treaty of Saint-Germain-en-Laye (September 1919) was signed with Austria. Sevres was with Turkey (1920), Trianon with Hungary (1920) and Lausanne replaced Sevres in 1923. **Answer: D.**
Which of the following European Powers was not invited to attend the Paris Peace Settlement of 1919 - 1920 because of the Bolshevik revolution in 1917?
Russia, now under the Bolsheviks, had signed a separate peace at Brest-Litovsk (1918) and was not invited to Paris. Italy, France and Japan were among the winning Allies present. **Answer: A.**
The European power that became a member of the League of Nations in 1926 after signing the Locarno treaty was...

Germany accepted its western frontiers in the Locarno treaties of 1925 and was admitted to the League of Nations in September 1926. Russia joined in 1934, and Austria and Hungary joined in 1920 and 1922. **Answer: D.**
Which Japanese city was destroyed by the use of the atomic bomb by the Allies in 1945?

The United States dropped atomic bombs on Hiroshima (6 August 1945) and Nagasaki (9 August 1945), which led to Japan's surrender. Of the options, only Nagasaki was a bombed city: Tokyo was fire-bombed, Okinawa was an island invaded, and Manchuria is a region of China. **Answer: C.**
Which one of these cities served as the Headquarters of the League of Nations?
The League of Nations had its headquarters in Geneva, Switzerland. New York is the headquarters of the United Nations. **Answer: D.**
Which World Power was instrumental in the creation of the League of Nations but never became a member of this International Organisations?

President Woodrow Wilson proposed the League in his Fourteen Points, but the US Senate refused to ratify the Treaty of Versailles in 1920, so the U.S.A. never joined. Japan and Italy were members at first, and the U.S.S.R. joined in 1934. **Answer: B.**
The disease that is socially hated and has devastated and affected millions of families and remains the pre-occupation of medical experts around the world is...
HIV-AIDS carries a strong social stigma, has killed and orphaned millions (especially in Africa) and has no cure yet, so medical research continues. **Answer: C.**

Identify the event which initiates blood clotting:

*Options as printed:* A) Excess flow of blood through a capillary.   B) Conversion of fibrinogen into fibrin.   C) Lysis of platelets at the wound site.   D) Production of thrombokinase enzyme.

Clotting starts when the damaged vessel wall and the platelets break down (lyse) at the wound and release thrombokinase (thromboplastin). This enzyme then triggers the conversion of prothrombin to thrombin, and thrombin converts soluble fibrinogen into insoluble fibrin (B), which is the last step. Options C and D both describe the beginning of the chain (the platelets break first, then thrombokinase is released), so the key is not certain.

**Intended answer: C (Lysis of platelets at the wound site).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.
A drug that makes the users see or hear things that do not exist is called a:

A hallucinogen (for example LSD) distorts perception so that the user sees or hears things that are not there. Stimulants speed up the nervous system, and depressants and sedatives slow it down. **Answer: A.**
The incubation period of a disease is the:

The incubation period is the interval between the entry of the pathogen into the body and the first appearance of signs and symptoms. The other options describe the period when symptoms are already present. **Answer: B.**
Time during which the symptoms of the disease appear.
Time between initiation of infection and the appearance of first signs and symptoms of the disease.
Time during which the physical expressions of the disease are diagnosed.
Time during which the signs and symptoms of the disease appear.
Smooth muscles differ from cardiac muscles in that, they have:

Smooth (involuntary, unstriated) muscle is made of spindle-shaped cells with one nucleus each. Cardiac muscle fibres are striated and branched (D), while cylindrical multinucleated fibres belong to skeletal muscle (C). Striations (A) are a feature of cardiac and skeletal muscle, not of smooth muscle. **Answer: B.**
The central nervous system is made up of:
The central nervous system (CNS) consists of the brain and the spinal cord only. Nerves and ganglia belong to the peripheral nervous system. **Answer: A.**
Choose the correct reagent from the list below that is used to test food samples for the presence of reducing sugars:

Benedict's reagent is heated with the food sample: a colour change from blue to green, yellow, orange or brick-red shows a reducing sugar. Sudan III tests for fats, and Biuret's and Millon's reagents test for proteins. **Answer: C.**
The digestive disorder caused by the absence of fibre in the diet is known as:
Fibre (roughage) adds bulk to the faeces and stimulates peristalsis. Without it the faeces become hard and move slowly, which is constipation. **Answer: C.**
One advantage of the biconcave shape of a red blood cell is:

The flattened biconcave disc has a large surface area compared with its volume, so oxygen diffuses in and out quickly. Option C is the opposite of the truth. Options A and D are less accurate: the shape is mainly explained by the large surface area. **Answer: B.**
To provide more space for the accommodation of more haemoglobin.
To provide a large surface area for rapid absorption of oxygen.
To provide a small surface for the rapid absorption of oxygen.
To reduce the distance between haemoglobin molecules and the cell membrane.
Identify the muscle that brings about the movement of substances within the digestive tract:

The wall of the alimentary canal contains smooth (involuntary) muscle whose waves of contraction, called peristalsis, push food along. Striated and voluntary muscles move the skeleton, and cardiac muscle is found only in the heart. **Answer: D.**
Which of the following enzymes is secreted in an inactive form to prevent auto-digestion?

Pepsin is secreted by the stomach wall as inactive pepsinogen, which is activated by hydrochloric acid. This protects the cells of the stomach, which are made of protein, from being digested. The other enzymes are released in active form. **Answer: B.**
When the blood glucose level is at 70mg/100ml (Low) of blood, a healthy human body will regulate the blood glucose level as follows:

A low blood glucose level makes the islets of Langerhans release glucagon. Glucagon makes the liver convert stored glycogen into glucose, which raises the blood glucose level. Insulin does the opposite: it lowers a high level by converting glucose to glycogen. **Answer: C.**
Glucose is converted to glycogen in the presence of glucagon.
Glucose is converted to glycogen in the presence of insulin.
Glycogen is converted to glucose in the presence of glucagon.
Glycogen is converted to glucose in the presence of insulin.
Urine produced by the kidney is excreted through:

Urine leaves the kidney by the ureter, is stored in the bladder and is finally passed out of the body through the urethra. The bladder only stores urine, the ureter only carries it to the bladder, and the collecting ducts are inside the kidney. **Answer: B.**
A person of blood group AB is described as a universal recipient because:

Group AB red cells carry both antigens A and B and the plasma has no anti-A or anti-B antibodies, so blood of any group (A, B, AB or O) can be received without clumping. Options B, C and D each leave out one group. **Answer: A.**
He/She can receive blood from any blood group.
He/She can receive blood from groups A,B and O
He/She can receive blood from groups AB,A and B
He/She can receive blood from groups AB and O
A virus is a nucleic acid core (DNA or RNA, never both) surrounded by a protein coat (capsid). **Answer: A.**
A nucleic acid core surrounded by a protein coat.
A mixture of DNA and RNA
A protein surrounded by nucleic acid
An outer envelope of lipids only.
Identify the stage in the life cycle of the pork tapeworm that is found in the muscle of the secondary host:

The embryo (onchosphere or hexacanth embryo) leaves the egg in the pig's intestine, bores into a blood vessel and is carried to the muscles, where it develops into the bladderworm (cysticercus). Eating undercooked pork with bladderworms infects man. **Answer: D.**
The liver is the largest organ in the body and because of its important functions, it has three blood vessels. Select the correct vessels that conduct blood to or from the Liver.

The liver receives oxygenated blood from the hepatic artery and blood rich in digested food from the hepatic portal vein, and blood leaves through the hepatic vein. The renal vessels belong to the kidney. **Answer: C.**
Hepatic artery, Hepatic portal vein, Hepatic vein.
Mesenteric artery, Hepatic portal vein, Mesenteric vein.
What is the name of the unique substance produced by the human body in response to invasion by disease-causing agents?

An antibody is a protein made by lymphocytes in response to a particular antigen; each antibody is specific to its antigen. The antigen is the foreign substance itself, and lymphocytes and phagocytes are cells. **Answer: B.**
The following organs are from the male and female reproductive systems respectively. Select the pair of organs that have equivalent functions.

The testes and the ovaries are the gonads: both produce the gametes (sperms and eggs) and the sex hormones. The other pairs do not have equivalent roles (for example the scrotum protects the testes, while the uterus houses the embryo). **Answer: D.**
Which of the following factors may likely result in multiple birth?

Fertility drugs stimulate the ovaries to release several eggs at the same time, which may be fertilised and give twins or more. Contraceptive pills and the diaphragm prevent pregnancy, and the number of partners does not change the number of eggs released. **Answer: A.**
In the Nitrogen cycle, the group of bacteria that convert nitrates in the soil into Nitrogen gas are called:

Denitrifying bacteria change nitrates into nitrogen gas, which returns to the air. Nitrogen-fixing bacteria change nitrogen gas into compounds, and nitrifying bacteria change ammonium compounds into nitrites then nitrates. **Answer: B.**
The purpose of installing a damp-proof course in the foundation of a building is to:
A damp-proof course is a layer of waterproof material (bitumen, plastic sheet) built into the walls near the ground to stop moisture from rising up the walls (rising damp). **Answer: A.**
Prevent rats burrowing into the building.
Identify the air pollutant that is correctly matched with its effect:

Carbon monoxide combines with the haemoglobin of the red blood cells (erythrocytes) more strongly than oxygen does, so less oxygen is carried. Sulphur dioxide causes acid rain, chlorofluorocarbons deplete the ozone layer, and global warming is mainly due to carbon dioxide and methane (not smoke). **Answer: C.**
Sulphur dioxide - depletion of ozone layer.
Carbon monoxide - reduces oxygen transport by erythrocytes.
Why is it necessary for a pregnant woman to register at an antenatal clinic early in the course of her pregnancy?

Early registration allows diseases (anaemia, malaria, infections) to be found and treated, so that mother and baby stay healthy. Option B is not the aim, C is too strong ("all" infections) and D is wrong because testing and counselling are confidential. **Answer: A.**
Early diagnosis and treatment of any disease will enable her and her unborn baby to be healthy.
Early diagnosis facilitates the birth process.
Early treatment protects her from all Infections.
Early diagnosis allows non-confidential HIV testing and counseling.
Water can be best purified in the home by:

Boiling kills the disease-causing micro-organisms, so it is the best home method of making water safe. Storing only protects water from re-contamination, and iron(III) chloride is not used to purify drinking water. **Answer: C.**
Storing in containers with tight-fitting lids.
Adding Iron III Chloride to it.
Most of the energy produced during aerobic respiration is stored as:

The energy released in aerobic respiration is used to make ATP (adenosine triphosphate) from ADP and phosphate. ATP is the immediate energy store of the cell. Glycogen is a long-term store, and starch is not found in cell walls. **Answer: B.**
Mitosis is the cell division which:

In mitosis one cell divides once to give two daughter cells genetically identical to the parent and to each other. Mitosis happens in all organisms (B), gives two cells not four (C), and sex cells are formed by meiosis (D). **Answer: A.**
Occurs during the formation of sex cells.
Identify the enzyme found in pancreatic juice which digests proteins.

Trypsin is the protease of pancreatic juice; it changes proteins into peptides. Pepsin comes from the stomach, erepsin (peptidases) from the small intestine wall, and enterokinase is the intestinal enzyme that activates trypsinogen. **Answer: C.**
A hormonal response differs from a nervous response in that, it is:
Hormones are carried by the blood, so the response is slow, but the effect lasts a long time. A nervous response uses electrical impulses, so it is rapid and short-lived. **Answer: D.**
The process by which gaseous exchange occurs in the alveolus is:

Oxygen and carbon dioxide move across the thin alveolar wall by diffusion, from the region of higher concentration to the region of lower concentration. Osmosis is the movement of water only. **Answer: A.**

Anaemia is a disease of the circulatory system which may result from:

i. Shortage of blood from the body

ii. Prolonged malaria infection

iii. Rupture of blood capillaries

iv. Fatigue and shortness of breath

Choose

*Options as printed:* A) if i, ii, and iv are correct   B) if i, ii, iii are correct   C) if ii and iv are correct   D) if i, ii, iii and iv are correct

Anaemia is a shortage of red cells or haemoglobin. It can be caused by loss of blood (i), by destruction of red cells in prolonged malaria (ii) and by bleeding from ruptured capillaries (iii). Fatigue and shortness of breath (iv) are symptoms of anaemia, not causes. The intended key is therefore i, ii and iii, but the question mixes causes and symptoms.

**Intended answer: B (if i, ii, iii are correct).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.
Give the name of the process by which the kidneys regulate the water and salt content of the body:

Osmoregulation is the control of the water and salt (osmotic) content of the body, done mainly by the kidneys under the control of ADH. Ultrafiltration and selective reabsorption are steps of urine formation, and homeostasis is the general term for keeping the internal environment constant. **Answer: C.**
The sebaceous glands of the skin:

The sebaceous glands open into the hair follicles and secrete sebum, an oily substance that keeps the skin and hair soft and supple and waterproof. Melanin is made by melanocytes in the epidermis. **Answer: C.**
Produce the skin pigment called melanin.
Protect the skin against microbial invasion.
Secrete sebum which makes skin supple.
Absorb harmful UV rays from the sun.

An albino woman married to a man with normal skin pigmentation, had four children with normal skin colour. The grandchildren of this couple were of mixed complexion; some albinos, and others normal. What genetic conclusion can be deduced from the above observations?

An albino mother ($aa$) and a normal father give children who all have normal skin, so these children carry the albinism allele but do not show it: the allele for albinism is recessive. The children ($Aa$) later give albino grandchildren when two carriers meet ($Aa \times Aa$ gives $aa$ with probability $\frac{1}{4}$). **Answer: B.**
The allele for albinism is dominant to that for normal skin pigmentation.
The allele for albinism is recessive to that for normal skin pigmentation.
Skin colour is controlled by traditional and cultural beliefs.
The alleles for albinism and normal skin pigmentation are co-dominant.
A potential consequence of deforestation is:

Without the plant cover and roots, rain washes (leaches) the mineral ions out of the soil and causes erosion. The ozone layer is depleted by chlorofluorocarbons, and acid rain comes from sulphur and nitrogen oxides. Eutrophication is caused by fertilisers and sewage. **Answer: C.**
The depletion of the ozone layer.
The leaching of soil mineral ions.
In an adult with normal dentition, there are more:

The adult has 8 incisors, 4 canines, 8 premolars and 12 molars. So there are more molars (12) than incisors (8). Canines (4) are fewer than incisors (8), premolars (8) are fewer than molars (12), and incisors and premolars are equal (8 each). **Answer: C.**
Identify the disease from the list below whose causative agent is a protozoan.
Malaria is caused by the protozoan Plasmodium. Syphilis and chlamydia are caused by bacteria, and thrush is caused by a fungus (Candida). **Answer: A.**
The cell wall of bacteria is composed of:

The bacterial cell wall is made of peptidoglycan (murein), a compound of sugars (carbohydrate) and amino acids (protein). Cellulose is the wall of plant cells, and chitin is found in the wall of fungi. **Answer: C.**
The most highly recommended method for disposing of plastic wastes below is:

Plastics are not biodegradable, so burying them leaves them in the soil for years, and burning releases toxic gases. Recycling re-uses the plastic and is the most highly recommended method. **Answer: D.**

Which of the statements below are correct aims for administering first-aid?

(i) To promote fast recovery

(ii) To replace medical treatment

(iii) To prevent worsening of an accident or disease condition

(iv) To relieve pain

Choose

The aims of first aid are to prevent the condition from becoming worse (iii), relieve pain (iv) and promote recovery (i). First aid never replaces medical treatment (ii): it only gives help until a doctor takes over. So (i), (iii) and (iv) are correct. **Answer: A.**
If i, iii, and iv are correct.
If ii, iii, and iv are correct.
If i, ii, iii are correct.
If i, ii, iv are correct.

Fertilisation is completed when the haploid nucleus of the sperm fuses with the haploid nucleus of the egg, giving a diploid zygote. Option D is wrong because the zygote is diploid. Options B and C only describe the contact or the place, not the completed fusion of nuclei. **Answer: A.**
There is fusion of the nuclei of the egg cell and sperm cell.
There is fusion of the egg cell and sperm cell.
There is union of the egg cell and sperm cell in the oviduct.
There is formation of a haploid zygote.
The term 'pure strain' refers to an organism that:
A pure strain (pure-breeding, homozygous) organism has two identical alleles for the gene, so it always passes on the same allele and breeds true. **Answer: B.**
Has un-identical alleles for a gene.
Has identical alleles for a gene.
Always produces the same type of genes.

One important quality of a material used for clothing is:

*Options as printed:* A) It covers our nakedness   B) It is absorbent   C) It contains cotton fibers   D) It provides warmth

Among the options, absorbency (the ability to take up sweat and moisture) is a property of the material itself, so the intended key is B. But "provides warmth" (D) is also a function of clothing materials such as wool, so the printed key is uncertain.

**Intended answer: B (It is absorbent).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.
Which of the following is true of playgrounds?
A playground is an open space planned in a community for play, games and recreation. It is not mainly a place for reflection, nor mainly for weight loss. **Answer: B.**
They are areas of reflection for youths.
They are areas where violence is condemned.
They are areas for cutting down body weight.
The most abundant component of blood plasma is:
Plasma is about 90 percent water, with dissolved salts, glucose, proteins and hormones. The cells and platelets are not part of plasma. **Answer: C.**
Which of the following is an example of a conditioned reflex?

A conditioned reflex is a response learned through experience and practice, so it is not inborn. Learning to walk is acquired in this way. Withdrawal from a hot object, coughing and yawning are inborn (simple) reflexes. **Answer: B.**
Withdrawal of the hand from a hot object

Questions 46 and 47 are based on the sketch of a mammalian eye focusing light. Study the sketch below and answer the questions that follow.

![Sketch of a mammalian eye focusing light: the rays are still converging when they reach the back of the eye (Questions 46 and 47).](/media/figures/cm/gce-ol-human-biology-2015-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_1.webp)

What type of eye defect is illustrated in the sketch?

In the sketch the light rays have not yet met when they reach the retina: they would cross behind the eyeball. This happens in a short eyeball or a weak lens, and it is called hypermetropia (long sight). In myopia the rays cross in front of the retina. Cataract (cloudy lens) and glaucoma (high pressure in the eye) do not change where the rays meet. **Answer: A.**

Questions 46 and 47 are based on the sketch of a mammalian eye focusing light (see the sketch below).

![Sketch of a mammalian eye focusing light: the rays are still converging when they reach the back of the eye (Questions 46 and 47).](/media/figures/cm/gce-ol-human-biology-2015-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_1.webp)

How could the eye defect demonstrated in the sketch be corrected?
Hypermetropia needs extra converging power, so a convex lens is placed in front of the eye to bring the rays together on the retina. Concave (biconcave) lenses are used for myopia. **Answer: A.**

One hour thirty minutes after eating a heavy starch meal, the blood sugar level of Mrs Mary Njoke rose from 7.8 mmol/dl of blood to 14.0 mmol/dl blood. Study the graph below of her blood sugar level against time and answer the question that follows.

![Blood sugar level (mmol/dl) against time in hours after a heavy starch meal (Question 48).](/media/figures/cm/gce-ol-human-biology-2015-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_2.webp)

How long did it take for the blood sugar level to return to its initial value?

*Options as printed:* A) 4 hours   B) 3 hours   C) 3 hours 30 minutes   D) 5 hours

On the graph the level is flat at about 7.8 until 1 hour, rises to 14.0 at 1.5 hours, then falls back to about 7.9 at 5 hours on the time axis. The question does not say from which moment the time is counted, so more than one option can be defended: 5 hours on the axis (D), 4 hours from the start of the rise at 1 hour (A), or 3 hours 30 minutes from the peak at 1.5 hours (C).

**Intended answer: not certain (5 hours read on the axis, 4 hours from the start of the rise, or 3 hours 30 minutes from the peak).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.
Identify the gland that secretes the hormones which regulate blood sugar level:

The islets of Langerhans of the pancreas secrete insulin (lowers blood glucose) and glucagon (raises it). The liver stores and releases glucose but is not an endocrine gland, and the pituitary and adrenal glands have other main roles. **Answer: C.**

A reflex action is a rapid, automatic (involuntary) response to a stimulus that does not need conscious thought. It may be controlled by the spinal cord or by the brain, so A and D are too narrow, and B describes only the pathway of an impulse. **Answer: C.**
A rapid response controlled by the spinal cords.
The pathway of an impulse along a neurone.
A rapid automatic response to a stimulus.
A rapid response controlled by the brain.

The common denominator of 8 and 5 is 40. So $\frac{1}{8}+\frac{2}{5}=\frac{5}{40}+\frac{16}{40}=\frac{21}{40}$. The trap is to add the numerators and the denominators separately, $\frac{1+2}{8+5}=\frac{3}{13}$ (option B). **Answer: C.**
Given that $3^{-2}\times 3^{p}=27$, then $p$ has the value

We add the indices of the same base: $3^{-2}\times 3^{p}=3^{p-2}$. Since $27=3^{3}$, we get $p-2=3$, so $p=5$. A sign error ($p+2=3$, giving $p=1$, or $-2-p=3$, giving $p=-5$) leads to a wrong option. **Answer: B.**
The denary number $27$ expressed in binary system is

Write 27 as a sum of powers of 2: $27=16+8+2+1=1\times2^{4}+1\times2^{3}+0\times2^{2}+1\times2^{1}+1\times2^{0}$, so the binary number is $11011_{2}$. Check by dividing by 2 repeatedly: the remainders read from the bottom are 1, 1, 0, 1, 1. Option A ($11101_2=29$) has the same digits in another order. **Answer: D.**
On a cold evening the outside temperature of a house is $-4^\circ\text{C}$ and inside the temperature is $12^\circ\text{C}$. The temperature inside the house is higher than that outside by
The difference is inside minus outside: $12-(-4)=12+4=16$. Subtracting a negative number means adding. The trap is to compute $12-4=8$ (option B). **Answer: C.**
Change the mixed number into an improper fraction: $12\frac{1}{4}=\frac{49}{4}$. Then $\sqrt{\frac{49}{4}}=\frac{7}{2}=3\frac{1}{2}$. Check: $3.5^{2}=12.25$. **Answer: D.**
In ascending order, $40\%$, $\frac{3}{5}$, $0.75$ can be written as

Convert everything to decimals: $40\%=0.40$, $\frac{3}{5}=0.60$ and $0.75$. In ascending (increasing) order: $0.40<0.60<0.75$, that is $40\%,\ \frac{3}{5},\ 0.75$. Option A is in descending order of the first two terms; the other options put $\frac{3}{5}$ before $40\%$. **Answer: C.**
An element in the set $S=\left\{\frac{2}{3},\ -4,\ 1.5,\ \sqrt{2}\right\}$ which is an integer is
Integers are the whole numbers $\dots,-2,-1,0,1,2,\dots$ (positive or negative). $\frac{2}{3}$ and $1.5$ are not whole numbers, and $\sqrt{2}$ is irrational. Only $-4$ is an integer. **Answer: A.**
$0.0596$ expressed correct to three decimal places is

We keep three decimal places: $0.059|6$. The digit after the third decimal place is 6, which is 5 or more, so we round up: $0.059+0.001=0.060$. Writing $0.059$ (option C) is truncation, not rounding. **Answer: B.**
The number $0.0188\times 10^{-1}$, written in standard form is
First write $0.0188=1.88\times10^{-2}$. Then $0.0188\times10^{-1}=1.88\times10^{-2}\times10^{-1}=1.88\times10^{-3}$ (the indices are added). **Answer: C.**
Bernard pays for electricity at a rate of $55\ \text{FCFA}$ per unit. Given that he uses $2$ units of electricity per day, his bill, in FCFA, in a month of $30$ days will be
Units used in the month: $2\times30=60$ units. Bill $=60\times55=3300$ FCFA. The units used per day ($2$) must be multiplied by the number of days before the rate is applied. **Answer: B.**
A trader sold a dress for $40{,}000\ \text{FCFA}$ at a loss of $20\%$. The cost price of the dress, in FCFA, was

A loss of $20\%$ means the selling price is $80\%$ of the cost price: $0.8\times\text{CP}=40\,000$, so $\text{CP}=\frac{40\,000}{0.8}=50\,000$ FCFA. The trap is to take $20\%$ of $40\,000$ and subtract it (option C, $32\,000$). **Answer: A.**
Given that $P:Q=3:1$ and $Q:R=2:5$, then the ratio $P:R=$
Make the value of $Q$ the same in both ratios. $P:Q=3:1=6:2$ and $Q:R=2:5$. So $P:Q:R=6:2:5$ and $P:R=6:5$. **Answer: B.**

Figure 1 shows the set $Q=\{\text{Chemistry}\}$ and $P=\{\text{Physics}\}$. The number of students who offer Chemistry or Physics is

![Venn diagram of figure 1: universal rectangle, circle Q containing circle P; 7 in P, 9 in Q outside P (question 13).](/media/figures/cm/gce-ol-maths-2015-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_1.webp)

In the Venn diagram the circle $P$ lies inside the circle $Q$. There are $7$ students inside $P$ and $9$ in $Q$ outside $P$. "Chemistry or Physics" is the union $P\cup Q$, which is the whole circle $Q$: $7+9=16$ students. Option C counts only the region of $Q$ outside $P$. **Answer: D.**
Given that $P\cap Q=\{\ \}$, then the sets $P$ and $Q$ are said to be

$P\cap Q=\{\ \}$ means that $P$ and $Q$ have no element in common. Two sets with an empty intersection are called disjoint sets. (A null set is the empty set itself, and "subsets" would mean one set lies inside the other.) **Answer: C.**
State the sentence that is a statement

A statement is a sentence that is either true or false. "He can write" is a declarative sentence, so it is a statement. "Sit down" is a command, "What time is it?" is a question and "The apple tree" is only a phrase, so none of these can be true or false. **Answer: A.**

Given the statements:

$p$: All Principals are attending a meeting.

$q$: John is a Principal.

then $p\wedge q$ means

The symbol $\wedge$ means "and": $p\wedge q$ says that both statements hold, that is, all Principals are attending a meeting and John is a Principal. Only option D combines the two facts (John is a Principal, and he is attending a meeting). Options A, B and C only repeat the conclusion that can be drawn about John, not the conjunction. **Answer: D.**
The meeting is attended by John
John is a Principal attending a meeting

The number of vertices for a tetrahedron is
A tetrahedron is a triangular pyramid: it has $4$ faces, $6$ edges and $4$ vertices (a triangular base with 3 vertices plus the apex). Euler check: $V-E+F=4-6+4=2$. **Answer: A.**
A regular polygon has an interior angle measuring $108^\circ$. The name of the regular polygon is a

The exterior angle is $180^\circ-108^\circ=72^\circ$. The number of sides is $\frac{360^\circ}{72^\circ}=5$, so the polygon is a pentagon. (Check: $\frac{(5-2)\times180^\circ}{5}=108^\circ$.) **Answer: D.**
A quadrilateral that has four equal sides, a rotational and point symmetry is called a
Four equal sides rule out a trapezium, a rectangle and a general parallelogram. A rhombus has four equal sides, rotational symmetry of order 2 and point symmetry about its centre. **Answer: C.**

The number of terms in the expression $-2x+6y-5t+6$ is

Given that $p=\frac{t-m}{t+m}$, then writing $m$ in terms of $p$ and $t$ gives
Multiply both sides by $(t+m)$: $p(t+m)=t-m$, so $pt+pm=t-m$. Collect the terms in $m$ on one side: $pm+m=t-pt$. Factorise: $m(p+1)=t-pt$. Hence $m=\frac{t-pt}{p+1}$. **Answer: A.**
The coefficient of $x$ in the expansion $\frac{1}{3}(2y-3x+w)$ is
Expand: $\frac{1}{3}(2y-3x+w)=\frac{2}{3}y-x+\frac{1}{3}w$. The term in $x$ is $-x=-1\times x$, so the coefficient is $-1$. Option A forgets to multiply by $\frac{1}{3}$. **Answer: C.**

Substitute $x=2y-1$ into $2x=3y+2$: $2(2y-1)=3y+2$, so $4y-2=3y+2$ and $y=4$. Then $x=2(4)-1=7$. Check in the second equation: $2\times7=14=3\times4+2$. The trap is to give the value of $y$ (option B). **Answer: A.**
When $f(x)=3x^{2}+kx-5$ is divided by $(x-2)$ the remainder is $11$. The value of $k$ satisfying this condition is
By the remainder theorem, the remainder on division by $(x-2)$ is $f(2)$. $f(2)=3(4)+2k-5=7+2k$. Setting $7+2k=11$ gives $2k=4$, so $k=2$. **Answer: C.**

Given that $T$ is directly proportional to $M$ and that when $M=4$, $T=20$, then when $M=3$, $T=$

Direct proportion: $T=kM$. From $20=k\times4$, $k=5$. When $M=3$: $T=5\times3=15$. In direct proportion $T$ and $M$ change in the same ratio, so $T$ must be smaller than $20$ when $M$ is smaller than $4$. **Answer: B.**

The determinant of $\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\c&d\end{pmatrix}$ is $ad-bc$. Here $\det=2y-3\times1=2y-3$. Setting $2y-3=1$ gives $2y=4$, so $y=2$. **Answer: B.**

Arrange the 8 numbers in order: $3,\ 4,\ 4,\ 5,\ 7,\ 8,\ 10,\ 12$. With an even number of values the median is the mean of the two middle values (the 4th and 5th): $\frac{5+7}{2}=6$. **Answer: A.**

Figure I shows how three identical resistors x, y and z may be connected in an electrical circuit. When the switch K is closed the current through the battery E is $4.5\ \mathrm{A}$. The reading of the ammeter of negligible resistance would be:

Light of wavelength $590\ \mathrm{nm}$ is incident normally on a grating of $8.0\times10^{5}$ lines per metre. The number of possible diffraction maxima obtained is

Which of the following wave types labelled A to D correctly matches its method of detection?

| B | Light | Photo cells |
| C | Gamma | Thermopiles |

Infra-red is detected by thermopiles (heating effect), light by photocells (or the eye, photographic film), gamma rays by a Geiger-Muller tube, and radio waves by receiver aerials. Only the pairing in row B is correct; rows A, C and D each swap the detectors. **Answer: B.**
Which of the following statements about the motion of objects can NEVER be true?

Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity, and a change of speed is a change of velocity, so a change of speed always means acceleration: A can never be true. A body's speed can change without the object accelerating.

A boy can move as a result of a constant resultant force acting on it.

Without air resistance both balls have the same acceleration $g$ whatever their mass (weight $mg$ divided by mass $m$). Starting from rest through the same height, $h = \tfrac12 g t^{2}$ gives the same time $t = \sqrt{2h/g}$ for both. **Answer: D.**
The time taken by x to reach the ground would be twice that taken by y.

Suppose a light spring is loaded with a mass of $50\times10^{-3}\ \mathrm{kg}$ and it extends by $10\times10^{-2}\ \mathrm{m}$. The force per unit displacement, K, and the period of oscillation are respectively,

Period $T = 2\pi\sqrt{m/K} = 2\pi\sqrt{0.050/5.0} = 0.63\ \mathrm{s}$ ($0.314\ \mathrm{s}$ is $T/2$, i.e. $\pi\sqrt{m/K}$). **Answer: A.**

In an experiment to determine the velocity of sound in air, a vibrating tuning fork of an unknown frequency is struck and held over the end of an open tube and the shortest length which gives a loud sound is $15.0\ \mathrm{cm}$. Assuming that the speed of sound in air at room temperature is $330\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, the possible frequency of the tuning fork is

In the resonance-tube experiment the tube is closed at its lower end (by water) and the fork is held over the open end, so the shortest resonant air column is a quarter of a wavelength: $L = \lambda/4$, $\lambda = 4\times0.150 = 0.600\ \mathrm{m}$. Then $f = v/\lambda = 330/0.600 = 550\ \mathrm{Hz}$ (end correction neglected). A snooker ball x moving with an initial velocity u makes an elastic head-on collision with an identical stationary ball y. Which of the sets of velocities below correctly gives the velocities of x and y after the collision?

| | X | Y |
|---|---|---|
| A | $u/2$ | $u/2$ |
| B | $u$ | $u$ |
| C | $u$ | $0$ |
| D | $0$ | $u$ |

Momentum: $mu = mv_x + mv_y$, so $v_x + v_y = u$. Elastic: relative speed of separation equals relative speed of approach, $v_y - v_x = u$. Solving gives $v_x = 0$ and $v_y = u$: the balls exchange velocities. A conserves momentum but loses kinetic energy, B and C violate momentum conservation. **Answer: D.**

Heating at constant power $P$ gives $P\,t = m c\,\Delta\theta$, so $\dfrac{\Delta\theta}{t} = \dfrac{P}{mc}$ and $c = \dfrac{P}{m\times\text{gradient}}$. The straight line in Figure 4 passes through the origin, through about $(5\ \mathrm{s},\ 2.9\ {}^\circ\mathrm{C})$ and $(10\ \mathrm{s},\ 5.7\ {}^\circ\mathrm{C})$ and ends near $(14.3\ \mathrm{s},\ 7.9\ {}^\circ\mathrm{C})$, so the gradient is about $0.55\ {}^\circ\mathrm{C\,s^{-1}}$. Then $c = \dfrac{1.5\times10^{3}}{60\times0.55} \approx 45\ \mathrm{J\,kg^{-1}\,K^{-1}}$. None of the four printed values matches the graph as drawn (the option $25\ \mathrm{J\,kg^{-1}\,K^{-1}}$ would need a gradient of exactly $1.0\ {}^\circ\mathrm{C\,s^{-1}}$, and $36.6$ a gradient of $0.68$).

The earth exerts a force of $9.8\ \mathrm{N}$ on a $1\ \mathrm{kg}$ mass at its surface of radius $R_E$. Suppose the $1\ \mathrm{kg}$ mass is moved to a point at a height $3$ times (thrice) the earth's radius ($3R_E$) above the earth's surface, then the force on the $1\ \mathrm{kg}$ mass becomes,

Gravitational force follows an inverse-square law in the distance $r$ from the centre of the earth. A height of $3R_E$ above the surface means $r = R_E + 3R_E = 4R_E$, so $F = 9.8\times(R_E/4R_E)^{2} = 9.8/16 = 0.6125 \approx 0.61\ \mathrm{N}$. Taking $r = 3R_E$ (forgetting the radius of the earth itself) would give $1.1\ \mathrm{N}$. **Answer: D.**
